I've been playing "Arma" since it was called "Operation Flashpoint". I have bought every version, and every addon. In all those years, the only thing that really changed is the graphics. This is both a good thing, and a bad thing.
Arma in its various iterations is first and foremost an infantry combat simulator, the vehicles and aircraft are mostly window dressing. It is not Call of Duty. It is the closest thing to real world infantry combat you can come to without enlisting. The AI, for infantry, is generally very competent in most conditions. Occasionally, their odd, out of character behavior seems very lifelike, even human. I won't go on at length, but at times, they'll behave very realistically.
Unfortunately, the AI is also the game's biggest shortcoming. Vehicle AI have always had the driving competency of a near sighted fifteen year-old Asian girl. They run into and over things/people with alarming regularity especially if they get near buildings.
They will occasionally wig out and glitch in place, or enter a Customer Service Feedback Vindaloop that never ends. I have lost count of the number of times I have executed my own team, which is at least quite therapeutic when the frustration becomes too intense.
It is in many ways a fantastic game, and when it's working right, it is absolutely glorious. When it's not working you'll need to take frequent breaks or risk chucking your PC off your balcony.
It is also still a 32-bit engine, which is horrifying because it is EXACTLY the kind of game that would benefit massively from the additional resources 64-bit would provide. I hope they get around to doing that eventually. -edit Is now 64-bit, OOHRAH! The Arma gods have smiled on us
Despite it's flaws, for anyone who is a keyboard commando, a mouse marine, a wannabe soldier, or a real soldier looking to relive his glory days, this is pretty much a must have, and Arma 3 is the best and most beautiful itteration yet. Just make sure you have a bottle of aspirin handy.

Some of you may be reading this because you are unsure of whether to get this game or player unkowns BG.
Short answer: just pay the extra money for PUBG
Long answer:
Although both games are extremely similar, there are some very significant differences between the 2 games, which I can attempt to summarise
1) H1Z1 features a pay to win mechanic, by which if you buy an airdrop with genuine money, you will get overpowered weapons delivered to you mid game. PUBG on the other hand puts random drops all over the map for everyone to use, which is of course fairer, and more fun for everyone.
2) the gunplay in H1Z1 is shoddy and unrefined, shooting any weapon in this game feels awkward and more difficult than it should be. PUBG on the otherhand has gunplay reminisent of a Tom Clancy 3rd/1st person shooter, making the experince feel much more comfortable and less clunky
3) PUBG features very well balanced and enjoyable "on the fly" weapon customisation, along with a large and exotic array of weapons to find and use. H1Z1 has neither.
4) Since PUBG's release only a few months ago, new FREE content has been added and effective patches and fixes have been implemented. H1Z1's new releases on the other hand mostly consist of crates, which can only be opened with real cash (CSGO style). And as of right now, PUBG feels far less buggy and is far better balanced than H1Z1, which at this point has been out over a year longer. oh, and the crates in PUBG are earned in game, free of charge.
5) Getting into a H1Z1 takes ages (from clicking on the game to actually being on the game map), simply because the menu layout is pure aids. PUBG on the other hand, has quick, minimalist menu's that don't waste your time. This increase in efficency is a common place difference between these 2 games.
6) PUBG from a graphical standpoint looks far, far better. enough said
7) if you have a mid level PC, then neither game is going to run very well in terms of FPS, which is pretty common for early access games of this type. but when H1Z1 hits 30fps, it's unplayable.
when people engage in gun fights in this game, the jump up and down and shimmy side to side, which not only is rediculous, but results in people running at only 30fps from ever getting a kill, simply because the jumping and moving animations are so erratic and poor.
PUBG however, solves this problem by making jumping a slower process and quickly charging directions slower. Meaning that even if you only run the game at 30fps, you can still hit a target thats jumping and shimming. I run the game at about 70fps so this doesn't effect me, but I have seen the effects through friends computers.
Basically, the company that runs H1Z1 has created a poorly polished game that they don't even want to correct, now that most of their profit comes from crates and not the core game, it's unlikely that it will even significantly improve.
PUBG's company releases new content and patches frequently and successfully, meaning that the game gets better and better by the week.
So don't buy this trash, get a game made by a company that actual cares about it's product.

Arma 3. Nothing to say but great things. It offers one of the realest FPS military experiences that they had to call it a simulator. Honestly. I've been an FPS junkie for about a decade, and I've never felt genuinely scared in firefights - even on easy difficulty. This game doesn't hold your hand with highlighting where guards are positioned. When you tie that to realistic gun sounds and soldier fatigue, you're playing a bit smarter than you would on CoD.
From previous installations from the Arma series, the controls are at their best. They rule because of their simplicity. Everything feels natural, and unlike other series in Arma where I had to spend 20 minutes configuring my controls, the in-game tutorial spelled everything out plainly. Commanding squads is challenging to begin with because of all of the options and commands, but rewards the tacticial approach for the player that takes their time.
The biggest drawback to the game would be a lackluster story and forgettable dialogue. Though the missions themselves cover a lot of terrain (there's even a fast-forward button) and offer some of the finest shootouts in gaming history, you're always forgetting what you're really doing it all for. I didn't want to divulge the energy in the games more strategic squad commanding elements, so I flaked out on the campaign. The emotional investiment just wasn't there. BUT there are heaps of user-made campaigns that will outshine it.
Also, just throw some salt off my system - the game is so graphically gifted that you'd only be able to max out its settings with SLI 1080s. But even on medium to high settings the game is beautifully optimized and will still look like a next-gen title. Because PC.
But the singleplayer isn't the main reason why you're scowering the reviews. Multiplayer servers and game types effectively make use of the giant maps. I just love how you can enter almost every building.Not only do they offer your standard death matches, CTFs, and game types you'll want to play again under Arma's mechanics, but Battle Royale and the user-made RP mechanics will keep you hooked for hours at a time. RPGs will require you to do a lot of reading of rules and better understanding controls, but it's definitely worth it for the role-playing nut.
I can't speak for Apex, but if its anything like the Arma 2 Operation Expansion, it'll be another thrilling game in and of itself.
Whether you're looking for a realistic military FPS or some hilarious player interactions in multiplayer, this game is well worth the retail price.

Some of you may be reading this because you are unsure of whether to get this game or player unkowns BG.
Short answer: just pay the extra money for PUBG
Long answer:
Although both games are extremely similar, there are some very significant differences between the 2 games, which I can attempt to summarise
1) H1Z1 features a pay to win mechanic, by which if you buy an airdrop with genuine money, you will get overpowered weapons delivered to you mid game. PUBG on the other hand puts random drops all over the map for everyone to use, which is of course fairer, and more fun for everyone.
2) the gunplay in H1Z1 is shoddy and unrefined, shooting any weapon in this game feels awkward and more difficult than it should be. PUBG on the otherhand has gunplay reminisent of a Tom Clancy 3rd/1st person shooter, making the experince feel much more comfortable and less clunky
3) PUBG features very well balanced and enjoyable "on the fly" weapon customisation, along with a large and exotic array of weapons to find and use. H1Z1 has neither.
4) Since PUBG's release only a few months ago, new FREE content has been added and effective patches and fixes have been implemented. H1Z1's new releases on the other hand mostly consist of crates, which can only be opened with real cash (CSGO style). And as of right now, PUBG feels far less buggy and is far better balanced than H1Z1, which at this point has been out over a year longer. oh, and the crates in PUBG are earned in game, free of charge.
5) Getting into a H1Z1 takes ages (from clicking on the game to actually being on the game map), simply because the menu layout is pure aids. PUBG on the other hand, has quick, minimalist menu's that don't waste your time. This increase in efficency is a common place difference between these 2 games.
6) PUBG from a graphical standpoint looks far, far better. enough said
7) if you have a mid level PC, then neither game is going to run very well in terms of FPS, which is pretty common for early access games of this type. but when H1Z1 hits 30fps, it's unplayable.
when people engage in gun fights in this game, the jump up and down and shimmy side to side, which not only is rediculous, but results in people running at only 30fps from ever getting a kill, simply because the jumping and moving animations are so erratic and poor.
PUBG however, solves this problem by making jumping a slower process and quickly charging directions slower. Meaning that even if you only run the game at 30fps, you can still hit a target thats jumping and shimming. I run the game at about 70fps so this doesn't effect me, but I have seen the effects through friends computers.
Basically, the company that runs H1Z1 has created a poorly polished game that they don't even want to correct, now that most of their profit comes from crates and not the core game, it's unlikely that it will even significantly improve.
PUBG's company releases new content and patches frequently and successfully, meaning that the game gets better and better by the week.
So don't buy this trash, get a game made by a company that actual cares about it's product.

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play. Lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes (each with his own distinct personality) to choose from. The banter between the different classes is entertaining to listen to. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow him to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or higher skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since November 2007 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

Saint's Row The Third is an open world sandbox action game developed by Volition and published by Deep Silver. Years after taking Stilwater for their own, the Third Street Saints have evolved from an urban street gang to a household brand name with Saints sneakers, Saints energy drinks and Johnny Gat bobble head dolls all available at a store near you. The Saints are the true kings of Stilwater but their celebrity status has not gone unnoticed. The Syndicate, a legendary criminal fraternity with pawns in play all over the globe, has turned its eye on the Saints and demands tribute or death. Refusing to bend the knee to the Syndicate, the Saints make a daring completely over the top escape and quickly find themselves in a very precarious situation. Dropped right into the heart of the Syndicate controlled city of Steelport with all of their assets taken...it's up to the Saints to reclaim their empire and show the Syndicate why the Third Row Saints are not to be trifled with. Having finished Saints Row 2 and immediately diving right into Saints Row The Third, I have to say that this game is an absolutely fantastic continuation of the series. To summarize, the plot is intriguing, the action superb and the soundtrack is excellent...this title is what a worthy sequel should strive to be.
Fans of the series will find many things familiar while also having alot of new elements to deal with as well which is always refreshing to have in a truly successful franchise. The narrative is very compelling and really grips you from the beginning of the title and forces you to want to see how it plays out as you progress through the game. Happily I am very proud to report that the gameplay, some factors of which I had a problem with in the previous title, has been greatly refined by Volition as the driving, fighting and shooting are all quite intuitive and silky smooth this time around. And as the leader of the Third Row Saints, you will quickly find yourself thrust into some of the most over-the-top action movie like sequences from the very first minute that the game starts which brilliantly sets the pace for the rest of the interesting story. Lastly, let me not forget to mention the wonderful character customization included in this title. Guns, clothing and abilities...there are just so many things you can use to really flesh out your character. With all the options available you will definitely be able to create the Saint that you want to be.
Visually, I find this game to be one of the most beautiful open world titles available. Saint's Row The Third utilizes an excellent blend of depth of field effects, terrific animations, detailed set pieces, gorgeous colors and wonderful lighting that really is quite pleasing to the eye. The city of Steelport is a large heavily populated metropolis and a very interesting place to explore. I constantly found myself spending quite a bit of time just wandering around this wonderfully crafted sand-box environment just to admire the view. The city itself is chock full of unique landmarks and strange residents to interact with as you progress through the great story. Also, the title seems to have taken a completely different artstyle, which seems anime-inspired or cartoonish, over the more realistic look of the previous Saints Row games and it's absolutely terrific and plays very well alongside the completely outrageous action. To summarize, graphically this game will not dissapoint as it manages to deliver quite the presentation to the eyes.
I really enjoyed this game from start to finish as it kept me highly entertained for some time. It does a fantastic job of immersing you and making you feel as though you really are the leader of this organization. I've not tried the co-op but Saint's Row The Thirds single player campaign definitely has much replayability. Also, there are plenty of Steam Acheivements to accquire and Steam Trading Cards to collect. Saint's Row The Third will take you on one heck of a wild ride and is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to open world action gamers.

I typically don't go for this sort of sandbox game. Running things over, killing people almost at random, doing crazy stuff just for the thrill of it is just not my cup of tea. This game is a huge exception. If you’re looking for a deep plot that makes sense, don’t look here. If you’re looking for characters that you could introduce to your mother, don’t look here. If you looking for a deep, tactical shooter or city management simulator, definitely don’t look here. However, if you are looking for one hell of a good time, this is your game. Stick your brain in neutral, sit back, and enjoy the insanity. I mean it when I say this game has issues in the mental department. You can gain reputation (exp.) by wearing things like S&M outfits on the street, as you shoot rival gang members for crying out loud. By the end of the game, your character will be so OPed that the Doom invincibility cheat code looks tame in comparison. The weapons are outlandish, the sidekicks are insane, and the city is your playground. The customization of cars, characters, and weapons is simply overwhelming in the number of different possibilities that are available. If you don’t like what you’ve done with your character, go buy a plastic surgeons office and rework your character however you like. (No, I’m not making this up.) I give this game a 4 out of 5 for mechanics. 3 out of 5 for story and plot (basic side missions with added commentary from sidekicks being main missions should not be done as often as it is in this game). For pure “what the hell am I doing, and why am I enjoying it so much” moments, 5 out of 5.

People often mention things like the purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bat and the previous game's sewage-shooting side quests as the first obvious examples of why Saints Row is fun, but it goes far beyond the in-your-face wackiness. Underneath the masterfully-escalating insanity of the story quests and the zaniness of the side content is a well-written, well-acted, and well-designed open world game. The banter feels natural, the controls are responsive, and the feeling of shooting up a rival gang, or using a tank to cause random mayhem, or careening through the streets dodging traffic is smooth from start to finish. Furthermore, unlike GTA IV, where the characterization and action are completely at odds, Saints Row the Third makes no effort to even pretend your character is anything other than a gleefully homicidal pyromaniac.
This is the rare parody that remembers that it also has to be a GOOD example of its target, and it always knows exactly how far to lean into a joke to have maximum impact without being too overt. Saints Row the Third, against all expectations, was one of 2011's best games. It's absolutely worth every penny.

The first two Saints Row games competed against Grand Theft Auto, but Saints Row the Third pulls away by embracing the ridiculousness that there were traces of in the second game. It's a nice open world shoot-em up with plenty of humour and a story that, as far as gang take over narratives go, does a fantastic job in not taking itself too seriously. Or, well... seriously at all. It's a little short, even with the add-ons, but it's pretty worth it.

I love the Arma series. Arma 3 definitely my favorite in the series by far, it has so much detail in it and it's extremely community friendly. The game isn't just a MilSim, it's also a Zombie survival game, a kart racing game, an RTS game, a role-playing game, and much much more. The massive multiplayer online community for this game has thrived off of it's community created and endorsed custom multiplayer modes, like classic Arma 3 DayZ, Altis Life, Wasteland, or even Battle Royale. There's plenty of servers to join, and plenty of gamemodes to try. All of them have their own unique kinks and features to make it a completely unique experience from the base game. There's even a massively in-depth editor mode in which you can create your own singleplayer or multiplayer scenarios using all the assets in the game, ranging from soldiers to scuba-submarines. With tonnes of script functionality implemented into the game, the editor truly is an endless pool of opportunities. The game as a whole is amazingly worth the base price itself, but if you can grab it on sale (especially the Winter or Summer sale) then it's an absolute steal. The only thing to look out for when purchasing this game are the minimum requirements. It takes a pretty good PC to run this game so make sure you have a proper set up before you invest into this game, other than that, it's fantastic and I highly reccomend it to anyone that enjoys any kind of First Person Shooter experience.

As a fan of the GTA series, and having played the first Saints Row. I wasn't sure if I liked the route that Saints was taking with the ultra ridiculous story. Yes GTA had it's weirdness but nothing quite like this. Saints Row 3 took everything in their own seires and GTA  and turned in into a insane mess of♥♥♥♥♥♥ And it works. This game was much more fun than I would have believed. The combat/shooting system feels good, I never felt as if it didn't do what I asked. It isn't perfect with random frame drops, and mission glitches. But none of that is enough to say that this isn't worth playing. Alot of times I have problems finishing games. But I dropped 20 hours on this without thinking twice and had fun doing it. With weapon/charater upgrades to get. And the fun of blowing up random crap. The one real gripe I have with the game is the driving/flying mechanics. They are just so stiff and boring. Don't get me wrong some of the  vehicles are fun but the actually driving and flying don't feel right at all. The  vehicles have no weight and don't seem to interact with the ground at all. I mean, I've played N64 games where the drivng was more fun so... But outside of that I have no major problems. And if you're a fan of weird crude violent games aka GTA or the first Saints. You'll love this one.

Then I got my hands on Saints Row The Third!  The missions weren't impossible so you could progress, and reeking havoc was done right and what I was longing for the GTA games to get right. I love the Arma series. Arma 3 definitely my favorite in the series by far, it has so much detail in it and it's extremely community friendly. The game isn't just a MilSim, it's also a Zombie survival game, a kart racing game, an RTS game, a role-playing game, and much much more. The massive multiplayer online community for this game has thrived off of it's community created and endorsed custom multiplayer modes, like classic Arma 3 DayZ, Altis Life, Wasteland, or even Battle Royale. There's plenty of servers to join, and plenty of gamemodes to try. All of them have their own unique kinks and features to make it a completely unique experience from the base game. There's even a massively in-depth editor mode in which you can create your own singleplayer or multiplayer scenarios using all the assets in the game, ranging from soldiers to scuba-submarines. With tonnes of script functionality implemented into the game, the editor truly is an endless pool of opportunities. The game as a whole is amazingly worth the base price itself, but if you can grab it on sale (especially the Winter or Summer sale) then it's an absolute steal. The only thing to look out for when purchasing this game are the minimum requirements. It takes a pretty good PC to run this game so make sure you have a proper set up before you invest into this game, other than that, it's fantastic and I highly reccomend it to anyone that enjoys any kind of First Person Shooter experience.

Overall a solid game and fun experience. At the core is fairly basic arcade-like TPS kill-hordes-of-enemies gameplay topped off by a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of character and gang upgrades to the point where you'll always be looking for something meaninful to buy. Money doesn't grow on trees and the game has a fun property purchasing metagame that lets you widen your money flow as well as get a discount for your various ganger disposing tools at owned buildings.
Running around with a gang is fun, but I've only ever found the giant hulk homies to really have a functional purpose outside of being a diversion. Character customization is great, however gang customization is more of a gimick as it really doesn't let you change much about them outside of what breakdance move they greet you with.
The music in the game is pretty enjoyable and modern and the adult swim radio station is hilarious and a great addition to the arsenal.Unfortunatly, there is no on-foot mp3 player like there was in the previous saints-row so you can't go raiding strip clubs to Kanye West's "Power" every chance you get.
There are many ways to get around and blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up as well. You can also drive anything from a souped up street car to an APC with a laser gun to a car crushing tank to a helicopter to a VTOL jet thing to an alien space craft to a personal plane to a tron bike.
Last and perhaps least, is the story line which has a bunch of interesting characters which even includes your own character who's an integral part of each scene and indeed the game's personality. The storyline isn't bad it's just not great. The game tries to put you into a variety of different environments which is nice, but it all pans out the same way more or less.
I'd give this game a solid 8/10.

So much more than just a GTA clone. Saints Row: The Third is basically all of the good things from every GTA game and GTA clone you can think of, with almost none of the annoying parts. Seriously, think of a feature from some other open-world sandbox crime-based game. Customizeable vehicles? Yup. Multiple home bases? Got it. Personal armory where you can swap out weapons easily? You betcha. Ability to make your own radio station playlist? Mhm. Level system with character upgrades? Also got it. Two player co-op play? Yep! And on and on and on. SR3 has an impressive feature set, almost the perfect feature set for a game of this type.
As far as gameplay goes, it's pretty solid and fun. Without giving away plot details the game cranks the ridiculousness up to 11 pretty quickly, but it's the fun kind of over-the-top, not the "seriously, how many bullet sponges can they throw at me" kind. Mission variety in the game is pretty huge as well. It's not just a long line if "steal this car, kill this guy, survive this wave of dudes", though there is a fair amount of that, too. My favorite is a mission where the object is to throw yourself in front of cars and ragdoll over as many of them in sequence as you can.  It adds a much-needed variety to the game.
On to the technical side of things. Combat is mostly intuitive, certainly not hard to get down if you've played any sort of third-person shooter before. Controls are well handled AND customizeable. I played the whole game on a WASD + Mouse setup and never felt like the game was punishing me for not using a gamepad, unlike some other big-name sandbox games. Two player co-op is handled pretty well, very easy to get working, and missions scale in difficulty so you don't feel like you're cheating just by having a second set of hands helping you out.
I'd say Saints Row: The Third is probably the best open world sandbox game I've played in a long time, and probably the best "GTA clone". It's definitely going in my favorites, and I'm now very much looking forward to the fourth and final entry in the series.

Arma 3 started off to a bit of a rocky start, but it has grown up since 2013 and at this point it is hands down the best Military Simulator Sandbox Game on the planet.
Helicopters fly like they do in real life and give good feedback matching what a real pilot would expect form a real helicopter, Anti-Air tanks have auto-cannons that lock on to enemy air vehicles and auto-lead when fired. Airplanes have Chaff/Flares, Maverick (fire and forget) long range missiles and with version 1.60, aircraft now have CCIP targeting systems for dropping bombs, firing rockets or calculating Aim lead on moving ground vehicles and other airplanes just like in the real world.
Artillery and motors uses targeting computers to give you click and kill ease of use. They also tell you time to impact and other real world information, that you can give to your team before hand.
Infantry controls handle very smoothly when compared to Arma 2, It's still not as smooth as say CS:GO, but it's damn close, and can be forgiven for being slightly clunky from time to time.
Driving is very solid experience, even with just a keyboard.
Time Trials will push to be a better player, and muliplayer has endless hours of fun.
The single player campaign isn't the greatest, but it will install in you real world battle tactics that will help you a lot in MP games.
Arma 3 simply is the best game at what it dose, and there really isn't anything quit like it.

Arma 3 started off to a bit of a rocky start, but it has grown up since 2013 and at this point it is hands down the best Military Simulator Sandbox Game on the planet.
Helicopters fly like they do in real life and give good feedback matching what a real pilot would expect form a real helicopter, Anti-Air tanks have auto-cannons that lock on to enemy air vehicles and auto-lead when fired. Airplanes have Chaff/Flares, Maverick (fire and forget) long range missiles and with version 1.60, aircraft now have CCIP targeting systems for dropping bombs, firing rockets or calculating Aim lead on moving ground vehicles and other airplanes just like in the real world.
Artillery and motors uses targeting computers to give you click and kill ease of use. They also tell you time to impact and other real world information, that you can give to your team before hand.
Infantry controls handle very smoothly when compared to Arma 2, It's still not as smooth as say CS:GO, but it's damn close, and can be forgiven for being slightly clunky from time to time.
Driving is very solid experience, even with just a keyboard.
Time Trials will push to be a better player, and muliplayer has endless hours of fun.
The single player campaign isn't the greatest, but it will install in you real world battle tactics that will help you a lot in MP games.
Arma 3 simply is the best game at what it dose, and there really isn't anything quit like it.

I used to like PUBG more but over time I've started to lean more towards this game. PUBG is too slow and clunky, with irritating visual, mechanical and physics glitches whereas H1Z1 is smooth, runs well and has likeable gunplay. If you can forgive the lower population (i.e. longer waiting times in lobbies) and the arguably bad hitregistration, H1Z1 is actually a pretty good game. I've had a lot more laughs with friends in this than in PUBG. It's probably due to the relatively shorter match time in H1Z1 - in PUBG, you spend maybe 20 minutes looting and playing carefully, making sure not to die to something stupid UNTIL you end up dying to something stupid. I'm talking about things you can't defend against, like the zone flipping you off and getting sniped from three different directions while trying to crawl through the open field that happens to be the only thing between you and safety.
The map design in H1Z1 is also far superior to that of PUBG. In PUBG, you can run into a building and find some jeans and a gas can wheras another guy will find an assault rifle or something. In H1Z1, you will almost always find a weapon in a building, and every weapon is usable.
I don't particularly like the Battle Royale genre but I've spent enough time to know that I prefer H1Z1 over PUBG.
(Fortnite: Battle Royale is also pretty cool, go check it out).

Arma 3 was one of my favorite games on PC along with Arma 2 right with it. I loved this game so much and It was one of those games I lost sleep over because there just so much to do.
I got this game back in 2014 because of Altis Life. It was a vanilla RP mod. I loved roleplaying games in Arma 2 as well and I played it for so many hours I lost count. It's probably at like a 1000 on my Steam profile. Anyway, this game was something special to me. I could RP in Altis Life servers or play A3L. If I felt like playing in a Battle Royale that was possible to and this was before H1Z1 even released so it was extremely fresh and new (Same people made H1Z1 BR by the way). If I wanted to play King of the Hill or Wasteland I could and I really enjoyed those. Oh and Realism mods were a thing with ACE/ACRE back which were incredible mods back then. I'm not sure how the Realism mod community is today though, I stopped playing it in 2014.
The only reason I didn't get this game on release was because I needed a new PC to run the game on good settings. I was very eager to play it because Arma 2 was probably my #1 game in PC history thanks to the RP mods and later came DayZ after which blew up and even became a standalone game. It was crazy how big Arma got after that. This game alone had like 6 main games in it. I had months and sometimes years of time into some of these mods. It actually makes me sad that those days are long gone because they were some of my favorite years in gaming. I made so many online friends playing this too that I just haven't had the same experience with any other game in history.
This is #2 on my list of favorite games. Arma 2 is my favorite but this is a close 2nd. Of course I recommend this game. 10/10

This game.....This GAME.
Where do I start, I love the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game, been trying to achieve MLG at BI's series for a long time now. I've played the Arma series since I was rekkin kids on A2 from 600 on Utes with my Ruski tool, holding a base right in the middle for a few hours every day. It's a beautiful and engaging experience, that leaves you on the edge of your seat, sometimes wishing you were holding your Grandma's face to squeeze tight (till she dies)... Tactical decisions are important, using the terrain and engaging with the movement structure of your enemies is a thrilling experience, adrenaline pulses as bullets and rockets fly closeby. You will never have to remember parts of maps (minute detail), as the maps on this are so big that it allows you to use your brain, instead of arena shooters which don't challenge the psyche.
Graphics - The original Arma  3 engine includes DX11 integration and standardised PhysX interactions, due to a new update recently the game has come to include Volumetric Lighting (big +), Upgraded textures (more vibrant), Water Refraction and a host of other improvements (60+ bug fixes - glaring bugs such as the offsight RPG Alamut Optic). The graphics second Terrain to Item models, however new improvements in the recent update have subsided these issues, Gear is of a signicantly high polycount as well as Vehicles.
ISSUES: Now I'm sure most of us have had a bad experience of Arma FPS lag. And for a long time now, BI has been using the BS excuse "It's mods."
Although partly true,  that is actually a lie. The way Arma simulates enemies, its peer to peer network structure, animation timers and no multi-threading support are the real reasons behind the terrible frames of Arma 3.
This. Needs. To. Stop.
Although too late for an A3 release, A4 must leave these issues behind.
Gameplay - Arma 3 can be a deeply tactical and engaging game. Many complex systems entwine with each other to create as much of a realistic experience as possible, for example:
- 27 Hit boxes on overall model (from head to toe)
- Multiple ammo types (ballistics, AP, EPR, special purpose ((need mods for some))
- Multiple types of vests (explosive resistant, harnesses, body armour, fba)
- Multiple attachments (flashlights, scopes, silencers, laserlights)
- Unique damage system that many call BS but is actually indepth af for example: Armour actually takes stress under duress, which creates a deeper and more realistic feel to armour.
- Your gun can deflect bullets
- Bullet penetration
Different types of team play are offered in Arma 3. From 2 - 80ppl, if you wish to be in a large group, there is one out there for you. Expanded group finding features such as the Squad pages and things such as Side chat to hook up with like minded people. There are several clans of varying sizes such as mine, however there are some humungous clans for the more mil sim oriented. Now here's the real thing that makes this stand out from other shooters, I think this is a big thing: anyone can be good at this game. All it takes is knowledge and sensibility when dealing with the sort of situations Arma 3 can spawn. Such as:
- Attacking a base of 14 people by yourself, watching as a chopper crash lands into the base, explosions and debris everywhere! Bodies and people flying to and fro..
- Singing Beyonce down your mic to someone before running out and blasting their head off
- Your first RPG heli kill
- Your first 9.3 heli kill
- Your first 7.62 heli kill
- Your first 5.56 heli kil- you get the idea!
- One 7.62 to get a double kill on a moving vehicle
- Lagging
- Dying by rocks
- Lagging
- Dying by terrain glitches
-Lagging
Everything from Capture the Flag to Zombie mods. A favourite of mine is Sa-Matra WS, a very good mod indeed! The varying game modes and the sandbox aspect of Arma 3 really engages the community and attracts newcomers! This game can be completely different dependent on which mod you play. However many of these can easily corrupt which leaves some users unable to resolve issues.
GLARING ISSUE: Horrendous desync issues have plagued Arma 3 since its inception, these have prevented any serious types of eSports leagues. This is a detrimental experience to gameplay, and you will run into it constantly you will get killed by lag constantly and if you are okay with this buy the game, if not DO NOT BUY THIS GAME EVER. (Wait till Arma 4)
Ergonomics - UI in Arma 3 has never been a problem with Bohemia taking a down-to-earth approach to UI design, clearcut menu's, expanded Map features such as markers, topography etc.
Mod support has been vastly expanded with a server browser that is noob friendly, a launcher that highlights and patches missing files and full Steam Workshop support. This is a 10/10.
Finally let me just sum up the experience you will get from this game. If you're looking for sophisticated group play, come to Arma, you'll find a group of weary game travellers such as yourself, who know there♥♥♥♥♥♥and can provide you with some irreplicable entertainment. Beware of lag and FPS issues, these are the two things hold this game back from a 9/10 or 10/10. It is my favourite game but it is still very imperfect.
Final Verdict: 8/10

This game is in a whole league of it's own. Most people would refer to it as 'That really unserious GTA clone' but no. It's so much more!
Let's get the bad out of the way first. The story, in comparison to the previous 2 (although I doubt many have played as SR1 was an Xbox exclusive that came out of the blue, and the SR2 PC port was just ATTROTIOUS), SR1 + 2 had deeper stories and also hung onto the small bit of seriousness the game had. Also the activities in the third game seem more like an after thought, there's less of them (but by no means am I saying there aren't many, there's still loads!) and they are all rediculously easy to beat in comparison to the rest of the franchise (SR1 was damn near impossible).
Onto the good. Where this game has strength is in it's Co-op. Everything about this game is built around the idea of a drop in/drop out co-op system. All activities scale up in target scores for two players, a lot of them adding almost a challenge aspect to it, a sort of "I'm better than you and I'm going to prove it!" mentality behind it. Missions are equally fun to do in co-op, though the tiny bit of 'story' this game has is even stranger as character voices bounce between players a lot.
This game also adopts a huge free roam map, similarly to GTA. You can do anything you want right from the get go, as after the first two missions you are set free. Whether you want to rob stores, go on a random murder spree or bat your partner down with a 10ft purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you have to choice to do so.
On unique co-op features, there's almost a kind of verses mode called "Cat and Mouse" if friendly fires on and you gun down your partner in crime, they have the option to trigger it, which results in you taking turns playing "Cat and Mouse" (The cat being a fighterjet and the mouse being a quad bike in most cases!). This is a blast to play and a nice bit of competition.
One final thing is that this game has FULL SUPPORT FOR XBOX 360 CONTROLLERS! The UI also changes to adopt the buttons as well (eg. if Y is to open a door, it shows up as the 360's Y button on screen) a nice touch for someone who likes to use the 360 controller like me (I find a keyboard and mouse is a bit flimsy on 3rd person games).
Overall I'd give this a strong 8/10, fun game but can get a bit repetitive, although co-op brings a nice chuck of that fun back, definately work a look if you're after something that's just fun and casual! (Also worth noting it may be worth buying the "FULL PACKAGE" version as is only slightly more expensive and contains all DLC released apart from 2, both removed by community request)

This game.....This GAME.
Where do I start, I love the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game, been trying to achieve MLG at BI's series for a long time now. I've played the Arma series since I was rekkin kids on A2 from 600 on Utes with my Ruski tool, holding a base right in the middle for a few hours every day. It's a beautiful and engaging experience, that leaves you on the edge of your seat, sometimes wishing you were holding your Grandma's face to squeeze tight (till she dies)... Tactical decisions are important, using the terrain and engaging with the movement structure of your enemies is a thrilling experience, adrenaline pulses as bullets and rockets fly closeby. You will never have to remember parts of maps (minute detail), as the maps on this are so big that it allows you to use your brain, instead of arena shooters which don't challenge the psyche.
Graphics - The original Arma  3 engine includes DX11 integration and standardised PhysX interactions, due to a new update recently the game has come to include Volumetric Lighting (big +), Upgraded textures (more vibrant), Water Refraction and a host of other improvements (60+ bug fixes - glaring bugs such as the offsight RPG Alamut Optic). The graphics second Terrain to Item models, however new improvements in the recent update have subsided these issues, Gear is of a signicantly high polycount as well as Vehicles.
ISSUES: Now I'm sure most of us have had a bad experience of Arma FPS lag. And for a long time now, BI has been using the BS excuse "It's mods."
Although partly true,  that is actually a lie. The way Arma simulates enemies, its peer to peer network structure, animation timers and no multi-threading support are the real reasons behind the terrible frames of Arma 3.
This. Needs. To. Stop.
Although too late for an A3 release, A4 must leave these issues behind.
Gameplay - Arma 3 can be a deeply tactical and engaging game. Many complex systems entwine with each other to create as much of a realistic experience as possible, for example:
- 27 Hit boxes on overall model (from head to toe)
- Multiple ammo types (ballistics, AP, EPR, special purpose ((need mods for some))
- Multiple types of vests (explosive resistant, harnesses, body armour, fba)
- Multiple attachments (flashlights, scopes, silencers, laserlights)
- Unique damage system that many call BS but is actually indepth af for example: Armour actually takes stress under duress, which creates a deeper and more realistic feel to armour.
- Your gun can deflect bullets
- Bullet penetration
Different types of team play are offered in Arma 3. From 2 - 80ppl, if you wish to be in a large group, there is one out there for you. Expanded group finding features such as the Squad pages and things such as Side chat to hook up with like minded people. There are several clans of varying sizes such as mine, however there are some humungous clans for the more mil sim oriented. Now here's the real thing that makes this stand out from other shooters, I think this is a big thing: anyone can be good at this game. All it takes is knowledge and sensibility when dealing with the sort of situations Arma 3 can spawn. Such as:
- Attacking a base of 14 people by yourself, watching as a chopper crash lands into the base, explosions and debris everywhere! Bodies and people flying to and fro..
- Singing Beyonce down your mic to someone before running out and blasting their head off
- Your first RPG heli kill
- Your first 9.3 heli kill
- Your first 7.62 heli kill
- Your first 5.56 heli kil- you get the idea!
- One 7.62 to get a double kill on a moving vehicle
- Lagging
- Dying by rocks
- Lagging
- Dying by terrain glitches
-Lagging
Everything from Capture the Flag to Zombie mods. A favourite of mine is Sa-Matra WS, a very good mod indeed! The varying game modes and the sandbox aspect of Arma 3 really engages the community and attracts newcomers! This game can be completely different dependent on which mod you play. However many of these can easily corrupt which leaves some users unable to resolve issues.
GLARING ISSUE: Horrendous desync issues have plagued Arma 3 since its inception, these have prevented any serious types of eSports leagues. This is a detrimental experience to gameplay, and you will run into it constantly you will get killed by lag constantly and if you are okay with this buy the game, if not DO NOT BUY THIS GAME EVER. (Wait till Arma 4)
Ergonomics - UI in Arma 3 has never been a problem with Bohemia taking a down-to-earth approach to UI design, clearcut menu's, expanded Map features such as markers, topography etc.
Mod support has been vastly expanded with a server browser that is noob friendly, a launcher that highlights and patches missing files and full Steam Workshop support. This is a 10/10.
Finally let me just sum up the experience you will get from this game. If you're looking for sophisticated group play, come to Arma, you'll find a group of weary game travellers such as yourself, who know there♥♥♥♥♥♥and can provide you with some irreplicable entertainment. Beware of lag and FPS issues, these are the two things hold this game back from a 9/10 or 10/10. It is my favourite game but it is still very imperfect.
Final Verdict: 8/10

I really like Arma, but as a fan I cannot fully recommend this game to others. I bought this game way back when it was in "alpha" stage, it's leaps and bounds better today than it was back then but one thing I cannot get over is the lack of content in the game when compared to Arma 2. When Bohemia Interactive first announced Arma 3 and said it would be a near-future setting I was giddy with joy at the possibilties of stuff in the game and degree of creative freedom it would allow the developers. But instead of that we got...
-Tons of reused/retextured equipment. All 3 of the factions (AAF, CSAT, NATO) use the same grendades, AT launchers, guns, HMG/GMG, vehicle turrets you name it, even the same weapons for aircraft! Believe it or not there are 9 different fedoras in the game (the ♥♥♥♥ were you thinking BIS???). What this means is that the factions don't really have anything much that sets them apart besides the uniform.
-Stunning lack of content for an Arma game, especially compared to Arma 2. It was a real disgrace that it took almost two years for the developers to put out jet aircraft for CSAT/NATO factions (when the game originally released AAF only had a jet fighter, community was scratching their heads). No idea what the deal is with this given the futuristic setting, they could've added anything almost.
-Bohemia Interactives total reliance on the modding community totally shows with this game, utterly disgraceful to depend on the community to fill in big content gaps because the developers were being lazy!
-DLC packs for this game are clear cash grabs and not worth the money charged for them by a long shot. $12 for a few sniper rifles, another $12 for two transport helicopters, the hell is this♥♥♥♥♥♥and why was it not in the main game?
Even three years after release and with the impending release of APEX, this game doesn't feel finished to me. So much is missing from this game when you compare it to previous Arma titles. I have literally no idea what the developers have been doing these past few years with the game. When Arma 3 was announced everyone was so, so excited for it but once it came out the enthusiasm for it just dropped, the game is barebones compared to Arma 2.
Game is fun but bugs need to be handled quicker :/

Arma 3 is the type of game you will never find anywhere else. It is an Awesome game, with a few major drawbacks.
The basic idea of Arma 3 is a military sandbox. What this means is that the developpers have created not a standalone game, but a pllatform for developpers like myself to create great stuff and add it to the Game.
We are talking about tremendous amounts of different gamemodes, maps, factions, vehicles, planes, helicopters, guns, accesories and more, all created by the community on top of the vanilla game.
The vanilla game is great. Great realism, Superb graphics, and awesome maps. Casual players will love some of the classic gamemodes, from Team Deathmatch to Role Playing, this game has it all.
But i really love about Arma 3 is that community mods give a totally different experience while playing. Playing with your friends using some mods is awesome. I even joined a public clan that recreated WW2 using Iron Front Mod, and it is awesome.
That said, Arma 3 present a few drawbacks: first, it is extremely painfull to get used to the hundreds of controls the game has, and you will probably need someone to help you on your first time. Good news, Arma 3 is known to have one of the best communities, and it is true. People are happy to help and guide you.
Arma has a big problem with optimisation, so be sure you meet the recomended specs, but expect casual framedrops.
Some of the controls are a bit counter-natural, like the in-game menu to open doors, which is done by scrolling down, selecting the actions you want to perform and then press space. With a little practice, you get used to it, but it is true that it is surprisingly hard to get the hand on everything, specially when you play with mods, whitch you probably will at some point.

A video game's first responsibility -- arguably its only responsibility -- is to show the player a good time. To say that Saints Row: The Third is a good time would be a severe understatement. Running naked around the fictional city of Steelport wiping out rival gangs with mind-controlling octopi delivered some of the most fun I've had this year. There may be a tendency to dismiss Saints Row as a Grand Theft Auto clone (it isn't) or as juvenile antics (it is) but when you just want to indulge in some mindless violence and sexual depravity, this will more than suffice. Saints Row the Third takes you out of Stilwater, the setting for the first two games, and drops you into the new city of Steelport. Three local gangs are well-entrenched, but the Third Street Saints aren't going to settle for fourth place. Your job throughout Saints Row the Third is to take over this new city and crush the competition.
After an intro mission sets up your exit from Stilwater you'll get the chance to customize your character. Customization plays a big part in the entire game, from your body to your dress to your vehicles. I love that, at a glance, no two players' games will look alike -- one will star a voluptuous vixen in a cocktail dress while the next may feature a blue sumo wrestler with cat eyes that speaks in zombie gibberish.
When you need a break from story missions you'll find loads of optional activities all over Steelport that boost your street cred and earn you cash. My favorites are the Insurance Fraud missions, holdovers from Saints Row 2 that ask you to run into traffic and cause as much bodily harm to yourself as possible before time runs out.
Pretty much anything you choose to do in Saints Row: The Third has been incentivized and will earn you either money or respect. Money can get you territory, weapons, upgrades, and threads. Respect works like experience points, unlocking new abilities such as "infinite sprint" and "no fall damage." Everything from near collisions while driving to running down the street naked earns you respect, which is fantastic game design -- we're constantly rewarded for simply playing the game. I was addicted to maximizing my hourly income and planning my character upgrades.

This game is awesome, if you are looking for a military simulator. It has bullet drop, bullet speed, real aerodynamics when it comes to planes and helicopters. It also has submarines! Though, I wouldn't recommend this game to people who like to play games for getting hig scores, racking up the kills, or destroying enemy teams by themselves. This game is all about stratedgy, patience, and experience. It will take forever to learn what everything does if you don't have someone teaching you literally EVERYTHING. Also, if you like sniping in battlefield and CoD, don't expect to begin racking up the kills. In ARMA, it's like being a real sniper. You find a spot, survey the area, and wait... do some more waiting... more, waiting... and possibly kill someone... and wait. Though, when you're surveying an area with heavy fire, you can get some kills possibly.
I would recommend this game to people who are interested in the journey more then winning, but still like winning(who doesn't?). Because your first several playing sessions, you will most likely not do much in terms of winning, or contributing. But, if you read the in-game manual, watch some tutorials, look up codewords for ARMA, then you will become the ultimate soldier.
(Also, there's something called "Zues". Should look it up, it's awesome. Basically turns the game into an RTS with players in First Person on the ground)

This game is awesome, if you are looking for a military simulator. It has bullet drop, bullet speed, real aerodynamics when it comes to planes and helicopters. It also has submarines! Though, I wouldn't recommend this game to people who like to play games for getting hig scores, racking up the kills, or destroying enemy teams by themselves. This game is all about stratedgy, patience, and experience. It will take forever to learn what everything does if you don't have someone teaching you literally EVERYTHING. Also, if you like sniping in battlefield and CoD, don't expect to begin racking up the kills. In ARMA, it's like being a real sniper. You find a spot, survey the area, and wait... do some more waiting... more, waiting... and possibly kill someone... and wait. Though, when you're surveying an area with heavy fire, you can get some kills possibly.
I would recommend this game to people who are interested in the journey more then winning, but still like winning(who doesn't?). Because your first several playing sessions, you will most likely not do much in terms of winning, or contributing. But, if you read the in-game manual, watch some tutorials, look up codewords for ARMA, then you will become the ultimate soldier.
(Also, there's something called "Zues". Should look it up, it's awesome. Basically turns the game into an RTS with players in First Person on the ground)

I played this game back from 2012, fiddled with it a bit more in 2014 and stopped playing the game altogether. I came back to the game recently, and I don't like what has been changed, I'll be honest.
I miss the old matchmaking and the fact that there arent 90 servers playing upward with 32/32 anymore, but everything else feels just like it used to. Nothing has been changed except for a few weapon additions and allot of changes to existing weapons, which is also quite disappointing. The best part about the game arguably was that it wasn't balanced. It seems valve are trying to balance everything out and try to cater to every playstyle, which I don't hate but if you're coming back to the game after a while, it'll sure feel different.
Don't listen to all the people that complain about the skins stuff, unless you're an extreme trader you shouldn't really be affected unless you're really really into skins, honestly for the occasional person that hops on for some good old fun you should be perfectly fine. There is still some of the great part of the community there, but now it's mostly populated by kids with way too many skins and hats. The community has moved on, and it saddens me a bit. I miss some of the old clans and servers I used to play with, and now there's barely any of them left except for private servers, a few clan servers, and some of the crazy x10 and randomizer servers and etc.
The game isn't completely destroyed, but I feel Valve will abandon it soon, as it's already dying as it is. We will never get a game as crazy and fun as the old TF2, but we can still reminisce on the good days.

I have a love and hate relationship with the former Operation Flashpoint and now Arma series. I love the immersion and the possibilities that this aging engine have delivered over the years. I love the havoc that it can create from seemingly smaller resources and that I have had the opportunity of trying out all the fantastic user made materials and modifications that have far superseeded the original game in reality and, dare I say it, fun. However, if you are like me, a loner that likes to battle it out with the AI, and at the same time likes to be immersed, I cannot in my right mind recommend this series anymore. If that's not you you can outright skip this review.
I started the game today to see the new and "improved", realistic graphics, only to realize that what would have been cutting edge a few years back, and actually were when this game were first released, now just looks and feels bland. Sure, the improvements have been many and well implemented, but to my eye I cannot really say that I see them clearly. Maybe I am too spoiled from memories of how a younger version of myself in awe sat and watched the sunset, listening to the sad tune of a blackbird in the game from which this series first came to light. It sucked me in. The game that instills the same feelings to me now is in a whole other genre, GTA V.
I want to be immersed. And graphics, and in a fairly large aspect audio design, is a big part of creating this immersion. I love how the cracks of bullets now bounce around in the valleys. And at the same time I abhore the way some sounds stick to one of your avatars "ears" and then follows it around when it turns around. A "bug" that has been reported since the game first released. That is something I have come to expect from indie titles where audio design isn't their strongest suit.
All these little cracks and niggles just throw me off me in the end.
Then there is the performance. And I will come at this from the angle of a loner that likes to play war with and against the AI. There were concerns that this game would suffer from the same performance hampering AI that Arma 2 suffered from. We were promised a much better experience this time around. There was an actual promise. Else I wouldn't even had concidered pre-ordering, which to this day I regret that I did. Anywho, I played in the alpha. Performance was abysmal to say the least. It was promised to get better in the final release. It never did. I caved in and bought an intel CPU, because tests showed an improvement in performance. And sure, I gained a few fps here and there. But when it came to playing with a larger amount of AI, say up to a 100 spread out over an island, it always would bog down. And I have tried it all like having the AI infested missions be battled out on a separate server or having headless clients handle some of the load and various AI caching mods. It never really got anywhere close to improving performance. In the end, all games would slow down to the teens in framerate on my client.
I am sure that having a good enough CPU with good enough caching might help as most of, if not all AI is rendered alive through scripting and stressing mostly one thread. But as it is I am not investing another swedish krona to better my personal experience of playing this game and in the future I will only buy another game from Bohemia Interactive if a) a CPU is produced with at least 200% better IPC than what I have now or b) the new game comes with a better engine and community reviews prove it playable even for a loner such as myself.

Due to my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC I did not play much of this game, but let me tell you it is great. The game is a simulator not a normal shooter. The game only has 3 maps however they are huge. Bigger then the maps in GTA and the such.
I am not in the service so I do not know the specifics of combats, however, I was in ROTC which is owned by the US Army so I know a decent amout about formations and things of the sort.
You can salute. Saluting is exactly like it is in the United States Military. Your ring finger touches you eyebrow. Your hand should be canted at a 45 degree angle. Your elbow is also paraell with the marching surface.
The formations are also very realistic. Line, Collum, Wedge, and Squad formations are done perfectly. Well, the AI is kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and gets out of formation quick but they initially get into correct formation.
The guns sound horrible, however, they sound weak and nothing like the real counter parts. The standard issue weapon is not even a real weapon used by the military. However, weapon balistics are spot on. Yes I even talked with my SAI in ROTC about this. The snipers has bullet drop that depends soley on distance and wind. This is not like battlefield which is static bullet drop. It actually depends of the weather and bullet drop is different for each sniper. Assualt rifes has reacoil and require precision to hit.
Overall, if you want to realistic experience this is the way to go. This is a simulator however, so don't go into this thing thinking it is going to be easy to learn because it is not.

This makes up the vast majority of the online aspect of arma 3, over the recent years a increase of life and other RP servers have taken over and pushed most of the military based arma servers to private groups.

For TL:DR, scroll to bottom for summary.
Arma 3 is a Military Simulator (milsim) which gives a focus on teamplay. Started as an Early Access title (one of the few Early Access titles that actually worked), gamers were able to submit feedback reports to the Arma 3 developers on a feedback website. This existed throughout Alpha and Beta phase until its full release. Because of this, the player base provided a lot of great feedback to the developer teams which ended up giving us a game much better than Arma 2. The player movement feels more fluid, the graphics are more clear, the world interactions and combat are better. Arma 3 is a little different in style from Arma 2, because it is more focused on a near-future war between NATO and CSAT (CSAT is a fictional Middle Eastern/Asian alliance).
Even after the game was launched, constant improvements have been made to the game, such as the introduction of the Marksmen update, which incorporated weapon bracing on world objects, the use of bipods on sniper weapons, vehicle-based turn-in/turn-out shooting (using a gun in a passenger vehicle) and the Helicopters update, which added a better physics model to helicopter flight and dynamics. These were released with DLC; but the actual mechanics were given to all players, which in itself: is generous of Bohemia to do so. Arma 3 just had a visuals update, which fixed the ugly water graphics glitch where water would animate above ocean level up terrain + other little changes here and there. With this aside, Arma 3 is a pretty solid game; but does have some steeper system requirements: thus may not work for everyone.
Arma 3 incorporates a coordinate system that real militaries use, squads, squad formations, identification of hostiles and movement is all a familiar thing to anyone who may have experienced time in the armed forces (I have not, but I know people who have and they were impressed). The game is not for your typical Call of duty or Rainbow Six or Battlefield type of player, the gunfights are much more challenging. In combat, you may have to zero in your sights to shoot down enemies from longer (or shorter) distances. The ballistics model in the game can be demonstrated clearly with the Virtual Arsenal/Virtual Training where the traces of each round can be viewed. Body armor matters in this game, as using lower-powered ammo will not cause as much damage (if none) to a target, thus forcing you to aim elsewhere or use a stronger gun. What is even cooler, is that if you shoot a enemy target far away with a lower-powered gun, the bullet velocity eventually slows down to the point where damage isn't as high as it would have been out the muzzle.
Vehicles have hitboxes; meaning that if a RPG strikes the side of an armored vehicle like an APC; the wheels/treads will likely take more damage than the vehicle's hull (unless a well-placed RPG shot gets in a weak spot). Grenades are useful, but not against armored targets (yes, frag grenades are almost completely useless against a 60 ton steel tank.) This encourages you to coordinate attacks on enemy targets, calling in airstrikes, specialists and other well-equipped units to deal with tougher hostiles, while your standard issue assault rifle will do just fine for infantry combat. The multiplayer in Arma 3 is the best, because you are around live players doing missions together which can be quite fun, even though there is a learning curve; it is well-rewarding when a mission succeeds and everyone makes it back alive. Arma has no shortage of tactical combat and planning. Keep in mind, this game isn't for everyone; simply because you don't usually join a server and have instant action all the time, it is more of a game of patience and finesse (or BLOW UP EVERYTHING if it is required).
In addition to the large maps and coordinated gameplay, this game has a rather good modding community with great mods coming out all the time. The game recently got a 3d mission editor which allows the use of a camera for much more precise object placement and better visualization. The game comprises of a nice scripting layer, which you can write your own custom scripts that can be executed in the game to present new operations. Modders have been able to make dynamic campaigns that are randomly generated and large scale. The modding capabilities are great, I have a USS Nimitz mod with an F-18, so I can do full carrier take-offs and landings, as well as in-flight refuel. Because I love to fly, a lot of my time is in the cockpit of a jet doing Combat Air Patrol (CAP) or Close Air Support (CAS) for ground units. Other times, I act as a transport pilot; but on many occassions I have done frontline ground assaults with a full squad armed with an SCAR CQB, RGO grenades and full body armor. This missions get hot sometimes, other times they are a walk in the park.
Arma 3 also has some diving units and missions; which are SEAL-level of awesome. You can board a small submarine and sneak up on the coast of an island, then walk inland and plant explosives on a enemy communications listening post. It is quite fun, and is even better when you do it at night. The AI in Arma 3 is much better than Arma 2, and the game has come a long way; I can vouch for that being a Early-Access Alpha and Beta contributor. Overall, if you are a fan of games which offer depth and a learning curve, Arma 3 is for you. The plus side of getting good at Arma 3, is you can turn your head back to those COD/BF/RS players and say: "You got nothing on me." If it isn't for that, it is just a great and enjoyable military simulator. If anyone has played Operation Flashpoint: Cold War Crisis; this is basically a modern reincarnation of that.
Summary -
Pros:
+ Realistic warfare.
+ Challenging combat.
+ Team oriented gameplay.
+ Great modding support and community.
+ High replay value.
+ Land, Air and Sea combat.
+ Good assortment of weaponry, vehicles and units.
+ Easy and intuitive in-game editor.
+ Strictly a skill-based experience.
+ The IP owners legally authorize modders to port Arma 1 and 2 content.
+ Unit customization and a virtual arsenal for loadout editing and saving.
Mixed:
= Some small DLC came out, but the developers did include the mechanics for free for non-DLC owners.
Cons:
- Some areas are poorly optimized, thus presenting sometimes poor performance.
- Not enough naval warfare.
- FOV in some vehicles without optics can appear zoomed in.
I recommend.

INGREDIENTS
6 to 6-1/2 cups all-purpose flour
6 eggs
3/4 cup water
2 teaspoons olive oil
SAUCE:
1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes
1-1/2 cups tomato puree
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1/3 cup water
1/3 cup tomato paste
3 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons minced fresh basil
1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley
1 tablespoon minced fresh oregano
1 garlic clove, minced
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon pepper
FILLING:
1 carton (15 ounces) ricotta cheese
2 cups (8 ounces) shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 egg, lightly beaten
2 teaspoons minced fresh basil
1 teaspoon minced fresh parsley
1 teaspoon minced fresh oregano
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/8 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon pepper
Step 1: Place 6 cups flour in a large bowl. Make a well in the center. Beat the eggs, water and oil; pour into well. Stir together, forming a ball. Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 8-10 minutes, adding remaining flour if necessary to keep dough from sticking. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Step 2: Meanwhile, in a Dutch oven, combine the sauce ingredients. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Step 3: In a large bowl, combine the filling ingredients. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Step 4: Divide pasta dough into fourths; roll one portion to 1/16-in. thickness. (Keep pasta covered until ready to use.) Working quickly, place rounded teaspoonfuls of filling 1 in. apart over half of pasta sheet. Brush around filling with water to moisten. Fold sheet over; press down to seal. Cut into squares with a pastry wheel. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Step 5: Bring a soup kettle of salted water to a boil. Add ravioli. Reduce heat to a gentle simmer; cook for 1-2 minutes or until ravioli float to the top and are tender. Drain. Spoon sauce over ravioli.
Yield: 6 servings.

Arma 3 is a well made next game in the Arma series with many options you can do.
Now I played many different modes and mods that I should give you a decent review about this game.
Story
I do know that there are not many people that want to buy Arma 3 because of the story, but it still has one and isn\'t bad.
It is a new story and does not have something to do with Arma 2 or else.
The story starts with a mission for you and another soldier to help out another Camp, but on you´re way there an invasion of the AFF starts over the hole Island and you and you´re superior that is with you at that time try to get to a safe place to reform their allies.
This get´s harder than though because the AFF troops are anywhere but helpfully there were some units from the UK that helps out and you can regroup with them and so the story starts where you try to get connected to another safe Island and do many different tasks.
Gameplay
You can control land sea and air craft vehicles or go by you\'re own foot on the maps Stratis or Altis and many modded maps.
There is not rally a task given to you by the game, besides the story, there are many different tasks given to you by community made co-op missions or PvP modes and also the complete different thing like a real life in modes like good known \"Altis Life\".
But besides Altis Life or other similar mods this is a military simulation game and give you many possibilities to let it feel
like that.
In co-op missions in a group of friends you need to make a briefing of the situation and make a plan or just go on patrol and get surprised by an attack of an opposite fraction and many more kind of situations.
There are too many different gameplay methods given to you by the community that I can not listen them all up here.

Arma 3 is a true military orientated sandbox game at heart.
-Campaign-
Arma 3's campaign does a good job at introducing the player to the controls and functions of arma although it is mostly throw away. The mission pacing can sometimes feel off and the AI feel mostly like robots. Although for me arma could do without a campaign I did enjoy trawling through most of it but found there to be steep difficulty curves here and there.
-Scenarios-
For me scenarios do a much better job of showing the core functions and the true range of the things to do within arma, new scenarios also get released with new DLC when said DLC adds a function, such as Sling-loading and VTOLs. Scenarios offer a good mix of excitement and challenge where it be scuba diving or trying to land a jet fighter on a aircraft carrier (Jets DLC).
-3den Editor-
The real power house of arma, with a bot of knowledge a new player can make a suite of missions and objectives with this simple tool. But the advanced user in the 3den editor can make anything happen especially when they have a grasp on the scripting side of arma mission making.
-Cooperative-
This makes up the vast majority of the online aspect of arma 3, over the recent years a increase of life and other RP servers have taken over and pushed most of the military based arma servers to private groups.

If you were expecting a review for the game, gtfoh. But if you were expecting/need a homemade ravioli recipe, then i got yo back fam
INGREDIENTS
6 to 6-1/2 cups all-purpose flour
6 eggs
3/4 cup water
2 teaspoons olive oil
SAUCE:
1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes
1-1/2 cups tomato puree
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1/3 cup water
1/3 cup tomato paste
3 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons minced fresh basil
1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley
1 tablespoon minced fresh oregano
1 garlic clove, minced
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon pepper
FILLING:
1 carton (15 ounces) ricotta cheese
2 cups (8 ounces) shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 egg, lightly beaten
2 teaspoons minced fresh basil
1 teaspoon minced fresh parsley
1 teaspoon minced fresh oregano
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/8 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon pepper
Step 1: Place 6 cups flour in a large bowl. Make a well in the center. Beat the eggs, water and oil; pour into well. Stir together, forming a ball. Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 8-10 minutes, adding remaining flour if necessary to keep dough from sticking. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Step 2: Meanwhile, in a Dutch oven, combine the sauce ingredients. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Step 3: In a large bowl, combine the filling ingredients. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Step 4: Divide pasta dough into fourths; roll one portion to 1/16-in. thickness. (Keep pasta covered until ready to use.) Working quickly, place rounded teaspoonfuls of filling 1 in. apart over half of pasta sheet. Brush around filling with water to moisten. Fold sheet over; press down to seal. Cut into squares with a pastry wheel. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Step 5: Bring a soup kettle of salted water to a boil. Add ravioli. Reduce heat to a gentle simmer; cook for 1-2 minutes or until ravioli float to the top and are tender. Drain. Spoon sauce over ravioli.
Yield: 6 servings.
Nutritional Facts:
Each 10 pcs. : 901 calories, 25g fat (13g saturated fat), 307mg cholesterol, 963mg sodium, 124g carbohydrate (17g sugars, 7g fiber), 45g protein.
