After spending 1000 hours with this title I am returning from the battlefield with a hefty review, so listen up soldier, it's time to debrief! Haha, just kidding. Arma 3 is made by Bohemia Interactors, the same developers that made Operation Flashpoint 1, 2 and Operation Flashpoint 3: Dragon Rising and all its notorious DLC packs. alkjdfljgaoirjgfsgh Arma 3 has had a rocky development cycle since development began in 1999 (Yeah, take that, Duke Nukem!). The biggest bump on this titles rocky road to going gold was when 3 of the members of the development team were caught by Greek military personel on the island of Lemnos, where they claimed that they were "just documenting the environment for a video game". It turned out these guys weren't the saints they tried to make themselves out to be after Greek secret police found explosives and make-shift pipe bombs in their hotel room that they had been staying in for 6 weeks. Tensions rose between Greece and the Czech Republic, and weeks after the mysterious release of the terrorists the Czech Republic was in favor of every single EU stimulus package to Greece, a nowadays declared failed state and international bombing range.
After causing international ruckus, Bohemia developers seemed to enjoy the time in the spotlight, so keeping a low profile was out of the window. Their next direction for their game environment was blatantly framing the Greek inspired island as the most idiotic place on earth. For legal reasons they had to change the name of the island, which they did, from Lemnos to Altis (which just happens to be old greek for "Goat ♥♥♥♥ers"). The alleged mistreatment of the Bohemian Rhapsody developers also caused them to remove all furniture on the island, and they placed signs in most towns saying that cilivians threw their belongings into the ocean to build a giant sea-base nation because of the Greek politicians incompetence. Destroyed Greek military vehicles are spread all over the island, together with mass graves, and I sometimes wonder if Altis would have had its current post apocalyptic atmosphere if the developer incident had never happened.
Arma 3 had a well received launch, and was declared "Best Arma game of 2013" by GameSpot. Bohemimi Contractors made an absolute killing on the title, and is now ranked the 13th most valuable company on the planet. It's inclusion of a mod makers tool kit as well as a film editor has provided the community with the tools to create endless amounts of content themselves, and, unfortunately, porn. The Arma film maker is notorious for being abused by people importing of female game characters and posing them in lewd and untasteful situations.
Looking forward Bohemo Mamani is looking for more Greece inspired environments for their next title. The developers just acquired a fully funcitonal T-90 tank, which they continously pose in front of on twitter with Bohemian flags, automatic rifles and wishes to visit Greece.
This game has multiplayer support up to 32 people, which is twice as many as the Xbox One version. Get the PC version.

The customization may not appeal to everyone, as most of the clothing is also crude or meant as a joke, but you can't please everyone. I suggest they just go naked. The models are large, bulbous, and cartoony as well which adds to the whole aspect of the game.
Regardless of the customization, the combat is amazing. Chuck civilians or enemies out of a cannon as you suck them up. Or, take control of vehicles and detonate them into other vehicles. Otherwise, you could just use traditional weapons and shoot everyone in the face.
The only other drawback is the amount of quests that need to be completed in order to unlock activities and main missions. Each homie has you complete three missions that are actual activities that you unlock after completing the mission. They get rather tedious and boring after doing nine of them in a row.
For people who enjoy an open world environment such as Grand Theft Auto, this game will definitely please you.

Arma 3 is a great military training game or representational life like army game. There are a few nuts and bolts that need to be tightened and bolted into place but overall it's a phenomenal shooter. It's a first-person and third-person shooter you can interchange what visual aspect you want to be in inside the game. In the campaign you play as Ben Kerry, a U.S. Army soldier that is a component of NATO peacekeeping military force. The game and online proceeds in the year two thousand thirty five. The campaign and maps made for the game take place on Aegean islands of Altis (Lemnos) and Stratis of Greece, in the Mediterranean Sea. The game itself has many DLCs that you can buy on G_2_A for very cheap(nickel-and-dime) prices. If you have a moderate(regular) computer or PC(Program counter) then this game should run fine around 35-45 frames. If you have a crappy computer or PC then I would suggest sticking to another game. You learn a lot about the military, air force, delta units and more in the campaign and online. It gets too the point were you start talking like a solider and forget(draw a blank) that it's a game. You can also have large indefinite amounts of fun and dip around with your friends.

The Saints Row franchise has long evolved from the first one, the franchise went from having a sort of "Miami Vice" vibe to it, to the most ridiculous Open World game ever; while that may be a great thing to a lot of people, it certainly wasn't to me, but then again, the game is still a LOT of fun to play.
~Visuals  8.5 / 10  "Overall looks pretty solid, though it lacks a level of detail."
Now, the game has certainly changed up to a more cartoony style by all rights. It isn't either a positive or a negative as in this case it gives SR3 it's own flavor while not damaging the previous art style the franchise was known for; however, it doesn't excuse the game from having just overall close to poor detailing on things that aren't "Main Characters", I found myself noticing bland textures on NPCs, the gameworld itself sometimes lack a lot of detail compared to other areas, etc, it's not really BAD bad, but it is noticeable. The game does have a lot of unique areas to help differentiate where you are - Yes, in this type of game this is a REALLY good thing.
~Soundwork  9 / 10  "Solid soundwork, could have a better soundtrack."
There's not much to say for the soundwork for this game, it's just very well done, even though the soundtrack isn't my favorite, but it's certainly varied enough to actually HAVE something you may like. The VA's for the main character, both female and male carry their own uniqueness to it, and are all very well done. The city itself sounds like it's alive with chatter about, cars honking their horns, etc, Volition did a fantastic job bringing that about, as well as the guns all have their unique flavor and power. Soundwork is just overall very, very nice.
~Gameplay [  7.5  / 10 ]  & Story  [  4.5  / 10 ]
Gameplay's pretty much standard Saints Row fare here. You aim by moving a reticule and pointing it to where you want to shoot, you have a "Sights" mode that lets you zoom in a bit for a bit better accuracy, but there's not that much difference between the two - you switch between a pretty expansive weapon tree, ranging from Pistols, Melee, Rifles, SMGs & Special Weapon, you place any equipped weapon of that class in each slot and change between em on the fly, pretty much standardfare shooter but works very well. Story... well, it starts out strong with a hectic heist gone wrong that ends up with our characters airborne and finding themselves in the end of a deal gone wrong. The game does a major sin to me by immediately killing off series staple, Johnny Gat, it sorta adds a temporary premise to the game, but is soon discarded for simple revenge, or just a means to bring about the insanity that ensues afterwards, the story as a whole doesn't make a lot of sense, more bad guys are introduced that want your gang dead and that's pretty much it.
Overall - 7.5 / 10 "Great game when it comes to just sitting down and creating chaos, look for an "engaging" story elsewhere."

Arma 3 is an unworthy heir to Arma 2. Arma 3 introduces better graphics and improved gameplay via a new engine. However, all the content I loved from Arma 2 has been replaced with absurdities. This includes: a cast of poorly thought out science fiction equipment. Space Iranians with lego camo? Caseless 6.5mm ammunition? Ka-Mi hybrid? What is this♥♥♥♥♥♥and what is it doing in a game that markets itself as a 'simulation'? In the Campaign, you play as part of a NATO -- which part? Turkey, perhaps? Bulgaria? Nope, it's the USA, again. This story is Asylum quality, it is uninspired and too boring to be funny. The game's multiplayer is limited to straight forward shooter missions, not wide open strategic engagements.
That is only the vanilla game. It can be discarded like Crackdown, and enjoyed for its Halo 3 Beta: mods. No more space Iranians or fantastical ammo, you're back in Cheranrus, driving on top of your Abrams tank, looking for insurgents. Bohemia supports its modding community, and that requires praise. I am reviewing the vanilla game, not user content and on its own, Arma 3 is a waste. I haven't bought Bohemia's latest DLCs, I expect them to give them to me for free -- like they did in Arma 2.

I love this game but the lack of content is outrageous if you don't count the overpriced DLC (which should've been in the base game from the beginning). Even with the DLC the game feels rather empty. Emplacements such as the mortar and 50 cal are reused across factions so there is no diversity in the game. Relatively few guns compared to the previous iterations of ARMA along with not many vehicles (total of 3 planes in the game, one for each faction). Vehicles have retained the HP system from previous games so don't expect realistic tank combat.
Some gameplay issues are present as well like exaggerated fatigue that doesn't simulate real life at all. Even if you remove all your gear, you can't run very far and tire out fast. Are these couch potatoes or soldiers?  Fatigue affects aiming as well so don't expect to be able to hit anything after running 10 meters while the AI snipes you. Speaking of AI, they can see through grass, smoke, bushes, you name it and they will snap to your head, instantly killing you every time.
There are some good things though such as the amazing graphics, though you will need a monster rig to run the game on max. Altis and Stratis make amazing settings for the game and there are some interesting spots you can find. Weapons feel and sound great and the customization options let you personalize your gun. AI can be smart sometimes and I've been flanked and they shoot where they think you are. If you pop out of a corner and then hide they will keep watching the corner and wait for you to pop out again so actual tactics are useful. Overall it's an okay game and I highly recommend getting it on sale with the DLC.

This is a fun game, BUT it is a very specific kind of fun, i.e. the gratuitous do-anything-and-kill-anything kind of sandbox fun. As has been mentioned in numerous reviews, the Saints Row series has abandoned any sense of realism and devoted itself to crafting an outrageous spectacle of blood and explosions, all to be set off by your virtual hand.
If you're looking for a challenge, don't play this game. The enemy NPCs can quickly become laughably impotent against the armory you can amass.
If you're looking for a good story, don't play this game. Despite a few interesting characters, the storylines are quite disconnected and illogical. Plotholes are plentiful to an almost intentional degree, and the interesting characters' stories are never explored.
However, if you're looking to indulge in feeling powerful, if you're looking for a bloody debris-littered sandbox in which to enact your every whim, if you're looking to become a gangster god that is all-powerful and free from consequences to take and destroy anything in sight...
Actually, wait for a bit before deciding on a purchase. Saints Row 4 is either coming out soon or out already, and promises to be much more ludicrous than all its prequels. Wait for the fourth, or just wait for a Steam sale.

Over all Arma 3 is a game you want to buy if you love military sims and have the time and patince to learn.

I have only played the campaign at the moment, and I have no-way near finished it.
So far in this campaign I have crept through a big valley full of trees with Alpha Squad trying to get to a safe camp while running into AAF forces.
And you have to play this game tactically.
You physically cannot just run out into the open and shoot randomly everywhere as you will instanly die.
You have to take cover, lean out behind trees, account for bullet-drop and physical exhaustion. And that is just some of the factors.
Another great thing about Arma 3 is it still retains a very-fun atmosphere without being a complete simulator.
I would rate this game a solid 10/10.
It is well worth the money.

I used to like this game, but ever since the recent update the fun has just gone out of it. You can no longer easily choose a server to play in yourself. If you want to play a gamemode such as control points, you'll go into a random server and you'll play control points once, but then the server will move you to another random server, and more than half the time, it will be a different gamemode even though you want to play control points. I really think Valve should bring the game back the way it was, where you could easily join a server quickly without lag, and then you could easily play with your friends.
I also think a way to create your own server for free would be very useful as well. Because when I try to create my own server using the "create server" option, none of my friends can join it and then it says "server not responding." So what are you supposed to do if you can't create a server for just you and your friends? That's honestly just dumb in my opinion.
I would probably recommend this game if it didn't get this silly update. But for now I'm saying... not recommended

As a newcomer to the Saints Row series, I was skeptical at first about touching the series. Grand Theft Auto IV had already covered my desire for an open world third person shooter with no strings attached. Eventually, friend suggestions and interest turned into a purchase of The Third.
I've not regretted that money spent.
At its heart, Saints Row: The Third is Grand Theft Auto strapped to a phallic missile and fired at a helicopter made entirely out of guns - and that's putting it lightly. While I feel that the humor can be grating at times, the game tries hard to remain aware of how it plays and feels. It knows it's hardly serious, it doesn't try much to be serious, and it remains unconcerned about making sense as it throws armed ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, fully cliched sci-fi grunts, and militarized Mexican wrestlers at you with a smile on its face.
When playing the game, there's a certain flow that one can appreciate. The game both understands the player's place as the biggest badass around, but never lets one get comfortable for too long. There are most definitely elements that spoil balance - invulnerability unlocks and tanks, for example - but a willing disregard of the elements that would otherwise break the fluid and varied combat present allow the game's method as a moderately-paced third person shooter to shine.
Aesthetically, the game knows its style. Realism is clearly not the goal within; while it does not pursue a cartoon style like Team Fortress 2 or Borderlands, it most definitely has its own look and feel which remains consistent throughout. Graphical quality itself is a bit of a toss-up; effects and texturing appear rock-solid, but model detail can feel lacking at times.
The audio department is another mixed bag. Many, including myself, were relatively disappointed by the game's music department. I, personally, made a personal mod for the music selection very quickly, so I'm likely biased - hearing Serious Sam and Tropico music probably has me spoiled. The game's voice acting, however, most definitely stands out, fitting the goofy atmosphere as well as the visuals.
Third party support is an odd topic. Modding is definitely possible - many modifications have been pumped out by the dedicated community already. When working with the game's assets, however, it can feel daunting to a new modder or one unused to its bizarre style of "openness". It feels as though the game was never designed or intended to be modded, yet the way it was programmed and packed made such user-driven changes only inevitable.
Performance-wise, The Third has given me nothing but trouble. It may simply be my PC's particular configuration, but driver crashes, uneven framerates, and lag between cooperative players have been ubiqutous in my playtime and nearly impossible to resolve. It is worth noting that I experienced these difficulties even before I began to install modifications, so they cannot easily be attributed to user content.
If you want to play in traffic for cash prizes, wiggle your bones into the walls of unlucky convenience stores, and play chicken with multi-trillion dollar military gunships, Saints Row: The Third has you covered - and even offers room for a friend to join you.
Just be ready to throw whatever notion of "sanity" you have to the wind.

... a unique game based on interesting ideas and concepts.
For peoples loving tinckering with scripts, 3d modelling and other game creation related stuff, probably a must have. On the other hand, if you expect something ready to use and easy to play, you will most likely not be happy.
I bought arma 3 in early alpha-state and since then, i have one real concern:
The performance of the underlaying engine is limiting in many ways.
So no matter, if using BI provided content or nice user-created content (maps, vehicles, weapons, missions and even total conversions), there is alway a feeling 'that could really run smoother'.
Stuttering and delays, especially in moments, where every little millisecond counts, are overpresent, very annoying and i think the main reason for many users to leave this game, earlier or later.
I am not sure if BI is really not able to do it better, or if there are primarily economical reasons to ignore all the related claims for many years now.
Conclusion: not recommended for common gamers

ARMA III is one of those games that is really cool in it's own unique way. Unfortunately, ARMA can't stay out of it's own way long enough to remain cool. Before I start, I should mention that this review is based only on my experiences of single player and the editors with the deal-breaking focus on the editors themselves. That said, I'm expecting the dislikes to rain.
This is a difficult one to review. As of writing I've played about 40 hours of almost exclusively single player/editor use. In some ways I really enjoy this game. The biggest draw for me was the editor(s) in this game. The ability to create my own skirmishes anywhere on this giant island and watch them unfold is awesome. You can basically make up any scenario you can imagine and play it out. This alone has kept me entertained for at least 30 hours by itself. I got past the extremely unintuitive user interface and AI quirks and genuinely had a good time hiking around and blowing stuff up.
But, if ARMA is anything, it's a shining example of why documentation is so important in software development. The documentation for ARMA's editors, both 2D and 3D, is bad. And when it's not bad, it's non-existent. What does the Game Logic object actually do in the editor when it seemingly has no inputs or outputs? Why do some modules need to be synced to each other when others don't? How are you supposed to figure out what to sync to what and when?
Usually, there is no answer. Or the answer is outdated or inconsistent between the different editors. Or you'll find other people asking the same questions with the responses basically shrugging. The answers I did find always came down to a 'copy paste this script' or 'follow these exact steps' with no further explanation as to why I was doing these things. That's great for getting something working instantly, not so great for learning how to use the systems and building the intuition needed to take things further.
I don't think this is about the complexity of the editor, I think this is about bad design decisions and lack of consistent, clear documentation. I've worked with Garry's Mod coding for at least a thousand hours and have developed software for many different languages from Python to assembly. The only reason I was able to accomplish these things was from the comprehensive documentation on how things worked and _why_ they worked. And even if they didn't have those things, they at least gave a brief snippit on what is required for the function/module to actually work. Something that the ARMA amazingly doesn't have for the vast majority of it's objects. Just looking at the MP editor modules on ARMA's own wiki page, only about 3% of the listed modules have documentation. The game TIS-100 is more approachable than the depths of these editors.
So, I've had fun with ARMA for the most part. But this well is running dry for me quickly. I wish it wasn't because this feels like the kind of game I would enjoy if ARMA didn't tie its own hands behind its back. For the reasons that I bought this game, I wouldn't recommend it. If you play it for multiplayer, your experience will probably be completely different. So, take this for what it's worth.

Overall an awesome game; would reccomend to anyone looking for high realism and tons of content.

The answers I did find always came down to a 'copy paste this script' or 'follow these exact steps' with no further explanation as to why I was doing these things. That's great for getting something working instantly, not so great for learning how to use the systems and building the intuition needed to take things further.
I don't think this is about the complexity of the editor, I think this is about bad design decisions and lack of consistent, clear documentation. I've worked with Garry's Mod coding for at least a thousand hours and have developed software for many different languages from Python to assembly. The only reason I was able to accomplish these things was from the comprehensive documentation on how things worked and _why_ they worked. And even if they didn't have those things, they at least gave a brief snippit on what is required for the function/module to actually work. Something that the ARMA amazingly doesn't have for the vast majority of it's objects. Just looking at the MP editor modules on ARMA's own wiki page, only about 3% of the listed modules have documentation. The game TIS-100 is more approachable than the depths of these editors.
So, I've had fun with ARMA for the most part. But this well is running dry for me quickly. I wish it wasn't because this feels like the kind of game I would enjoy if ARMA didn't tie its own hands behind its back. For the reasons that I bought this game, I wouldn't recommend it. If you play it for multiplayer, your experience will probably be completely different. So, take this for what it's worth.

我爱玩H1Z1，可因为沉迷游戏，使得生活中的我一直浑浑噩噩一事无成，后来我在游戏里认识了一个女孩，她家里似乎非常有钱。她玩的很6，游戏里从未见她用过重复的皮肤，各种绝版层出不穷，我还记得她经常用的一套双子星，常年稳占亚太前十。我们经常一起打，一起站房顶发呆。
有一次我俩训练服单挑，在我连败十几次之后，她突然说道：“如果有一天你能赢了我，我就嫁给你！”
我心里有些惊喜，却并不在意，那时候我虽然沉迷游戏，却分得清游戏与现实，游戏里的感情，终不过是水中捞月，望梅止渴，永远慰藉不了生活的空虚。
后来在大学毕业的毕业典礼上一件事情颠覆了我的整个人生，那天大家喝了很多酒，唱了一夜的歌，凌晨大家散场的时候，系里那个我暗恋了四年的女神突然找到了我，她一脸娇羞，低眉垂手，小声说道：“游戏里我说过的话，依旧算数！”
我浑身一颤：“什...什么？”
她嫣然一笑，道：“我很早就知道那是你，我也一直玩H1Z1，对不起，一直没跟你说。”
夜风吹起她的长发，城市五彩的霓虹灯是我们的背景，我觉得，我的一生没有什么时候比那一刻更幸福。
后来我为了赢她一次，开始苦练，抽废品厂，开箱子。但这些没有足够的经济基础是做不到的，于是我终于告别了过去颓废的自己，开始了人生的蜕变，拼命工作，学习，挣钱，游戏也渐渐玩的少了。
三年后，我已经是一家上市公司的老板，家境殷实，事业有成，我想，是时候旅行当年的承诺了。
可天意弄人，我们再次见面的时候是在婚礼现场上，新郎却不是我，收到喜帖的当天，我开车赶到了她所在的城市，赶上了她的婚礼。
神圣而庄重的礼堂上，她白裙胜雪，明艳照人，宛如当年模样，旁边他的新郎英俊潇洒，一表人才，旁人无不称赞他们是天作之合，郎才女貌，酒过三巡，我跑到卫生间里大哭一场，偶遇了同时来补妆的她。
“为什么不等我？”我攥紧拳头，来压制内心的歇斯底里。
她低着头道：“对不起，我们都不是当年那个只会玩游戏的小孩子了，曾经我说话的话你就当从没听过吧，我们终究要面对现实，况且看到你今天的成就，我真的很欣慰，你会遇到比我更好的女孩的，再见。”
看着她渐行渐远的背景，我终于明白了，逝去的才叫青春。
最后我把公司交给了一个信得过的朋友，自己在郊区租了间个面阴的小房子，买了一台二手电脑，练了一个小号，我每天最喜欢的事就是在训练服不起眼的地方站着，等一个永远等不到的人，等她跟我说，“如果你打赢我一次，我就嫁给你！”

PREFACE:
Normally I'm not someone who cares greatly for shooters, I can't use a controller to play competitively and using my KB+M setup is as comfortable as sitting on a bed of porcupine yet this is one of those games where I simply don't mind putting up with it for just how much FUN it is to play.
I'm sure you've heard everyone tell you ALL about how competitive the game is and how you got all these skilled ways to play with sticky jumping and rocket jumping and whatever else kind of movement based skill you can think of (There's obviously more you can do than just that) but I'm not good enough at the game for that stuff so I'm just going to talk like a normal player who hasn't invested 1000 hours into the game (Cuz obviously I haven't, as you can see)
I used to play this a lot back when I first heard of it a few years ago where I used to be...FAIRLY skilled, I ran a pretty good scout (I recall fighting off a whole team by myself once, whether that speaks of how bad they are or how good I am is ENTIRELY up to you, it was probably the first.)
Most of that play time was from back then.
NOW, ABOUT THE GAME ITSELF!
You've got 9 classes to choose from, scout, soldier, pyro, demoman, heavy, medic, spy, engineer and sniper and a TRUCK load of weapons, all of them having a pretty nice balance from my experience (Except the demoman's melee, I hate the demoman.)
Each cover a very specific thing and can counter one of the classes, the heavy is essentially a tank, the medic is...well...the medic (healer), the scout can move faster than the other classes and has a double jump, they're pretty good for combat specifically since they can move out of gunfire pretty easily, demoman, pyro and soldier are the best at offense in general as they possess AoE such as grenades, rockets and a flamethrower (Which is essentially just a big middle finger to a clustered group of enemies.)
The easiest class to play is probably the engineer since all you gotta do is build a turret and dispenser and use the turret as a shield and the dispenser to heal you and give you building materials to fix the turret (Both max level of course)
You get the idea how the classes work.
The weapons tend to have different effects like one lets you teleport to your teleporter (Engineer) or causes bleed damage to the enemy when you hit them (Also engineer), one is just a mid range ball that sets the enemy on fire (Pyro) and of course if the weapon has a strong enough effect then it has some drawback like it lowers your health or something.
As for game modes, there's a considerable number, all objective based, Mann Vs Machine is one of my favourites though, I really enjoy defense based game modes, it's a lot like Payload actually except there's no players in this mode (I mean, unless you have more people than you can have on your team join, then they become the machines.), king of the hill and capture the points, there's several gamemodes you can choose from so just look through them in-game, it doesn't take long to download the game anyway.
PERFORMANCE:
You could run this on a toaster to be frank, my laptop has an i3 3110M, 4GB's of ram and Intel HD 4000 and could get a playable framerate in this game, it wasn't great or stable but it was certainly playable.
I run most games on my desktop mind you (i5 4460, GTX 750 Ti, 8GB's of ram) so I just max the settings out.
MAPS:
They are plentiful and I can never say that I disliked any of them particularly, they've all been decent at worst and truly amazing in the best scenarios.
OVERALL:
It's a brilliant game, there are people who have got thousands of hours in this game and I can see why, the game is fun, charming and has a skill ceiling that puts CS:GO to shame.
Don't let the skill ceiling comment put you off if you're new, there's a practice mode where you can go against bots until you can git gud and you tend to not see highly skilled players since I think they have some sort of rating system going on.
PS: I know this holds no water or relevance but the music is damn catchy!

Saints Row started as a forgettable GTA clone, and it might have stayed that way had the second game seen an opportunity for some rather over-the-top silliness and background insanity that stood out amid the semi-realistic setting and gritty violence of a street gang.
The third game has taken those little bits of insanity and run with them. While there are some disadvantages to removing the subtlety from the craziness, it doesn't diminish the fact that Saints Row 3 is inescapably fun to play. Whether you follow the main plotline or not (and I would, as it leads to some hilarious moments and opportunities for new stuff to use), you can spend hours committing all sorts of mayhem across Steelport with your rowdy band of ninjas or strippers or aliens or alien stripper ninjas.
The game is very ambitious in that it tries to fit so much in, but since it's a sandbox game, you really have the option to pick and choose what you like, and the game happily lets you. Rather than being a confusing mess, it's more like an all-you-can-eat buffet of cinematic action, cartoonish violence, and colorful silliness.
If you can get it on sale, get the DLC. I normally don't care that much about the bonus content, but here, the bonus missions give you an even bigger genre pool to play with, from B-grade horror film to kitschy Japanese game shows.
The only string is that this game doesn't take itself seriously at ALL. The entire time, it's laughing at itself an expects the player to at least chuckle. If you're looking for a serious game, you (probably) won't find it here.

FALLOUT 4 REVIEW
Share. We’re giving this post-nuclear RPG a glowing endorsement.
BY DAN STAPLETON Most of the way this huge roleplaying-shooter game works is carried over from its excellent predecessors, Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas. It is the Skyrim to Fallout 3’s Oblivion, if you will – it iterates on the previous game’s already amazing systems, and it’s similarly dense with locations to explore, genuinely creepy monsters to fight, and superbly engrossing post-nuclear atmosphere that blends unsettling gore and death with dark comedy. After more than 55 hours played I may have seen an ending, yet I feel like I’ve only begun to explore its extraordinary world; from the look of it, I’ll easily be able to spend another 100 happy hours here and still see new and exciting things.

A story that begins as a basic search for your lost family evolves into something much more complex and morally nuanced. Like in Fallout: New Vegas, we’re drawn into a struggle between several groups competing for control of the region, and deciding which of their imperfect post-apocalyptic philosophies to align with made me pause to consider how I wanted events to play out. Even the highly questionable Institute has a tempting reason to side with them, and turning away from them in my playthrough wasn’t as clear-cut a choice as I’d expected. I was impressed by the sympathy shown toward the villains, too - even the most irredeemable murderer is explored and given a trace of humanity.

The main story isn’t nearly as gripping an attraction as the huge number of well-written side quests.
Of course, as is the tradition with developer Bethesda Game Studios’ open-world RPGs, the main story isn’t nearly as gripping an attraction as the huge number of well-written side quests you’ll come across just by wandering through the ruins of the Boston area, now known as The Commonwealth. I found it difficult to complete even the most basic point-A-to-point-B task without being sidetracked at least twice by enticing detours. An abandoned comic book publisher office? How can I not explore it? Boston’s famous Fenway Park? Gotta see what’s become of that. A crumbling high school with heads on pikes outside? I bet there’s great loot in there! Practically tripping over new discoveries like this, I feel like a kid on Easter whose parents are bad at hiding the candy.

Attention to detail is evident everywhere.
Exploration has its own rewards, as this is the most diverse Fallout world yet, with dilapidated urban areas, ominous dead forests, eerie swamps, a desolate area mired in a hellish radioactive haze, and even some areas that look borderline hospitable like beaches and budding farms. The Commonwealth’s much more color-saturated than Fallout 3’s Capital Wasteland, though it has its fair share of grays and browns, and it shares New Vegas’ bright blue sky (as opposed to oppressive clouds) when it’s not night time or raining or green with a terrifying radiation storm. It’s often beautiful. Attention to detail is evident everywhere – Fallout 4 might not be a leader in all areas of graphics technology (character animations are still a weakness) but from the intricate Pip-Boy wrist-computer interface (which completely changes when you’re in power armor), to careful arrangement of skeletal remains that tell the tragically dark or tragically funny stories of long-dead characters, to tattered poster art on the walls, to even raindrops on your visor (if you’re wearing one) it’s consistently impressive.
Over Powered
Perhaps because this adventure is such a long haul, Fallout 4 is  a bit overeager to hook us in the beginning. After a brief glimpse of pre-war life in Fallout’s familiar-but-strange near-future and a retelling of the events on the day the bombs fell in 2077, we barely have time to get our hands dirty in the post-apocalyptic era before Fallout 4 throws us into a big action moment: You’re given a suit of the big, stompy power armor and a heavy weapon, and put into an intense brawl against the series’ most iconic monster.

It’s certainly not an unconventional idea for a game with a long progression arc to give us an early taste of the powerful toys we’ll gain access to later in order to motivate us to work for them, but with Fallout it’s a misstep that trods on the series’ beloved feeling of working our way up from almost nothing to become the dominant force in the wasteland. This bothered me less and less as I began to explore, but knowing that armor was available when I wanted it made me a little cockier than I wanted to be when setting out into a hostile, unforgiving world.
It Builds Character
“
The decision of what to do with the single point you get each level has a significant impact.
One of the first things a returning Fallout player will notice after creating a character with the intuitive push-and-pull face-sculpting tool is that the entire concepts of skill points and traits have been consumed by the perks system, unifying all character progression under one big, elaborately animated Vault Boy chart with so many unlockable options you have to scroll through them to see them all. While this streamlining does mean giving up a lot of minute control over where your character improves with each level, it also means the decision of what to do with the single point you get each level has a significant impact, and therefore those decisions represent a commitment and are tough to make: do you want to spend it on a new low-level perk, increase the level of an existing one, or pump it into a SPECIAL attribute like Luck to boost certain stats and also open up a new, more powerful perk, like the Mysterious Stranger, that you’ll be able to unlock with your next level?

Fallout 4’s crafting system gives even more motivation to compulsively collect everything that isn’t nailed down.
As if I didn’t already have enough of a hoarding problem, Fallout 4’s crafting system gives even more motivation to compulsively collect everything that isn’t nailed down. It’s so easy, too - grabbing things out of containers happens quickly in window that pops up when you look over it. Every item in the world is made up of material components, most of which you can intuitively guess: bottles are needed for glass, a desk fan will provide you with steel and gears, and a roll of duct tape is worth its weight in gold. I once went on a desperate search for pencils so that I could extract the lead they contained to use for radiation shielding. (Apparently Fallout's alternate universe never switched to graphite.) Nothing is worthless junk, which means that managing the weight of your inventory is a constant series of agonizing decisions of what to take with you and what to leave behind.

Oh man...words cannot express what happened to me after playing this. The Video Game "Cleanse". If you are someone that can tolerate the Minecraft substitute, enjoy. If you are like the dozens of people that tried my order, RUN!
First of all, for taste I would rate this a 5. So good. Straight to the point and simple...I was a happy camper.
BUT (or should I say BUTT), not long after playing about 20 minutes all hell broke loose. I had a gastrointestinal experience like nothing I've ever imagined. Cramps, sweating, bloating beyond my worst nightmare. I've had food poisoning from some bad shellfish and that was almost like a skip in the park compared to what was going on inside me.
Then came the, uh, flatulence. Heavens to Murgatroyd, the sounds, like trumpets calling the demons back to Hell...the stench, like 1,000 rotten corpses vomited. I couldn't stand to stay in one room for fear of succumbing to my own odors.
But wait; there's more. What came out of me felt like someone tried to funnel Niagara Falls through a coffee straw. I swear my sphincters were screaming. It felt like my delicate starfish was a gaping maw projectile vomiting a torrential flood of toxic waste. 100% liquid. Flammable liquid. NAPALM. It was actually a bit humorous (for a nanosecond)as it was just beyond anything I could imagine possible.
AND IT WENT ON FOR HOURS.
I felt violated when it was over, which I think might have been sometime in the early morning of the next day. There was stuff coming out of me that I ate at my wedding in 2005.
I played FIVE ROUNDS of this innocent-looking game so I told a friend about what happened to me, thinking it HAD to be some type of sensitivity I had to the Minecraft substitute, and in spite of my warnings and graphic descriptions, she decided to take her chances and take it off my hands.
Silly woman. All of the same for her, and a phone call from her while on the toilet (because you kinda end up living in the bathroom for a spell) telling me she really wished she would have listened. I think she was crying.
Her sister was skeptical and suspected that we were exaggerating. She took it to work, since there was still 99% of achievements left. She works for a construction company, where there are builders, roofers, house painters, landscapers, etc. Lots of people who generally have limited access to toilets on a given day. I can't imagine where all of those poor men (and women) pooped that day. I keep envisioning men on roofs, crossing their legs and trying to decide if they can make it down the ladder, or if they should just jump.

Saints Row 3 is a 2 players co-op open world game similar to the GTA series.
The overall main story campaign is about 25 hours long and the whole thing is just an insane excuse for the absolutely outrageous things you can do. You will be able to hijack military equipment and wreck havoc in the craziest ways, jack into cyberspace and even go around naked beating up people etc.
Graphics is very bright and colourful. The open world looks nice and is great fun to drive around in. Music and sound are crisp. Seriously, driving around at breakneck speeds ramming into pedestrians with a friend while blasting techno tunes is something that definitely has to be experienced at least once.
Downsides, although funny, SR3 story feels too rediculous and nonsensical at times. The city itself feels kindda small. Co-op only allows for 2 players. Early missions are also only just knockoffs of the repeatable quests. Too many DLCs released also feels and stinks too much of corporate greed.
SR3 is a good and worthy sequel and is technically superior, but SR2 has a better and more mature story compared to it. It really depends on your taste. If you enjoy a more serious and darker story, SR2 is better (If you can endure it's horrible console port problems). Otherwise SR3 is just great fun to co-op with a friend.
Overall Rating: 9.0 / 10

There are just two improvements I would reccommend.

(One of the most popular mp game modes is sandbox Wasteland, where players roam around completing missions, earning cash, killing each other, buying weapons/gear/vehicles, and building bases. If my fps was actually at a competent speed, I would spend all day on Wasteland servers. But we need a single player version with AI teams to join/compete, with randomly spawning missions and the like.
Still, even without those two things, I highly recommend Arma 3. If you can play competently in Arma, yet suck at CoD, you are doing war the right way.

-The online community has breathed life into what should have been a forgotten game, the community has created entire major updates, created cosmetics and maps for this game, and have even created multiple (unused) weapons that are fully coded and with working mechanics that could eventually be moved from their private servers to live matches.
-Weird, yet fun, gameplay. This game has so many quirks such as, rocket/sentry jumping, grenades that are used to kamikaze at enemies,electric signs that one hit wet players, and much more.
-Cool and intresting cosmetics and a good leveling system (acheivements give items to players)
-Wacky play styles like friendly sandvich carrying hoovies, pyrosharking with an electric sign an killing anyone that comes into the water, ninjaneer (teleporting behind enemy teams), and more that couldn't be explained if you haven't played the game.
Cons (Oh Boy)
-The online community despite breathing life into this game, can be very toxic and disses on people who don't spends hundreds of dollars on cosmetics, seperating the gaming community into p2p and f2p.
-This game lies, it is not free, its $0.99 for "premium" benefits, and although that sounds stupid and not important, basically all these complaints are.
-Valve doesn't care anymore, with csgo soaring they have kind of abandonded this game, leaving a very small team of people who are still passionate about this project, also if anyone brings up the jungle update, just ignore them, its just a myth at this point.
-This game has terrible balancing in weapons and with teams, there are so many games where its just 5 vs a lone player who tries his best to stall into the game coordinator gets more players into the game. Weapons like the dead ringer and phlog are crutch weapons that give a player an "I win" card  with the dead ringer letting you survive basically any attack and get away with it, going invisible then suprising the enemy. The phlog is just an overused meme at this point letting you kill a 450 hp heavy in a few seconds and completely crushing any enemy who dare comes near you when they activate the weapon.
I do recommend this game, athough their were loads of cons, they were all pretty minor and the gameplay, style, and characters make up for their mistakes tenfold.

The fact that the developers chose to take the third instalment of the series into the relm of being campy, almost to the point self-depracation, makes this game by far more intertaining. You're not just stealing cars, shoot people and running missions, you're also making fun of the fact that the Saints gang has gotten so famous. Not only are they doing ads for their own energy drinks, but even the cops who are chasing you durring the tutorial mission aren't just trying to arrest you, but also get your autograph. Add to that the open world gameplay, the characters, the dialog, the ability to complete a few key missions in two seperate ways and the fact that you can basicaly make your character invincible without having to cheat just by getting them to Lvl. 50, and the game does what GTA doesn't; gives you a hell of a good time and makes you laugh like a crazy person, often at the same time. Just be aware that the Full Package deal doesn't include 2 of the DLCs, but it only costs a few dollars to buy them as well.

Arma III; great game, but...
Arma III checks all the boxes for a simulation. Incredible graphics, massive scope, high level of detail, everything a person would want for a simulation. The short time I played it, I was blown away by its realism. Therein, lies the problem.
Arma III continues a trend I noticed first with the Gran Turismo series of games. GT2 was an fun game to play. A little cartoonish with the graphics and not entirely accurate to real life, but it was real enough to enjoyable. Since then, the Gran Turismo games have become more realistic and I'm in awe everytime a trailer comes out. I haven't bought a game since GT3. GT3 wasn't fun to play, it was too real. The cars required a level of control that I couldn't provide using a controller and TV screen. This is the same issue I have with Arma.
The first time my character died, I think I was receiving fire from in front of me. Each time after that, I couldn't tell you where I was being shot from. After the 10th or 15th time, enough was enough. It was very realistic, and very frustrating. No feedback from my speakers, or anything on screen to indicate where the enemy was. Effectively, I was being punished for playng a computer game on a computer. WASD and a mouse werenot enough for me to play this game.
To sum up:
If you enjoy shooters like Halo or Doom, this might not be for you.
If you were frustrated by the unforgiving nature of MS Flight Simulator, this game is definitely NOT for you.
If you have a thing for playing the most realistic games available, this is the game for you!

This is my favorite game of all time.
Pros:
+Extremely realistic (AI acts intelligently, weapon handling depends on fatigue, distance, etc)
+Great community (for the most part)
+Thousands of great mods (try Exile, King of the Hill 1944, Breaking Point, Battle Royale, Epoch, etc., all available for free from Steam Workshop. Other mods can be downloaded from
+Ability to make your own scenarios/mods
+No running and gunning- tactics and planning are the only way to win
+Huge learning curve keeps kids away (this is a very good thing)
+Looks great, even if the framerate is on the low side. I get 30 FPS playing KOTH on an i5-2500k with 12GB RAM and a GTX 560. Not a beast of a computer, but it has no problem running this game.
+Ability to play in third-person or first-person views.
Cons:
-Can't drag a fallen team member to safety before reviving (this is a big difference from Arma 2)
-Updates can mess with mods
-The vanilla game doesn't have a huge selection of uniforms/guns (this can be easily fixed though with mods, so it's no big deal; however, some servers don't support mods which makes the selection useless)
-Still expensive. You need the DLC, as many servers require it.
In summary, buy this game if you want a mature shooter that values tactics and punishes a lack of teamwork. This isn't a twitch shooter like Call of Duty or Battlefield; it is a game that tries to be as realistic as possible and entirely succeeds, in my opinion (note: I have nothing against COD or BF).
It is worth the money.

Saints Row: The Third
Over the top, GTA sandbox style gameplay, except, ABSURD & TOTALLY CRAZY! I haven't played the previous SR games yet (and I read many comments and reviews about their bad reviews for the PC version: Poor porting) although, looks like Volition did good setting themselves apart from GTA "serious" setting, with this SR3.
SR3 PROS:
-Absurd and surreal activities
-Insane plot twists
-Totally funny NPC
-Massive depth to world (lots of side missions, although GTA have more)
-Simple combat and driving models (can too simple be bad?)
-Handsome graphically (the game looks good, although the draw distance is poor).
-Huge variety of character customizations (clothing, tattoos, piercings, etc.)
-Cool upgrade system for your gang, weapons, and abilities.
-Awesome radio stations and even shop music!
SR3 CONS:
-Game instability (even for a patched game, still crashed a few times).
-Eye-popping misogyny.
-Tedious sniping (takes forever to aim properly).
-Stupid enemies (very easy gameplay).
-Gameworld ain't that big compared to GTA IV.
-Average to subpar story-based DLC.
Overall, I would recommend anyone interested on this CRAZY absurd GTA-style game, to give it a whirl... especially if you love sandbox games!
RATING: 8.5 / 10.
PS. If you do seek to acquire this game, look for the "Complete Package" tag on the game's name... that way, you'll end up buying the game with all DLC included!
...SR4 coming August 2013... get ready!

This is my favorite game of all time.
Pros:
+Extremely realistic (AI acts intelligently, weapon handling depends on fatigue, distance, etc)
+Great community (for the most part)
+Thousands of great mods (try Exile, King of the Hill 1944, Breaking Point, Battle Royale, Epoch, etc., all available for free from Steam Workshop. Other mods can be downloaded from
+Ability to make your own scenarios/mods
+No running and gunning- tactics and planning are the only way to win
+Huge learning curve keeps kids away (this is a very good thing)
+Looks great, even if the framerate is on the low side. I get 30 FPS playing KOTH on an i5-2500k with 12GB RAM and a GTX 560. Not a beast of a computer, but it has no problem running this game.
+Ability to play in third-person or first-person views.
Cons:
-Can't drag a fallen team member to safety before reviving (this is a big difference from Arma 2)
-Updates can mess with mods
-The vanilla game doesn't have a huge selection of uniforms/guns (this can be easily fixed though with mods, so it's no big deal; however, some servers don't support mods which makes the selection useless)
-Still expensive. You need the DLC, as many servers require it.
In summary, buy this game if you want a mature shooter that values tactics and punishes a lack of teamwork. This isn't a twitch shooter like Call of Duty or Battlefield; it is a game that tries to be as realistic as possible and entirely succeeds, in my opinion (note: I have nothing against COD or BF).
It is worth the money.

I gonna recommend this game even though i will be talking about lots of its negatives in this review.
Pros
-Things like my profile picture exist
-The online community has breathed life into what should have been a forgotten game, the community has created entire major updates, created cosmetics and maps for this game, and have even created multiple (unused) weapons that are fully coded and with working mechanics that could eventually be moved from their private servers to live matches.
-Weird, yet fun, gameplay. This game has so many quirks such as, rocket/sentry jumping, grenades that are used to kamikaze at enemies,electric signs that one hit wet players, and much more.
-Cool and intresting cosmetics and a good leveling system (acheivements give items to players)
-Wacky play styles like friendly sandvich carrying hoovies, pyrosharking with an electric sign an killing anyone that comes into the water, ninjaneer (teleporting behind enemy teams), and more that couldn't be explained if you haven't played the game.
Cons (Oh Boy)
-The online community despite breathing life into this game, can be very toxic and disses on people who don't spends hundreds of dollars on cosmetics, seperating the gaming community into p2p and f2p.
-This game lies, it is not free, its $0.99 for "premium" benefits, and although that sounds stupid and not important, basically all these complaints are.
-Valve doesn't care anymore, with csgo soaring they have kind of abandonded this game, leaving a very small team of people who are still passionate about this project, also if anyone brings up the jungle update, just ignore them, its just a myth at this point.
-This game has terrible balancing in weapons and with teams, there are so many games where its just 5 vs a lone player who tries his best to stall into the game coordinator gets more players into the game. Weapons like the dead ringer and phlog are crutch weapons that give a player an "I win" card  with the dead ringer letting you survive basically any attack and get away with it, going invisible then suprising the enemy. The phlog is just an overused meme at this point letting you kill a 450 hp heavy in a few seconds and completely crushing any enemy who dare comes near you when they activate the weapon.
I do recommend this game, athough their were loads of cons, they were all pretty minor and the gameplay, style, and characters make up for their mistakes tenfold.

So, this game is a battleroyal first/third person shooter that offers competitive matches and ranks in solos and has two other more unbalanced modes. (Duos & Fives) The game has no tutorial and straight up drops you into the battle arena without any hints or tips on how to survive. I think that this is one of it's biggest flaws, even though it has a lot more then that. But my biggest 'complaint' has to be about the way the dev team treats this game, even though Daybreak is racking in a ton of money their people responsible for the balancing and mechanics of the game are treating the game as a joke.
One of the great flaws of the game must be the lack of guidance within it. As I has stated before there is not tutorial or any forms of tips and hints that might guide you and at least teach you a bit about the game and it's meta at the moment. Imagin being a new player to the game, without any sort of idea what it's about or the weapons within it. One would literally not know that the AR is the main weapon one has to have, they might get discouraged due to the amount of times they die to the weapon whilst having maybe an AK or a pistol.
Another flaw is the unbalance in the weapons at the moment, for example other weapons except the AR, the Shotgun or the frag grenade are never considered due to how useless they are. The game offers no diversity in it's play style.
Even though all of these problems with the game plague it, the game is still fun for what it is. Thusands of people enjoy the way it plays and it's meta. But for the 20 euros that it is currently worth, I think it is an unworthy game of being in your library.

I bought Arma 3 way back in the heady days of Early Access past. I remember, very distinctly, playing a bit with it, playing some multiplayer with friends, and thinking to myself "This is cool, but it feels unfinished". So I let it sit for a while.
Arma 3 came out of early access, and that feeling of unfinished-ness never faded. The amount of content in the base game is frankly embarassing. There's basically one of everything: one OPFOR IFV, one BLUFOR IFV, one OPFOR assault rifle, one BLUFOR assault rifle, etcetera. The content that is there feels much less like it belongs in a series touted as a realistic infantry environment simulator, and more in the latest AAA shooter- firearms with tinny unconvincing sound, vehicles with fictionalized designs and paint schemes that make them look like they just rolled off the set of a bad low budget scifi film, CSAT infantry have goddamn bugeyes on their helmets. The underwater gameplay is a one-trick pony of a gimmick- there's a single underwater-capable rifle in the entire game and there's rarely a reason to actually do the sort of frogmen ops the rebreather gear lets you do unless you absolutely positively must find some way to cram it into a mission you're making.
On top of all that, they nixed the old DLC policy that I absolutely loved- wherein, if you didn't have a DLC, you could still make full use of its content but at a lessened (visual) quality. Instead, you just can't make use of DLC equipment and vehicles- you get a large popup telling you to buy the DLC (or at least, that's how it was last time I played).
It's frustrating. Arma 3 iterates so well on Arma 2 in some areas, and completely fails to deliver in most others. The new movement and physics are a massive step forward from Arma 2, the new flight modelling on helos (while not being DCS quality or anything) is great, the game looks significantly better. But there's barely any content (a problem BIS won't be correcting: they're already selling DLC), and what content is there feels jarringly disconected from the idea of realistic infantry combat this franchise sells itself on.

Man alive, where to start.  I got a hold of this bad boy in the free weekend.  I just screwed around with the editor, because that is my true love.  So, what's there to say?
It is mostly the same as ARMA 2, with improvements and a few keyboard tweaks here and there.  The graphics a hell of a lot better.  But that, combined with the larger maps, ravages all but the very best computers, even on low settings.  The gunplay is massively improved.  I can't lay my finger on anything specific, but it just feels smoother.  CQB used to be a pain, but that has become a heck of a lot of fun.  The varying stances, while perhaps a little gimmicky, are useful on occasion.  The Steam workshop is a gift from Heaven above, makes looking for mods so much easier.  The weapon resting is far better than anything I saw in mods for A2.  It is probably my favorite improvement.  3den, the 3d editor, is also a huge improvement.  Golly Moses, it is so, so much better than the old 2d one.  The precision it gives you is astounding.  All in all, this is an absolute reccomend for anyone who enjoys milsims.  BI took everything you loved from the original and made that better, while taking everything wrong and making it right.
TL:DR, this game is frickin' amazing.  Stop reading this nerdgasm and buy it already.

My review will briefly describe the premise of this game, and why you should get it.
Team Fortress 2 is, for those you didn't know, a class based FPS with lots of customizability for both playstyles and characters and a built-in virtual micro-economy (if you like trading).
Point 1. The game is free.
Point 2. The game is very customizable in terms of playstyle, you can use different weapons for any playstyle you like.
Point 3. Hats. And as well as hats, special hats which are dubbed "Unusual." These are the most coveted, most expensive items in the game, and everyone wants them. They have a cool effect given above your head, and a wide variety of effects to get.
Point 4. Easy to develop or get custom content (Mods/Maps) for. This only applies to those who make or use custom content in source games.
Point 5. The maps. (Or at least, a single amazing map.) cp_gorge is the best map in TF2 imo, and can allow any class or playstyle you like. cp_gorge is best map fam. Period.
I hope this review helped you in your purchase decisions...

Simply saying this "game" is fantastic just doesn't quite do it justice. Since 2010 I have enjoyed ARMA II and III, being introduced first into the original DayZ Mod. Experiences earned here are timeless, and I have been priviledged to see the development of the series. Arma 3, simply put, is my favorite game to play. I have also learned a fair amount while doing so. It is an experience you can find no where else, with a development team that is passionate to create the best, asking for criticism along the way- with DLC you can try before you buy via the editor, and nonetheless isn't game breaking or necessary by any means if you don't happen to want any extra content.
I would vote yes again and again. Participated in the Arma 3 Alpha, and it has been an absolute joy to see this game become more and more polished. The greatest investment steam has to offer. The learning curve is significant, but completely worthwhile to learn. Do not feel broken by the complexity. It is a masterpiece of art, with very thrilling experiences. And, even years on from the DayZ mod, I still remember my first online kill with absolute clarity.

Some quick jokes:
You can spend less time reading the TOS than the ingame manuals.
This game is best played while listening to Vietnam war music.
Anti-Air vehicle means you can ♥♥♥♥ up anything with enough shells.
I had a helicopter pick up my SDV from the ocean, and drop me at a base where I joined my team and fought off tanks and helicopters.
Cons:
1. The AI is kinda dumb when tasked with certain objectives, such as lifting certain cargo or driving.
2. It's very hard to see enemies through all the bushes and crap, but they can see you despite visual cover.
3. The editor is overburdened by copies with minor differences, such as 2 infantry types not having different abilities, only a different loadout. ( Which you can change anyways. )
4. You cannot change the abilities of units. ( Changing a medic to an ammo supplier. )
5. Theres not a whole lot of different vehicles in certain categories. ( This is negated by mod support. )
6. You cannot change certain properties of vehicles. ( Changing mounted gun types, or special conditions such as spawning an SDV with the hatch closed. )
7. There is no melee mechanic, if you run out of ammo, you better find some more or hide for the rest of the game.
8. The editor is a bit confusing and some things seem broken. ( I don't know if it's bugs or I need to learn scripting. )
9. You have to hold every AI's hand in the editor, there is no setting to allow them to do what they want to. ( You must tell them what to do, the only thing you don't have to instruct them to do is to fire upon enemies or get to tactical positions within a small radius. )
10. In my opinion, the DLC content to price ratio is not very good. ( For example, one DLC costs $11.99 and adds two helicopters. )
11. The weapon types are limited to rifles, 2 smgs, pistols, and launchers. ( I think it would be cool to use stuff like flamethrowers, rifle grenade launchers, flashbangs, ordanance signal grenades, shotguns. )
Pros:
1. With the editor you can create amazing and fun scenarios. ( I recreated Normandy D-Day and had a blast shooting rockets and artillery at enemies. )
2. It is very realistic, which is a preference.
3. You can attack from sea, land, or air.
4. You can create scenarios and publish them for others to play.
5. Using helicopters, you can transport small vehicles and supplies to your teammates.
6. You can tell drones to engage targets, or control them yourself.
7. You can kill people by ricocheting bullets off of vehicles and objects.
8. You can go into a VR simulation and test out guns and vehicles, and bullet trajectories are shown to help you understand a gun's power and penetration.
9. You can give commands to people in your squad, as long as you outrank them.
10. You can place explosives on the ground. ( But I don't think you can plant them on walls and objects. )
11. Theres a large array of guns, but kind of like the copied soldiers I mentioned before, most of them are just the same but with certain attachments already attached.
12. Theres alot of equipment. ( Smoke grenades with different colors, two types of frag grenades, glow sticks, rangefinders, medic kits. )
13. You can make different types of areas in the editor. ( Slums, housing, junkyards, minefields, stuff like that. )
14. The tutorials cover pretty much everything, the only time I scratched my head in confusion was playing before I did the tutorials.
15. Theres an inventory system, allowing you to loot ammo and weapons from fallen soldiers and store guns in vehicles.
Overall 9.2/10

Both a move forward and a misstep for the series, this best-selling entry in the Saints Row IP is a mixed bag of improvements and rushed work. The work itself is not harmed by the rushed feeling but it is hindered in that it lacks gameplay content available in prior games; dynamic melee combat is reduced to weapon unique nutshots and posing opportunities as well as a more restricted selection of guns. It lacks variety of the city; there are no slum area of tralier parks or high mountain climbs and it can be hard to remember just where that jump was as the city looks too homogenous ultimately. You can't even pick up the mailboxes to throw them at innocents ala Saint's Row 2!
It does introduce many gameplay advances, like boduken, which is jumping straight into cars in a rush of that-broken-glass-be-damned-even-if-I-sit-on-it-for-hours-driving-this-car-at-high-speeds. More appropriately, it features far tighter vehicle physics than it's predecessors and slightly expanded scope to customisation of vehicles and guns. In addition, the spate of awesome flying vehicles is one of the game's main drawing cards. When it comes to your avatar as "The Boss", you can also design most any protagonist concept that comes to mind. I've made a grayscale Bruce Lee Noir Detective and a grown-up-Tintin-gone-bad.
All that being said, in spite of the mixed bag experience, this game is also an example of how porting to the PC can and should be done right. Unlike Saints Row 2, which deserves it's reputation as one of the worst PC ports of the 7th generation console era, this is the other end of that spectrum, with DX11 support and the bells and whistles that often entails.
The first four hours of this is pure fun; after that, it repeats itself and the story really feels strung out. The game unfortunately does feel like a beginning, a muddle, and an end. Pick it up cheap if you're in doubt and see for yourself just how off the mark this entry is ... and just how fun it can still be. If a fan of the series, go in with low expectations. All players be warned; the end-game element is really easy to ruin for yourself by using the game's levelling system to become virtually invulnerable (provided you don't stay in any about-to-explode vehicle).
I've personally been left with the odd feeling that this game is an odd metacommentary of the (then) current state of modern gaming industry, coming of age as a medium yet what really does any of this virtual 'enabling' stand for? Not bad for a game that was pushed out of a far too short and imposed development cycle!
Lastly, there has been an effective mod scene, assembled mostly from those that made Saints Row 2 work on the PC when it was abandoned by the porters and the devs, that can help break up replay monotony and address design oversights, like a lack of vanilla mission replay functionality.

My review will briefly describe the premise of this game, and why you should get it.
Team Fortress 2 is, for those you didn't know, a class based FPS with lots of customizability for both playstyles and characters and a built-in virtual micro-economy (if you like trading).
Point 1. The game is free.
Point 2. The game is very customizable in terms of playstyle, you can use different weapons for any playstyle you like.
Point 3. Hats. And as well as hats, special hats which are dubbed "Unusual." These are the most coveted, most expensive items in the game, and everyone wants them. They have a cool effect given above your head, and a wide variety of effects to get.
Point 4. Easy to develop or get custom content (Mods/Maps) for. This only applies to those who make or use custom content in source games.
Point 5. The maps. (Or at least, a single amazing map.) cp_gorge is the best map in TF2 imo, and can allow any class or playstyle you like. cp_gorge is best map fam. Period.
I hope this review helped you in your purchase decisions...

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

After over 200 hours, I'd say it's safe to write a review. To start off with, this is one of my all time favorite games. If I were given the choice to reccomend it, I would probably reccomend it, but it all just depends on the type of gamer you are. To start off with, it is a fun, team based game that allows you to communicate to your teamates via chat and voice. There is an assortment of classes to choose from when playing, and each has their advantages and disadvantages. Everyone has their favorite, and again, it depends on what kind of gamer you are to find which class you truly favor. Although, certain classes can overpower others in different ways, you have to find ways to overcome these challenges, and that will ultimately make you a great player. This game is pretty hard to get into, because when you play multiplayer (which is virtually the only game mode you can play) you will get matched against people much higher and better than you. Even I, at level 57, am matched against people almost double my level. But, once you start getting into the game, you will get better, and that will make it much more fun.
Another really cool feature about this game, is that it is really heavily infuenced by the community. The community makes maps, weapons, and cosmetics, and some of which are good enough to be actually commercially sold in-game. This brings another community feature up, which is that it runs mostly off of the communty market, rather commercial market, which is really cool.
One disadvantage when getting this game is that you pretty much have to pay to get any cool items, but that little deposit could make you a profit, all depending on how you use the money, and how the market fluctuates.
So as you can see, I really enjoy this game and would reccomend most of the time, and hope you enjoy it too. Hope this review helps and happy holidays!!!!

Some quick jokes:
You can spend less time reading the TOS than the ingame manuals.
This game is best played while listening to Vietnam war music.
Anti-Air vehicle means you can ♥♥♥♥ up anything with enough shells.
I had a helicopter pick up my SDV from the ocean, and drop me at a base where I joined my team and fought off tanks and helicopters.
Cons:
1. The AI is kinda dumb when tasked with certain objectives, such as lifting certain cargo or driving.
2. It's very hard to see enemies through all the bushes and crap, but they can see you despite visual cover.
3. The editor is overburdened by copies with minor differences, such as 2 infantry types not having different abilities, only a different loadout. ( Which you can change anyways. )
4. You cannot change the abilities of units. ( Changing a medic to an ammo supplier. )
5. Theres not a whole lot of different vehicles in certain categories. ( This is negated by mod support. )
6. You cannot change certain properties of vehicles. ( Changing mounted gun types, or special conditions such as spawning an SDV with the hatch closed. )
7. There is no melee mechanic, if you run out of ammo, you better find some more or hide for the rest of the game.
8. The editor is a bit confusing and some things seem broken. ( I don't know if it's bugs or I need to learn scripting. )
9. You have to hold every AI's hand in the editor, there is no setting to allow them to do what they want to. ( You must tell them what to do, the only thing you don't have to instruct them to do is to fire upon enemies or get to tactical positions within a small radius. )
10. In my opinion, the DLC content to price ratio is not very good. ( For example, one DLC costs $11.99 and adds two helicopters. )
11. The weapon types are limited to rifles, 2 smgs, pistols, and launchers. ( I think it would be cool to use stuff like flamethrowers, rifle grenade launchers, flashbangs, ordanance signal grenades, shotguns. )
Pros:
1. With the editor you can create amazing and fun scenarios. ( I recreated Normandy D-Day and had a blast shooting rockets and artillery at enemies. )
2. It is very realistic, which is a preference.
3. You can attack from sea, land, or air.
4. You can create scenarios and publish them for others to play.
5. Using helicopters, you can transport small vehicles and supplies to your teammates.
6. You can tell drones to engage targets, or control them yourself.
7. You can kill people by ricocheting bullets off of vehicles and objects.
8. You can go into a VR simulation and test out guns and vehicles, and bullet trajectories are shown to help you understand a gun's power and penetration.
9. You can give commands to people in your squad, as long as you outrank them.
10. You can place explosives on the ground. ( But I don't think you can plant them on walls and objects. )
11. Theres a large array of guns, but kind of like the copied soldiers I mentioned before, most of them are just the same but with certain attachments already attached.
12. Theres alot of equipment. ( Smoke grenades with different colors, two types of frag grenades, glow sticks, rangefinders, medic kits. )
13. You can make different types of areas in the editor. ( Slums, housing, junkyards, minefields, stuff like that. )
14. The tutorials cover pretty much everything, the only time I scratched my head in confusion was playing before I did the tutorials.
15. Theres an inventory system, allowing you to loot ammo and weapons from fallen soldiers and store guns in vehicles.
Overall 9.2/10

The concept is really cool, but I think for a $40 price tag I expect fewer issues.  There are better games for your money IMO.

If you have not played Saints Row 3 yet, you are missing out big time.
This game, like Grand Theft Auto, incorporates TPS and RPG, and takes place within a criminal world with a goal of becoming the most powerful criminal enterprise.
However, this game added in a little spice to make it significantly more entertaining than your classic Grand Theft Auto series. Saints Row 3 provides an experience point system, but what really takes the spotlight of the show is how exaggerated everything is. In this game, you will be looking at the most ridiculous stunts and effects throughout the whole playthrough, and I must say, they are worth every penny.

Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.
