I'm bound to get a metric tonne of dislikes for this, but I'll live with it. Please note that I'm only giving it a negative review because of my history with the Arma franchise (starting with Armed assault, moving through arma 2 and all its expansions and playing using ACE mod on each) and the fact that I had certain expectations when I inevitably pre-ordered this game.
Now please note, I have no issue with the setting, near future is fine provided it is done correctly, and in that regard I believe Arma 3 really shines. I have yet to play a game set in the near future that is as 'believable' as Arma 3, because the majority of the weapons and vehicles already exist... and a lot of them are outdated.
My issue with arma 3 is the fact that there is a shocking lack of content with the base game, there is a massive step downwards in terms of realistic fidelity, and the performance of the game is abysmal, even with someone with a computer that is massively overpowered for the game. Now, the argument could be made that no where else could I turn for a game that seamlessly integrates combined land, sea and air warfare on a massive scale, and I would believe that argument if Arma II and it's expansions didn't exist. That's the problem, this has all been done before, and to a much better standard.
Why do soldiers only flinch when shot, and continue to fight back as if nothing happened? In Arma 2, if I shot the leg/arm of an AI, his movement would be impaired or his aim would be impaired, in Arma 3, nothing is simulated whatsoever. Instead, enemies take multiple hits to be downed, even with extended armour turned off!
I don't understand why Bohemia decided to create 3 factions that are more or less mirror images of one another (the reused assets between mounted MG's, grenade launchers, missile launchers alike is puzzling and frankly, lazy.), I don't understand why they removed core features such as dragging/carrying wounded allies to be healed properly by a dedicated medic, as opposed to the magical 'heal all' FAKs we have in game, and I don't understand why they're still using the same tired engine as they used 20 years ago for a game that is on a much greater scale in both terrain, amount of buildings and graphical fidelity.
Don't get me wrong, Arma III is a stroke of technical genius, managing to take the virtual reality engine and make it look THIS good is mind blowing, but what's the point in looking good, if the game runs like♥♥♥♥♥♥ Even when installed on an SSD, there is still the stutter loading when playing online, and I've found that in cities etc. the framerates are completely unplayable when playing with a reasonable player count of 30+.
So here are what I consider to be the pros, and the cons:
Pros:
- Beautiful looking game
- Interesting concepts behind a near future setting
- Movement is easily better than the previous games
- Stance system (whilst part of movement, is good enough to be mentioned on it's own)
- Bipods (when they work) are really damn cool
- AI is much smarter than previous installments, reacting better to cover and suppression
- Sound design is much better, although guns still sound a bit 'off', something I rectify quite quickly with sound mods
- Inventory system is really nice and intuitive
- Steam workshop support makes mods easier to use, however due to the file size limit only really supports basic mods which I couldn't care less for.
- Campaign is a bit more cohesive this time around, previous campaigns felt a bit aimless
- Pre recorded voice lines
Cons (there are a lot of them):
- The game caters to more casual players (will explain with the following points)
1. Ammo pool showing how many shots are left in your gun, regardless of difficulty setting is ♥♥♥♥ing stupid
2. AI can tank several rounds, and fire back with perfect accuracy with nothing more than a flinch, gone are the days of crippling someone's arm to reduce their accuracy or taking out their legs to stop them from moving
3. Vehicle crosshairs almost never line up with their HUD counterparts, and cannot be turned off
4. Weapons have poor penetration value, I've seen the argument being made that in the future armoured vests will allow you to survive longer, which I can appreciate, but that does not stop the fact that the kinetic force of a bullet would still wound you to the point where you are ineffective. I don't mind the soldiers surviving, but at least incapacitate them for ♥♥♥♥s sake.
5. Magical FAKs that heal you to the point where a dedicated medic is a luxury, not a requirement.
6. (More of a server issue than the game itself) Everyone is running casual epoch, altis life etc servers. These far outnumber the traditional game servers, which I think speaks for itself really. It's a game targetting people who aren't here for an authentic military shooter. It's here for people that want to use third person, sprint everywhere and not take things seriously.
- Each faction is practically identical, there is no assymetrical balance like the previous games, everyone has one assault rifle, one type of grenade, one type of MBT, one type of transport helicopter, one type of attack helicopter, ONE JET EACH (wtf?), and the exact same grenade launchers, missile launchers, UAV's, UGV's and submarines. The recycled content is ♥♥♥♥ing lazy.
- The DLC's thus far have offered very little content for their price. For example BAF in arma 2 added an entire new faction to play, with vehicles and weapons respectively. Whilst I can't comment on the expansion pack, Operation arrowhead was practically a new game, and from the PR that bohemia have released, TANOA seems about the most compelling part of Apex, which will probably run like♥♥♥♥♥♥because the amount of trees etc.
- I don't like Altis. Personal preference.
- Game runs like absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥on several rigs I've tried, including a 5960x, 24gb of ram, 2x Titan X's in SLI all running from an ssd to remove any loading stutter. It's just not possible to get this game running nicely.
- Hardly any weapons/vehicles per faction. I touched on this briefly, but it was months until CSAT and NATO got jets, and they're both ground attackers only? Why? Why is there only one large transport vehicle shared between each faction? Why does each faction have the exact same UAV's, the same UGV's, submarines, grenades, chemlights, smoke grenades, ghillie suits, armour etc etc etc. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥.
- Why does it take multiple bullets to drop a guy at 1m? Unless I'm using 7.62, 12.7 or intermediate cartidges, armour seems to sponge bullets for absolutely no reason.
- Why can I not drag wounded allies? Or carry them?
This game drives me insane because I wanted to like it so desperately. Each iteration in a series should build upon it's predecessor, and in many regards Arma III improved in many ways, but took so many steps back that I can't recommend this game to anyone.
Now ACE 3 definitely makes this game a lot easier to stomach, but the base game is still unfortunately there. It's unfortunately the only way I could say you should play this game if you're used to Arma II. I'm sure I'll get a lot of arguments from people saying that mods will fix X, Y and Z, but the fact is; Arma II didn't need fixing, so why should Arma III?

===
H1Z1: King of the Kill Overview
===
H1Z1: King of the Kill (KoTH) is a multiplayer 150-man battle royale game. The game has a price tag of 20 USD, and is available on Steam, developed and published by Daybreak Games. It uses a third-party launcher, also created by Daybreak Games, which also requires a third-party account that is registered and validated via. email in order to play. Personally, I find the whole set up for multiple accounts/usernames to be very confusing at times, whereas if you have multiple usernames on one account (for some reason), then you have to be using the correct one in order to play the game you want to play. In order for it to be the correct account, you must've linked it with your Steam account prior. I no longer find this as much of a hassle, but it was for me in the beginning, so if you are a new player reading this review before purchasing the game, make sure you are aware that possible launch errors and login issues may occur due to Steam/Daybreak Games account confliction, or by not running Steam as an administrator. Besides that, below you will find my Pro's and Con's of KoTK.
===
Pro's and Con's of H1Z1: King of the Kill
===
[Pro's]
+ Good optimization for high-end and low-end PCs
+ Playable on both NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards
+ Mutliple server locations for the optimal gaming experience
+ Servers are near lag/connection-stutter free
+ Balanced gameplay; everyone starts off the same way, but only one true victor reigns supreme
+ Duo's and Five's mode allows for playing with friends, and making new ones along the way
+ Local and team-based voice chat support
[Con's]
- Hitboxes and hit detection are both completely BROKEN
- Lack of text/team chat
- BattlEye anti-cheat (near pointless when attempting to detect hackers within a game)
- For the amount of issues this game tends to have, the 20 dollar price tag is pretty hefty
- Weapon/apparel cosmetics (microtransaction-land)
- Low framerates (< 60) in some areas of the map
- Confusing Daybreak Games registration
- Errors occur when using "an incorrect username"
- Errors occur when not loading Steam as an administrator for the first-time launch of the game
===
Conclusion of My Review of H1Z1: King of the Kill
===
Overall Score: 6.5/10
Would I recommend this game?: That's hard to say. As of now, let's stick with "Yes."
Other Statements: Be wary of the rogue hitboxes.

Please note that I'm only giving it a negative review because of my history with the Arma franchise (starting with Armed assault, moving through arma 2 and all its expansions and playing using ACE mod on each) and the fact that I had certain expectations when I inevitably pre-ordered this game.
Now please note, I have no issue with the setting, near future is fine provided it is done correctly, and in that regard I believe Arma 3 really shines. I have yet to play a game set in the near future that is as 'believable' as Arma 3, because the majority of the weapons and vehicles already exist... and a lot of them are outdated.
My issue with arma 3 is the fact that there is a shocking lack of content with the base game, there is a massive step downwards in terms of realistic fidelity, and the performance of the game is abysmal, even with someone with a computer that is massively overpowered for the game. Now, the argument could be made that no where else could I turn for a game that seamlessly integrates combined land, sea and air warfare on a massive scale, and I would believe that argument if Arma II and it's expansions didn't exist. That's the problem, this has all been done before, and to a much better standard.
Why do soldiers only flinch when shot, and continue to fight back as if nothing happened? In Arma 2, if I shot the leg/arm of an AI, his movement would be impaired or his aim would be impaired, in Arma 3, nothing is simulated whatsoever. Instead, enemies take multiple hits to be downed, even with extended armour turned off!
I don't understand why Bohemia decided to create 3 factions that are more or less mirror images of one another (the reused assets between mounted MG's, grenade launchers, missile launchers alike is puzzling and frankly, lazy.), I don't understand why they removed core features such as dragging/carrying wounded allies to be healed properly by a dedicated medic, as opposed to the magical 'heal all' FAKs we have in game, and I don't understand why they're still using the same tired engine as they used 20 years ago for a game that is on a much greater scale in both terrain, amount of buildings and graphical fidelity.
Don't get me wrong, Arma III is a stroke of technical genius, managing to take the virtual reality engine and make it look THIS good is mind blowing, but what's the point in looking good, if the game runs like♥♥♥♥♥♥ Even when installed on an SSD, there is still the stutter loading when playing online, and I've found that in cities etc. the framerates are completely unplayable when playing with a reasonable player count of 30+.
So here are what I consider to be the pros, and the cons:
Pros:
- Beautiful looking game
- Interesting concepts behind a near future setting
- Movement is easily better than the previous games
- Stance system (whilst part of movement, is good enough to be mentioned on it's own)
- Bipods (when they work) are really damn cool
- AI is much smarter than previous installments, reacting better to cover and suppression
- Sound design is much better, although guns still sound a bit 'off', something I rectify quite quickly with sound mods
- Inventory system is really nice and intuitive
- Steam workshop support makes mods easier to use, however due to the file size limit only really supports basic mods which I couldn't care less for.
- Campaign is a bit more cohesive this time around, previous campaigns felt a bit aimless
- Pre recorded voice lines
Cons (there are a lot of them):
- The game caters to more casual players (will explain with the following points)
1. Ammo pool showing how many shots are left in your gun, regardless of difficulty setting is ♥♥♥♥ing stupid
2. AI can tank several rounds, and fire back with perfect accuracy with nothing more than a flinch, gone are the days of crippling someone's arm to reduce their accuracy or taking out their legs to stop them from moving
3. Vehicle crosshairs almost never line up with their HUD counterparts, and cannot be turned off
4. Weapons have poor penetration value, I've seen the argument being made that in the future armoured vests will allow you to survive longer, which I can appreciate, but that does not stop the fact that the kinetic force of a bullet would still wound you to the point where you are ineffective. I don't mind the soldiers surviving, but at least incapacitate them for ♥♥♥♥s sake.
5. Magical FAKs that heal you to the point where a dedicated medic is a luxury, not a requirement.
6. (More of a server issue than the game itself) Everyone is running casual epoch, altis life etc servers. These far outnumber the traditional game servers, which I think speaks for itself really. It's a game targetting people who aren't here for an authentic military shooter. It's here for people that want to use third person, sprint everywhere and not take things seriously.
- Each faction is practically identical, there is no assymetrical balance like the previous games, everyone has one assault rifle, one type of grenade, one type of MBT, one type of transport helicopter, one type of attack helicopter, ONE JET EACH (wtf?), and the exact same grenade launchers, missile launchers, UAV's, UGV's and submarines. The recycled content is ♥♥♥♥ing lazy.
- The DLC's thus far have offered very little content for their price. For example BAF in arma 2 added an entire new faction to play, with vehicles and weapons respectively. Whilst I can't comment on the expansion pack, Operation arrowhead was practically a new game, and from the PR that bohemia have released, TANOA seems about the most compelling part of Apex, which will probably run like♥♥♥♥♥♥because the amount of trees etc.
- I don't like Altis. Personal preference.
- Game runs like absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥on several rigs I've tried, including a 5960x, 24gb of ram, 2x Titan X's in SLI all running from an ssd to remove any loading stutter. It's just not possible to get this game running nicely.
- Hardly any weapons/vehicles per faction. I touched on this briefly, but it was months until CSAT and NATO got jets, and they're both ground attackers only? Why? Why is there only one large transport vehicle shared between each faction? Why does each faction have the exact same UAV's, the same UGV's, submarines, grenades, chemlights, smoke grenades, ghillie suits, armour etc etc etc. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥.
- Why does it take multiple bullets to drop a guy at 1m? Unless I'm using 7.62, 12.7 or intermediate cartidges, armour seems to sponge bullets for absolutely no reason.
- Why can I not drag wounded allies? Or carry them?
This game drives me insane because I wanted to like it so desperately. Each iteration in a series should build upon it's predecessor, and in many regards Arma III improved in many ways, but took so many steps back that I can't recommend this game to anyone.
Now ACE 3 definitely makes this game a lot easier to stomach, but the base game is still unfortunately there. It's unfortunately the only way I could say you should play this game if you're used to Arma II. I'm sure I'll get a lot of arguments from people saying that mods will fix X, Y and Z, but the fact is; Arma II didn't need fixing, so why should Arma III?

===
H1Z1: King of the Kill Overview
===
H1Z1: King of the Kill (KoTH) is a multiplayer 150-man battle royale game. The game has a price tag of 20 USD, and is available on Steam, developed and published by Daybreak Games. It uses a third-party launcher, also created by Daybreak Games, which also requires a third-party account that is registered and validated via. email in order to play. Personally, I find the whole set up for multiple accounts/usernames to be very confusing at times, whereas if you have multiple usernames on one account (for some reason), then you have to be using the correct one in order to play the game you want to play. In order for it to be the correct account, you must've linked it with your Steam account prior. I no longer find this as much of a hassle, but it was for me in the beginning, so if you are a new player reading this review before purchasing the game, make sure you are aware that possible launch errors and login issues may occur due to Steam/Daybreak Games account confliction, or by not running Steam as an administrator. Besides that, below you will find my Pro's and Con's of KoTK.
===
Pro's and Con's of H1Z1: King of the Kill
===
[Pro's]
+ Good optimization for high-end and low-end PCs
+ Playable on both NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards
+ Mutliple server locations for the optimal gaming experience
+ Servers are near lag/connection-stutter free
+ Balanced gameplay; everyone starts off the same way, but only one true victor reigns supreme
+ Duo's and Five's mode allows for playing with friends, and making new ones along the way
+ Local and team-based voice chat support
[Con's]
- Hitboxes and hit detection are both completely BROKEN
- Lack of text/team chat
- BattlEye anti-cheat (near pointless when attempting to detect hackers within a game)
- For the amount of issues this game tends to have, the 20 dollar price tag is pretty hefty
- Weapon/apparel cosmetics (microtransaction-land)
- Low framerates (< 60) in some areas of the map
- Confusing Daybreak Games registration
- Errors occur when using "an incorrect username"
- Errors occur when not loading Steam as an administrator for the first-time launch of the game
===
Conclusion of My Review of H1Z1: King of the Kill
===
Overall Score: 6.5/10
Would I recommend this game?: That's hard to say. As of now, let's stick with "Yes."
Other Statements: Be wary of the rogue hitboxes.

After over 200 hours, I'd say it's safe to write a review. To start off with, this is one of my all time favorite games. If I were given the choice to reccomend it, I would probably reccomend it, but it all just depends on the type of gamer you are. To start off with, it is a fun, team based game that allows you to communicate to your teamates via chat and voice. There is an assortment of classes to choose from when playing, and each has their advantages and disadvantages. Everyone has their favorite, and again, it depends on what kind of gamer you are to find which class you truly favor. Although, certain classes can overpower others in different ways, you have to find ways to overcome these challenges, and that will ultimately make you a great player. This game is pretty hard to get into, because when you play multiplayer (which is virtually the only game mode you can play) you will get matched against people much higher and better than you. Even I, at level 57, am matched against people almost double my level. But, once you start getting into the game, you will get better, and that will make it much more fun.
Another really cool feature about this game, is that it is really heavily infuenced by the community. The community makes maps, weapons, and cosmetics, and some of which are good enough to be actually commercially sold in-game. This brings another community feature up, which is that it runs mostly off of the communty market, rather commercial market, which is really cool.
One disadvantage when getting this game is that you pretty much have to pay to get any cool items, but that little deposit could make you a profit, all depending on how you use the money, and how the market fluctuates.
So as you can see, I really enjoy this game and would reccomend most of the time, and hope you enjoy it too. Hope this review helps and happy holidays!!!!

so after DX12 most important things for A3 would be: putting 64-bit engine(for both client AND server)into actions, making A3 really-multithreading or better relying about Message-passing code(preferably over some ERlang code, perhaps. considering scalability advantages even against other MP-langs or MP-libs/wrappers to overcome)especially in AI code(most stress, even in ~ short battles/matches).
generally i would recommend A3. but not for casual gamers. if you one of newbie in milsim or even in action games at all - you may be disapointed/frustrated at first time or even angry(if you read some reviews - you may had expressions of). its game for gamers really Knowing what they need and why. cuz most fun in A3 rolled over three things: teamplay, challenge, replayabliliy. and editability/moddabiliy.(but it worth another, separated review i guess).

Silly game with silly missions and a silly story with silly characters. Decent length too, but that might vary depending on how much you can stick just faffing about or doing little side-missions and whatnot. Youll be getting a decent amount of time out of it no matter what you do really which - in todays world of 5 hours being classed as "long" - will last you what might feel a short eternity.
Maybe it jumped the shark a bit... well, a lot more than it should have compared to its predecessor, but it would have been better had it stuck to its guns in that regard. Theres a little too much flip-flopping between actual serious business going down and "I am going to go beat that mascot in the face with a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;.
The really, really annoying part of the entire game was the rival gangs/police. Until you can work up a bit of cash to upgrade yourself or buy a bunch of buildings to hide in you really cannot start a thing against them without being chased to the ends of the Earth by rubberbanding drivers, armour-clad bullet-sponge brutes and helicopters. You clip one of their cars or taunt a single member in the street and suddenly half the city is against you which only escalates.
All in all, its a proper games game: plenty to do, doesnt take itself seriously and youll probably have the most fun doing whatever the hell you like rather than what it wants you to do. Not a masterpiece by any stretch of the imagination, but nobody should struggle to derive entertainment from it.

That the 3rd St Saints gang color is purple and their leader is saying things like, "No rules? Sounds good to me", certainly didn't hurt the interpretation of the world as anarchicly immorally funny. Saint's Row the Third is the game your mother warned you about. It is over the top vulgar, hilarious, obscene, and fun. It's like GTA if GTA recognized that the only reason it was fun is because of the mayhem you can cause in its sandbox environment. Nearly every campaign mission is designed with this in mind, often offering you infinite ammo with explosives and early access to highly overpowered weapons of mass destruction like aircraft, UAV drone missiles, tanks, etc.. It also has a cheats function (remember those?) so you can play how you'd like to. The music soundtrack is excellent, incorporating everything from Sublime, to hip-hop, to House (courtesy of deadmau5), to metal...the radio stations are all a joy to listen to and the menu music and customization music is also enjoyable. Speaking of customization, this game caters to everyone's need to play dressup. Unlike GTA you can customize just about everything about your character - tattoos, black eyes, build, hair style - it rivals The Elder Scrolls in this regard. You can even give yourself custom taunts and celebrations, *and* pick your voice actor. The guns are upgradable and vary nicely, and you can spend your hard-earned cash not only on property but also upgrades for your character like increased health, dual-wielding, all the way up to infinite ammo. Even your cars can be upgraded and modified, want to punt 24" rims on your Prius? Go ahead! Why not add underglow and a modded engine while you're at it! I was pleasantly surprised with this game since I'm not a huge fan of sandboxes (I don't like collecting arbitrary stuff, which you can in this game too - sex dolls in fact) but the sense of humor and joking atmosphere of Saints Row easily places it as my favorite sandbox game I've yet played.
Pros:
Humor
Sountrack
Customization factor
Weapons (upgradable)
Outrageousness
Fun factor
Variable gameplay
Custscene direction
Cons:
Stupid follower AI
No real 'redeeming' factor to this game
While going around blowing stuff up and smacking people with a giant purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to a hip-hop soundtrack is fun there isn't anything deeper here. As I said, this is the game your mother warned you about, there isn't really any gaming as art here (you could be pretentious and say the over the top outrageousness is but, whatever) so there isn't any redeeming quality to this game and, as usual, follower AI is incompetent at best, but this game was a lot of fun and very relaxing. The gameplay is solid and varied (lots of cool side missions to do) and overall I had a great time. If you like sandboxes it's a must buy and even if you don't you'll still probably have a lot of fun with the campaign like I did. A-

So after playing every arma game I decided to purchase this one as soon as it was announced. I have played quite a bit of this game and in fact it is currently my favorite game. The community age group is great for the most part. The modding community is great for the most part as well, in fact the game would be nothing without  it in my opinion. Recently Bohemia Interactive has decided to take a turn and shoot themselves in the foot and screw over the modding community. They recently updated their terms saying they own the rights to every mod created in their game and have the right to claim it as their own and resell it. This in my opinion is extremely screwed up and has made a lot of developers stop their work. In fact they have actually already done this before putting this in their terms. The Kart DlC is just a direct port from an arma 2 mod and their latest release of the Official p90 mod is ripped straight from someone else. On top of this they threaten the original creators with DMCA's to take down their work because they don't want people getting the dlc for free for example. This is so wrong in so many ways. Back to the actual game though. The game itself started out development great and the ideas were amazing but it feels like the game now is being rushed, is a side project, and just a money grab. The core mechanics are quite buggy without the use of mods. The graphics (If you can run them at the highest settings) are very washed out. (this is supposed to be changed in the apex update) The optimization is god awful. I am lucky to get 60 fps and you can see my specs on my profile. The server tools are broken and not even fully explained.
- Decent Core mechanics
- Great Modding Community
- Great Concept
- Horrible Optimization (FIXED)
- Quite a bit of bugs (FIXED)
- BI has taken a turn for the worse and just wants to get money (Pretty Much Stopped ths)
Wait it out and see if they go back to their roots and improve the game. I can't fully recommend this game in good conscious at it's current state and the way the developers are taking things.

Team Fortress 2, also known as TF2, is a incredible game where you find friends (and lots of people who don't like you), play the objective (Ha, who am I kidding. no one does that!) and shoot people (Well that should be obvious). On the topic of community, I will warn you, even though its free most people will hate on you for playing the game free, and almost make you feel like you should buy stuff. All in all, I'd say its worth the space it takes up on your hard drive, and even the money you might spend on it.

I went into 'Saints Row - The Third' expecting a cheap but acceptable 'Grand Theft Auto' clone...
Being honest, the basic gameplay is almost identical: a third person sandbox shooter with driving.
But whereas GTA is meant to be serious and gritty, 'Saints Row - The Third' is just outrageous and ridiculous...which makes it far more fun to play in my opinion...what other game has you able to fight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s (who are armed with machine guns) using only a a gigantic♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
You play as a mob boss (who you can completely customise the look and voice of) and work your way to ruling the city with your gang. The storyline is engaging enough, the characters are more than interesting (even if some of them are just your standard stereotypes) and the gameplay can get crazy. There are also plenty of side missions with lots of variety to them (from simple driving quests, to beat-em up quests...even quests where you take control of a tank and just create as much mayhem as you can).
Like I said, the gameplay can get crazy. You have a large variety of weapons and vehicles, which you can also customise. As you level up and progress through the story you also gain "homies" - gang members who will follow and help you out in the world. They can be normal grunt homies who you can customise the look of, or specific characters from the storyline. You can also improve your own abilities to literally become a god character, impervious to almost all damage, infinite ammo for weapons, etc. Furthermore, the game world itself is fairly large, with plenty of collectables. It will definitely take a while to complete the game.
There is online co-op and plenty of DLC (some of which is just cosmetic, but the additional gameplay DLC's are hilarious and fun).
Overall it is definitely worth a look for any gamer, especially if you want to be entertained.

Having played a lot of Battle Royal in H1Z1 (before they split the game), I can say this game mode is pretty fun. But, it is just ONE game mode. So, ask yourself if it is worth buying a 20€ game for just ONE gamemode, a gamemode previously part of another game!?
-----
Daybreak claims that they will be adding more gamemodes, but that's yet to be seen. We don't know what gamemodes or how many will be added. Reading the early acces page they claim to add additional gamemodes and game rules. Judging the history of this game/development, I would not be supprised if they only add slight variations of the ONE gamemode Battle Royal.
Before the split, there already where 3 variants of this game mode, you had one without zombies, one with zombies and one with special rewards for winning! This last mode was behind a cash wall and you need to buy tickets for real hard cash to join this mode.
Technicly they could say they have 3 gamemodes. Then you have the same game with team of 2, or team of 5 players. So there you have it, 5 gamemodes! :P
We have to wait and see what the new gamemodes are, if any are added!
Ask yourself, knowing this, is ONE gamemode still worth 20€?
-----
Let's inform you some more, because this game has a rocky history with many claims that never became reality!
They ones claimed to NEVER add pay2win mechanics to this game, then airdrops where added to survival mode that gave you food, water, weapons and ammo! Airdrops are behind a paywall from real hard cash! Though they changed the way this works but still ...
They claimed this game would become free2play ones released. Guess what, it's 20€ with additional supply crates and cosmatic microtransactions! Even payed gamemodes like the Battle Royal variant (Green Dawn) and airdrops for ingame loot.
Again, ask yourself, is this game worth 20€, with possible new gamemodes behind cash wall, with micro transactions and many broken promises?
Then the worst part, the recent split of H1Z1 into two games.
This game, King of the Kill, was part of the original H1Z1. You had survival servers and Battle Royal servers! Now you have the survival game, 20€ and the battle royal game for another 20€! And what would happen if say a new gamemode is added to King of the Kill, which becomes very popular, will they split agian? Who knows!?
This split would not be the worst of things, if they cut the price in half. Would be fair since they cut the game in half but nope, now you pay 2x20€ for something that ones was 1x20€, for something that ones was promised to be free2play!
Also, remember you now need to pay double for microtransactions. Getting a new piece of clothing from a microtransaction was universal availible for all servers and gamemodes. Now, if you want that same piece of clothing be prepared to buy the same item twice!!!
Knowing all of this, ask yourself is ONE gamemode worth 20€?
-----
With this out of the way you might want to know if this ONE gamemode is fun and yes, I said I have lots of fun with this gamemode. So let's get into that!
You spawn with around 150 other players on a large open map. Everyone drops down from the sky with a parasute. It's now time to land as fast as you can, so you can be the first to loot weapons, ammo, backpacks and more. So you can be the first to blast others in the face.
After a few minutes a savezone is drawn on your map, because toxic fog will be released and slowly drive you towards the savezone. This mechanic is fun and usefull to drive the remaining players towards the same spot.
Though there is only ONE map it's big enough to be fun for a long time. Mainly because a lot of things are random. Not the map itself but your spawn location is random, weapon spawns are random and the savezones are random. One match ends in an urban location and another on top of the mountains.
All seems good, but there is also a lot wrong with the game and it's mechanics!
Spawning for example! You don't spawn at the same time as your enemies. It depends on your loading time, internet connection and random bad luck (sometimes the game takes 2 or 3 times longer to load). This means people with faster hardware and internet connection land faster, getting guns fasters and thus have an increased change to win!
Next problem is that hitbox detection and netcode are so random. With a bit of bad luck you can shoot somebody in the head for multiple times without them dieing. While other times you one hit kill them.
Same with the shotgun, it's spread pattern is random. So you can almost get sniped from long distance with a shotgun while other times you can't hit/kill somebody at close range! And it's all luck, or badluck depending how it ends!
On top of that there aren't many weapons and in the end it comes down to AR15 for long range, shotgun for close range. Perhaps the AK47 (though it got nerved) or if you are lucky the hunting rifle (sniper that only drops from airdrops). All the other weapons are just useless compared to the above, so bows, crossbows and pistols are ignored! You only use them if they are the first weapon you can find early game.
-----
Eventhough this gamemode is a lot of fun, even with all it's flaws, I can't recommend it to anyone! Specially knowing that this ONE gamemode was part of another game!
Perhaps if they fix the core issues (spawning, hitbox detection, etc) and add more gamemodes AND lower the price to 10€ or less, then and only then it might become worth it!
For now, it's a big NO NO. Not recommended!

Saints Row 3 (they hate it when you call it that) is definitely fun, completely ridiculous, and not as good as Saints Row 2. It's more palatable, perhaps, and the port to PC is way, way better, but it loses a bunch of the things that I liked about the second game, like:
-The mildly serious tone. The world of Saints Row 2 was dumb, but not completely insane. This game has zombies in it. Saints Row 2 did not.
-The insane character generator. Sure, Saints Row 3 lets you be a golden man with a zombie voice, but removes a lot of the sliders, clothing options, and more bananas customization options like hand-to-hand fighting style and default facial expression.
-The sprawling, varied city. More detail on individual characters and items means fewer different characters and items, and fewer distinct locations. Saints Row 2 felt like a city, while 3 feels like just part of 2.
Despite all this, 3 is great. The writing is great, some of the missions are incredible, and there's some smart gameplay changes. The DLC isn't really any good, so you can avoid it if you want, but the main game is a fun romp, especially in co-op.

I'm rewriting the recommendation in light of the DLC.  If GTAIV took all the seriousness and none of the stupid from Vice City, then Saint's Row: The Third took all the stupid and none of the seriousness.  Be ready for just about anything plot-wise.  The voice acting is fantastic, the story is ridiculous, and the gameplay is hectic.  That's not a claim I often make.  In so many games these days I feel like the combat is very deliberate, and you can plan your way through it.  SR:TT isn't like that, and actually punishes you for it.  Many times your first instinct  (kill everything) is your best one.
As for the DLCs, I had fun with Genkibowl and Gangstas in Space.  Genkibowl takes the whole activities thing to new levels of ethical violence and Gangstas in Space features some great new character additions.  I though Trouble with Clones was too serious and left too many gaping plot holes (something that saint's row has surprisingly few of) with the exception of the mission Tour de Farce, which featured you shooting bees at people and Pierce in short shorts.  That one was fun, but not worth the DLC price.
That said, you should buy this game.  It's worth your time.  NOTE: Not safe for work, kids, or arguably adults either.

This was my introduction to the Saints Row series, and I picked it out because I heard it had character customization. I've enjoyed the GTA series, so the similarities it had with that franchise also interested me.
It's pretty obvious from any trailers, or the very beginning of the game, but it's not a very serious game. It does share that with GTA, but it also exagerrates it much more than GTA does. It's not just the fact that there's an auto shop called Rim Jobs, or that there's a gang with merchandising and celebrity status, but also the fact that you can upgrade your character to the point where they can jump off a 40 story building, smack into the ground, and not take any damage.
Like I said, I was sold from the moment I found out there was character customization, so I didn't really have any other expectations for the gameplay. It's a really fun game, though. The combat is smooth and easy to use. Missions can be difficult, but not in a frustrating way. I liked all the characters, and the collectables were easy enough to track down that I was willing to find them all, which I never did with GTA IV.
If you like GTA, give this game a shot. If you like silly games, character customization, third person shooters, and/or sandbox games, then those aspects might be worth checking out in this game, too.

This was my introduction to the Saints Row series, and I picked it out because I heard it had character customization. I've enjoyed the GTA series, so the similarities it had with that franchise also interested me.
It's pretty obvious from any trailers, or the very beginning of the game, but it's not a very serious game. It does share that with GTA, but it also exagerrates it much more than GTA does. It's not just the fact that there's an auto shop called Rim Jobs, or that there's a gang with merchandising and celebrity status, but also the fact that you can upgrade your character to the point where they can jump off a 40 story building, smack into the ground, and not take any damage.
Like I said, I was sold from the moment I found out there was character customization, so I didn't really have any other expectations for the gameplay. It's a really fun game, though. The combat is smooth and easy to use. Missions can be difficult, but not in a frustrating way. I liked all the characters, and the collectables were easy enough to track down that I was willing to find them all, which I never did with GTA IV.
If you like GTA, give this game a shot. If you like silly games, character customization, third person shooters, and/or sandbox games, then those aspects might be worth checking out in this game, too.

H1z1 has a pretty bad reputation for being extremely buggy and filled with hackers and cheaters. However, recently Daybreak has taken the initiative and is rolling out lots of updates relatively frequently which keep me coming back again and again. Obviously, no game is perfect and there are still issues and bugs such as hitreg, desinc, and reload bugs. Overall, I would recommend this game because it is a very fast pace, arcade style BR game in which you can jump in and play for hours. The skill floor is relatively low due to how straightforward the game is; but there is a huge skill ceiling, which players can always strive for. If you prefer faster paced and more chaotic BR experience buy H1z1 kotk. If you prefer more tactical camping-style BR experience, buy PUBG. Personally, I prefer KOTK and will stick to playing this game.

A fair warning to any new players to this game; prepare to be crushed relentlessly. Team Fortress 2 is a very hard game to get into initially, and the community does not really help that much either, with how much they hate new "Free-to-play" players. I would recommend going to Youtube to look up some basic guides on how to get started in the game, particularly from a gentleman by the name of MrPaladin.
Once you overcome that enormous barrier to entry, however, you have one of the most rewarding multiplayer games out there in terms of skill ceilings and teamwork. You feel great when you finally destroy those 5 engineers turtling on Dustbowl on last. It is satisfying when you go on a godlike killstreak with a Direct Hit, etc. The amount of different mechanics to master requires thousands of hours just to grasp at, and I myself am still just a below average player. But that's what keeps this game consistantly at the most played games on Steam; the neverending quest to get better and better at the game.
I would not reccomend this game to anyone who does not want to put in time to get good at a game, as this game demands it in spades. However, if you want to play a refreshingly different and fun fps to what the "Triple A Games Industry" offers, give it a go. Just make sure you do your research on how to play, and for god's sake, don't waste your money on the Mann Co Store.

Ill admit it, I am an arma noob. I recently picked up the game and decided to get to grips with the mechanics. After trying to rush enemies and getting destroyed instantly I looked up a guide. I played a bit more and decided to try out the multiplayer. God damn that was a good idea. I joined an invade and anex server, modified my soldier and set off to take a town with around 10 other players. They were really kind and showed my the ropes of the game. After some small skirmishes we had pushed up to a church by a forest. We held off there until one squad member went down. "3 tanks direct south of our position" I checked my compass and found 3 tanks rolling out of the forest. We were slaughtered, but I managed to survive. I soon realised I was the last one left. I hid in the grass and let the enemies pass. I them dragged some squad members into the church and revived them. Soon after we had the whole squad up. And we were behind the enemie forces. What followed was the best gaming moment of my life. A charge behind the tanks, followed by some explosive charges, brought the hostile assault to its knees. Our squad was hailed by the other players for saving them.
10/10 would save everyone again.

HONEST REVIEW FOR H1Z1 KOTK.
Ok. Ignore literally all of the reviews calling this game buggy. it is a early accses game and bugs are expected. though I have ran into my own few game breaking and round ending bugs this game is incredibily enjoyable in my opinion. Its a nice relaxed, chaotic, massive, online battle. There could be more guns and variety in the game but overall I think that the guns given are good enough. I also wouldl like to see more use to pistols by maybe making rifles more rare since rifles are super easy to find making things like pistols and bows super irrelevent. Your weapon list will almost always be filled with a ar, ak, and a shotgun. But that doesnt mean this game doesnt have enough, personally this game makes up for its lack of content in its variety in the way the game can turn out. The gas is also a interesting way to push players into the same area after a certain amount of time. but I do think that the map and compass system in the top right was way to confusing and made me get killed by the gas multiple times because I didnt know where I was going. not sure if that was just me or not.
FINAL VERDICT - This game may have some bugs and a little less content then Id like, but that doesnt mean its a blast. And for 20$ i could ask for much more. If you catch this game on sale Id more than reccomend it and if you like open world, survival, fun, shooters. Id highly reccomend you to buy this game at full price like I did.

This is, in many ways, what most of us have wanted GTA to be ever since GTA3. Whereas GTA itself has gone all gritty and real with GTA4, Saints Row picked up the lunacy of San Andreas, stuffed it into a rocket dressed like Elvis and blasted off to adventure. Starts at absurd and escalates from there. If you've played GTA, you know what to expect in gameplay, but the weapons are nicely detailed and well-planned and just feel pretty good. Late-game weapons are hilariously destructive. Your character is extremely customizable, and you can even create an account on the Saints Row website to upload and download characters. Car customization is pleasantly robust, and you can use your modded cars all you want and just respawn them later when you blow them up. Good soundtrack; writing is pretty hilarious and includes very likeable characters. A little buggy, but not too bad. My biggest complaint is that the story is a bit on the short side and sadly can't be repeated in the same save, where it really seems like this game should have a New Game + feature; that aside, this is overall a very well stuctured and cathartic GTA-alike. Oh yeah, also, you can do anything multiplayer. Anything!

I may be a bit late to the party on this one, but I'm not about to pass up a chance to talk about this game. Let me start off by saying that in terms of gameplay and mechanics, the Saints Row series is very similar to Grand Theft Auto, a series which I personally have never really been a fan of. But stealing cars and running over ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s isn't what makes this game fun; it's the sheer level of ridiculousness that encompasses, well, every damn thing about this game. Whereas GTA tries to keep things realistic and serious to a degree, SR3 tosses that aside in favor of laser shotguns, deadly game shows and a giant weaponized purple phallus. And that's just the beginning. Everything about this game had me both laughing out loud and awkwardly covering my screen whenever the family was around. And the game isn't all about being outrageously insane; there's an interesting storyline, and a world with lots to explore. Add on some fun side missions and a ton of hilarious minigames (such as driving a tiger around town or running in front of cars to claim insurance money), and the result is the most awkward fun you can have.

'Twas the night before christmas in 2012, and I was bored out of my mind. I found the christmas steam sale, that I had been unaware of, and saw Saints Row The Third on sale. I thought it looked fun and decided to buy it.
Oh how that night became a blast. As I didn't know what I was getting my self into, except some game that seemed to be similar to GTA, boy did that game knock me of my chair. Beginning with a robbery where the Saints use a huge mask in the likeness of Gat, where they even decide to steal the whole vault, while the forces who try to stop them even asks for their autographs.
After the first mission, I got to create the Saints boss (the player character) however I wanted, so being a pervert like I am, obviously I went with a hot female boss with maxed out "Sex appeal" (which means huge breasts) voiced by Laura Bailey. But if you like guys, you can of course make a male boss, also with maxed "Sex appeal" (so a huge package), if that's your thing.
I don't want to spoil much more of the game, but I'm amazed at after that, they just kept on doing more and more insane crazy stuff with amazing humor to go with it all. And to me it felt even more hilarious hearing the boss voiced by Laura Bailey as I had heard her voice other game characters that can be considered more "prude" if I may say so.
So in the end I spent most of that night before christmas, and the days after chrismas having an incredible blast with the game. Whether it was doing random extra missions like insurance fraud missions (where you try to get hurt as much as possible), or the amazing story missions, the game kept me smiling for a long time.
If you like humor, I would definitely recommend this brilliant game. Or if you like sandbox like games, I would also recommend this. Or if you're just bored like I was, give it a shot, and you might have one of the best times of your life.
10/10 - from a guy who was bored as hell the night before christmas 2012.

ARMA gameplay is so different and less homogenized than the other shooter games out there such as CS;GO, Battlefield, and other modern-day gunfighting games. It's a game for thinkers and tacticians. It's a game for people who are patient and who enjoy executing a well thought-out plan.
Let's get right down to the basics; ARMA at it's core is all about combined arms gameplay, meaning that compositions of infantrymen, motorized and mechanized vehicles, helicopters, support units, and CAS are all conducted in unison to perform a common goal depending on the scenario. You can charge a factory inhabited with militants with a large column of unstoppable tanks in an organized attack, or you can complete similar objectives with a small team of 4 during a night mission.
The shooting is not like your classic FPS with head-tracking and ray tracing. With the massive scale of ARMA comes realism, and bullet drop, stamina, and ammunition type all change the dynamics of your weapon. Different calibers have different 'feels' to them, and equipping the proper gear for an operation is like choosing the right cameras, lights and crew for a movie set. You need proper scopes that are for your chambered caliber, you need to learn how to zero in your sights, and how to ultimately master long-range marksmanship. The shooting reintroduces the aspect of skill-based combat.
Vehicles don't feel very optimal, but they do the job and they function as they are supposed to. Vehicles for each faction feel different, and they all serve a purpose, whether it's transporting ammunition and gasoline to the front lines, or conducting artillery fire missions on far away targets. The helicopter flight modules are very realistic and fun to use especially as an experienced flyer, and doing gun runs with a stealth A-10 feels even better.
The AI in the game is terrible especially when in a combined arms group. Commanding feels clunky and annoying, and your AI teammates make remarkably bad decisions and don't stick to formation under certain circumstances. That's why you need to play this game
Having more players in a mission with you is quite literally a fun multiplier. Picking roles and cooperation are the best parts of the game.
Altis and Stratis look fantastic and the architecture and design make you feel like you are in a genuinely mediterranean location. The water is fresh and blue, and the trees shimmer in the sunlight as they are supposed to. The ground is home to a lot of detail, with rocks you can use as cover, seastacks obscuring different locations, and ruins with plenty to discover. The modelling is fantastic and the weapons are crisp and sound spectacular. The only issue is that this game runs surprisingly bad, utilizing only two cores of your processor (or something like that), meaning that you would have to play on medium to low settings if you have a lower-end system.
It's♥♥♥♥♥♥unless you're playing with friends. Zeus is a fantastic addon with on-the-fly mission creation, but I wouldn't think about playing it in public even once. Battle Royale is overhyped, island life is boring and requires too many mods. MILSIM is fantastic but as always there are good groups and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ groups out there.
Overall it's a fun game and you get a lot for your money.

Borrowing elements of other open-world games, Saints Row: The Third provides an alternative, outrageous style which does enough to feel fresh, is designed well and easily one of the top of the genre. While it will not displace the familiar Grand Theft Auto series, it provides a more laissez-faire approach which will no doubt feel en vogue to more casual players.
The game handles solidly, and has enough fluidity in controls in comparison to similar console ports. Co-op mode is adequate with mild connectivity issues, but one gets the same experience from playing a single player campaign.
Missions are diverse, and the environment of Steelport is well modeled with much possibility to explore. The plot, while borders on preposterous, fits well with the general theme and climaxes into a lightning-quick dénouement.
Overall a dashingly divergent piece, ranging anywhere from capricious to whimsical, but most players would enjoy it nonetheless.  A game that certainly adds to the notion that open world action-adventure games are á la mode.

This game is a good game. Everything that I like about it is good, and the feel of the game is, overall, very neat and well done.
I, however, do not like this game. Don't get me wrong, this game is a pretty good game! It has everything it needs to be a game. I just believe that this game is no where near as good as it could have been, and it is no where near where it needs to be to live up to what Saints Row 2 brought us.
Saints Row, as a series, has always been really interesting. Starting off as a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ GTA clone, and then becoming something that was so much better than that, it has evolved again into something that seems to be lacking in a lot of the things 2 brought us. The characters are way less likable, the quality of the game feels cheaper, and it just feels way more empty than 2 ever did.
I think the worst part of the game is the way THQ decided to ♥♥♥♥♥ it out. I know that THQ is failing as a company, and I would have been okay with one or two DLC packs. THQ decided that 500 billion DLC packs was more than okay, and bascially tore apart the game, segmenting huge chunks of it. Stuff that should have been a part of the game to begin with, obvious stuff. No, I don't want to buy the ability to put in cheat codes you huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. And the whole Clones DLC bit, that was fun, but they botched that up too. The powers you get at the end? Those would have been super fun to hold on to.
I really dislike a lot of the characters that 3 introduced, or reintroduced. Even Johnny Gat, one of my favorite characters, was completely removed due to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ circumstances. A schedualing conflict, at best. The conclusion to that was to kill off the character. I think the only character that improved at all was Pierce. Pierce actually became a decent character. The nerd girl was okay too, but not very memorable.
All in all, I won't put in as many hours into this game as I put into Saints Row 2. It just doesn't have the same feel, even if the game is 'better,' in a sense that it has better tech behind it. 2 was so good, and 3 can never match up to it. I thought it was just nostalga at first, but I went back and played through 2, and I can easily conclude that it isn't at all rose-tinted glasses. 2 had its share of problems. 3 is just...not even there.
I can only hope that Saints Row 4 will be to 3 what Saints Row 2 was to 1.

This game is not GTA. It doesn't try to be realistic or polished to perfection. It's a trigger-happy, gung-ho, arcade-ish shooter backed by high testosterone levels (I'm guessing one of the game developers is kinky), acceptable oldskool bugs (that form part of the gameplay frustration in terms of difficulty) and an insane amount of movie parodies right till the very end. lol, "2 days till retirement." The more of a movie buff you are the more you'll find this game hilarious. Like there's a plane called "Snipes 57". LOL, seriously! Volition may have even parodied some other games, like the sky diving sequence from Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II.
There's even a cameo appearance by Burt ♥♥♥♥ING Reynolds! Yup. The real deal! And for wrestling fans there is Rob Van Dam and Hulk Hogan doing the voice for the commentator characters. I bought this game for $9.99 on steam. It was worth it. But the Humble Bundle was just a complete steal!

The game is decent in it's own. But most of the fun lies in user created content.
One of the few games where in 1 moment you can be cutting reporters heads off as ISIS, the next bombing a school as an American drone operator. Amazing!
There are hundreds community game modes: role play, role play as ISIS, roleplay as Nazis, roleplay as real military. There are also a few min to modes like capture the island, capture the flag and such.
There are hundreds of communities that make and play new scenarios every week. That's where a lot of the fun is, now with the new ZEUS game master, which allows to craft a scenario in minutes, be God, pretty much dungeon master and craft the experience for other players.
All of this complimented by decent visuals, huge immersive terrains, which scale into real life size, not like wildlands, where it feels compressed and unrealistic there are also community made terrains and you can play on the terrains from previous Arma titles.
But it's not all sunshine and flowers, the games biggest strength is also it's biggest weakness. For example there is no furniture in any of the buildings. They expect people to make their own scenarios and place down furniture, this is ok, because the game requires a good pic to run any decent. Having furniture would make the game run a lot worse, so it makes sense, but thankfully the modding scene for this game is huge and there's a mod, which adds furniture. There are anime mods, star wars, mech, Nazi, ISIS and even Vietnam mods.
All the mods make this game amazing and allow ISIS to train their troops.
All of that makes this unique and never ending experience, and a lot of the mods have ended up making their own games like Dean hallway made zombie panic after making Amos for this game. And then player unknown aka. Brennan heart made his mod into a game called fortnight battlegrounds to death fight

I tend to have a hard time being a bad guy in video games. Whenever there is a choice between doing something moral and something immoral I tend to go with the first, because it helps my feeling of immersion: my character is acting close to the way I imagine I would in similar, far-fetched circumstances. (Even if in reality I’m more likely to hide under the bed hoping the problem will go away.) My aspirations to Heroism and being a Good Guy hold true even if the character I’m being handed is a morally dubious anti-hero, like Niko Bellic from Grand Theft Auto IV. Though the world of GTA IV is that of a gangster movie and definitely larger than life, there still is a kind of grittiness and realism to it. Because of that, I felt bad if my car swerved and accidentally hit an innocent bystander. For the rest of the time, you were mostly killing other criminals so the violence was justified. Sort of. However, any semblance of virtual morality went straight out the window while I was playing Saint’s Row: The Third.
Saint’s Row: The Third is not surprisingly the third installment of a franchise, one which ran parallel to GTA for a while: in both series you play a gangster in a big, sprawling city that is your playground and you can engage in various criminal activities all over the place to your heart’s content. There is a storyline running through the main missions and there are optional activities that can also be played separately from the story as mini-challenges trying to beat your own initial score and to evolve your character while gaining assets. Most GTA games were somewhat serious even if they cracked more of a smile during the San Andreas and The Ballad of Gay Tony incarnations. Saint’s Row started out serious, got goofy in the second installment and in its third outing has cut ties with reality completely and exploded into an ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic celebration of absurdity. The game is crass, juvenile and a whole lot of fleeting fun.
It starts at full speed with a spectacular bank heist gone wrong, then sees you skydiving through the length of a plummeting plane and have a gunfight in midair while holding a teammate who is cussing you out for being an inconsiderate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It plays like a parody on action movies. The story boiled down: you want to take over the city of Steelport with your gang and are eliminating competition while fighting the authorities who are trying to take you down. Absolutely no one cares about collateral damage, be it to property or civilians. To call the main concept a story – with a proper beginning, middle and end – is actually giving it too much credit; it’s more like a series of ludicrous vignettes strung together tenuously. Consequences of plot don’t impact your free-reign activities all that much. Early on you get a penthouse for you and your homies, which is later besieged and blown up. However, it is magically restored once the mission in question ends and you can still go out on the town without getting instantly apprehended.
As if the situations you end up in aren’t silly enough as-is, the game encourages you to keep pimping your character to look as odd as possible, making the cutscenes he is placed in look even more crazy. For most of the game, my counterpart was a shirtless, black muscleman with a big dragon tattoo on his chest, runny mascara under his eyes and an odd hat. He proved he could maintain a good sprint while in high heels and carrying a rocket launcher. (...)

That's not h1z1 fault, but I bet you that this connection is making my loading screens longer than necessary and laggy when I need my FPS the most.
I use super-low graphic settings (I'm not spoiled, it is a laptop, not a super-laptop) but the game servers always has the final say in rendering other opponents on long distances. You can set the grass to render at 500, but the opponents will be visible no matter what distance they're at.
I would also like to point out that every online-game has issues with built-in features on windows, like xbox app and other "capturing" devices. They "eat up" both cpu, memory and internet speed. I'm just saying that after tweaking windows to NOT interrupt or bother at all, this game runs perfectly on my 2013 laptop. I believe I have 8 gb ram but only 4 gb can be used before the laptop crashes (no matter what game). The cpu is actually overclocking itself on 2.3, so to be fair it's only at 1.83 ghz. My harddrive is ... well.. My new 1TB extension/backup harddrive writes and reads faster than this laptop can move it's own mouse across the desktop. So the built in harddrive is really not optimal. Saints Row 3 is a sandbox third-person shooter, in the style of GTA. However, where GTA has become more serious and realistic, Saints Row 3 is ridiculous and, at times, completely insane. Sexual content and violence is not only common in Steelport, it's completely normal. It's true that the humor is a bit juvenile, but they take it to such extremes that I couldn't help but laugh at how silly the whole thing is.
I loved this game. I found that most of the game's mechanics were a lot of fun. There were some amazing main missions, and the side activies were enjoyable (I loved the Genki ones). One downside is that a lot of the guns suck. Instead, I used the basic pistol until the endgame for its accuracy. The controls and camera are fine. The story is stupid but it works. The varied music appeals to many tastes. There's lots of character customization, which I am grateful for.
SR3 requires the stomach for sex and violence, but if you're okay with that, this game is really fun and can keep you busy for quite a while. It's a great co-op game. Get the DLC if the price drops; Genkibowl and Special Ops Vehicle Pack are my top picks.

Who, even among scholars in the field, could keep up with the flood of attacks on Pius XII that began in the late 1990s? John Cornwell gave us Hitler’s Pope , and Michael Phayer followed with The Catholic Church and the Holocaust . David Kertzer brought charges against Pius XII in The Popes Against the Jews , and Susan Zuccotti reversed her previous scholarship to pen Under His Very Windows: The Vatican and the Holocaust in Italy . Garry Wills used Pius as the centerpiece for his reformist Papal Sin , as did James Carroll in Constantine’s Sword . So, for that matter, did Daniel Goldhagen when he wrote what proved to be the most extended and straightforward assault on Catholicism in decades: A Moral Reckoning: The Role of the Catholic Church in the Holocaust and Its Unfulfilled Duty of Repair .
Meanwhile, the essays and occasional pieces were collected in such volumes as Holocaust Scholars Write to the Vatican , and The Holocaust and the Christian World , and The Vatican and the Holocaust , and Pope Pius XII and the Holocaust , and Christian Responses to the Holocaust ”and on, and on, until we seemed to be facing what the exasperated reviewer John Pawlikowski called “a virtual book-of-the-month club on institutional Catholicism, anti-Semitism, and the Holocaust.”
The champions of Pius had their share of book-length innings as well”although, one might note, never from the same level of popular publisher as the attackers managed to find. In 1999 Pierre Blet produced Pius XII and the Second World War According to the Archives of the Vatican and got Paulist Press, a respectable but small Catholic house, to publish it in America. Ronald Rychlak finished his first-rate Hitler, the War, and the Pope , and the hardback was brought out by a press in Columbia, Missouri, known mostly for printing romance novels. For the paperback edition, Rychlak’s work was picked up by the book-publishing arm of the Catholic newspaper Our Sunday Visitor .
Those are both fine presses in their way, and Rychlak has done well for them. But one can reasonably point out that Our Sunday Visitor is not quite at the level of distribution, advertising, and influence enjoyed by Doubleday, Houghton Mifflin, Knopf, and Viking”the large houses that issued the books against Pius. The commentator Philip Jenkins recently suggested that this disparity in publishers sends a message that the mainstream view is the guilt of Pius XII, while praise for the Pope belongs only to the cranks, nuts, and sectarians.
Jenkins’ suggestion is worth considering. Still, no one can say Pius’ supporters were squashed or censored. In just six years, Margherita Marchione managed five books in praise of the Pope. The Thomistic philosopher and novelist Ralph McInerny, aggravated by the deluge of attacks, issued a splenetic volume called The Defamation of Pope Pius XII , while Justus George Lawler (a writer best known in Catholic circles for his liberalism) penned a witty evisceration of Pius’ critics called Popes and Politics: Reform, Resentment, and the Holocaust . José Sánchez added Pope Pius XII and the Holocaust , and a slew of German and Italian books might be mentioned as well, prompted, for the most part, by the popular visibility of the English-language criticisms even in Europe.
But it was primarily in book reviews and responses that the defenders of Pius XII fought out the war”which is something of a problem. Every pope precipitates biographies, hagiographies, and maledictions, like the dropping of the rain; it is part of the job to be much written about, and the works on Eugenio Pacelli that began to appear when he became pope in 1939 seem innumerable. But no supporter has yet produced a book-length biography in the wake of the recent years of extended blame. Even Rychlak’s Hitler, the War, and the Pope was essentially reactive, devoting a thirty-page epilogue to a catalogue of the errors in Cornwell’s book.
We have seen this pattern before. Rolf Hochhuth’s play The Deputy premiered in Berlin in 1963, and its picture of a greedy pope, concerned only about Vatican finances and silent about the Holocaust, immediately caused a firestorm of comment from the intellectual world. Everyone who was anyone felt compelled to weigh in.
Hochhuth himself faded away when he tried to extend his censure to Winston Churchill, penning a play in 1967 that claimed Churchill had ordered the murder of the Polish General Wladyslaw Sikorski and, later, the murder of the pilot who had crashed Sikorski’s plane. Unbeknownst to Hochhuth, the pilot was, in fact, still alive, and he won a libel judgment that badly damaged the London theater which had staged the play. Thereafter, Hochhuth found it harder to get a hearing”although, interestingly, the current notoriety of Pius XII seems to have resurrected the playwright to some degree, and in 2002 the Greek filmmaker Constantin Costa-Gravas released a movie version of The Deputy with the English title Amen (or Eyewitness , in other copies).
Even without Hochhuth, the wide discussion about Pius XII he initiated in 1963 went on for several years. It produced some overheated journalistic attempts to cash in on the public interest, such as Robert Katz’ Black Sabbath and Death in Rome (the latter being the target of a successful libel suit, this time brought by Pius XII’s niece, Countess Elena Pacelli Rossignani). But the era brought forth as well three more serious and scholarly”indeed, by today’s standards, quite moderate and thoughtful”attacks: Guenter Lewy’s The Catholic Church and Nazi Germany (1964), Carlo Falconi’s The Silence of Pius XII (1965), and Saul Friedlander’s Pius XII and the Third Reich: A Documentation (1966).
The brouhaha also prompted the Vatican to begin releasing material from Pius’ pontificate, which appeared from 1965 to 1981 as the eleven-volume series Actes et Documents . In part by relying on these new documents, but even more by simply gathering their forces and investigating each of the incidents taken as the core of the indictment, the defenders gradually tamped down The Deputy ’s claims about Pius XII and the Holocaust. Pope John Paul II was a consistent advocate for his predecessor, and even once-popular notions about Pius”that he was, for instance, the great reactionary opponent against whom Vatican II turned”gradually seemed to lose steam by the late 1970s and early ’80s. It took more than a decade, but the reactive reviewers appeared to carry the day, and the popular magazine press and major book publishers lost interest.
A few commentators noted that the whole thing hadn’t entirely died. The historian Michael Tagliacozzo said he kept an open file labeled “Calumnies Against Pius XII.” But most were unprepared when the criticism began again in the late 1990s. To journalists and cultural commentators, Hitler’s Pope seemed almost to come out of nowhere in 1999, and it received almost entirely ecstatic reviews when it first appeared. A few skeptical journalists who remembered the Hochhuth battles” Newsweek ’s Kenneth Woodward and the New York Times ’ Peter Steinfels, notably”doubted Cornwell’s conclusions, but it had been years since they had investigated the topic, and they were unprepared to provide details about the book’s errors.
Time was needed for scholars to gin up the machine again, double-check the claims in Hitler’s Pope , and publish the reviews. Some of the results proved deeply embarrassing for Cornwell, particularly the falsity of his boast that he had spent “months on end” in the archives, when he visited the Vatican for only three weeks and didn’t go to the archives every day of that. The Italian letter from Pacelli that Cornwell placed at the center of his book as evidence of deep anti-Semitism had been, he claimed, waiting secretly “like a time bomb” until he did his research.

So I decide to join an Arma 3 Altis Life server cause ya know, for funs and such. I join in, get some free money that they give you in the bank to start off, and begin to walk out of said bank when I see around 3 guys in masks with full on assault rifles run in...♥♥♥♥♥♥ So I proceed to run away from them further into the bank, and around 3 minutes later they fish my♥♥♥♥♥out of there, and say that they won't kill me, but only if I join them. If not, they'll rob me and take me as hostage. Well considering such an offer, money or death, I thought to myself, eh. ♥♥♥♥ it. 2 hours later I'm one of them. We end up high-jacking a lamborghini looking car, and decide to sell it to this one guy who put in a request for one. We sell it to him, then proceed to mug him and rob him entirely for around 25K, then drug him, kidnap him, take his clothes and then leave him naked in the middle of a giant forest, with both legs shot out, DayZ style. All is well until about 2 hours later and the same dude comes in with a group of 4 more bodyguards, shoot us up in a drive by, rob us for all we've got as we're dying, and then leave us to die on the side of a road. All this within the time lapse of about 4 hours.
If you hadn't already guessed, this game is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome. The game is VERY realistic, and it takes actual brains and game-sense to know how to win a Battle Royale. It's not like a game like H1Z1 where you can just get a lucky spawn, get some weapons, and call it GG. Instead, the game is made for a more realistic approach, to where a guy who knows how to use a very small and weak pistol can outsmart and beat a guy with one of the more stronger AR's in the game. Teamwork is crucial in a game like this, so when you do operations with other players, you have to make sure to communicate with one another. Give callouts, provide cover fire if a teammate is running to a more advantageous point or trying to advance on an objective or such. See a teammate who's gotten his leg shot out and is crawling on the floor unable to walk? Go and heal em if you have a med-kit, as you pretty much can't Lone-Wolf this sort of game, unless you're a sniper, and even then it's difficult to get around without getting killed if you aren't the best at stealthing people, as you won't be able to face them head on with said sniper rifle.
The mods in this game are also very good. They range from adding new guns, vehicles, enemy / teammate types, either new or from previous games, all the way to adding a full on Zombie Survival mod with multiple working servers, and constant updates and support. It's funny because the Dayz Mod for Arma 3 is actually better than DayZ standalone itself.
My main issue with the game would probably be performance wise. Bohemia Interactive has been known for not being the best at making the Arma series very clean to run, and as such, you see people on 980Ti's sometimes be on the low 50's to 60's in terms of FPS. But if you have the computer that can handle it, then you'll be able to run it without having to worry about this issue.
TL;DR - I give this game a drugged and kidnapped pedestrian out of 10. The gameplays the best I've seen out of any shooter ever. ( Battlefield 4 is for men? This game makes those players look like the CoD group. ) The players are around 95 percent super friendly and awesome ( the 5 percent is from that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you always find in pretty much any game ever ) , the graphics ( if you can run em ) are REALLY good looking, but as mentioned, are pretty heavy to run, and if you ever get tired from running player made operations with friends, then mods will keep you playing for a loooooong time.
In all seriousness, get this game. If you're into TRUE tactical shooters that take actual skill, logic, and game-sense to play and not just "Who has the most OP gun", then this game is for you.

Here is my favourite stir fry recipe:
Ingredients
1/2	 bunch of	 fresh coriander
3	 cloves of	 garlic
1	 thumb-sized piece of	 fresh ginger
1	 bunch of	 spring onions
1	 fresh red chilli
1	 lime
2	 carrots
1	 head of	 broccoli
2	 higher-welfare skinless chicken breasts
250	 g	 medium free-range egg noodles
50	 g	 unsalted cashew nuts
vegetable oil
freshly ground black pepper
1-2	 tablespoons	 low-salt soy sauce
1	 tablespoon	 fish sauce
Method
1.Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stalks, then keep aside for later. Peel and finely slice the garlic, then peel and matchstick the ginger. Trim and finely slice the spring onions, deseed and finely slice the chilli and cut the lime into wedges. Trim, peel and thinly slice the carrots at an angle.
2. Cut the broccoli into small florets, then finely shred the stalk, discarding any gnarly bits. Cut the chicken into 1cm strips. Cook the noodles according to packet instructions, then drain and refresh under cold water. Drain again, toss in a little oil and put to one side. Lightly toast the cashew nuts in a non-stick frying pan until golden, then tip onto a plate to cool.
3. Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok. Season the chicken with a pinch of pepper, then add to the pan and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, or until golden. Add the coriander stalks, garlic and ginger and cook for a further minute.
4. Next, add the spring onions, carrots and broccoli and stir-fry for a further 2 minutes, then add the cooked noodles. Keep stir-frying until the noodles are warm and the chicken is cooked through. Stir through the soy and fish sauces, then remove from the heat.
5. Divide between bowls, sprinkle over the nuts, sliced chilli and the reserved coriander leaves, then serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

Be aware - if yoy are a CoD or BF fan and in looking for casual, easy game to play with a beer - ARMA 3 is not for you. But if you wanna play a serious game where you have to think and work hard - make sure to check it out.
