Here we have a game with rough animations, terrible performance problems, AI issues, overpriced DLC, a massive learning curve, and glitches out the bum.
Yet it very well could be my favorite game right now.
It goes to show how much can be overlooked and forgiven when you have a game as broad and huge as this. There's a fully 3D editor that has so much depth and complexity that you can spend hundreds of hours tinkering with it to create a perfect mission. There are tons of weapons and vehicles, and with mods you can have an absolutely MASSIVE library of military hardware to play around with (I'm talking literally hundreds of guns, all of which can be customized with different sights, suppressors, attachments, and ammo types). There are tons of different game modes to play online, from slow-burning and long-lasting games like Altis Life to shorter, confined experiences like the absolutely fantastic and thrilling Battle Royale. The campaign is pretty neat, too, but it's really more of an afterthought and not really important to the main package.
This is a game that has hundreds, maybe even thousands of hours of content available. Paired with a broad selection of mods, you can easily sink over a thousand hours into this game. As of this review, I'm 503 hours in, and I'm still learning new things to try. There's so much I want to do that I have no doubts I'll be over a thousand hours in before I stop playing.
ArmA 3 is a very flawed title with a lot of glaring, potentially unfixable problems. But the continued and dedicated support of the dev combined with a thriving mod community and a massive amount of content out of the box makes this an easy $60 purchase. It's absolutely worth trying out if you're willing to put time and effort into a proper military simulator like this.

Welp, I quess it is my time to make an review of this... This is going to be pretty hard one...
Anyway, where to begin...
When I first time played tf2, it was on xbox 360 console with orange box, but later I realised that console version will never receive any updates like what PC version did.
So after some years later when I got myself proper PC or just very cheap laptop firstly, I couldn't get tf2 because PC disc version weren't no longer in stores and I couldn't before be able get money on steam wallet, but until when the Medic update came, so did tf2 become f2p, I was pretty excited to be able to play it, I did tutorial (it wasn't covering all the classes and stuff.) and went training against bots.
Some days later, I decided to jump in actual multiplayer action and I was having good times in there, then I got myself my first hat, but never wearing that one ever again, except when fooling someone being pretty new to game and dominating them.
Later I found out the way to get money to wallet and I started to do what other usually did when getting crates and others, eventually I got bored with casual mode and went for community servers, after searching and checking most of server, I ended up in mario kart where I eventually got new friends in there.
Also, when I first time got chance to play Scream Fortress, my first time were actually pretty good since the entire server decided to co-op to take down the merasmus and enjoy the loot and no one were troll killing anyone on treasure island.
Some months or so later, I have become well known to that server and having good times with new friends, until new mvm update came by and we decided to play it a while, until I became an "veteran money grabber" player in it, then the some mvm updates later, I became an "Veteran Dosh Medic" or so.
I can't remember that much what happened, so let's put it like this.
Some of my friends started to stop playing tf2 and tf2 started to have CS:GO updates in it, when eventually even I decided to make an promise that if I ever uncrate an unusual if future updates are the same CS:GO stuff and there weren't any major update like "meat your match", even it was pretty terrible update, but it was major and it got balanced out later on and they promised to give two new class updates with actually new weapons with stats and not reskinned or repainted ones, but it takes longer to arrive due to the lack of developers working on the update, but they did give an list of changes and banned lots of hackers, sure hackers are not caring if they banned their account and are making new ones, but it was biggest ban wave ever before.
Now, the reason why I still play this even there is pretty much reason to it, but it isn't just those new weapons updates that are on progress, tf2 has that certain charm that keeps me coming back, but I'm usually now playing in 2 "major" community servers, one for fun one for competive fun and sometimes playing with group on mvm whenever they decided to do some and I rarely play this game longer than 4 hour or even less.
So... Is this game worth in your attention, after some terrible updates and perhaps not yet mentioned, terrible player group? (I mean those kinds that are pretty aggressive towards new players and toxic in certain community)
It actually depends on your interest in this game and understanding in team based shooter, where every classes has advantages and weaknesses, also if you don't care if some player are complaining on something about you and it could be anything what they can find from you.
Well, I say give it an try since it is free and then decide is it worth your time.
Quick note to other who are reading this and knows more of what is going on tf2 or other, I'm only telling my personal experience and what I know from this game and I pretty much understand that there are lots of things what I'm leaving out from this review.
I also wish there is an maybe button rather than yes or no, I chose yes, because it being free to try it out, but it is still close to maybe.
Welp, that's all for now.

Here we have a game with rough animations, terrible performance problems, AI issues, overpriced DLC, a massive learning curve, and glitches out the bum.
Yet it very well could be my favorite game right now.
It goes to show how much can be overlooked and forgiven when you have a game as broad and huge as this. There's a fully 3D editor that has so much depth and complexity that you can spend hundreds of hours tinkering with it to create a perfect mission. There are tons of weapons and vehicles, and with mods you can have an absolutely MASSIVE library of military hardware to play around with (I'm talking literally hundreds of guns, all of which can be customized with different sights, suppressors, attachments, and ammo types). There are tons of different game modes to play online, from slow-burning and long-lasting games like Altis Life to shorter, confined experiences like the absolutely fantastic and thrilling Battle Royale. The campaign is pretty neat, too, but it's really more of an afterthought and not really important to the main package.
This is a game that has hundreds, maybe even thousands of hours of content available. Paired with a broad selection of mods, you can easily sink over a thousand hours into this game. As of this review, I'm 503 hours in, and I'm still learning new things to try. There's so much I want to do that I have no doubts I'll be over a thousand hours in before I stop playing.
ArmA 3 is a very flawed title with a lot of glaring, potentially unfixable problems. But the continued and dedicated support of the dev combined with a thriving mod community and a massive amount of content out of the box makes this an easy $60 purchase. It's absolutely worth trying out if you're willing to put time and effort into a proper military simulator like this.

Why buy Saints Row: The Third? Character customization. Chaos. Hilarious dialogue and story. The goofy side of GTA, without any seriousness. A nice-looking UI. All that backed up by a game in which you shoot people.
If you had to guess what the story of a crime-focused open-world video game would be, you'd probably say "a guy is trying to get out of the crime business but gets pulled back in and has to work his way to the top." Not the case in SR3. You're at the top almost from the beginning. And nobody gets out of a life of crime in Saints Row 3:
SR3 celebrates and revels in gang culture in the dumbest way possible. To paraphrase one reviewer, it's GTA in the eyes of those crazy parents and watchdog groups who think GTA is just one big murder-fest. It glorifies crime without ever taking itself seriously. I'd cite specific examples, but doing so would rob the game of its magic. You need to see it for yourself.
But the stupidity demonstrated in-game is inversely proportional to the mastery of game design demonstrated by Volition. Story beats guaranteed in a typical game of this genre are ignored or turned on their head. And the over-arching story feels relevant - almost a social commentary on the people who would try to censor this game.
I was pretty thoroughly convinced that I made the right purchasing decision after the first mission. Doubly so after the first three. Aside from a minor slog in the second sixth of the game as all kinds of new side-missions are introduced without any story context, the game pretty much starts great and stays great throughout.
Note that AMD graphics cards do not work well with the game's vehicles. I still played through the entire game -- 8fps driving or not, it's awesome. Reviews indicate that the DLC sucks. I'd avoid the DLC but definitely buy the base game.

Who, even among scholars in the field, could keep up with the flood of attacks on Pius XII that began in the late 1990s? John Cornwell gave us Hitler’s Pope , and Michael Phayer followed with The Catholic Church and the Holocaust . David Kertzer brought charges against Pius XII in The Popes Against the Jews , and Susan Zuccotti reversed her previous scholarship to pen Under His Very Windows: The Vatican and the Holocaust in Italy . Garry Wills used Pius as the centerpiece for his reformist Papal Sin , as did James Carroll in Constantine’s Sword . So, for that matter, did Daniel Goldhagen when he wrote what proved to be the most extended and straightforward assault on Catholicism in decades: A Moral Reckoning: The Role of the Catholic Church in the Holocaust and Its Unfulfilled Duty of Repair .
Meanwhile, the essays and occasional pieces were collected in such volumes as Holocaust Scholars Write to the Vatican , and The Holocaust and the Christian World , and The Vatican and the Holocaust , and Pope Pius XII and the Holocaust , and Christian Responses to the Holocaust ”and on, and on, until we seemed to be facing what the exasperated reviewer John Pawlikowski called “a virtual book-of-the-month club on institutional Catholicism, anti-Semitism, and the Holocaust.”
The champions of Pius had their share of book-length innings as well”although, one might note, never from the same level of popular publisher as the attackers managed to find. In 1999 Pierre Blet produced Pius XII and the Second World War According to the Archives of the Vatican and got Paulist Press, a respectable but small Catholic house, to publish it in America. Ronald Rychlak finished his first-rate Hitler, the War, and the Pope , and the hardback was brought out by a press in Columbia, Missouri, known mostly for printing romance novels. For the paperback edition, Rychlak’s work was picked up by the book-publishing arm of the Catholic newspaper Our Sunday Visitor .
Those are both fine presses in their way, and Rychlak has done well for them. But one can reasonably point out that Our Sunday Visitor is not quite at the level of distribution, advertising, and influence enjoyed by Doubleday, Houghton Mifflin, Knopf, and Viking”the large houses that issued the books against Pius. The commentator Philip Jenkins recently suggested that this disparity in publishers sends a message that the mainstream view is the guilt of Pius XII, while praise for the Pope belongs only to the cranks, nuts, and sectarians.
Jenkins’ suggestion is worth considering. Still, no one can say Pius’ supporters were squashed or censored. In just six years, Margherita Marchione managed five books in praise of the Pope. The Thomistic philosopher and novelist Ralph McInerny, aggravated by the deluge of attacks, issued a splenetic volume called The Defamation of Pope Pius XII , while Justus George Lawler (a writer best known in Catholic circles for his liberalism) penned a witty evisceration of Pius’ critics called Popes and Politics: Reform, Resentment, and the Holocaust . José Sánchez added Pope Pius XII and the Holocaust , and a slew of German and Italian books might be mentioned as well, prompted, for the most part, by the popular visibility of the English-language criticisms even in Europe.
But it was primarily in book reviews and responses that the defenders of Pius XII fought out the war”which is something of a problem. Every pope precipitates biographies, hagiographies, and maledictions, like the dropping of the rain; it is part of the job to be much written about, and the works on Eugenio Pacelli that began to appear when he became pope in 1939 seem innumerable. But no supporter has yet produced a book-length biography in the wake of the recent years of extended blame. Even Rychlak’s Hitler, the War, and the Pope was essentially reactive, devoting a thirty-page epilogue to a catalogue of the errors in Cornwell’s book.
We have seen this pattern before. Rolf Hochhuth’s play The Deputy premiered in Berlin in 1963, and its picture of a greedy pope, concerned only about Vatican finances and silent about the Holocaust, immediately caused a firestorm of comment from the intellectual world. Everyone who was anyone felt compelled to weigh in.
Hochhuth himself faded away when he tried to extend his censure to Winston Churchill, penning a play in 1967 that claimed Churchill had ordered the murder of the Polish General Wladyslaw Sikorski and, later, the murder of the pilot who had crashed Sikorski’s plane. Unbeknownst to Hochhuth, the pilot was, in fact, still alive, and he won a libel judgment that badly damaged the London theater which had staged the play. Thereafter, Hochhuth found it harder to get a hearing”although, interestingly, the current notoriety of Pius XII seems to have resurrected the playwright to some degree, and in 2002 the Greek filmmaker Constantin Costa-Gravas released a movie version of The Deputy with the English title Amen (or Eyewitness , in other copies).
Even without Hochhuth, the wide discussion about Pius XII he initiated in 1963 went on for several years. It produced some overheated journalistic attempts to cash in on the public interest, such as Robert Katz’ Black Sabbath and Death in Rome (the latter being the target of a successful libel suit, this time brought by Pius XII’s niece, Countess Elena Pacelli Rossignani). But the era brought forth as well three more serious and scholarly”indeed, by today’s standards, quite moderate and thoughtful”attacks: Guenter Lewy’s The Catholic Church and Nazi Germany (1964), Carlo Falconi’s The Silence of Pius XII (1965), and Saul Friedlander’s Pius XII and the Third Reich: A Documentation (1966).
The brouhaha also prompted the Vatican to begin releasing material from Pius’ pontificate, which appeared from 1965 to 1981 as the eleven-volume series Actes et Documents . In part by relying on these new documents, but even more by simply gathering their forces and investigating each of the incidents taken as the core of the indictment, the defenders gradually tamped down The Deputy ’s claims about Pius XII and the Holocaust. Pope John Paul II was a consistent advocate for his predecessor, and even once-popular notions about Pius”that he was, for instance, the great reactionary opponent against whom Vatican II turned”gradually seemed to lose steam by the late 1970s and early ’80s. It took more than a decade, but the reactive reviewers appeared to carry the day, and the popular magazine press and major book publishers lost interest.
A few commentators noted that the whole thing hadn’t entirely died. The historian Michael Tagliacozzo said he kept an open file labeled “Calumnies Against Pius XII.” But most were unprepared when the criticism began again in the late 1990s. To journalists and cultural commentators, Hitler’s Pope seemed almost to come out of nowhere in 1999, and it received almost entirely ecstatic reviews when it first appeared. A few skeptical journalists who remembered the Hochhuth battles” Newsweek ’s Kenneth Woodward and the New York Times ’ Peter Steinfels, notably”doubted Cornwell’s conclusions, but it had been years since they had investigated the topic, and they were unprepared to provide details about the book’s errors.
Time was needed for scholars to gin up the machine again, double-check the claims in Hitler’s Pope , and publish the reviews. Some of the results proved deeply embarrassing for Cornwell, particularly the falsity of his boast that he had spent “months on end” in the archives, when he visited the Vatican for only three weeks and didn’t go to the archives every day of that. The Italian letter from Pacelli that Cornwell placed at the center of his book as evidence of deep anti-Semitism had been, he claimed, waiting secretly “like a time bomb” until he did his research.

Arma 3 is the true sequel to the beloved Operation Flashpoint (Or as it’s known on steam as Arma: Cold War Assault.)
I say that, because as an old school flashpoint “get of my lawn” guy, Arma 3 is the first truly unique version of the Flashpoint formula that just feels right. OFP is one the best games of all time, nobody forgets being abandoned on Everon, with nothing but your M16 and hundreds of Soviets between you and the evac ship. Or as Victor Troska leading the Resistance and throwing that T55 between buildings just so that Hind can’t snipe you with a rocket. And all of the mods, all of them. (Here’s looking at you FFUR, ECP, FDF, BW) But, alas back to the task at hand. Eventually the first Arma came out.
Arma was fun mostly because it was like OFP with new graphics which was nice for a while, but something about it just wasn’t that enthralling, it felt like the game was shooting for the extra point and missed. Not very far off, but enough to just feel a little to hollow. I also have fond memories of the campaign breaking on multiple occasions, the gigantic lag spikes in MP, and the absolutely hilarious voiceovers. “2 FALL BACK INTO FOORMATIOOOON.” Oh and that disappointing AI pathfinding, I remember screaming "Just go into the damn house!" When I was using the editor, but Sergai felt like he should just hang outside of the doorway then awkwardly crane his neck at the oncoming enemy. Yes, by the "not recommended' you can kind of tell this is going to be a rant.
This game used to be very fun, but with it's current flaws, it's not. These reasons will be stated below.
1. The lack of balance.
Most class based games I have seen have certain classes counter other classes so that no class dominates all the entire game. An example of this would be Winston vs Genji in Overwatch.
However, in TF2, there are overpowed classes that dominate other classes and make them obsolete. These include:
1.Soldier ( If you know how to rocket jump and aim your rockets properly, you win)
2. Engineer (Just get 4-6 engineers and the enemy can never capture the objective)
3. Medic ( DPS+Uber= no one can counter you)
Additionally, there are certain weapons in TF2 are way too overpowered.
The Engineer's rescue ranger makes it impossible to destroy sentrie, since the engineer can heal his sentries away from damage)
The Machina does a lot of damage without ANY ( SInce the sniper can be easily found without tracer rounds revealing his shots) disadvantages.
The dead ringer makes the spy impossible to find and kill. (since he can just  escape when damaged, recharge, and repeat)
Since these overpowered classes and weapons makes most other playstyles obsolete, this makes most players have a linear playstyle. This makes the game very stale, and lead the game into it's next problem:
2. Lack of updates.
Yes, everyone knows that the Pyro update is coming out, but we don't know when. Therefore, at it's current stage, the game gets boring very fast. This is because the playstyle has been relatively the same for the past 2 years, due to the lack of updates. Additonally, since the lack of major patches leaves most overpowered and overused weapons unchanged, the playstyle of most players don't change.
Until an update arrives, this game is likely to remain boring.
3.  Team balancing.
I feel like this is the biggest problem in Team fortress 2. Whenever a team starts losing in a match, most people on the losing team leave. This basically makes the losing team's situation worse, and eventually leads to the disapperance of the losing team. Now, a simple solution to this would be having new players fill the void left by the rage quitters. However, since the matchmaking syestem of TF2 is extremly slow, not enough players show up to fill the gap. Therefore, this makes it very frustrating for players who constantly get stuck on the losing team (which is about 90% of all teams formed in TF2, since most of them lack coordination).
4. Hackers.
Almost all games I have seen have a good anti-cheat syestem that rids hackers when their game-breaking ways are noticed by players in a match. However, in Team fortress two, hackers encountered in a game never get kicked, since the removal of players have to be done by vote kicking. The problem with this syestem is that not all players show up in the vote kick option. Therefore, hackers somehow NEVER appear in the vote kick option. This makes hackers remain in matches and break the game for everyone else. Now the reason why hackers are a major problem is because many matches have hackers that aren't dealt with. Until valve comes up with a better anti-cheat syestem, this problem will continue making tf2 a frustrating game.
In conclusion, while this game has a lot of potential to be very fun,  these potentials can never be acheived until the problems above are solved.
I hope you enjoyed my little rant, and if there are a lot of mistaken points, please understand that this is coming from someone who may not have played this game to it's fullest potential.

Saints Row was a great game; shallow in places, but overall good and had its funny and badass moments.
Saints Row Two brought great humour and some over the top moments to the game, as well as improved nearly EVERYTHING, except multiplayer.
Saints Row The Third is a different bag of treats. Much to my disappointment, you don’t need to work for anything in it. It is an easy task to acquire most any of the interesting vehicles and weapons. The whole story has been replaced with nothing but “over-the-topness” and jokes. No seriousness to contrast the silly. Not to mention around HALF the games Achievements are DLC related. So, you can’t “Finish” the game without spending more money.
If you are looking for some mindless shenanigans’, this is a game for it. It is fun; more so multiplayer, but the novelty will only last so long.
I’d say the game is a buy, just for the “spice” of variety. There’s no other game that plays quite like it. But I’d say wait for a sale.

EDIT: I finally got into the modded server area of Arma3. I'm almost ashamed to say I put 7 hours into a Epoch mod+Ryan's Zombies and Demons server. It was a blast. Looting buildings, building a sanctuary. Getting spotted by a zombie horde was terrifying, all of a sudden you'd start hearing screams and moans and turn around and you see the zombies teeming out of a city. Crazy fun. Highly suggest Epoch or Exile to anyone looking for good servers to play.
My computer is definitely not up-to-par with running this on full graphics. Sometimes it makes engagements are 200+yards very hard, especially with no magnification. But I still have had some of my best gaming experiences in this game.
Find a group of guys. Find a clan, a casual thing, or just a server with the same people playing consistently. Your experiences in this game will skyrocket. I mainly play co-op servers, just doing made up missions on the map against spawned AI. Its a blast. I've participated in missions that lasted 4 hours in real time, and ingame spanned early morning to over night to the next morning. All because we encountered an APC, and our AT guy was the first one shot by it in an open field. At night.
There are no limits to travel. If you want to run across the island, feel free! It'll take you a couple hours I'd imagine real time, I've never done it though. Everything is detailed, towns have houses where you actually clear buildings, opening doors and such. And tactics work. PvE is hard without a squad using comms, let alone PvP.
For an epic military simulator, you've got your dream game. Not for a COD fan just looking for a change of scenery. Its an entirely different FPS. You can do most things you would in real life. Pretty crazy.
Gameplay: 10/10
Optimization: 10/10, I can adjust my settings down and still get 50fps.
Community: 8/10, a little hard to get involved but once you are, amazing.
Overall: 9.3/10

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Yes. This game is worth it for many reasons, mostly because It offers you, the player, an immersive experience that puts you in the shoes of a field operative in a war. This game not only has a great features, but a highly advanced ones in which are iconic to the Bohemia Interactive experience.
This game makes it different from other FPS games in a vast variety of ways. Not only does this game add open worlds in which allow the player to experience great amounts of scenery (Based off of real life places) it offers many mechanics which were only fantasized about during its time. The Arma series has set a staple in the community for being the original bearer of a world in which everything is totally interactive in every way possible.
Ballistics, or the physics of projectiles is what really gave Arma its name. Just like any other FPS, the ballistics of a game really sets in how it feels when you play it. Sure, bullets that follow the guns crosshair exactly the the center of the screen are nice, but in the Arma series, they have taken it to the next level by adding their own Advanced Ballistics. Bullets are now affected by, Distance, Time, Angle, and even wind. Every shot you make must be made with precision and calculation. One of the Iconic additions of Arma3 was the Subsonic weaponry, it really made shows the player how effective bullet drop actually occurs in reality.
In games such as Call Of Duty, being able to operate a vehicle is a once in a lifetime opportunity, with little to no actual experience. Arma has made a staple into FPS Military games by allowing players to interact with the vehicles in everymanner. Vehicles like Tanks, Cars, Helicopters, and Drones, are all Drivable and operable, in which all abide by realistic physics aswell. Helicopters are affected by stress on the rotors, Autorotation is possible, and much more that makes you feel like you are actually operating a helicopter. Vehicles also have a advanced damage system in which different areas that are damaged can affect the performance of the vehicle. For example, if your Tank tracks Are RED, your vehicle will move extremely slow, or not at all, simulating damage.

One of the newest additions to the game, was a enhanced radar system, along with new jets and a new and improved damage system for them. The radar system was introduced to make dogfighting and arial combat more realistic, and it did exactly that, It added a whole new level on the playing field in which made it more stressfull to operate the jets. Along with jets having radar systems, Anti aircraft Artillery are also given this ability to have a radar to spot other aircraft.   This addition really makes dogfighting a whole new system all together, blowing away all the other gaming competitors.
Moving in a FPS game is vital, especially when there are enemies around the corner. Arma3 has added a totally new meaning to movement, as the standard movements were, Standing, Crouching, and Prone, but in Arma 3 you get 13 more movement factors, by giving you different levels of all the stances. You can lean in both directions, and even lunge out and lean aswell, giving you a heavy advantage over other players. Now you can kill enemies without running from the corner and hoping that your weapon spray will kill the enemy.  Along with new stances, fatigue was added to Arma3. The more items you lug around, the less stamina you get, making you think about what is needed to bring with you, and what might be needed. The Stamina system makes the player become more aware of their movements and actions.

There's not much I need say in this section as it is simple. Sound is realistic, in such way that, shockwaves abide by the speed of sound, and speed of light. If you see a bomb go off 2 kilometers away, you will not hear it untill a while after, simulating the speed of sound. Also, the core sounds of the game are quite realistic of what you would hear in real life, although could be improved in my opinon.

Yes. This game is worth it for many reasons, mostly because It offers you, the player, an immersive experience that puts you in the shoes of a field operative in a war. This game not only has a great features, but a highly advanced ones in which are iconic to the Bohemia Interactive experience.
This game makes it different from other FPS games in a vast variety of ways. Not only does this game add open worlds in which allow the player to experience great amounts of scenery (Based off of real life places) it offers many mechanics which were only fantasized about during its time. The Arma series has set a staple in the community for being the original bearer of a world in which everything is totally interactive in every way possible.
Ballistics, or the physics of projectiles is what really gave Arma its name. Just like any other FPS, the ballistics of a game really sets in how it feels when you play it. Sure, bullets that follow the guns crosshair exactly the the center of the screen are nice, but in the Arma series, they have taken it to the next level by adding their own Advanced Ballistics. Bullets are now affected by, Distance, Time, Angle, and even wind. Every shot you make must be made with precision and calculation. One of the Iconic additions of Arma3 was the Subsonic weaponry, it really made shows the player how effective bullet drop actually occurs in reality.
In games such as Call Of Duty, being able to operate a vehicle is a once in a lifetime opportunity, with little to no actual experience. Arma has made a staple into FPS Military games by allowing players to interact with the vehicles in everymanner. Vehicles like Tanks, Cars, Helicopters, and Drones, are all Drivable and operable, in which all abide by realistic physics aswell. Helicopters are affected by stress on the rotors, Autorotation is possible, and much more that makes you feel like you are actually operating a helicopter. Vehicles also have a advanced damage system in which different areas that are damaged can affect the performance of the vehicle. For example, if your Tank tracks Are RED, your vehicle will move extremely slow, or not at all, simulating damage.

One of the newest additions to the game, was a enhanced radar system, along with new jets and a new and improved damage system for them. The radar system was introduced to make dogfighting and arial combat more realistic, and it did exactly that, It added a whole new level on the playing field in which made it more stressfull to operate the jets. Along with jets having radar systems, Anti aircraft Artillery are also given this ability to have a radar to spot other aircraft.   This addition really makes dogfighting a whole new system all together, blowing away all the other gaming competitors.

Now you can kill enemies without running from the corner and hoping that your weapon spray will kill the enemy.  Along with new stances, fatigue was added to Arma3. The more items you lug around, the less stamina you get, making you think about what is needed to bring with you, and what might be needed. The Stamina system makes the player become more aware of their movements and actions.

Assuming you're a veteren of the Arma franchise and at least played Arma 2 before purchasing this one, here is a bunch of comparisions to Arma 2.
Pros (these may include pros from Arma 2 aswell):
- MUCH better optimised than Arma 2, no idea what they have done but this runs much smoother than Arma 2.
- No more thermal sights, I tend to really only play KOTH and have yet to be killed by any thermal sight.
- Animations are much more realistic.
- Audio is much better, as of a recent update the sounds (especially distant gunfire) are higher quality.
- More to it, sounds bland I know but there are more things you can do, such as sit and shoot, set up bipod/lock prone position.
- As well as being better optimised the game itself is much prettier than Arma 2.
- Kills are very satisfying, especially when it comes down to a tactical kill.
- There is so many options for tactical play, like there is so much you can do in order to gain a tactical advantage.
Cons (these will include cons that are also present in Arma 2):
- Snipers, although they are a true threat in war, they are also 90% cause of death in this game.
- Control scheme changed, quite a bit actually enough so that you may have to shamefully ask how to do a certain action or be forever lost in Arma 3's key binding options.
- Lag and desync still exist, and will probably kill you at least once (I know all games can experience lag but Arma has a very unique form of desync that can make pilots/drivers crash and soldiers teleport).
- FPS drops/stutters, whilst rare they can and will happen at some point (I randomly got about 11FPS at one point, when I regularly get over 30-40FPS maybe more).
- Bugs, you see some traumatising s*** and I am not refering to the terrors of war, I am refering to the dead guy 50ft in the air that keeps teleporting above you.
- Third person, this game has the option to go third or first person and most beginners will go TP as the game can be clunky to begin with but as a true FP player it can be annoying when someone hides in cover and peeks out lightening fast and instantly mows me down, or when I have a guy suppressed and move to a new spot he waits until I move to strike.

Overall is a good game that will annoy and frustrate you, but will always tempt you back for more.

Assuming you're a veteren of the Arma franchise and at least played Arma 2 before purchasing this one, here is a bunch of comparisions to Arma 2.
Pros (these may include pros from Arma 2 aswell):
- MUCH better optimised than Arma 2, no idea what they have done but this runs much smoother than Arma 2.
- No more thermal sights, I tend to really only play KOTH and have yet to be killed by any thermal sight.
- Animations are much more realistic.
- Audio is much better, as of a recent update the sounds (especially distant gunfire) are higher quality.
- More to it, sounds bland I know but there are more things you can do, such as sit and shoot, set up bipod/lock prone position.
- As well as being better optimised the game itself is much prettier than Arma 2.
- Kills are very satisfying, especially when it comes down to a tactical kill.
- There is so many options for tactical play, like there is so much you can do in order to gain a tactical advantage.
Cons (these will include cons that are also present in Arma 2):
- Snipers, although they are a true threat in war, they are also 90% cause of death in this game.
- Control scheme changed, quite a bit actually enough so that you may have to shamefully ask how to do a certain action or be forever lost in Arma 3's key binding options.
- Lag and desync still exist, and will probably kill you at least once (I know all games can experience lag but Arma has a very unique form of desync that can make pilots/drivers crash and soldiers teleport).
- FPS drops/stutters, whilst rare they can and will happen at some point (I randomly got about 11FPS at one point, when I regularly get over 30-40FPS maybe more).
- Bugs, you see some traumatising s*** and I am not refering to the terrors of war, I am refering to the dead guy 50ft in the air that keeps teleporting above you.
- Third person, this game has the option to go third or first person and most beginners will go TP as the game can be clunky to begin with but as a true FP player it can be annoying when someone hides in cover and peeks out lightening fast and instantly mows me down, or when I have a guy suppressed and move to a new spot he waits until I move to strike.

Overall is a good game that will annoy and frustrate you, but will always tempt you back for more.

I strongly recommend this game to others. Despite being 10 years old at this point, and many of the unique weapons being degraded in usefulness over that time, it still provides a blast for anyone who installs. In comparison to other FPS games that I've played (CS:GO, BO3, etc.) Team Fortress 2 offers a unique elemental charm that keeps drawing me back to it. One of the main proponents to this may be the characters, who each have individual, interesting personas behind them, only strengthened more by the videos Valve posts (e.g. "Meet The" series, Expiration Date). Another draw may be the unique weapons and gameplay, where you don't always have to be shooting but rather can play different roles. The Medic's main focus isn't destroying everything in sight; it's healing. The Engineer creates buildings that help everyone on the team and fight for him. The Spy can easily slip behind enemy lines and commit various forms of sabotage. These unique traits are helped by how each has it's own counter; the Spy is easily discoverable by a Pyro, the Engineer's buildings are disabled by the Spy, and the Heavy's slow movement can become a huge burden when facing off against a Scout. This creates balanced and fun gameplay, where you never know what will happen because people keep making up new strategies to complete one of various goals.
As with any game, TF2 has it's fair share of problems. the amount of people on each team occasionally is unbalanced, detracting from the point I made about counters. In addition, updates have not been as plentiful in recent years, most likely due to the age of the game. This prevents fresh content that spices up the game even more. Despite this, I think it is a great game overall, and definitely worth the download.

I really want to love Arma, but I just cant bring myself to. It's the most realistic game ever, and it has probably a lifetimes worth of content. Beautiful graphics and the complexity of the gameplay isn't actually all that daunting once you get used to it. But thats not the problem. The problem is the dog-dirt AI. Its seriously the worst AI I have ever seen in a video game, EVER. I actually cannot describe how awful it is.
Should you attempt to use AI to help you drive a vehicle, God have mercy on your soul. Try and be the gunner? The driver is going to do his best to run into walls and flip the tank in a ditch. See an enemy? Well then he is going to turn the tank around, expose the weak rear armor, and stop in an open field. Tell him to move? Nope, suddenly they forgot how to obey commands and do a weird back and forth jerking roll thing. Try and be the driver? The gunner in a tank with thermal optics will somehow miss a tank sitting 3 feet in front of him. Your infantry teammates will engage the enemy by breaking cover, running into the middle of the street, and spraying on full auto. Vehicles constantly get stuck on rocks, lampposts, trees, ditches, ect. Sometimes they won't spot an enemy in the open while they are being used as target practice, and other times they pull of aimbot level first-shot headshots from 500m while standing upright. Helicopters and planes are more effective as kamikaze weapons, and single enemies with rifles can easily take out a wing of attack helos.
I really really want to love this game, but its virtually impossible to enjoy with AI teammates. I have every AI enhancement mod I can find, nothing helps.  Every time I come back to it I get so mad. Whether its my M1 driver stopping in an open field and then un-learning how to drive so we can be RPG fodder or my gunner in an apache refusing to engage enemy infantry in the open leading to an early demise, the AI in this game is insanely poor. It makes the AI out of battlefield 2 look like rocket science. AI able to take the initiative and get in a technicals .50 without being specifically ordered to approach the vehicle, and then you having to get in and switch spots for 10 minutes to finagle them out of a passenger seat into the obviously useful position is a pipe dream in this game. Its super enjoyable to walk around and play in Zeus mode, but unless you have great internet you are going to get very, very, very upset.

Immersive & trying // Recommended for those that cherish depth & complexity
*I recommend this particularly for its multiplayer.
+ Extremely mod friendly; enjoys full support from the Steam Workshop
+ Visuals & environmental design, save for a few issues here and there (i.e. empty buildings), has largely aged well & looks fantastic
+ Employs a deeply challenging level of realism
+ Multiplayer is still very active; boasts a wonderful variety of gameplay & modded servers to choose from
+ Long, content-packed single player campaign; player choices do affect potential endings, as there are several
+ Time control is back from Arma 2; player can speed up the passage of time, which helps SIGNIFICANTLY to combat the monotony of walking/running very long distances between objectives
+ Enormous map/playable area
+ User-created scenarios & a very easy-to-use scenario creator
+ Boasts incredibly varied gameplay mechanics; from piloting/driving myriad vehicles & gunships, to underwater missions, & everything in-between
+ Map & squad mechanics are back; while they may feel clunky to use in a combat scenario, a little practice goes a long way & serves to open up a slew of options on the battlefield
- Sound design is very hit & miss; some weapons sound identical to others, & vehicle sound effects tend to sound strangely muted
- Dialogue is also hit & miss; while I found the voice-acting to be done largely well, some of the dialogue is a bit awful
- Soundtrack often felt cheesy or inappropriate
- Mission pacing often feels very uneven; I felt that it often leaned too far into the realm of the tedious in the interest of realism (shouldn't be a bad thing in theory, but for the pruposes of a video game, it can put players to sleep in some missions)
- The initial learning curve is considerable, & the tutorial felt inadequate overall; mechanics are amazing on paper, but take an inordinate amount of time to master

Sooo. as someone who isn't a big time BR player i've tested Playerunknowns Battleground and wasn't fully happy. the framerate was a-s-s, the Server lagged (you shot someone and it didnt recognize, you pick stuff up and it takes 5 seconds to be actually in your inventory). So i quickly looked for an alternative til its out of its early bird stages and the devs fixed it a bit more.
So I thought about H1Z1 KOTK. I just saw some videos on it, read a lot of negative reviews (mostly of those people hyped for PlayerUnknowns Battleground) and people generally had a Split mind about H1Z1 KOTK as a BR game.
But i tell you, This game is way better to play at the moment (04.27) It runs with over 60 FPS, i didn't experience any lag and the customizations are fun, and add to the addictive-ness similar to CSGO skins.
As a player who mostly plays Competitive First Person Shooters for years and never really got into the Survival game business (except rust ) i can really recommend this game (H1Z1 KOTK) to anyone who is interested in Battle Royale games. I quickly found servers to play on with 140 people on it, got the hang of it quickly. Got to finally experience a battle royale without Lag, without HUGE FPS DROPS (as in Playerunknowns) and i'm definitely seeing myself playing this game for hours and hours.
if you're interested in Playerunknowns Battleground, you should definitely wait some weeks or maybe months, since its hardly playable (i had maybe 2-3 rounds where i really got to enjoy the game) and get this game instead. This game runs waaaaaaay smoother, Is fun! has pretty Graphics! and you will see yourself get addicted to it if you're into games like these.
Buy H1Z1 KOTK if you're into BR games. Or wait a few months til PUBG finally fixes its major FPS losses and Lags in their Servers or Netcode if you really want to play that.
I'm not picking sides in this H1Z1 KOTK vs PUBG War. I find both games appealing and i will defintely play both of them a lot. But for now H1Z1 KOTK is far more playable (=enjoyable) than its very hyped Competitor.

Sooo. as someone who isn't a big time BR player i've tested Playerunknowns Battleground and wasn't fully happy. the framerate was a-s-s, the Server lagged (you shot someone and it didnt recognize, you pick stuff up and it takes 5 seconds to be actually in your inventory). So i quickly looked for an alternative til its out of its early bird stages and the devs fixed it a bit more.
So I thought about H1Z1 KOTK. I just saw some videos on it, read a lot of negative reviews (mostly of those people hyped for PlayerUnknowns Battleground) and people generally had a Split mind about H1Z1 KOTK as a BR game.
But i tell you, This game is way better to play at the moment (04.27) It runs with over 60 FPS, i didn't experience any lag and the customizations are fun, and add to the addictive-ness similar to CSGO skins.
As a player who mostly plays Competitive First Person Shooters for years and never really got into the Survival game business (except rust ) i can really recommend this game (H1Z1 KOTK) to anyone who is interested in Battle Royale games. I quickly found servers to play on with 140 people on it, got the hang of it quickly. Got to finally experience a battle royale without Lag, without HUGE FPS DROPS (as in Playerunknowns) and i'm definitely seeing myself playing this game for hours and hours.
if you're interested in Playerunknowns Battleground, you should definitely wait some weeks or maybe months, since its hardly playable (i had maybe 2-3 rounds where i really got to enjoy the game) and get this game instead. This game runs waaaaaaay smoother, Is fun! has pretty Graphics! and you will see yourself get addicted to it if you're into games like these.
Buy H1Z1 KOTK if you're into BR games. Or wait a few months til PUBG finally fixes its major FPS losses and Lags in their Servers or Netcode if you really want to play that.
I'm not picking sides in this H1Z1 KOTK vs PUBG War. I find both games appealing and i will defintely play both of them a lot. But for now H1Z1 KOTK is far more playable (=enjoyable) than its very hyped Competitor.
Thank you for reading,  and game on! (whatever game you prefer)

Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community.  So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
No Caption Provided
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.
The biggest divergence from the game's origins comes in the cooperative mode, Mann vs. Machine. In it, you and a few other human players must prevent hordes of robotic incarnations of TF2's classes from delivering a bomb to your base. The money you earn from destroying robots can be spent on mid-match upgrades to your attributes and weaponry, which can be crucial to success. Even on the easiest level, the robot legions are fierce enough to test the mettle of an unorganized team. This is a mode where carefully planned weapon choices and defensive strategies can mean the difference between succeeding and having to try, try again. You can play this mode for free, but you won't be eligible to earn rare prizes or complete challenges unless you pay a dollar for a Tour of Duty ticket. Though it lacks the frenetic unpredictability of competitive play, the cooperative mode can still provide satisfaction for those dedicated enough to see it through.
But competition is the real draw, and the Team Fortress 2 community can certainly be competitive. On some servers, you might be berated for unwitting breaches of etiquette, while on others, you might be welcomed with helpful tips and ubercharges. You can even ask for help on certain servers and be paired up with another player who is willing to give you some tips through chat. The community around TF2 is an intriguing one, not just for their deep knowledge of and passion for the game, but for their creative efforts in designing new weapons, items, and maps that have since become part of the experience. It feels like a community of curators, without whom the game may well have dwindled away and passed into obsolescence years ago.
Staying relevant even a year after release is rare for a competitive shooter, and yet, here's Team Fortress 2, still lively after seven years in the business. At times it feels like the same game you could have played back then, and at other times it feels like no one will ever quite nail class-based shooter competition the way TF2 does. The experience has evolved over the years without compromising what made it so great in the first place, so though your free-to-play options may have increased considerably in the past few years, there are few that do it as well as Team Fortress 2.

Once you got used to the mechanics, H1 was extremely fun. Then they released the combat update. The combat effectively removed the skill in the game and replaced it with sheer luck. The hit register seems to be twice as bad as well as the desync. The AR is completely random in the amount of damage it will do. Someone could be standing still and you could hit them 5 times and they turn around and will kill you in 3 hits with the same weapon. Also, the amount of hackers seems to have doubled. Prior to the combat update, I never ran into anyone who I legitimately though was hacking, so far I've run into 3-4 people who were very obviously hacking. I love this game, it's very fun to play but the fighting mechanics don't seem to require skill, instead they require sheer luck which is a trait I do not seem to possess because I lose almost every gunfight I get into when I hit people 5+ times with the AR which apparently does 22.5 damage per shot. Not a good game anymore...pity.

Team Fortress 2, despite what people say, will statistically survive for a long time, for one simple reason: originality. It is SUCH an original game, for example, you can hit people with a FISH, there is a community game mode where all a weapon's stats are multiplied by 10. Tf2 can get so many laughs and 'How the hell'-s, even without community servers and dlc. Another great thing about TF2 is that it is just SO REPLAYABLE! There are so many weapons in the game, every one warranting a different play style. There are also many weapon re-skins, such as the Batsaber, which can really make the game more enjoyable, and you can even do cosplay in-game! Another great thing about weapon re-skins is that it makes movie makers very happy inside the Source Filmmaker, as it is easy to make hilarious skits with the TF2 characters and weapons :) Here's to an original game, which is fun to play, and will always have a dedicated playerbase.

Firstly, I've a big fan of the ARMA series since back during the Operation Flashpoint era. ARMA 3 is simply the next step in the evolution of this particular franchise... but is it a big enough step?
You might like this game if:
Singleplayer (Base Game): 6/10 - The main campaign is rather lackluster. It works, it is difficult, and it actually does a halfway decent job in making you feel like a cog in a larger machine. However, there are a number of missions that completely break immersion and force you to make unintuitive choices in order to beat a mission. The AI is... decent, and does the job.
Singleplayer (Sandbox): 9/10 - Wow, the community add-ons and scenarios really take this game to the next level. There are so many mods out there that can completely overhaul the experience (for the better). Thanks to the steam workshop, the installation of mods is quite easy.
Multiplayer (coop): 10/10 - Simply the best coop experince I've ever had. Working alongside a team of 20+ players attempting to accomplish a combined arms mission is fantastic. How is this different from say: BF4 or COD? This can be answered in 2 ways:
Stability: 5/10 - Unfortunately, you'll need a beefy machine to really play this game. Basically, this engine will only utilize 1-2 cores. Meaning that you cannot use your 3/4/5/6th core to help with this game. You'll also need a beefy videocard as well. (Check the specs if you don't believe me) Aside from that, due to the nature of this open-world game, I have run into a number of bugs, mostly due to the AI running into problems. This is nothing a restart won't fix, but by the 3rd version of your game, I expect better.
Value: 10/10 - For me, who loves tactical realism and military simulation games, I'd easily drop full price for the base game. The developers, Bohemia Interactive Studios, are constantly making new patches and content for the game. This quality ALONE is why I support this developer. In addition to that, the community provide a plethora of new scenarios, mods, graphic overhauls, weapons, skins, AI scripts, and more. The modding community here is easily equal to the ones that provide content for the Elder Scroll's series.

If you came for a review, you should look somewhere else. I came here to spread my Welsh Cake Recipe.
Ingredients:
225g plain flour
85g caster sugar
½ tsp mixed spice
½ tsp baking powder
50g butter
, cut into small pieces
50g lard, cut into small pieces, plus extra for frying
50g currant
1 egg
, beaten
splash milk
There are two methods to making this:
Methods
1. Tip the flour, sugar, mixed spice, baking powder and a pinch of salt into a bowl. Then, with your fingers, rub in the butter and lard until crumbly. Mix in the currants. Work the egg into the mixture until you have soft dough, adding a splash of milk if it seems a little dry – it should be the same consistency as shortcrust pastry.
2. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured work surface to the thickness of your little finger. Cut out rounds using a 6cm cutter, re-rolling any trimmings. Grease a flat griddle pan or heavy frying pan with lard, and place over a medium heat. Cook the Welsh cakes in batches, for about 3 mins each side, until golden brown, crisp and cooked through. Delicious served warm with butter and jam, or simply sprinkled with caster sugar. Cakes will stay fresh in a tin for 1 week.

一个萌新的一点心得
------游戏------
如果你还没有购买游戏，且对大逃杀类型的游戏没有过多的兴趣的话，不要盲目的跟风购买，游戏中没有所谓的CHINA NO.1，就算有反正我玩了二十个小时是没遇到过，68rmb可以买你更喜欢的东西（+1党 土豪无视即可）
------装备------
开局会有一些衣服及装饰，游戏中可以捡到或制作防弹衣。头盔分摩托头盔和战术头盔，用哪个看个人喜好就好。头巾和帽子和手套是纯装饰品，不想戴着就撕了和绷带，捡到的衣服背包身上有的话就撕了，游戏中捡不到裤子，别的衣服或装备都能捡到。背包分旅行背包和军用背包，军用的格子会大一些。另外说一句眼镜或面具不会挡子弹
------武器------
游戏内的枪支瞄准方式和其他沙盒类游戏没有太大区别，值得提的一点个人总是感觉射击方式很粗糙，可能刚开始玩的时候会有些不适应，多玩玩就好了，近距离霰弹枪跳着打，远距离就AR点射，当然有狙击枪更好（狙击枪只在空投物资里捡到过），AK适合近距离中距离tututu。弓箭和十字弩？没听说过
------驾驶------
正常的驾驶模式，shift氮气加速。进车可以把钥匙拿走，有钥匙的话可以上车就走（不论是自己的车还是别人的车），没钥匙就进车点火线，6s点着一样可以开走，不过会有噪音。车翻了下车F可以把车翻回来，不懂原理是什么= =
------开局------
落地后前10s谁有枪谁是爹，怕死落在荒野里也可以，不过物资难找要看运气。搜东西要快不要贪，东西够用就走，游戏神装很简单，不需要太多东西，拿多了死了也是送给别人。武器90发子弹就完全够用，防弹衣和头盔有条件就穿上一个带上一个，绷带10个左右，急救箱1-2个，凝血剂一个就够，没有也无所谓。受伤状态先凝血剂再绷带再急救箱。有军用背包东西随便塞就行，到安全的地方再拿出来分，武器槽满了别把枪塞背包里
------玩法------
如果开局你活了下来，有两种选择，找别人干或者找掩体（石头和树）怂着跟着安全区走。怂着可能被别人发现，出去干可能干不过别人。喜欢怎么玩就怎么玩
------空投------
游戏内时不时会有飞机轰鸣而过，之后会空投物资，物资落地后会有一波空袭，如果空袭离你近就看着天躲，躲开之后就去捡物资就好了（注意点旁边有没有人），里边的狙击枪一定要拿走，在游戏后期很重要。别的看着拿，拿太多也用不完（物资落地会有信号烟）
以上纯属个人见解!!!
CHINA NO.1!!!!!

So okay, where do I start? I think the best way to start is to talk about the positive aspects of the game. Well, it is quite funny if it is working. And they have updated some things like the car physics, the map and the Lobby system. The thrill of hunting people down, getting better equipment from them and then start hunting again is a good concept. The game is based on much skill but also luck is a part of it (like if you are killing one from the side/ behind or if you find good loot in the beginning). I think these are the good points about the game.
BUT this game is BUGGY AS ♥♥♥♥. okay it is Early access but the ammount of the bugs is just too high.
Let's describe a normal round of H1Z1 KotK. You have to wait a ridiculous amount of time just to get in the queue and at the loading screens if you want to enter a game ( 90 seconds queue and loading screens in my case up to 90 seconds). In one case, you are in the waiting room where you have to wait up to 60 seconds again. The other possibility is that the game directly starts... with a not closeabel (for about 5 seconds) opend inventory and in the first person view so you can't control the parachute. Then after you closed the inventory you can see your spawn and you have to decide where you want to land. The End of the Story: The Spawns are unfair AF! Some spawns are over a complete city where you can loot everything and get 2 Kevlars and 15 million guns while other spawns are about one church... ONE CHURCH with only a pistole. And yes, that's exactly the church where at least three other people are landing.
But sometimes you can't decide where you should land because the textures arent loaded yet. Sometimes they still arent loaded untill you are on the ground. The only downside is that playing SR3 by yourself is only half the fun; co-op can bring the experience alive in even more ways, as you share the insane, absurd chaos with a friend.

Over-the-top elements don't really stick with this game. The characters are portrayed as "criminal badasses", but when I read the first game's plot synopsis, they were a gang that was supposed to stop gang violence altogether. Now they're international superstars hellbent on killing everyone and everything in their path just to get by. Oh, and they say a character's dead, but there's never a body shown after their initial "death". To me, it's just grounds for a plot device for them to return. I'm talking Gat and Loren, of course. Killbane's death is convincing, since you're right there delivering it to him.
Overall, though, it's the same addicting gameplay that GTA brought us. Though, you can take over 'hoods by buying lots, stopping rival gang operations, and doing activities. The only fun ones are Prof. Genki and Cyber Blazing; the rest are frustrating since the over-the-topness required kinda outperforms your thirst for a challenge, and instead just gives you hand cramps.

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

Arma 3 is a very realistic, modern combat simulator. It takes the good things of Arma 2 and expands upon them, erasing all the issues of Arma 2 as well!
Despite it's hefty £35.99 pricetag Arma 3 offers the most realistic combat around ultimately creating the most realistic and immersive experience ever given out of the series and of all games for that matter! The campaign is actually rather decent offering immersive combat from all different scenarios and for those newcomers an in-depth tutorial. Other than campaign Arma (and the whole franchise mind you) have been best known for their challenging multiplayer experience and Arma 3 has kept it the same way offering the same gamemodes like CTF, Domination, Epoch etc. Workshop mods and maps have also been introduced as well as a 3D editor! If you didn't like or understand the eye-cancerous 2D editor that Arma 2 (and previous titles in the franchise) boasted then this is your time to get creative with the new free Eden 3D editor update.
This game has possibly the best graphics I have seen yet, it's outstanding, the breathtaking views from atop the grassy mountains are amazing along with the fluent animations. Textures are tesselated as well which is always a plus and no matter what setting you are on it looks frankly AAA.
The controls have stayed the same as Arma 2 ensuring that players coming from the second title can continue to play at ease.
Despite Arma 2's flop in optimization Arma 3 makes up for it offering 60fps+ experiences on max graphics. This game is a breeze to run on most systems however I can only say this for singleplayer. If you delve into the multiplayer side of the game you will begin to see the cracks. It is rare for you to ever hit over 30fps on a server with more than 30 people on it no matter what CPU you have (this game is VERY CPU dependant) however the singleplayer campaign or scenarios will have you going for at least 10 hours.
Arma 3 is a VERY good game with stunning visuals and sophisticated yet easy to learn controls and an amazing community of experts on the game always willing to help!
