This review is written from the perspective of a single-player gamer, who generally avoids online gaming as he works night shifts -- it ain't easy being English-speaking while the English part of the world sleeps. ;-)  (Also, bear with the capitalisation scheme of the game titles here, which are sadly the official spellings -- they've changed with every version of the game.)
Like all Bohemia Interactive titles, the roughness around the edges shouldn't distract you from the fact that in that carbonaceous lump, a diamond is sequestered within.  Although it is better optimised than ARMA 2 was (especially on release), the "ultra" and "high" settings should be considered as of 2015-2016 technology: a high-end gaming rig from 2012 will not cut it for the higher settings in the here and now.  But if you're willing to put up with the occasional stutter and the slight degradation in texture quality, bumping down the settings a little will give you a gorgeous sandbox miles ahead of ARMA 2 (graphically and otherwise) running as smooth as silk.  If you're part of the lucky upper crust who can afford better gaming rigs, well, screw you, you privileged jerk. ;-)
Diverging from the design philosophy of the original ArmA and ARMA 2, Arma 3 focuses on leaner and meaner -- less content, more features.  Where the Armories in ArmA and ARMA 2 were by far my favourite feature, unlocking all sorts of new things to play around with (in the same game mode: no campaign twinking here), the Virtual Reality training in Arma 3 is almost depressing, giving you little in the way of fun.  Even the Showcases, while impressive, are more of scenarios than any sandbox style of game.  While the Editor is just a few clicks away -- and much improved with the new Eden editor as of the 1.56 release -- out of the box you have to rely on the Workshop to get "random" play.
Where Arma 3 truly shines, however, is in pure unadulterated gameplay, with infinite improvements in the fluidity and stability of the game itself.  There's less of it to enjoy, but what's there is superior: ragdolling characters (rather than horrifically bad canned animations), better ballistics, smarter AI (within limits), gorgeous lighting and shadow effects, nighttime graphics that aren't a dozen desaturation filters, stance adjustments, a much improved sound engine, a lengthy campaign with halfway decent voice acting (whereas ARMA 2's was a fairly short campaign with... questionable acting), and so on.  Every piece of content that was missing from ARMA 2 comes back with a vengeance in the form of community mods like the Community Update Project, with only a few exceptions, and high quality Arma 3-only content mods fill in the gaps.  You might not have the same single player experience you could get out of ARMA 2, but you'll be so busy enjoying what you've got that you won't even care.

As expected with a classic Valve title, Team Fortress 2 is outstanding in quality, gameplay and more. You get to play as one of nine classes of troops in-game, each with their own special strenghts and weaknesses.

I'm gonna get slammed for this review, but you know me:
Arma 3 was recommended to me by a mutual friend at the time, so I looked into it, as well as insisting to pay $60 "the price of a full game" for a shooter that was released over 2 years ago.
I thought I would be amazed with Arma 3... I wasn't.
First strike, I was met with poor optimization and horrendous frame rate issues, even with the terrible looking standard graphics the maximum frames I could only achieve 27. I can already hear everyone shouting "You're PC is trash! Git gud, Stealth...Poorass." I will have you know that this is quite the machine I have with an AMD Radeon R7 370 Graphics.
Arma 3's single player offering is a joke. It's worse than Star Wars Battlefront EA singleplayer. After the first mission I just stopped. But then I tried Arma's multiplayer, what the game is praised for. Now I do respect that Arma 3 is supposed to be one of the most realistic military shooters on the market. But perhaps its a bit... too realistic... You're going to spend more time walking with your squad from point A to point B, getting lost and checking your map and compass often alot more than actually fighting in the game.- I've only been in 1 firefight. I would take Battlefield over Arma any day.
I was going to rate Arma 3 a 5. But gets held back to a 4/10 due to it's poor optimization, terrible AI, and dull gameplay.
This was my first refund on Steam and I couldn't be happier to get my full $60 back.
That's gonna do it for Arma 3 and I will see you on the next review. Let's form up! ~Stealth 1548

Hmm... Team Fortress 2?
Team Fortress 2, in my opinion, is probably one of the BEST FPS games out there due to it's style, how easy it is to get the hang of and of it's unique playstyle. Team Fortress 2 is one of those games which you can just never get enough of, but there's even more. To begin with, we have the play style. There's almost always a class that you'll love, I guarantee it. Some classes like scout require flanking, soldier requires being good at close combat, etc. The weapons which you can find/craft will most likely change your playstyle, too. If you go pyro, you'll usually just W+M1 to kill enemies but with the backburner, a weapon which does critical damage to people's backs, you'll have to be sneaky. Next up, the hats, probably the most known thing in Team Fortress 2. I mean, TF2 is free to play, but I'd personally invest a few dollars to get some cosmetics for most of your classes, as long as you play them. It isin't necessary, but it's much more nicer to have a cool looking class than just no hats. (don't think anyone is a noob if they don't have hats, they could be pubstomping on a regular basis!) Also, don't buy cosmetics from the mann co store, it's way too overpriced, just buy a cheap 50 cent item to become a premium player, which includes the mann co cap (kinda ugly, but good to at least start with) a backpack which can carry much more (+250 slots, I'm pretty sure) and you can get all blueprints, trading cards, etc. I don't want to spoil all the fun you can have in this amazing game, so try it out!

So being an arma fan from Operation Flash Point this seemed like a no brainer purchase. So today i did my first real online expierence.
So i joined a server and pretty much right away it got restarted with a new mission. It started with a bloke telling me to not assaign myself to somehting or ill be kicked. What a douch right?.... After about 3 or 4 minutes we see sight of a tank, a team mate of mine gets knocked too the ground and i find myself (as the medic in the team) dragging my team mate behind a building whist the rest of the squad are shooting away.
We then move up to our objective which is to capture a Forward Operating Base on top of a hill. As we start to walk up the hill we come to across another fire team like ours on this huge map being commanded by the same guy and hiding in the grass as the were being targeted by a attack chopper. Later on on different missions we had Air support dropping bombs on targets we requested (controlled by other players), Air drops of ammo and medevacs. There is a vast scenario created by players who want to be as envolved as the rest of the players. if your looking for a more grown "Battlefield" then i think this is worth the money.

While taking quite a few steps backwards, Saints Row The Third manages to eclipse its predecessor in most of the critical categories.  Gunplay has massively improved and sits comfortably around being enjoyable and slightly repetitive.  Weapons, although less in quantity, have greater variety in their functionality.  Vehicles of all types still exist (including boats, helicopters, airplanes and even VTOLs) with the same customization system as Saints Row 2.  Overall, enough of the critical content remains and the gameplay has been refined.
Significant steps taken backward must be noted however.  The in-game cinematics are a travesty compared to its sibling; the animations are stunted, the choreography uninspired, the humor patently missing and the "edge" completely amiss.  Mission replay is gone.  Character customization is paltry, emphasizing outfits over individual pieces.  This list continues for quite some time, outfitting Saints Row The Third was a hard blemish.

Quick side-note before getting into the actual review: if you're having issues with load times, move the game over to an SSD if you have one. The poor optimization combined with the game seemingly loading the entire world at once (or at least a large portion is being loaded) leads to connection time-outs and "running man" on a computer that should otherwise handle even the reccomended specs by a large margin. This might not fix the issue for everyone since sometimes the game just hangs/freezes due to actual bugs, but I haven't seen this suggestion anywhere else online and I wanted to share what worked for me with everyone else.
It took me ~10 hours of "game time" to get this to work (see above SSD comment), but once I did manage to get it to function, I was thoroughly satisfied with the game. As buggy and non-functional as the game can be at times (or as the community might have you believe "LITERALLY ALL OF THE TIME, HOW DID HE HEADSHOT ME?! RAGE), it's rather fun and has something to do for mulitple types of playstyles. Most take the "Kill" part of "King of the Kill" and latch onto that aspect of the game (i.e hunting/PvP), but for myself I like playing a bit of a different minigame: I prefer playing
.
The game isn't NEARLY as fun or skill oriented in solo play (still fun and definitely more intense, though). Get a duo buddy or find a group if you can help it. I have had so many laughs just looting and driving around the map. The most monotonous activities and moments in KotK (there is a lot of dead time between gas rounds) become so much better when you're on voice comms with a full team of 5 and one person randomly blows up a barrel in the background without saying anything. Thanks, Dylan. Always keeping the team on our toes. Good thinking.
Overall, I would rate KotK at about 6.5 out of 10 Review Units™. One caveat to ALL of this is that this game is absolutely not worth 20 dollars. Wait for a sale (at the time of writing, there is a weeklong sale going on at 40% off ($12 USD), which is the price this game should be listed at). If you can help it, do not buy this product at full price. It's far too unpolished and it's also in Early Access. As fun as it is, and as many hours as I've logged now and plan to in the future, I can't justify such a high price for what is a multiplayer-only, single-mode game. There's no content outside of gameplay; keep this in mind.
Good luck with your purchase and your gameplay.

A suggestion I would make is get familiar with the game, If you don't already know how to use your compass or read a map, then go learn how to do that. It's not that hard at all. Once you find yourself to be comfortable with your knowledge of the game then go find a Milsim unit. That in my opinion is the best way to experience the game. Having huge amounts of players doing opreations in Arma 3 is one of the best things you'll ever see in gaming. Especially when you have Infantry, Tanks, Jets, and Helicopters all working together. Hmm... Team Fortress 2?
Team Fortress 2, in my opinion, is probably one of the BEST FPS games out there due to it's style, how easy it is to get the hang of and of it's unique playstyle. Team Fortress 2 is one of those games which you can just never get enough of, but there's even more. To begin with, we have the play style. There's almost always a class that you'll love, I guarantee it. Some classes like scout require flanking, soldier requires being good at close combat, etc. The weapons which you can find/craft will most likely change your playstyle, too. If you go pyro, you'll usually just W+M1 to kill enemies but with the backburner, a weapon which does critical damage to people's backs, you'll have to be sneaky. Next up, the hats, probably the most known thing in Team Fortress 2. I mean, TF2 is free to play, but I'd personally invest a few dollars to get some cosmetics for most of your classes, as long as you play them. It isin't necessary, but it's much more nicer to have a cool looking class than just no hats. (don't think anyone is a noob if they don't have hats, they could be pubstomping on a regular basis!) Also, don't buy cosmetics from the mann co store, it's way too overpriced, just buy a cheap 50 cent item to become a premium player, which includes the mann co cap (kinda ugly, but good to at least start with) a backpack which can carry much more (+250 slots, I'm pretty sure) and you can get all blueprints, trading cards, etc. I don't want to spoil all the fun you can have in this amazing game, so try it out!

Oh man. Where to even begin with this one. It would be an extreme disservice to simply call Arma 3 a shooter, as it is so, so much more than that. Arma 3 is a military simulator. This is a distinction that it’s developers hold sacred and are proud of, and one to which I can attest is completely accurate and deserved. But it’s even more than that. Arma 3 is a gaming platform, upon which so much has already been and will continue to be built for years to come.
At its core though, Arma 3 in a supremely excellent military sim. The graphics are stunning, the gameplay is excellent, the mechanics are solid, and Bohemia Interactive has done an absolutely amazing job packaging this all together. New comers to the Arma series (as I was) may initially be overwhelmed by the game’s complex mechanics and decidedly different pace from your typical FPS/shooter. Enemy engagements happen at much greater distance than is typical in the genre and are often brief, brutal, and more times than not will conclude with your demise. There is no handholding here. No mini-maps, no enemy UI icons/indicators, no hit markers, no health bars. If you get shot a couple of times, you will find yourself unceremoniously dispatched. While this creates a high barrier for entry and a steep learning curve for new players, it provides a unique and distinctive play style. Situational awareness, cover, teamwork, suppressive fire, and generally moving purposefully and as if your♥♥♥♥♥depended on knowing what was behind the next ridge or hiding in the bushes are paramount to your success. Add to these infantry mechanics the amazingly rendered vehicles, armor, helicopters, and planes, each with their own realistic mechanics to learn and master, and you end up with a truly amazing military simulation experience.
Out of the box, Arma comes with a great single player campaign comprised of 3 separate acts, each containing ~12-15 missions. The campaign focuses on a well crafted story of a military conflict that has erupted over Arma 3’s two HUGE islands of Stratis and Altis. You play the part of a NATO soldier who finds himself stuck in the middle of a complex engagement. The campaign is rewarding, and challenging. (I have yet to complete it as I’m stuck on one mission that I simply can’t seem to complete.)
However the single-player campaign is FAR from the end of this title. The mission editing tools have allowed this amazing community to develop some absolutely awesome single player missions, all of which can be downloaded free of charge from the Steam workshop and numerous other sites around the interwebs. I would also recommend you check out the supremely excellent full game conversion single player mods Whole Lotta Altis and Dynamic Universal War System which will provide countless additional single player hours and could be completely stand alone titles in themselves.

Q. What is Arma 3? Is it like Counter Strike or Battlefield?
A. Nope. Its more akin to GTA or Saints Row, but with realism instead.
Q. Say what? It's open world with missions and stuff?
A.  Yes, totes!
Q. So it isn't an FPS?
A. It can be played first or third person.
Q. What stuff can I do?
A. You can use tanks, apc's, helicopters, boats, submarines, cars, jets, UAV's, rocket launchers, machine guns, grenades, command troops, and a whole bunch more.
Q. And game modes?
A. There is a campaign with a storyline, there are single scenarios you can play, there is multiplayer with all kinds of co-op or competitive gameplay and there is even a mission editor and extensive mod support.
That means the community (and you!) can create any scenario you have in mind in the editor and play it in singleplayer, multiplayer, against other players or AI.
Q. Wait.. what? I can make my own stuff and play it with friends?
A. I know, right!
Q. So.. how would you rate it?
A. 7.9 aubergines - get it!

This game is a really fun game. The game can look beautiful if you have the hardware to run it, and it shows how complex PC games can be. Though, I do have some problems that are listed along with the good things.
Pros:
-Encourages teamwork
-A very realistic simulator
-great graphics
-Very fun and easy to role play
-Many game modes made by the developers and community
-Includes useful controls such as using alt to look around without moving your aim
-no microtransactions like most triple A games have
-gives you thr zues DLC for free
Cons:
-HORRIBLE Helicopter contorls, though thats a given for a pc game
-A lot of players on the role play servers such as altis life RDM instead of actually role playing
-the optimization is the WORST (I have a gtx 970, and on ultra, I only get 20 to 30 fps. compared to the witcher three, on ultra with hairworks and V sync on I get 45 and maybe 30)
-Some players do mic spam, which is a problem in a lot of games including this one
-Third person is unfair, and ruins some of the role play, like being able to see over walls and such
Other thoughts:
Although this is a simulation game, I just want to give people a disclaimer. Since this is a simulation game, there won't be as much action as games like battlefield and insurgency. Another disclaimer, as someone who really likes large scale battles in urban areas, this wouldn't be the game for you, unless you stayed in the cities for most of the time. From what I've experienced, all of the main battles take place during your travel to a place such as a checkpoint or a city.

Madness. But also honest. SRTT is a GTA3-style game (you know how GTA3 plays right?) that goes overboard with excess (side missions are integrated into the plot through po-faced absurdity, customizations, weapons and upgrades are all impressive, and the story missions themselves (skydiving onto a high-rise penthouse to Kanye West's "Power" is a fitting example in all senses)). Also, much peurile humour.
Don't mistake all of the above as sociopathy, because the game's earnesty about excess is far more comfortable for me to grasp than the attitude of other games, where my guy will try to be moral and human during a dialogue only moments after schooting hundreds of men in the face. There's also an uncomfortable dark side; one "humourous" mission is set in a sex club, which seems far more sinister in retrospect since my guy (a woman) woke up naked and drugged after being sold as a sex slave, with strong implications that she was♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ The game is much more mature than it lets on.

The Good: Entertaining story with well written characters, graphics look amazing in DirectX 11, lots of things to do, tons of customization options, huge open world that is full of life, radio stations are great to listen to, crazy, crazy, crazy
The Bad: Side missions can be very difficult, way too many enemies to shoot, ragdoll physics are annoying, may offend some people, look ugly in DirectX 9
A game claiming it's one of the craziest around is something that would be hard to live up to. Thankfully Saint's Row: The Third does and man is it crazy. Parachuting out of planes, shooting tanks while falling out of the sky, God of War style boss fights in virtual reality, beating people up with giant purple ♥♥♥♥♥♥? Yeah, I'd say that's crazy, but The Third offers even more!
The story is really great with awesome characters and witty dialog. Johnny Gat dies in the beginning mission (that's no spoiler), but returning characters like Pierce and Shaundi return, and the new characters are just as great such as the bit brute Oleg and the nerd Kenzie. This time around you are famous and the Saint's own the city, but they lose it because three new gangs move into town: The Morningstar, Deckers, and Luchadores. A para-military group STAG has also moved in with heavily armored guys, tanks, and VTOL's (jets) that, yes you can fly and keep in your garage.
A lot of the story missions are interesting and completely varied to help deliver this interesting and entertaining story. From going inside a super computer and fighting as a walking toilet, blow-up doll, or fighting in a Luchadore match, and shooting cars with a rocket launcher from a helicopter, to just running around and killing everything is a huge blast and each mission is different. Of course there are side missions such as Trailblazing where you drive around in a fireproof suit on an ATV and run into people and cars to blow them up to earn seconds on a clock as you blow through a checkpoint race. There are other side missions that let you pimp your girls around, Insurance Fraud lets you get hit by cars to earn money, Mayhem lets you use pre-determined weapons to cause as much destruction as possible and a lot more. My favorite are the Genki matches which is like a gladiator type game show. There is no shortage of things to do in The Third with collectibles to be found, assassination missions, car theft missions, and tons of challenges.
Saint's Row doesn't stop there with a ton of cars to drive as well as a bunch of customization options for building your character, upgrading and decking out cars, to a crap ton of upgrades, for you and your guns even. You can use your phone to call in homies to help you fight, deliver vehicles, and even customize how your gang looks and taunts. You can run around and buy property to increase your respect rating and how much control you have over that territory.
But what about the world you play in you say? It looks amazing with DirectX 11 features exclusive to PC which makes the game look ten times better than that of the consoles and the world is huge and bursting at the seams with life. The game never looks boring, feels boring, or sounds boring with great radio stations with funny commercials, and even one radio station dedicated to Adult Swim. I just can't describe how crazy this game is because you have to play it to experience it. The controls are silky smooth with great car control, and even aircraft control nicely. Is there anything wrong with the game? Yeah there are some irritating issues like ragdoll physics when you get blown up, there are way too many enemies to kill, and the side missions are extremely difficult, but these things can be easily overlooked. If you love open world games I would say Saint's Row: The Third is the best out there and there really isn't anything quite like it.

I'm going to start off by saying that this game is great.
A little background information: I joined steam a few years ago just to buy h1z1. i payed $20 and have racked up 2000+ hours in h1z1. (since the game split into two seperate games: 1300 hours in just survive 700+ hours and counting on KOTK) All of my hours have been spent playing Battle Royales. 2000 hours of fun for the price of a 3 hour movie.
This game is great for all types of people. survivors (camp till last alive), killers (kill everyone you see!), casual gamers, tryhard gamers, groups of friends etc.
The basics of this game are very simple: Land from the sky with a parachute, grab a gun, kill people. done.
Skill is a huge factor in King Of The Kill. For the most part. In a perfect world (no Dsync, no lag, etc.) the player with better aim wins. but this is not a perfect world. Lag and Dsync are a part of most games, some more than others, deal with it.
RNG is also a huge factor in this game.
example: you land in a two story house and only find an R380 while another player lands at a trailer just out back of your house, finds an AR15, a shotty, a helmet and a lammy
Daybreak has done an amazing job with this game. I'm not saying that this game is perfect, it's far from perfect.
Here are the 3 things that should be focused on during updates instead of new hitmarkers and vehicle HUD are:
Dsync: This is probably the biggest thing that needs to be fixed. Focus on making the game accurate. If i shoot someone in the head, i expect to knock off their helmet or get a headshot. it's as simple as that.
The Shotgun: the shotgun is very unpredictable and unreliable at times. everyone has experienced a time where they wish they would have just hipfired with an ar instead of pulling out a shotgun from 2 feet away and pumping someone directly in the chest just to damage them for 22 health.
Ping Lock: the ping lock will be introduced in this patch, hopefully we see improvements and everyone plays on their own servers :)
We have to keep in mind that this game is still in early access and it's thrived to become one of the top games played. I cant wait for the finished product of this game.

6. A3 has some features that should be in everygame such as some AI behaviour. The AI flees, loots dead bodies and uses abandoned vehicles. Human instinct!
I'm trying to keep this review short so i will stop it there and get on with the small list of cons...

1. I know I said AI behaviour was a pro but it can also be a con. My teamates wont heal me unless I order them. There pathfinding is awful and sometimes dont budge at all.
2. All that needs to be said is an AI (Hostile) can spot me looking at them.. Lying one 1 Kilometre  out in a ghille suit...
3. Some of the physics are cancer. Hit a rock and get launched backawards. Legit.
Summing ARMA 3 up its a flagship for simulators but AI needs to catch up with the standared of the game.

This is my review on ARMA 3. At the time of this review I have capped over 2,000 hours on the game.
Pros:
1. A front runner in Military simulation further improvved with Mods.
2. Stunning graphics. (Especially with Mods)
3. A3 hosts a great multiplayer community, with plenty of Game Modes & new ones being developed constantly.
4. Plenty of MODS to improve gameplay and extend the games life span.
5. DLC's are mostly free. Most features are just platform updates. Sadly the biggest features of DLC packs are paid.
6. A3 has some features that should be in everygame such as some AI behaviour. The AI flees, loots dead bodies and uses abandoned vehicles. Human instinct!
I'm trying to keep this review short so i will stop it there and get on with the small list of cons...
Cons:
1. I know I said AI behaviour was a pro but it can also be a con. My teamates wont heal me unless I order them. There pathfinding is awful and sometimes dont budge at all.
2. All that needs to be said is an AI (Hostile) can spot me looking at them.. Lying one 1 Kilometre  out in a ghille suit...
3. Some of the physics are cancer. Hit a rock and get launched backawards. Legit.
Summing ARMA 3 up its a flagship for simulators but AI needs to catch up with the standared of the game.

ARMA is absolutely one of my all time favorite games . I have yet to find a military simulator as good as this one. Having said that this game has two major problems. Number one performance. It doesn't matter what graphics card you have. You will seldom have more than 30 frames per second. It doesn't matter if you have Titans running in SLI The game will struggle to get more than 40 frames per second at most.This is mainly due to poor optimization Especially with multi core CPUs. This is something that really needs to be fixed. However it does not hinder game play as much as you think since This game is a lot slower pace than most FPS games This is due to the fact that real war is rather slow. Second problem Is DLC While this game does have some really good DlC Such as the upcoming one That includes an entirely new map. A lot of the DLC is Somewhat annoying Take for instance The marksman DLC All of the marksman weapons are in the game and Can be used without purchasing the DLC however they can only be used for a limited time before you must purchase the DLC. Think of Grand Theft Auto and add humor and cusomizations galore to the mix and you have yourself a fun game. You can make your character anything you want him/her to be from a purple nudist to a gigantic bobblehead in pimped out threads. The campaign itself is a good 12 hours, but if you add the DLC to the mix and get to 100%, you have an additional 13 hours making the game about 25+ hours of enjoyment. You can choose to replay some of the quirky missions if you like and once you've played for long enough and there isn't much to do, you can buy god mode and infinite ammo to just screw around (but be warned, once you save it, you CANNOT TAKE THE OVERPOWERED PERKS AWAY!). A lot of big name voice actors are in here as well and the in-game radio contains exceptional music.

H1Z1: King of the Kill is a battle royal game made by Daybreak. It's been in early access for almost 2 years now and the progress for this game have been, and still is slow. It seems like the devs are working when they feel like. With all the money they got, they can do whatever they want. This scares me since the game is really broken atm.
It seems like they are listening more to the community now and pushes out more updates frequently. The cause for this is that there is a new competitor on the market. That game is called Player Unkown's Battlegrounds. A far superior game in my opinion, since the devs are working on it non stop and listening to the community.
The idea for this game is great and if they work on it on a regular basis, I think it might turn out to be pretty good. So what is H1Z1: King of the Kill? The game is a typical battle royal game, where 160 players are parachuted over a big map, where the goal is to be the last man standing. You scavenge for weapons, ammo, armour and other resources to get the advantage of your enemy. The game feels very arcade-ish, where you for example can drive top speed in a car, jump out and shotgun someone in the face. There are a lot of WTF moments where you suddenly getting one-shotted from a guy you clearly have the advantage over. It feels like everything is based on luck and not skill, since there a so many cheese-factors in the game. The winner is always the guy who is hoarding the most helmets, kevs, medkits etc.
The game is of course fun to play with a friend or in a squad, and if you don't mind the mediocre frame rate and server stabilty it can be fun. It need proper balance tho, since some weapons are OP atm and the end game is always "car warfare", where everyone is driving cars and jumps out like a super human and kills everyone. It's not fair in my opinion, and I want a game which is a tad more realistic. Graphics are great, gameplay is ok when it works, but balance and rework is everything to get this game functional again.
I'm going to stay updated and I hope they finish this game, since it got  potentials!

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding cheese cake recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1 cup digestive plain sweet biscuit crumbs
3 tablespoons sugar
3 tablespoons melted butter
40 ounces softened cream cheese
1 cup sugar
3 tablespoons flour
1 tablespoon vanilla
1 cup sour cream
4 eggs
Directions:
For The base:.
If you're using a dark pan, preheat the oven to 350. If you are using a shiny pan, 375.
Combine the crumbs, melted butter and 3 tbsp sugar well and pat onto the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan. I also like to very very lightly butter the sides of the pan so that the cheesecake will not stick later on.
Bake for 10 mins in your preheated oven and remove. Let it cool while you prepare your batter.
For the batter:.
Make sure everything is at room temperature.
Combine sugar, cheese, flour and vanilla in a big bowl and mix on medium speed till well combined. Don't forget to scrape the bowl as you're doing this.
Mix in the sour cream till its incorporated well. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing well after each addition.
Pour the batter into the springform and let it bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes After the baking time, turn off the oven and leave the door ajar. Let the cake cool in there for about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the cake and let it cool thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Release the sides of the springform.
Eat.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding cheese cake recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1 cup digestive plain sweet biscuit crumbs
3 tablespoons sugar
3 tablespoons melted butter
40 ounces softened cream cheese
1 cup sugar
3 tablespoons flour
1 tablespoon vanilla
1 cup sour cream
4 eggs
Directions:
For The base:.
If you're using a dark pan, preheat the oven to 350. If you are using a shiny pan, 375.
Combine the crumbs, melted butter and 3 tbsp sugar well and pat onto the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan. I also like to very very lightly butter the sides of the pan so that the cheesecake will not stick later on.
Bake for 10 mins in your preheated oven and remove. Let it cool while you prepare your batter.
For the batter:.
Make sure everything is at room temperature.
Combine sugar, cheese, flour and vanilla in a big bowl and mix on medium speed till well combined. Don't forget to scrape the bowl as you're doing this.
Mix in the sour cream till its incorporated well. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing well after each addition.
Pour the batter into the springform and let it bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes After the baking time, turn off the oven and leave the door ajar. Let the cake cool in there for about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the cake and let it cool thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Release the sides of the springform.
Eat.

From developer and published Valve, comes Team Fortress 2. Released all the way back in 2007, TF2 has been a popular game for ten years now for many different reasons. With more players joining every day, there’s something about TF2 that keeps bringing players back for more.
Maybe it’s the 500+ achievements that prove to be a challenge for all achievement hunters out there. Maybe it’s the hats and upgrades constantly being added to the game over time. Maybe it’s the constant servers always online for players to head online and battle each other.
With servers all over proving to be a challenge for even experienced players, there’s somewhere for everyone. There’s a class for everyone to play and there’s things all the time for people to enjoy. There are numerous different maps and play types.
I personally love this game because each round is something new. There’s never a round that is exactly the same. I love playing this game both with my friends and without my friends. There’s never a dull moment. Although a simple team versus team game, there is a lot of strategy that’s needed. You really need to think about things, and you can’t just go flying into battle. (Well, you can, but usually it ends in you being killed countless times.)
Each round lasts approximately 10 minutes, without overtime. With numerous different types of levels to play, there’s sure to be one for you that you enjoy. I personally love King of the Hill and Payload. I find them really challenging, especially when it’s a full team of 12 versus 12.
Of course, the in game chat can be really horrible at times, especially with such a prejudice to certain players and classes (new players are often screamed at, and some classes are just hated for their roles in the game – snipers, spies and pyros mostly). Also on some maps, if you play the game how you’re meant to, people will have a go because they’d rather have a death match (rather than play the level, get the experience and move on with the game and their lives). However, I’ve met some lovely people on the in game chat, and you’d be surprised at how many people are actually happy to help the new players out with tips and tricks in team chat.
Overall, this is a really fun game if you like shooters. It’s fun to play online with your friends, it’s fun to play without your friends, and it’s one of those that really gets you thinking on strategy. I really recommend this to everyone who likes to play shooters, and it’s definitely a massive challenge for achievement hunters. (I’ve played 29 hours, and I still only have 18 out of 520 achievements.)

When the GTA series started becoming more serious, the Saints Row series chose to appease the other half of us by becoming more ridiculous and over the top. Saints Row the Third is as whacky, immature and over the top as it gets, giving you absurdly powerful rewards in a short time, loads of upgradeable weapons, tons of car mod opportunities and an un-hindered tag along co-op mode, allowing for even higher levels of hilarity with a friend. The story however may feel disjointed and lack context at times, plus, some will find their rewards less special because they get so many so quickly. That isn't always bad however, because some of us just want to start going nuts as quick as possible, taking to the streets with a friend and delivering an underhanded rocket launcher swing to the groin of a man wearing a mascot costume. This game is not for the easily offended or those who like a slow boil, but it welcomes those like myself who was bored by GTA4's lack of sandbox wonder.

In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I’ve been turning over in my mind ever since.
“Whenever you feel like criticizing any one,” he told me, “just remember that all the people in this world haven’t had the advantages that you’ve had.”
He didn’t say any more, but we’ve always been unusually communicative in a reserved way, and I understood that he meant a great deal more than that. In consequence, I’m inclined to reserve all judgments, a habit that has opened up many curious natures to me and also made me the victim of not a few veteran bores. The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person, and so it came about that in college I was unjustly accused of being a politician, because I was privy to the secret griefs of wild, unknown men. Most of the confidences were unsought — frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions. Reserving judgments is a matter of infinite hope. I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.
And, after boasting this way of my tolerance, I come to the admission that it has a limit. Conduct may be founded on the hard rock or the wet marshes, but after a certain point I don’t care what it’s founded on. When I came back from the East last autumn I felt that I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever; I wanted no more riotous excursions with privileged glimpses into the human heart. Only Gatsby, the man who gives his name to this book, was exempt from my reaction — Gatsby, who represented everything for which I have an unaffected scorn. If personality is an unbroken series of successful gestures, then there was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life, as if he were related to one of those intricate machines that register earthquakes ten thousand miles away. This responsiveness had nothing to do with that flabby impressionability which is dignified under the name of the “creative temperament.”— it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again. No — Gatsby turned out all right at the end; it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams that temporarily closed out my interest in the abortive sorrows and short-winded elations of men.
My family have been prominent, well-to-do people in this Middle Western city for three generations. The Carraways are something of a clan, and we have a tradition that we’re descended from the Dukes of Buccleuch, but the actual founder of my line was my grandfather’s brother, who came here in fifty-one, sent a substitute to the Civil War, and started the wholesale hardware business that my father carries on to-day.

This game is a sinful waste of a fantastic idea. This game started with genuine potential and brilliant ideas. When I started playing it, it was by far the buggiest game I had ever played, but I saw the potential. I won't completely reiterate what hundreds of people have already said, but they completely destroyed this game. As others have said, it started with the changing of hands to Daybreak. Daybreak is simply milking this game for all it is worth. The game had very solid, raw gameplay (raw in a good way). But instead of fixing bugs, they added skins. And instead of getting a clean version out for a release, they 're-released' the game (yet it is still in EA). Splitting the game was potentially great. I for one didn't care for the zombie side, so a focused Battle Royale game was exciting. Their obvious and biggest mistake was their huge 're-release' update. They replaced the original map which was FANTASTIC and again 'raw' with a glossed up piece of crap: Z2. The new UI was complicated without necessity. The old UI had some oustanding flaws which could have easily been patched up, but instead they replaced it with an even more flawed UI. I am just appalled by what has become of this game.
TLDR: This game was a fantastic idea. The raw, simplistic style that made this game so great was destroyed by marketing. Developer focus transitioned from true development to a marketing tool. Don't waste your time with this game anymore.
PS: I have all 3 green dawns (all legit), and I have 1k hours on H1Z1 (500+ hours pre-split). I truly feel bad for anyone who didn't get to experience this game pre-split. It was on the road to being a historical classic.

I was a little worried about a game published by THQ since "Space Marine" came out, but I have to admit that I am pleasantly and extremely impressed with "Saints Row the Third".
Though the game is incredibly wacky and spoofy, it also brings home some important and realistic points about crime and gang life that I think bring a little maturity to the game. There's plenty of things to do, though once you've done them, you'll definitely have your favorites and your "Damn, I have to do this one AGAIN??".
The story and atmosphere are great, and I haven't seen many other games that weren't full-on RPGs that had this level of detail for a city. I would compare the level of detail to that found in "Batman: Arkham City" and "TES: Skyrim", but "SR3" has a very unique style all on its own. The game mixes RPG, arcade, and 3rd-person shooter elements that combine in awesome ways. See for yourself.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

ARMA 3 is a great game if you don't like having fun, like me.
You're going to be fed bitter morsels of fun only after suffering like Sisyphus. But unlike Sisyphus, you will eventually succeed and the fleeting moment of victory will be much better as a result of your misery. It's even better when the suffering is compounded by playing with friends. After multiple restarts because a BDRM annihilated you with pinpoint accuracy from 3 miles away, you'll have a great time.
The main problem with this game is that it's set in 2035 and you're fighting Post-Human Space Iranians in a tank from the 70s. Thankfully, this game is supported by an excellent modding community and you can use mods to take the game back to the greatest era of human history; The Cold War. You might not get the chance to die on the atomic battlefields of the North German plains, but you can get pretty close to it thanks to this game and the dedication of the modding community.
Eventually, you will reach the mod singularity where you will simply have too many mods. You will spend hours in virtual arsenal making the perfect loadout. You will think  "Finally I create a decent depiction of an Iraqi republican guardsman circa 1991!" but you will feel nothing.
Thanks to this game I have had to confront the existential horror of consciousness, and I would recommend it to anyone.

Most realistic war / military game ever. The game is very easy to mod and the community has ended up making some very fun gamemodes and a variety of mods. Some of my favorite custom gamemodes are "Altis Life" and "King of the Hill". This game also has a ton of realism units  / milsim units that do custom missions. Even though this game has been out for three years, it is still being worked on with new updates, maps, etc. The map "Tanoa" is expected to come out sometime this year, and they just released the "Eden 3D Editor" a couple days ago.
Overall this game is amazing. With the surplus of mods and gamemodes this game never gets old. If you are interested in buying this game you will need a good computer to run it. Some servers have custom veichles and other things that drops your FPS low. Also, this isn't like most games where you can just go play for 15 or 30 minutes. For gamemodes like "Altis Life", I usually set aside 3-5 hours to play. But I'd give this game a 10/10 for the realism, and the easy access to mods.

This game is pretty much an essential for any FPS player, but i must warn you:
If you are just starting the game for the first time, DON'T waste all of your money on random hats. But if you do decide to buy hats or other things, USE THE STEAM MARKET, not the in-game store. You'll end up paying 10 bucks for Bonk Boy, when you could just go to the market and buy a STRANGE bonk boy for about 50 cent to 1$. But here's something even better! You can use sites like Backpack.tf and Scrap.tf to buy and sell items for keys and refined metal, which you can use to open crates and buy unusuals. But i have another warning for you: you either need to be a professional trader or a professional scammer to get an unusual. It will most likely take you WEEKS to trade for enough keys for an unusual. You could buy one with your money, but you could end up paying 200 bucks for a hat with a bubbling effect. But enough ranting, it's a great game for a free fps, and i highly recommend you check it out if you haven't already.

The sequel to one of the greatest (the greatest imo) military games of all time. Does it deliver? I'd say yes. Most of the time. First of all, the game is better optimized and as a result the performance, at least in my experience, is a lot better. Naturally the game looks better too. Of course, you're probably not gonna buy the game for the base experience. You'll buy it for all the mods and gamemodes available (like Life and Breaking Point or Exile). I can confirm it's definitely worth getting it for that. But, while the game did improve on 9/10 fronts, like for example, the gunplay is better, the weapons are costumizable, the physics, while not perfect are at least present; the game to me lacks a certain feeling. It's something that I can't put my finger on exactly, but I can try to describe it. When I'm trying to decide if I should play an Arma 2 mod or an Arma 3 mod, nine times out of ten, I'll go with Arma 2. For some reason, that game feels better and has that "x-factor", Arma 3 doesn't. Take this with a huge grain of salt. This whole last part might not apply to you.

Saints Row The Third carries on with the same theme as the previous in the series only a bit more crazy. The amount of upgrades built into this game is just amazing, from upgrades to guns and cars, to upgrades that effect you as a player like no fall damaged and the ability to recieve no damage cause by bullets, the list goes on. The story to this game on the other hand has it's ups and downs. On the possitive side it does keep you entertained and lets you follow the story and doesn't branch out of control. Unlike the previous Saints Row this one doesn't let you pick which gang you would like to get rid of first, the three gangs in the game are in all essence one big gang working togther, this is the reason for the linear story line which in my mind was a bad idea however the story does use this very well. Overall this game doesn't let the franchise down but shows us a good amount of what could be comming in the future.

When the GTA series started becoming more serious, the Saints Row series chose to appease the other half of us by becoming more ridiculous and over the top.  Saints Row the Third is as whacky, immature and over the top as it gets, giving you absurdly powerful rewards in a short time, loads of upgradeable weapons, tons of car mod opportunities and an un-hindered tag along co-op mode, allowing for even higher levels of hilarity with a friend.  The story however may feel disjointed and lack context at times, plus, some will find their rewards less special because they get so many so quickly.  That isn't always bad however, because some of us just want to start going nuts as quick as possible, taking to the streets with a friend and delivering an underhanded rocket launcher swing to the groin of a man wearing a mascot costume.  This game is not for the easily offended or those who like a slow boil, but it welcomes those like myself who was bored by GTA4's lack of sandbox wonder.

TF2 is a classic cartoonish FPS with a nostalgic feel and an immersive atmosphere. Gunplay is incredibly enjoyable and the map selection, and class options contribute to an overall enjoyable experience. In my opinion, Turbine CTF is the most enjoyable gamemode/map combination and playing scout or sniper is always a challenge. Overall, although some may view this game as outdated, it stands as one of the best FPS games on the market and with no price, it is a must-have. TF2's legacy will continue to live on as one of Valve's most successful games and it has absolutely earned such a title. I will likely continue to play this game for as a long as I have a computer that is capable of running it, which isn't difficult to have considering its graphics. I would reccomend TF2 to any gamer and all ages.

The game is very fun and can be played alone or in a team of 2 or 5 members. The goal is to survive until the end. Over 100 players start all over the map. After certain time intervals the map is made smaller and wrapped with lethal gas. All over the map are for example houses and campsites you can loot.
Pro:
- There are enough players so it will be exciting.
- Animations and player controls work fine and smooth.
- The map is well designed and provides almost everywhere loot places. Even if you end up somewhere away from cities you can find good equipment.
Cons:
- There are not enough weapons. Every round you try to loot an AR or AK and a shotgun. There is no greater selection.
- The rewards are not valuable and worth barely. The most valuable thing you win at the first places are two different bags. These bags contain 1 of only 5 skins. After a few conquer you unlocked everything.
- While playing you get randomly crates which can be opened by a key. But these keys are only available in H1Z1 Store and costs around 2.50 €.
Conclusion: Its really a funny game with normal graphics. If you are looking for fun alone or with friends, this game is perfect for in between. But if you're looking for a game where you want to achieve something (like a level), you are definitely wrong. I'm wondering what next updates would bring, because this game is still expandable.

PLAYERUNKNOWN'S Battlegrounds is a much more tactical style of battle royal game and cannot be compared to H1Z1, they just don't have anything in common except the type of game. This game has come so far over the past few months gaining major updates. People complaining about the Devs not working on the game are quite ignorant and uninforment this game recieves regular updates and the servers are being worked on constantly. The servers get reset weekly (you can go to Daybreak's website if you need proof of that). This game is fun, addicting, intense, and a great game to play with friends. There are issues with people from other countries with high ping playing on the wrong servers, but in my opinion that doesn't break the game it just gives a slight advantage which isn't all that much anyways. In conclusion the only real way to decide if this game is something you like is to try it for yourself. Steam has refunds now so why not.

I'd like to say before getting into this review that I currently as of righting this review I have about 330 hours on the game, and that may seem like a lot to some people, but I'm basically still considered a noob.
Arma 3 is a military simulator, you have it all; drone, helicopters, jets, infantry, boats, tanks, mortars, etc.
It's not one of those game you jump into and almost instantly understand, it takes a lot of time and dedication to get as good as some of the people who play it. If you're one for realistic bullet physics and a much more realistic games this is for you.
Most of the gamemodes you find will require mods you must download, they're super easy to install but if you download them off a launcher like A3 Launcher or WS Launcher it can take an extremely long time, especially if your internet speed isn't the greatest.
Optimization is not the best for this game, but you really can't do a lot about that right now, it's a huge open world game, with ranging map sizes and explosions, players, and mechanics working in the background, it's bound to have some issues. Though, I don't think that goes without saying it's flawless, it does have lots of issues too. I'd recommend going to YouTube and searching some optimization fixes, some are extremely easy and helpful, they can give you a boost of 30+FPS sometimes, which is amazing. I've also noticed some memory leaking in this game, if you do play for 12+ hours without rebooting the game you'll most likely crash, this is mostly an issue for people with lower amounts of Ram, that being 4-8GB, so that's something to look out for.
The single player in Arma 3 from what I played is actually really fun, I played some of the Arma 2 single player and got bored after the first few missions, but that's not the case with Arma 3, it seems to have a much better story to it and is definitly something you should try if you haven't already.
The only thing left I think I would like to talk about is the DLC, Arma 3's DLC is extremely over priced in my opinion.
It can bring a lot more fun to the game but it's also not worth the $15.99 for one of them. I do understand how modeling those guns, vehicles, and clothing isn't easy, I know first hand, but that doesn't mean it's worth $15.99 for one of them, it seems a little extreme for what you get. I also don't like the way they handle the DLC in the game, you can't pick up the guns and scopes in the game (Which is completely understandable) but for some reason they allow you to pick up the clothing like the ghillie suits, but once you do you get spammed with ads all over your screen, and there is also one that covers your crosshair and optics entirely so you have to either take of the suit or wait for it to go away.
Time for some pros and cons.
-Endless amounts of fun and hours to sink into this game
-Realisim
-Graphics are still good looking
-Good singleplayer
-Great Multiplayer experience
-Absolute tons of gamemodes to try out
-Lack of optimization in some aspects of the game
-Sometimes long download times for mods
-Memory leaks and crashes (On systems with low amounts of RAM)
-Expensive DLC
I'd like to finish by stating some of the gamemodes you guys should check out.
-King Of The Hill, it's a great multiplayer experience, I would suggest finding a lower pop server 30-40 people because more then that causes extremely low FPS.
-Sa-Matra Wasteland, Yes! You all need to try this, it's so much fun, so far my favorite gamemode in this entire game, it's not complete though without trying Chernarus map with it. It's fun on the default maps, but Chernarus just brings other light to the gamemode entirely. (Chernarus does require a big download, but Sa-Matra Wasteland on default maps does not.)
-BattleRoyale, this is also one of the best gamemodes to try. If you like the combat in DayZ, those tense moments where you're on the edge of your seat shaking, hoping to god you don't get shot then this is for you. It's extremely tense, especially when you're down to the last few remaining survivers.
-Arma 3 Life, it's not my cup of tea, but that doesn't mean it's not yours. I like watching people like FrankieonPC play the Life games, he makes them fun to watch for me, Anyways. It's all about working, you have to work for your money to buy a gun and do some epic things that Frankie does, it's an extremely grindy gamemode, but it could be also fun if you're into that sort of thing.
That's all guys, thanks for reading! I really hope you consider trying this out!

I'd like to say before getting into this review that I currently as of righting this review I have about 330 hours on the game, and that may seem like a lot to some people, but I'm basically still considered a noob.
Arma 3 is a military simulator, you have it all; drone, helicopters, jets, infantry, boats, tanks, mortars, etc.
It's not one of those game you jump into and almost instantly understand, it takes a lot of time and dedication to get as good as some of the people who play it. If you're one for realistic bullet physics and a much more realistic games this is for you.
Most of the gamemodes you find will require mods you must download, they're super easy to install but if you download them off a launcher like A3 Launcher or WS Launcher it can take an extremely long time, especially if your internet speed isn't the greatest.
Optimization is not the best for this game, but you really can't do a lot about that right now, it's a huge open world game, with ranging map sizes and explosions, players, and mechanics working in the background, it's bound to have some issues. Though, I don't think that goes without saying it's flawless, it does have lots of issues too. I'd recommend going to YouTube and searching some optimization fixes, some are extremely easy and helpful, they can give you a boost of 30+FPS sometimes, which is amazing. I've also noticed some memory leaking in this game, if you do play for 12+ hours without rebooting the game you'll most likely crash, this is mostly an issue for people with lower amounts of Ram, that being 4-8GB, so that's something to look out for.
The single player in Arma 3 from what I played is actually really fun, I played some of the Arma 2 single player and got bored after the first few missions, but that's not the case with Arma 3, it seems to have a much better story to it and is definitly something you should try if you haven't already.
The only thing left I think I would like to talk about is the DLC, Arma 3's DLC is extremely over priced in my opinion.
It can bring a lot more fun to the game but it's also not worth the $15.99 for one of them. I do understand how modeling those guns, vehicles, and clothing isn't easy, I know first hand, but that doesn't mean it's worth $15.99 for one of them, it seems a little extreme for what you get. I also don't like the way they handle the DLC in the game, you can't pick up the guns and scopes in the game (Which is completely understandable) but for some reason they allow you to pick up the clothing like the ghillie suits, but once you do you get spammed with ads all over your screen, and there is also one that covers your crosshair and optics entirely so you have to either take of the suit or wait for it to go away.
Time for some pros and cons.
-Endless amounts of fun and hours to sink into this game
-Realisim
-Graphics are still good looking
-Good singleplayer
-Great Multiplayer experience
-Absolute tons of gamemodes to try out
-Lack of optimization in some aspects of the game
-Sometimes long download times for mods
-Memory leaks and crashes (On systems with low amounts of RAM)
-Expensive DLC
I'd like to finish by stating some of the gamemodes you guys should check out.
-King Of The Hill, it's a great multiplayer experience, I would suggest finding a lower pop server 30-40 people because more then that causes extremely low FPS.
-Sa-Matra Wasteland, Yes! You all need to try this, it's so much fun, so far my favorite gamemode in this entire game, it's not complete though without trying Chernarus map with it. It's fun on the default maps, but Chernarus just brings other light to the gamemode entirely. (Chernarus does require a big download, but Sa-Matra Wasteland on default maps does not.)
-BattleRoyale, this is also one of the best gamemodes to try. If you like the combat in DayZ, those tense moments where you're on the edge of your seat shaking, hoping to god you don't get shot then this is for you. It's extremely tense, especially when you're down to the last few remaining survivers.
-Arma 3 Life, it's not my cup of tea, but that doesn't mean it's not yours. I like watching people like FrankieonPC play the Life games, he makes them fun to watch for me, Anyways. It's all about working, you have to work for your money to buy a gun and do some epic things that Frankie does, it's an extremely grindy gamemode, but it could be also fun if you're into that sort of thing.
That's all guys, thanks for reading! I really hope you consider trying this out!

Realistic? No. Fun to play? Yes.  Absurd?  Oh, god, yes.  Not many games can actually make me laugh out loud.  First the bad: The sandbox part of the game seems much more limited than SR2.  The world is probably the same size, but it feels smaller, and the limited number of 'collectibles' makes exploring less rewarding. It doesn't help that Steelport is a blighted hole that lacks the interesting realized neighborhoods that Stilwater had.  Yes, you can steal a taxi, ambulance, or fire truck, but nothing special comes of it.  Lastly, the game is haunted by the usual bugs that seem to survive restarting the game and may require you to restart your OS.
The good?  Well, it is fun!  It is funny!  I mean laugh-out-loud funny.  The overarching missions are a lot of fun, even though they're not as deep as they were in SR2. As with SR2, the soundtracks are good too (Hybrid!).  In the end, I recommend it, though I wouldn't pay more than $40 for it.

A sandbox game in the vein of Grand Theft Auto, with a few significant differences.  One of the best is, during a mission if you die, you have the option of restarting the mission in the same state as you were when you initially started it.  Additionally, longer missions have checkpoints you can restart from if you die/fail.  It is somewhat surprising how much better that small change makes the game.  You play a joyful psychopath, unrepetant for his or her actions, and reveling in the sort of absurdity these sorts of game make possible.  Add in huge character customization options, enjoyable combat, customizable vehicles and gang members, and great environment and you get an excellent game.

First of all, This game is amazing!
The graphics; fantastic. The amount of "stuff" to do; outstanding. The ability to run well on low end PC's; Ehh...
Anyways, this is Arma 3. It is a military shooter, which captured the realism of anything from Infantry Firefights to Drone warfare, and CAS runs.
Pros:
-Looks amazing on high graphics
-Amount of "Stuff" to do; amazing
-Modibility; 11/10 there are some amazing mods!!
-Community is Fairly decent
-A lot of effort put into this game as far as mechanics.
-Endless fun with friends
-All of the controls!!
Cons:
-All of the Controls!!
-!!!MAJOR LEARNING CURVE!!!! (as far as how to drive, fly, shoot, range targets, list goes on!)
-CPU and MRAM are a Major key to how well this game plays.
(Basically, the CPU, AND MRAM are what make this game playable. With a good i7, and 32 gigs of Ram, I was able to get 60 fps on Ultra settings with low terrain, and minimal post processing effects at 1080p [When I did not have GPU Yet; I now have a 980ti, and it still can be a bit buggy] But if you want good terrain, FXAA, Post processing, HDR, Bloom, All that good stuff, you must have a vary good GPU!!!!)
-Somewhat poorly optimized on multiplayer servers mainly. Singleplayer, peice of cake!
-Must have good Computer!!!!
-Very Time consuming. Like...... A lot.... I have 1,000 hours, and Idk how.
-DLC Watermarks >:(
Anyways, if you are even remotely considering of buying this game, DO IT!!
If you do, GET THE APEX DLC!!!! It is the best DLC out of all of them, but the map it adds is difficult to run, even for me. (1080) but looks amazing!!!

After playing for over 800+ hours in this game, I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a large scale combat simulator. The physics, penetration systems and weapon mechanics are a lot better than they were in ARMA II. However, with all of these things comes a new demand for processing power.
This game is VERY CPU intensive. I do not recommend playing this on AMD CPUs, mostly because it relies heavily on Intel's hyper-threading. I can play this pretty decently on my FX 4130, some of my friends play with an FX 8350, but there are a lot of performance bottlenecks. You get increased performance running on higher settings than running on lower settings. I'll explain why.
On lower settings, the game assumes your GPU is unable to handle the load. So I switches the dependency to render a lot of things on the CPU. By switching it to a higher setting, the engine balances the load off of your CPU to both the CPU and the GPU.
===============================================================
As far as gameplay, there are a lot of mods and scenarios, both outside of Workshop and in the Workshop. I spent hours playing around with these mods, Zeus and making little invade/defend scenarios. RHS, CUPS, MCC Alive, and ACE are the biggest ones if you are looking for the realism aspect. The editor is nice and easy to understand once you get the basics down, so you could create single player scenarios. I have not tried to mess with scripting or server-side scenarios. The community is somewhat decent sized and there's always something to play as far as multiplayer.
===============================================================
The downsides to this game can also have a -lack- of content. In comparison to ARMA II, there is not a lot of content as far as vehicles and weapons. The helicopters and marksman DLC is a nice addition to the game, but it still feels -empty-. I am hoping that in future DLCs, there will be newer weapons and vehicles. It feels like there was a lot more time focused on what the unit is wearing rather than what he's using to pump lead.
===============================================================
Wasteland was a lot more fun on ARMA II because everyone had a chance of getting good gear and vehicles, worked together to build bases and overall the team aspect was there. In ARMA III, not so much. It seems more like a really huge deathmatch map, little chance to get a vehicle outside of civilian cars, where everyone just runs to try to be the first one to camp the gun stores. There's really no team play in relation to doing missions except in rare occurences. Stratis is the lesser of two evils as far as the default maps are concerned. Altis is just way too huge, way too open and you end up traveling for hours to find somewhat decent gear in order to be disappointed by some guy who went to the vehicle store from all of his hard-earned cash from gun store camping to buy a tank or an attack chopper.
===============================================================
In Altis Life, the biggest game mode, it can be fun to an extent, but the hours of grinding to catch up with people already well off in terms of money who have been playing forever is nearly impossible. Ever since they implemented the gang system and made rebel gear the absolute end-game gear while civilians and police only get access to the garbage weapons, it makes the game a little unfair for those starting out. RDM is common and the servers are hit and miss on whether or not they are moderated. There is really no "RP" despite it being hailed as an RP game mode.
===============================================================
Invade & Annex (Spin off of Domination for ARMA II) is probably my favorite game mode. It requires team work and coordination to control AOs, some servers only allow gear depending on your role (I prefer playing a medic and playing support roles over assault/marksman), and not everyone just hops into a jet (Most servers require you be in TS to coordinate with surface units before bombing the♥♥♥♥♥♥danger close). Great game-mode if you are new and trying to learn the mechanics of the game.
===============================================================
King of the Hill is... okay. The factors that determine whether it's going to be fun, in my opinion, are:
A. It doesn't have vehicles outside of transports
B. Infantry-based
C. How many players are actually in the server
D. Does the server have an auto-balance
KOTH would be so much better if it were smaller scale, focused more on infantry combat and AO control, rather than which team is stacked the most against the others. By stacked, I mean:
BLUFOR: 5 Players
OPFOR: 28 Players
Independent: 16 Players
Once a team is stacked on the AO, there's really no chance to win. There's too much high ground and way too many places to camp an AO. It's even worse when offensive vehicles are involved, because these vehicles sit on the outskirts of combat, probably 1000+ meters away, with view distance turned up and thermals. It makes it really unfair for those people just starting off, even worse when it's an AA just camping the choppers coming out of a base.
===============================================================
Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a good experience just playing around with scenarios in single player or team-based game modes in multiplayer. The only thing I wish this community would do is make more objective-based game modes, like capture the flag, team deathmatch, or something that really puts infantry-based combat as priority over most multiplayer game-modes where whoever has the best gear, vehicles and numbers stacked against everyone else wins. In short, quality over quantity.

Experiences in ARMA 3:
1) Our arma regiment uses a modded server, including a new map, ace (which adds some depth to the medical system and some other nifty features), TaskForceRadio (people must be close to each other or have a radio at the correct frequency to communicate) a bunch of new items, vehicles etc.
The Zeus/GM/HQ/leader of the regiment who sets up and manipulates our scenarios on the fly gives us our next mission.
We're going to insert via helicopter near an enemy (All enemy is AI) base and take it over. We get our equipment together (I take medical supplies, as medic) and mount up.
We have our usual banter as we approach the landing site, our Zeus directs the AI pilots of the helo to land but the AI just keeps going, either because they think we are being shot at or because they can't figure out how to land at the designated point.
We're now passing over the point, going into enemy territory. I think our Zeus realises this and commands everyone to bail. Now we're being shot at, I start getting my parachute from the helicopter's inventory. Out of the corner of my eye, I see bullets light up the cockpit and one of the pilots slumps forward, the helicopter descends. I replace my backpack full of medical supplies with the parachute and prepare to jump... but now the helicopter is too low. If I jumped now, I'd probably fail to open my parachute soon enough and injure myself severely, so my only choice was to wait 'till the helicopter was low enough and just hope I don't get shot as I get out.
I dismount as it's about to touch the ground and bullets start smacking the helicopter from the side that I had gotten out. I quickly run around to the other side without taking any injuries. Our squad has landed in a clearing that is surrounded by forest, in a kind of Y shape, with our squad at the intersection of open area. We're all spread out along this clearing, and the enemy has surrounded us entirely. A couple of our men were already dying and more were going to follow. I hear over the radio our Zeus and another team leader call for a retreat back to the base, but with so many enemies around us, that was near impossible.
I stay behind the helicopter, trying to spot enemies from my position, but with only gunfire as my indicator, it was near impossible to know exactly where the bullets were coming from.
I remember that I've left all of my medical supplies in the helicopter, which I need since people are getting shot to♥♥♥♥♥♥ so I go up to the door and see if I can reach the inventory inside. I can't, unfortunately, so the only way I was going to get those supplies was to hop inside the back and expose myself to gunfire. One of my squad-mates, a marksman, obviously has the same idea, he probably left his ammunition and bandages behind after grabbing a parachute. He hops in and I follow suit, I quickly close the door, grab my bag and get out. Great, now I can actually be of some use, since I can't see where the ♥♥♥♥ these guys are shooting from (I could've used the map to see them, but I feel like that's kinda cheat-y).
I take a look around, still trying to spot enemies, but I just can't see them, so I give up trying to fight back and bolt it toward one of my team-mates (the marksman from before). (By this time, there were only like three or four of us left.) He was patching himself up, so I helped him out by bandaging him up a little. We're both switching between prone and crouching stances, trying to shoot the enemy and patch ourselves up as we get shot. Eventually, it's just us two, there's still gunfire, but it's died down a little. He turns to me "So, what do you think we should do?", I reply "I think we should just make a run for it".
And so we do.
He has more stamina than me, considering I'm carrying about 40 rolls of bandages, 80 syringes and several litres of blood, so I naturally fall behind. I try to run full on even after running out of stamina, but I get shot in the head and my character hits the deck. Luckily, the wound isn't fatal so I take some cover and quickly patch myself up and inject some morphine into me. (At this point I think I'm basically a high mummy.) I try to keep up with my squad-mate... but I take more gunfire which causes me to take cover... and when I do, I hear mortar fire.
A mortar hits the ground right in front of me...
And I live. My Torso is badly damaged but I live, so I start bandaging myself and giving myself morphine... but then I hear another mortar...
And I still live.
And then another...
Still alive.
And then another...
Still alive.
And then I die.
I respawn back at our forward base... my team mate manages to make it back without dying. He is the only survivor.
2) This a story from some random KoTH server.
A helicopter pilot does a parachute run over the capture area. I jump out, aiming toward a tower that had friendlies occupying it before, that I still assumed had friendlies inside. I manoeuvre myself as I drop, and I'm about to miss the tower but I manage to pull it in and just land on the edge where a man was standing...
"Crawford killed xxxx" ... oh, that was an enemy... and I... crushed him? I look over to the other guy on the tower... he's patching himself up with a bandage... and I shoot him. I rank up, and some music plays.
I replay in my head the events that have just occurred.
-I parachuted onto a tower
-Drop kicked the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of a guy as I land
-Kill his friend
-Awesome music played
♥♥♥♥ yeah.
