Experiences in ARMA 3:
1) Our arma regiment uses a modded server, including a new map, ace (which adds some depth to the medical system and some other nifty features), TaskForceRadio (people must be close to each other or have a radio at the correct frequency to communicate) a bunch of new items, vehicles etc.
The Zeus/GM/HQ/leader of the regiment who sets up and manipulates our scenarios on the fly gives us our next mission.
We're going to insert via helicopter near an enemy (All enemy is AI) base and take it over. We get our equipment together (I take medical supplies, as medic) and mount up.
We have our usual banter as we approach the landing site, our Zeus directs the AI pilots of the helo to land but the AI just keeps going, either because they think we are being shot at or because they can't figure out how to land at the designated point.
We're now passing over the point, going into enemy territory. I think our Zeus realises this and commands everyone to bail. Now we're being shot at, I start getting my parachute from the helicopter's inventory. Out of the corner of my eye, I see bullets light up the cockpit and one of the pilots slumps forward, the helicopter descends. I replace my backpack full of medical supplies with the parachute and prepare to jump... but now the helicopter is too low. If I jumped now, I'd probably fail to open my parachute soon enough and injure myself severely, so my only choice was to wait 'till the helicopter was low enough and just hope I don't get shot as I get out.
I dismount as it's about to touch the ground and bullets start smacking the helicopter from the side that I had gotten out. I quickly run around to the other side without taking any injuries. Our squad has landed in a clearing that is surrounded by forest, in a kind of Y shape, with our squad at the intersection of open area. We're all spread out along this clearing, and the enemy has surrounded us entirely. A couple of our men were already dying and more were going to follow. I hear over the radio our Zeus and another team leader call for a retreat back to the base, but with so many enemies around us, that was near impossible.
I stay behind the helicopter, trying to spot enemies from my position, but with only gunfire as my indicator, it was near impossible to know exactly where the bullets were coming from.
I remember that I've left all of my medical supplies in the helicopter, which I need since people are getting shot to♥♥♥♥♥♥ so I go up to the door and see if I can reach the inventory inside. I can't, unfortunately, so the only way I was going to get those supplies was to hop inside the back and expose myself to gunfire. One of my squad-mates, a marksman, obviously has the same idea, he probably left his ammunition and bandages behind after grabbing a parachute. He hops in and I follow suit, I quickly close the door, grab my bag and get out. Great, now I can actually be of some use, since I can't see where the ♥♥♥♥ these guys are shooting from (I could've used the map to see them, but I feel like that's kinda cheat-y).
I take a look around, still trying to spot enemies, but I just can't see them, so I give up trying to fight back and bolt it toward one of my team-mates (the marksman from before). (By this time, there were only like three or four of us left.) He was patching himself up, so I helped him out by bandaging him up a little. We're both switching between prone and crouching stances, trying to shoot the enemy and patch ourselves up as we get shot. Eventually, it's just us two, there's still gunfire, but it's died down a little. He turns to me "So, what do you think we should do?", I reply "I think we should just make a run for it".
And so we do.
He has more stamina than me, considering I'm carrying about 40 rolls of bandages, 80 syringes and several litres of blood, so I naturally fall behind. I try to run full on even after running out of stamina, but I get shot in the head and my character hits the deck. Luckily, the wound isn't fatal so I take some cover and quickly patch myself up and inject some morphine into me. (At this point I think I'm basically a high mummy.) I try to keep up with my squad-mate... but I take more gunfire which causes me to take cover... and when I do, I hear mortar fire.
A mortar hits the ground right in front of me...
And I live. My Torso is badly damaged but I live, so I start bandaging myself and giving myself morphine... but then I hear another mortar...
And I still live.
And then another...
Still alive.
And then another...
Still alive.
And then I die.
I respawn back at our forward base... my team mate manages to make it back without dying. He is the only survivor.
2) This a story from some random KoTH server.
A helicopter pilot does a parachute run over the capture area. I jump out, aiming toward a tower that had friendlies occupying it before, that I still assumed had friendlies inside. I manoeuvre myself as I drop, and I'm about to miss the tower but I manage to pull it in and just land on the edge where a man was standing...
"Crawford killed xxxx" ... oh, that was an enemy... and I... crushed him? I look over to the other guy on the tower... he's patching himself up with a bandage... and I shoot him. I rank up, and some music plays.
I replay in my head the events that have just occurred.
-I parachuted onto a tower
-Drop kicked the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of a guy as I land
-Kill his friend
-Awesome music played
♥♥♥♥ yeah.

I have enjoyed playing this game for over 700 hours. Most of the time I played the vanilla version of Arma 3, even though this game has amazing third party and steam workshop support. The visuals in this game look absolutely stunning, the design and graphics have aged pretty well. The campaign takes quite a lot of effort and time, I have come really far in the campaign but thus far not completed it. This is mainly due to two factors. The first, I'm not the best squad leader, especially with how the commanding works in Arma 3 with AI. Second, the AI is genuinly ludicrous.
Starting off Arma 3 has a lot of gamemodes due to all the modifications that are out there on the Steam Workshop, Armaholic and more. The main gamemodes that are played are: Milsim, Tactical Realism, Roleplay (Altis Life, Takistan Life, Life, Project Life, etc.), gungame, end-game and many more custom gamemodes that are made by the community.
I mostly enjoyed playing roleplay, usually Altis Life with friends. Friends and/or clans are a big part of Arma 3. I must say you can enjoy this without having any friends to play with, but the joy mostly comes in when you play with friends and clans.
I could say I enjoyed the game exceptionally, but that's due to my nature. Arma 3 is a military simulation game, and that means it's trying to be realistic. Many people I've talked to over the years of playing this game started out thinking this would be like a regular shooter. Well, let me tell you it really is not. Arma 3 tries to simulate all factors that change your combat capabilities, such as stamina, weapon sway, weigth and injuries. It really does a good job at it too. If you get shot with a high caliber rifle, you can get one shot in any area of your body or bleed out.
Imagine GTA series on steroids and take all the idiotic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t away. Multiply that by ten and you'll get how awesome and fun this game is!

I have enjoyed playing this game for over 700 hours. Most of the time I played the vanilla version of Arma 3, even though this game has amazing third party and steam workshop support. The visuals in this game look absolutely stunning, the design and graphics have aged pretty well. The campaign takes quite a lot of effort and time, I have come really far in the campaign but thus far not completed it. This is mainly due to two factors. The first, I'm not the best squad leader, especially with how the commanding works in Arma 3 with AI. Second, the AI is genuinly ludicrous.
Starting off Arma 3 has a lot of gamemodes due to all the modifications that are out there on the Steam Workshop, Armaholic and more. The main gamemodes that are played are: Milsim, Tactical Realism, Roleplay (Altis Life, Takistan Life, Life, Project Life, etc.), gungame, end-game and many more custom gamemodes that are made by the community.
I mostly enjoyed playing roleplay, usually Altis Life with friends. Friends and/or clans are a big part of Arma 3. I must say you can enjoy this without having any friends to play with, but the joy mostly comes in when you play with friends and clans.
I could say I enjoyed the game exceptionally, but that's due to my nature. Arma 3 is a military simulation game, and that means it's trying to be realistic. Many people I've talked to over the years of playing this game started out thinking this would be like a regular shooter. Well, let me tell you it really is not. Arma 3 tries to simulate all factors that change your combat capabilities, such as stamina, weapon sway, weigth and injuries. It really does a good job at it too. If you get shot with a high caliber rifle, you can get one shot in any area of your body or bleed out.

H1Z1 is technically the perfect game when it comes to a battlegrounds style of game. It is fast paced and is addictive. The problem is that the game is broken in every sense. Here are the ways in which it is broken and what it is good at.
Pros:
Fast gameplay
Interesting
Addicting
Cons:
-De-Sync, like a lot of it. Bullets do not hit when it clearly looks like they should.
-You better have a top of the line computer because people will beat you simply by loading the game quicker.
-No option to not play competitively.
-Competitive rankings are kind of hard to understand and do not show true skill.
-There is basically no skill matching. I have had the game for 3 weeks and I am plat 1, but every game I am matched with a server full of diamond and royal ranked players.
-Toxic player base.
-Loot crates are stupid and will cost you a fortune.
-Close quarters combat gameplay is 100% unplayable. I am not over exaggerating, it is basically unplayable. The only options for cqc is a shotgun that is glitchy, laggy, has an unbalanced amount of damage depending on range.
-No weapon attatchments. None.
-The option of first person is a joke. If you use first person, you will not be a good player. Unless you somehow can weild the shotgun correctly.
-RNG loot makes zero sence in a game that makes you find a weapon in the first 10 seconds or you die.
-Random spawing in this game makes or breaks the round that you are about to have.
-Vehicles are a necessity to win, no question.
-Vehicles are extremely glitchy. They are the only way in which you can win, but are a death traps.
-There are essentially 3 options when it comes to using guns and again, they have zero attatchments.
-The game has a rediculous amount of issues with loading and ult tabbing. The game crashes more than any other program I have ever had in my life.
-Daybreak does not address any gameplay, optimization, or server issues. None at all.
In conclusion, if you ask any person that has played this game about the list of cons above, they will undoubtably agree with me. I wrote a review on Arma when I first got it just over a year ago. I've decided to revise it today after having a lot of experience with the game (1300+ hrs).
Arma defines itself as a military sandbox. If you break that sentence down, that's saying that it is a free-to-do-what-you-please game that uses military assets and a military theme. So if you can do what you please, why are so many people buying the game then writing a bad review because they can't do what they want? I'll tell you why.
It's because they don't give the game a fair chance. There are so many millions of things to do in Arma, but many of these new players just play the stuff they come across first. A prime example is the campaign. Anyone who's played Arma knows how god damn awful the campaign is. But because it's there in bright bold letters on the menu, it's often the first thing new players go into. And that's why they end up disliking the game. Because they have a bad singleplayer experience, they choose not to try anything else.
If these people had spent a couple of hours toying around in the editor, trying various servers, maybe even looking to join a community - I guarantee every person on the planet can find something they enjoy in this game. And if there is nothing they enjoy, well, it's a sandbox so go make it. Go create that gamemode, that mission, that group.
What I'm trying to say is that Arma is what you make it. If you only play the campaign or only play wasteland servers, you won't ever know how awesome this game is. So go off the beaten track and experiment with crazy things in this game. Don't refund it because you don't like every part of it. Find what you do like and expand on it.
TL;DR:
Arma requires a bit of time and a bit of experimentation to start enjoying. But once you've found the enjoyment it's an amazing game. Don't give up just because the campaign is dog♥♥♥♥♥♥

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play. Lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes (each with his own distinct personality) to choose from. The banter between the different classes is entertaining to listen to. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow him to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or higher skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since November 2007 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

Pro's :
1.Graphics

3.Endless Possibilities
The graphics in this game are down right amazing as long as you are playing on something higher than low the graphics will not look like someone♥♥♥♥♥♥on your computer monitor! The Gameplay is downright amazing there are so many things you can do with this game it's insane, From flying in a helicopter and protecting your fellow teamates to putting your boots on the ground to help out your teamates and eliminate enemies together. As far as realism goes this game is doing amazing. Then comes the endless possibilities! With all these hours in this game I have had some time to mess around with the game whether it be adding mods to the game or going against AI with my friends on multiple servers that offer the fun and tactical gameplay! I enjoyed Wasteland, Altis Life, Arma 3 Life etc. But what really made me enjoy the game was the servers that had there own little touch to the game that made the game feel different, That's why I had so much fun adding mods to the game and enjoyed things like Arma 3 Life when it was popular and stuff around those areas where fun to me and I'm sure they can be fun to you! This game is a whole lot a fun and worth the buy 100% but with such an amazing game there of course has to be some cons to it because no game is ever perfect.
Cons:
Minor glitches in the game like being able to see through walls to flying sky high into outer space are only a few of the minor glitches that can be found in this game, None of the glitches are enough to make you rethink buying the game or enough to make you uninstall it and never want to play it again but for the rare amount of times that it happens it can get really annoying.
Another problem that this game has is the lag that it creates because of how good the graphics are, Although I don't get the massive amount of lag that some people get I do hear people complaining about how the lag kills there computer and there is just no point in playing the game. Although the lag is annoying at times as long as you have a good computer the game won't kill you as much the game can be run on a decent computer hell I used to run it on an old computer I got from Best Buy years ago! The game in general is not the problem for your lag it is the servers and the fact that so much stuff is happening at the same time that it causes you to lag and if the server doesn't restart frequently then you might want to find a new server. It's all a matter of finding a server that you enjoy and you feel as if you can play on it even if it does lag you a little, I have yet to meet someone that doesn't have a super computer that doesn't have minor lag in the game and that is the only problem with the game if you don't have a decent computer you might as well not even bother wasting your money and your time.
After reading that I hope you understand how fun this game can be as long as you are sure than your computer can handle such a heavy game! If you do get the game I hope you enjoy it and get as much hours as I did into the game or maybe even more. The realism is waiting for you!

It's hard to describe such a game. It's not like anything you've played before and I'm not talking about realism.
Arma (and Operation Flashpoint <- Codemaster took over and screwed up) series are unique and both founded by Bohemia Interactive Studios. Arma (formerly called Armed Assault) doesn't offer just a singleplayer campaign, few other missions and about ten multiplayer maps, plus some guns. No. Arma offers you campaign, few other missions and some multiplayer missions, plus 290 square kilometre of terrain and some basic gear, guns and vehicles divided between five factions (counting civilians). But hey, how could you play this game over 1 400 hours with that little? Well, that's good question, Arma offers scenario editor, which is easy to use and alow you to create your own missions, way better than any other official mission. Just check the workshop, you'll see.
The community made missions (<- let's call them scenarios) aren't just about doing tasks, given to you at the briefing. There's a wide selection of randomly generated scenarios, like 'Invade & Annex' for example. Seriously, (almost) everything is possible in the scenario editor.
Now this is important part: MOD SUPPORT. There's hundereds, maybe thousands of user made mods and addons. Including maps, vehicles, guns, gear, new game mechanics, factions.
Now let's be honnest for a while, Arma have age long problem with optimization, it's about CPU and AMD CPUs aren't best for Arma. If you have AMD CPU you'll have problem with FPS, if you have Intel CPU you SHOULD be fine. But the good thing is, Arma isn't fast-paced game so even 15 FPS is still very playable.
If you're really a member of PC Master Race, you'll buy it and give it a try, because Arma is something console peasants won't see for a long time.
Did I mention there's a lot of milsim units/clans which simulate real world army's?
They're recruiting.
SOME FACTS:
AI actually think, in some cases it's even smarter than players, that's why some people don't like it.
You can shoot through walls if you have enough powerfull gun, that's why some people hate AI.
100 square kilometre maps are small.
I have 30 friends on Steam, who have ArmA 3, their average time spent on it is around 870 hours.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Despite its early access label, this is a very solid game. Gameplay is smooth, gunplay is enjoyable, and it runs fantastically. It's a great, open world, aren-styled shooter. Whether you play first, or third person, it's great. Each time you load in, it's a different scenario - not something you find in alot of shooters, which is nice. In general, the community is quite fun, and friendly when it comes to you killing them - or vice versa. There's a whole spectrum of awesome skins- from your everyday, mundane clothing- to whacky, colourful, outlandish suits (with matching masks)! There's regular updates, tweaks, and constant feedback.
So, the negatives. If you've just bought this, prepare yourselves for a wolrd of salt, anger, and general ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Being someone new, in game like this, can be hell- espeically if you're not particularly fast at grasping new systems, and mechanics. Being placed in a game with someone, who has over 1000 hours, is very unfair (there should be a matched ranking system, honestly), because obviously, they know the game better - from aiming techniques, to insane survivability.
Either way, it's by far one of the best game's I've played - even when it was 'Battle Royale'. If you're willing to stick to it, through salt-induced hell, it's definitely worth it.

I can't say I love this game like I did Saints Row 2. Why? Because there's less game.
Saints Row 2 was a huge leap. It had a funny story, some serious moments, and all around awesome sandbox fun. SR: The Third has the first, has the second, but lacks all the sandbox fun. I never had to grind off the activities to get Respect, I never had to travel around the city for clothing, missions, or cars. Everything was given to me and I had no reason to run off exploring.
The polish, however, is MUCH better, meaning the game works out of the box. There's also more content when it comes to weapons and gang related stuff, but still... the game just isn't there.
I blame DLC, since this game has a Season Pass and tons, tons, and tons of DLC planned for it. I think I'll go back to Skyrim, or Saints Row 2. Why? Because those two games actually gave me what I paid for: A full game.

As someone who has played since 2009, before the game became free-to-play, TF2 has always been my favorite first-person shooter... If calling it such a thing would even be appropriate with the combat mechanics it has.
Pros:
-Combat is fun and different from the regular FPS format based (closely or loosely) on how physical combat would be, with TF2 instead being far more dynamic and ridiculous.
-There's plenty of room for players to grow and apply skill in gameplay without the initial learning curve being atrociously harsh and unrewarding for beginners.
-A plethora of options for individual customization allowing players to experiment and choose what suits them best, what is the most enjoyable, what would be the most situationally effective, and/or whatever else they might want.  And of course, this includes that which TF2 has become most (in)famous for...
-Hats!  \o/
-An active community that has long been and is still creating items, maps, comedic and educational TF2 videos.
-Valve has given the classes and the game as a whole true character exceeding what shooting games normally exhibit, with amusing, personality-expressing voiced lines, cooperative and class-specific taunts, map and item design, holiday events, and out-of-game content.
-Aside from the standard game modes, the sheer variety of cool and silly alternative game modes the community has brought to life is impressive, beyond any other shooting game that I'm aware of.  Randomizer, Prophunt, Zombie Fortress, Deathrun, Vs. Saxton Hale, Pyro Dodgeball, Surfing, 10x Weapon Stats, and more.  For anyone wanting something a little different, TF2's got you covered.
-As far as I'm aware TF2 is still fielding the same level of graphical complexity/quality that it was in 2007, so it won't be as taxing on system resources as some more recently released games, and thus relative to those games TF2 will be less problematic for people trying to run the game on less-than-modern computers.
-It's free.  =D
Other:
-Random Crits are Fair and Balanced™
Cons:
-The population of the community has been in decline for a while now, and Valve seems to be gradually losing interest in the game as well.  It's far from being dead, but it's no longer the grand ol' hat simulator it once was.
-The in-game community, the people you'll meet and talk with in server chat, they're... Not the nicest group around.
-Game balance isn't perfect... (Soldiers, I'm looking at you.  >.> )
-There isn't a readily accessible and/or intuitively displayed in-game help system.  The tutorial is largely unhelpful with actual gameplay beyond the basics of the basics, and the hints shown during loading screens - while being useful information - are presented one at a time at random rather than in a way that would be more relevant to player activity in-game or in any manner that would be even *sort of* organized for access on demand.
-There are still hackers despite the presence of Valve Anti-Cheat, and in my experience community server admins are in short supply or in some cases even tolerate certain hackers, and more often than not votebans fail even against the most obvious of hackers.
-As the flip side of the graphics aspect mentioned above, the game doesn't exactly look fancy either, for those who are into that kind of thing.  (In my personal opinion though this isn't an issue.)
Overall rating: 9/10, worst 1968 war simulator.

This game will go down as one of my favorites of all time, but in it's current state, I cannot recommend it to someone who hasn't played it before. In this review, I'm going to measure good things and bad things that have happened all throughout this game's lifespan so far. These are the positives and negatives I have experienced with this game, some have become better since past times, others continue to get worse.
Gameplay/Controls
+TF2 plays and controls in a very specific way, the movement may be difficult to adjust to for newcomers, but there are many hidden techniques withing the game engine that make room for plenty of skill improvement (Like rocket jumping)
+/-This game offers a wide variety of ways to play, such as MvM, Payload, KOTH, Control Points, etc. Unfourtunately, some of these gamemodes are less balanced than others, and others are hardly ever played (Making wait times very long). Payload, MvM, and KOTH are my personal favorites.
-Casual matches do not balance players based on skill what so ever, this means that games usually boil down to one team destroying the other. Which isn't fun on either side when it happens all the time.
-The matchmaker for casual is also slow, sometimes getting into a game takes upwards of 5 minutes, which doesnt sound like a long time, but when every match only lasts a few minutes because one team destroys the other, you'll be waiting more than playing.
-Some classes have lower skill ceilings than others; soldier, scout, medic and demo being the most viable in competetive, whilst the other 5 are almost obsolete. This means more than half of this games cast isn't even worth your time if you want to play this game seriously.
-/+Game breaking bugs are found and fixed constantly.
Community
> Allow me to say something before I begin, I am not making fun of, calling out, or insulting anyone specifically. This games community has positives AND negatives, as much as we'd like to believe they saved this game, they have their problems.
+Community is active and passionate about what they do, some create content to be featured in future updates, while others stay involved with "future" updates and keep the community informed.
+/- Passionate players of this game are constantly providing their opinions on "new" content. This was a good thing in the past, but nowadays it mostly comes down to either over-positivity or nonstop complaining.
- People tend to over-hype content for this game, the community has a tendency to over-involve themselves with "upcoming" events and end up dissapointed despite wether or not the event was good or bad.
- Community servers are♥♥♥♥♥♥ This is the only part of this game that I will blatantly refer to as ♥♥♥♥♥♥. The admins are ♥♥♥♥♥y, the players are mostly as bad as the admins, the rules don't get enforced, just stay away from the community servers unluess you like trading.
+Trading has been made extremely fun and accessible by the community, and you can even make profits of great amounts.
Content
>This is by far the worst and best part of this game, it is also the most controversial topic amongst players. These are the reasons for such controversy.
+Content refreshed this game constantly and has kept it alive over it's almost 10 year lifespan, despite it being good or bad, it's kept the game fresh over the years.
-Recent updates have ruined the game and thrusted the community into an irrepairable state of whining, introducing casual mode and competetive mode was an awful idea.
-/+Updates are usually a 50/50 chance of being good or bad. And since updates only come along once every 6 months or so, this means the community can go almost a year without good, refreshing content.
-The game only has a tiny production team, who haven't been very open about the content they plan on releasing, leaving the community afraid for the games impending death.
-Competetive mode, though I haven't played it myself, I have heard nothing but complaints about it. Most people are saying it's full of hackers and slow starts to games.
Soundtrack/Graphics (Aesthetics)
+Game still looks great even almost 10 years after it's release.
+Soundtrack conveys the wacky hardcore action of this game perfectly, whether it's the robotic sounds of MvM or the nostalgic main theme.
+SFM animations that come with content updates deserve their own reviews entirely, they're very well put together to sum it up simply.
-There are some very minor visual bugs that exist in this game, mainly due to it's old age.
I don't recommend playing this game in it's current state. The community is too toxic/whiny and the game itself is riddled with issues right now. However, this game has had a mainly positive go of it so far, and when you consider how old the game is, you have to appreciate or respect it to some degree.

Man where do I begin? Well lets start with when I bought this game close to release. The hype was real back than. It was an enjoyable clown fiesta at first. The bugs were there, but the hype and fun clouded that...Unfortuantely however, around 2 months later they updated some stuff which rendered my game completely unplayable. This happend right when I bough the game for my friend. Right when we tried to play the daybreak launcher would open for 2 minute and go black for me. (While still counting gameplay hours) So a week goes by and I get tired of it so I send a email. I tried everything they told me but nothing worked. They even began ignoring me. You could just feel their corporate greed and disregard for their players. So I gave up. About a year later I got a new pc and thought to myself "Oh h1z1 should work now" And to my suprise it did. I started playing with my friend but he quit after a few days, because guns and doors wouldn't load for him unless he waited 2 minutes. So I started playing myself. Slowly but surely the fun turned into agony. I thought to myself "Surley it's my fault I'm getting all these bugs and not the game."  I thought that for quite some time until I started playing duo's and fives with my other friends. And watching videos.  Bug after bug, crash after crash. Every other game we would get stuck on the "sending you to game mometarily" screen. And the only way to fix this was to re launch. (While still counting gameplay hours)
The hit registration got/was so bad (My guess is the unstable code) that the shotgun was no longer viable. This was after a year in early access amazing right? The driving was almost as bad if not worse. You would always hit invisible objects and explode instantly. Combined with the ping spikes it was unberable. Months later the game is still the same. Only the ping was fixed and shotgun (barely). Seeing hackers is normal now.  This made me realize my first feeling was spot on. Daybreak is the prime example of corporate greed and incompetence. They rather focus on advertisment deals and micro-transactions than their players.

1. Do  you value your time input?

Stripping a game of more features than you add is not the way to make a sequel, & that's exactly what THQ did here. Granted plenty of things have been added & this game would have been one of my favorites of all time had the sandbox you were given these new tools to use in not been complete garbage. The streets are almost empty and rarely more than 30 feet long, unlike Saints Row 2 which featured giant highways with constant traffic & far more vehicles to choose from. The vehicle & crib editors had their share of features removed as well, vehicles usually only have 3-5 options for customization and cribs have none. Even the weapons have been watered down, 2 pistols, 2 shotguns, 2 rifles, & a handful of "specialty" weapons that get old fast. A proper PC port of SR2 would have kept me entertained far longer than this. You don't "out GTA GTA" by copying their dismal brown city THQ.

While Team Fortress 2 has it's flaws I honestly find it to be the most enjoyable class based shooter I've played. This game is humorous, charming, and extremely addictive.

+Free to play
+The ability to customize the 9 classes with a large assortment of cosmetics
+Fun game-modes that range from capturing points to some sort of sport thing that is kind of difficult to describe.
+An extremely fun co-op mode in which you have a rare chance to win items that can be sold for a lot of money
+Many different weapons to change how you play with different classes
+An awesome soundtrack
+9 Classes with some really great voice lines
+The game is still being updated
CONS
-As of right now there are A LOT of hackers
-Random crits
-The game only has around six people actively working on it.... Meaning the updates come out very slowly. But hey quality over quantity, right?
-A few balancing issues but a lot more balanced than Overwatch
------------
All in all I feel the game is still worth playing so I would say you should absolutely check it out! After all it's free to play, what do you have to lose?

Ok, so I've had the pleasure of playing the previous ArmA games, started out with ArmA 2 but played some of the original and it has been an interesting ride to see how things have progressed since then. I also had the pleasure of opting in for the ArmA 3 beta, allowing me to play it before it was released and I can say for one this game has grown so much since dev stage. The only issue I have is the lack of the "last stand" stance that was removed at some point after beta, but only because I thought it was unique being able to shoot while lying on your back. But its really a trivial issue, the biggest issue you'll hear about is the lag issues during multiplayer which hopefully they'll be focusing on within the next year because it has been an issue since the previous games. But don't let that deter you from buying this amazing game. When you get it, it'll take some time to learn as this game has a steep learning curve but before long you'll get the hang of it and you'll be able to ignore the issues multiplayer has and you'll be speaking the lingo of the community while you're assaulting a large, heavily fortified enemy base. Theres hundreds of things you can do in this game and thats without the mods. As dumb as it sounds, one of my favorite things to do is play a sandbox mod (which you can easily find on the workshop here on Steam) and just fly around and explore the islands as theres hundreds of miles of detailed landscape to explore plus it helps me keep up my flying skills. Mods are another thing, there are thousands of them and each one brings something new to the table, the mod community is outstanding. Now... multiplayer lag issue aside, the other issue a lot of people have are the paid DLC that has been released; the helicopter dlc, marksmen dlc, etc. All these things probably should have been included into the vanilla game but after spending so much time in the game and realizing that it has hours upon hours of replayability then the extra $30 isn't that big of a deal. Its well worth the price of the game and DLC, especially with the upcoming Eden expansion which gives us a new tropical island to explore... things just get better and better with this game. See you on the battlefield!

Lack of updates, due to the team itself being understaffed and Valve no longer caring for their own games it appears, matchmaking having flat out removed some features for no real reason, making playing Casual a nightmare, and players themselves, at least from my experience, being either unco-operative or lacking any shred of humour.
The game is a decade old, but sadly, it does feel like it's a dying game. I hope it's not the case, but that's upto Valve ultimately to fix, I'd say.

Ok, so I've had the pleasure of playing the previous ArmA games, started out with ArmA 2 but played some of the original and it has been an interesting ride to see how things have progressed since then. I also had the pleasure of opting in for the ArmA 3 beta, allowing me to play it before it was released and I can say for one this game has grown so much since dev stage. The only issue I have is the lack of the "last stand" stance that was removed at some point after beta, but only because I thought it was unique being able to shoot while lying on your back. But its really a trivial issue, the biggest issue you'll hear about is the lag issues during multiplayer which hopefully they'll be focusing on within the next year because it has been an issue since the previous games. But don't let that deter you from buying this amazing game. When you get it, it'll take some time to learn as this game has a steep learning curve but before long you'll get the hang of it and you'll be able to ignore the issues multiplayer has and you'll be speaking the lingo of the community while you're assaulting a large, heavily fortified enemy base. Theres hundreds of things you can do in this game and thats without the mods. As dumb as it sounds, one of my favorite things to do is play a sandbox mod (which you can easily find on the workshop here on Steam) and just fly around and explore the islands as theres hundreds of miles of detailed landscape to explore plus it helps me keep up my flying skills. Mods are another thing, there are thousands of them and each one brings something new to the table, the mod community is outstanding. Now... multiplayer lag issue aside, the other issue a lot of people have are the paid DLC that has been released; the helicopter dlc, marksmen dlc, etc. All these things probably should have been included into the vanilla game but after spending so much time in the game and realizing that it has hours upon hours of replayability then the extra $30 isn't that big of a deal. Its well worth the price of the game and DLC, especially with the upcoming Eden expansion which gives us a new tropical island to explore... things just get better and better with this game. Personal Rating: 9/10
Replayability: High
Budget: Affordable - The price has dropped enough.
Length: It's mostly multiplayer - the singleplayer campaign is... Very difficult.
I was a fan of Operation Flashpoint - Dragon Rising and Red River, as well as Arma II.
I have to admit, the same problems that plagued Arma II still ravage Arma III to a degree.
It's unnecessarily difficult to set your keyboard up for this game.
They've certainly improved on it, now the keyboard mapping recognizes double tapping a button and even holding it, versus just pressing it.
That said, a lot of things in this game, could be handled through smart menus rather than having buttons for it.
It becomes impossible to remember where everything is toggled for.
That said, the game is without a doubt the greatest military simulator I've ever seen, and the AI is actually fairly smart (except for the friendly AI which appears to be stupid in comparison - but I mostly think it's because the friendly AI is subject to much more scripting than the enemy AI).
The inventory system is a welcome change from Arma II that had an incredibly complicated inventory system, and the fact that you can change everything from your uniform to your weapon mods is super great!
The game is, like I said, very difficult in single player, because the enemy can spot you before you can reasonably spot the enemy - but that isn't because the game is unrealistic, it's because it's pretty difficult to spot an enemy on a 28 inch monitor in 1080p, if there is a simulated distance of 500 meters between you, and the enemy is wearing camuflage.
This game will probably be a good thing to try with occulous rift once it comes out. It doesn't help that the enemy soldiers use camuflage that is actually much better suited for the terrain you play in, during the campaign - not that it matters the other way around, because I don't think the AI is set to differentiate between camu patterns.
There is no melee combat in the game, which was a bit of a bummer for me, but I don't think you would ever get a chance to use it anyway, because as I mentioned, you will often end up spotted by an enemy long before you're even able to notice that combat has started around you.
The game lacks an easy mode, where you stop to be wounded after bandaging your wounds and being out of combat for a while - Of course, that wouldn't be realistic, but it would still make the game a little less hardcore for those that find the difficulty a bit too steep.
In operation flashpoint, when you reached a checkpoint, your squad was revived, wounds were healed and new squad members even spawned with full ammo.
In Arma III, I find myself running out of ammo very quickly, I'm only capable of carrying one rifle (an option to carry a rifle instead of a secondary weapon, such as a rocket launcher, would be welcome), and if I get hit at any point - It's going to affect the rest of the mission, and missions are very very long.
This is a bit too brutal for my liking - it wouldn't matter in a multiplayer game, but in a single player campaign where the missions are so long that I often feel like I could make a full time job out of playing the game, it's too much.
That said, you can't ask for a more realistic military infantry simulator. It very accurately represents what it feels like to be in the infantry.
The producers should have put in some optional missions that were skippable, showing some of the less exciting parts of being in the armed forces, such as building a camp, weapon and gear maintenance, dealing with a complicated and sometimes not 100% efficient chain of command and the many menial duties of being a soldier.
It'd be cool if there was a "I'm military" mode that could be activated, which results in you being assigned to a fire team in your unit, instead of basically being a joker.
The AI in your unit does operate like a military unit, with proper "fire and movement" maneuvers, but you're left out of this, because the producer knew the player wasn't necessarily going to be able to keep up with that, but some players have it the other way around, they sit there, confused, wondering why you're not getting advancement orders, why your team is acting like they have orders, but they didn't reach you.
That said, I think that it's GOOD that they did it like they did, because this game is supposed to be for everyone, and not just for people with military experience, but it wouldn't have taken them that much longer to incorporate a mode like that.
With the verdict that sometimes, the realism level in this game makes it TOO difficult to play through a limited interface, such as keyboard+mouse and monitor, then I can really recommend this game to anyone who likes military simulators.
It's not your average run of the mill FPS game though, so if you like high-paced and less punishing gameplay, I recommend something like battlefield instead.

SR3 is not GOTY and has it's shortcomings but they can be overlooked because of the non-stop action and laughs it provides.

Overall, this is about as close as you will get to being a soldier without enlisting in the armed services.

This game will go down as one of my favorites of all time, but in it's current state, I cannot recommend it to someone who hasn't played it before. In this review, I'm going to measure good things and bad things that have happened all throughout this game's lifespan so far. These are the positives and negatives I have experienced with this game, some have become better since past times, others continue to get worse.
Gameplay/Controls
+TF2 plays and controls in a very specific way, the movement may be difficult to adjust to for newcomers, but there are many hidden techniques withing the game engine that make room for plenty of skill improvement (Like rocket jumping)
+/-This game offers a wide variety of ways to play, such as MvM, Payload, KOTH, Control Points, etc. Unfourtunately, some of these gamemodes are less balanced than others, and others are hardly ever played (Making wait times very long). Payload, MvM, and KOTH are my personal favorites.
-Casual matches do not balance players based on skill what so ever, this means that games usually boil down to one team destroying the other. Which isn't fun on either side when it happens all the time.
-The matchmaker for casual is also slow, sometimes getting into a game takes upwards of 5 minutes, which doesnt sound like a long time, but when every match only lasts a few minutes because one team destroys the other, you'll be waiting more than playing.
-Some classes have lower skill ceilings than others; soldier, scout, medic and demo being the most viable in competetive, whilst the other 5 are almost obsolete. This means more than half of this games cast isn't even worth your time if you want to play this game seriously.
-/+Game breaking bugs are found and fixed constantly.
Community
> Allow me to say something before I begin, I am not making fun of, calling out, or insulting anyone specifically. This games community has positives AND negatives, as much as we'd like to believe they saved this game, they have their problems.
+Community is active and passionate about what they do, some create content to be featured in future updates, while others stay involved with "future" updates and keep the community informed.
+/- Passionate players of this game are constantly providing their opinions on "new" content. This was a good thing in the past, but nowadays it mostly comes down to either over-positivity or nonstop complaining.
- People tend to over-hype content for this game, the community has a tendency to over-involve themselves with "upcoming" events and end up dissapointed despite wether or not the event was good or bad.
- Community servers are♥♥♥♥♥♥ This is the only part of this game that I will blatantly refer to as ♥♥♥♥♥♥. The admins are ♥♥♥♥♥y, the players are mostly as bad as the admins, the rules don't get enforced, just stay away from the community servers unluess you like trading.
+Trading has been made extremely fun and accessible by the community, and you can even make profits of great amounts.
Content
>This is by far the worst and best part of this game, it is also the most controversial topic amongst players. These are the reasons for such controversy.
+Content refreshed this game constantly and has kept it alive over it's almost 10 year lifespan, despite it being good or bad, it's kept the game fresh over the years.
-Recent updates have ruined the game and thrusted the community into an irrepairable state of whining, introducing casual mode and competetive mode was an awful idea.
-/+Updates are usually a 50/50 chance of being good or bad. And since updates only come along once every 6 months or so, this means the community can go almost a year without good, refreshing content.
-The game only has a tiny production team, who haven't been very open about the content they plan on releasing, leaving the community afraid for the games impending death.
-Competetive mode, though I haven't played it myself, I have heard nothing but complaints about it. Most people are saying it's full of hackers and slow starts to games.
Soundtrack/Graphics (Aesthetics)
+Game still looks great even almost 10 years after it's release.
+Soundtrack conveys the wacky hardcore action of this game perfectly, whether it's the robotic sounds of MvM or the nostalgic main theme.
+SFM animations that come with content updates deserve their own reviews entirely, they're very well put together to sum it up simply.
-There are some very minor visual bugs that exist in this game, mainly due to it's old age.
I don't recommend playing this game in it's current state. The community is too toxic/whiny and the game itself is riddled with issues right now. However, this game has had a mainly positive go of it so far, and when you consider how old the game is, you have to appreciate or respect it to some degree.

(wasn't expecting a run and gun, but i was expecting to play a war game, not a run around grinding gold with stupid rules and having to have a job rpg) i would say avoid it.. i tried so hard to get a refund, but steam sucks, and i couldn't even get a real response from a human being.. now im stuck with this useless single player game.. i keep trying to force myself to find something fun to do with it, and it can't be done...  on the other hand technically and graphically it;s amazing and the attention to details is great... it was just squandered on a community with terrible terrible terrible ideas on how it should be played... the addition of official servers wih official game modes, would make this game a 10 out of 10... until then, its like a 2..  unless you like pretending to be an under paid truck driver that gets harrasse by lame people who think they are digital police..
i personally wish i never spent a dime on this game...

While Team Fortress 2 has it's flaws I honestly find it to be the most enjoyable class based shooter I've played. This game is humorous, charming, and extremely addictive.
PROS
+Free to play
+The ability to customize the 9 classes with a large assortment of cosmetics
+Fun game-modes that range from capturing points to some sort of sport thing that is kind of difficult to describe.
+An extremely fun co-op mode in which you have a rare chance to win items that can be sold for a lot of money
+Many different weapons to change how you play with different classes
+An awesome soundtrack
+9 Classes with some really great voice lines
+The game is still being updated
CONS
-As of right now there are A LOT of hackers
-Random crits
-The game only has around six people actively working on it.... Meaning the updates come out very slowly. But hey quality over quantity, right?
-A few balancing issues but a lot more balanced than Overwatch
------------
All in all I feel the game is still worth playing so I would say you should absolutely check it out! After all it's free to play, what do you have to lose?

Arma 3 is essentially just a major improvement over the last, while also having different enough experiences to be worth buying as an Arma veteran. With the amount of content that is currently available in this game I can't not recommend it, and the existing content really is a lot of fun. This being said I have almost exclusively played single player and koth so I'll critique those.
Probably the best thing about this game to me is the single-player, and it's because it capitalized on the parts of Arma 2's campaign that were fun, but really short and mostly just filler garbage. All of this game's missions are short-burst, short-term little missions that revolve around an objective and have you return to the main hub once finishing, akin to scenarios in Arma 2, other than the fact that the missions are connected. This really was the best way the campaign could've been approached since this game is praised for its gameplay and doing something as nonscripted as the Arma 2 campaign just isn't interesting enough to play, and people who liked Arma 2's singleplayer rarely compliment it. Because of that, I think the singleplayer alone would be enough to buy this game if one doesn't really like Arma 2's campaign but they enjoyed the gunplay and gameplay.
Multiplayer's kinda what you'd expect from this series, with the Arma Life roleplaying still going strong and a few other really fun gameplay modes like Wasteland (sandbox Arma pvp), and I'd strongly recommend getting this game if you're a fan of sandbox or rp stuff in Garry's Mod, or Minecraft, or DayZ/Unturned (any sandbox game is comparable to this game other than the combat, which makes this an interesting multiplayer game if you're into that stuff) since they're similar. Something recently incorporated by the devs of this game is koth (King of the Hill), where you go into cities from a base and siege it with manpower. It was a really nice change in pacing for this game, since it's largely controlled by you (the pacing) and it appeals to more of the singleplayer fans that like the siege reconnaissance Arma 2 represented, as well as taking different roles at or away from the battlefield, like the snipers and field medics, as well as the breachers and pilots and all that (which are supported by a perk and character system that I thought were cool for roleplaying). It's hard to say if I'd buy this game for one gamemode, but the amount of options really gives you the liberty to choose what you enjoy the most and explore the content there.
Overall, this game has a really solid singleplayer and multiplayer compared to most as well as previous editions in Arma, and the release that is this game is justified to buy based on its content additions and a newer (and clunkier) control scheme that compliments this game better than Arma 2's did, and overall improvements to the fun of this series. I'd recommend it to you if you enjoyed sandbox/rp stuff or milsim, or if you're a fan of the series already.

H1z1 has the potential to become one of the best games out there. But unfortunately, at its current state, it’s not. I cannot recommend this game. There are many things wrong with this game, one of the things being hackers. If you play a lot of solo games you will know. You are in the top 10 having the game of your life fighting a decent player, (around your skill level) but then, a hacker speeds from out of nowhere and kills you both, this will then happen to everyone else in the match. Another major problem is hit registration, the hit registration in the game is well, Sh*t. The shotgun is the worst example of this. You will be in a situation where you are fighting someone with a shotgun at close range. And well, the shotgun decides to shoot "blanks". Recently, I played a game of duos with my friend. He was killed by somebody with an AR-15, and it was up to me to kill the guy who killed him. I used the element of surprise and came behind him with my shotgun. And unfortunately it decided to shoot "blanks". Allowing him to kill me in one shot. Optimization, the optimization settings for this game are poor. And really need to be improved. I myself don’t really have much to say about this… Daybreak are updating the game quite often. But no, they are not fixing the game, they are adding more skins. Yay! More money for Daybreak. Recently, they added a new update I myself have not played it yet, but I have noticed that people are complaining that is hard to see whether you get a headshot or not. As I said, I haven’t played the new update yet but I hope there is an option to change to the default crosshair settings if I don’t like it myself.
This has been my first serious review, so if you don’t like it then sorry. This is how I personally feel about the game and if you don’t agree then that’s fine. Thank you for reading.

Very fun game, despite the hurdles and problems.
-Multiple Gamemodes: From Payload, King of the Hill and CTF, to Mannpower, PASS time and more.
-One game is never the same: You'll ALWAYS have a fun time with a different experience.
-9 different classes, every one of them took a year each to develop (not really)
-Different Loadouts: Many Primary, Secondary and Melee weapons for each class, that makes possible playstyles almost infinite.
-Everyone looks different: It's very rare that you'll find two Scouts looking the same. Everyone has a certain style and fashion sense, so you'll never get bored of seeing the same look, cause there isn't any.
-An amazing community, and a chance to befriend many wonderful people.
-Hats
-Hats
-Hats
-Updates that have actual content can take a year or more to roll out.
-The developers don't talk much to the community, although that's a huge improvement from the silence we've been getting before.
-Some weapons are still unbalanced, making some Loadouts unusable while making others overpowered.
-Some bad apples in the bunch: from squeakers, to hackers and people who kick other people from servers for killing them and pushing the payload (Looking at you, Watchtower friendlies.)
-Trading is getting progressively harder, because the economy is slowly crumbling.
-Badly optimized.
Regardless, it's a game that I had fun with for more than 2000 hours, and I intend on playing more. If somehow you don't have this game in your library already (Come on, it's 2017), then you should download it. You're almost guaranteed to have fun.

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels.
There are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objectives for both teams to achieve.
'Mann Verses Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play.

Personal Rating: 9/10
Replayability: High
Budget: Affordable - The price has dropped enough.
Length: It's mostly multiplayer - the singleplayer campaign is... Very difficult.
I was a fan of Operation Flashpoint - Dragon Rising and Red River, as well as Arma II.
I have to admit, the same problems that plagued Arma II still ravage Arma III to a degree.
It's unnecessarily difficult to set your keyboard up for this game.
They've certainly improved on it, now the keyboard mapping recognizes double tapping a button and even holding it, versus just pressing it.
That said, a lot of things in this game, could be handled through smart menus rather than having buttons for it.
It becomes impossible to remember where everything is toggled for.
That said, the game is without a doubt the greatest military simulator I've ever seen, and the AI is actually fairly smart (except for the friendly AI which appears to be stupid in comparison - but I mostly think it's because the friendly AI is subject to much more scripting than the enemy AI).
The inventory system is a welcome change from Arma II that had an incredibly complicated inventory system, and the fact that you can change everything from your uniform to your weapon mods is super great!
The game is, like I said, very difficult in single player, because the enemy can spot you before you can reasonably spot the enemy - but that isn't because the game is unrealistic, it's because it's pretty difficult to spot an enemy on a 28 inch monitor in 1080p, if there is a simulated distance of 500 meters between you, and the enemy is wearing camuflage.
This game will probably be a good thing to try with occulous rift once it comes out. It doesn't help that the enemy soldiers use camuflage that is actually much better suited for the terrain you play in, during the campaign - not that it matters the other way around, because I don't think the AI is set to differentiate between camu patterns.
There is no melee combat in the game, which was a bit of a bummer for me, but I don't think you would ever get a chance to use it anyway, because as I mentioned, you will often end up spotted by an enemy long before you're even able to notice that combat has started around you.
The game lacks an easy mode, where you stop to be wounded after bandaging your wounds and being out of combat for a while - Of course, that wouldn't be realistic, but it would still make the game a little less hardcore for those that find the difficulty a bit too steep.
In operation flashpoint, when you reached a checkpoint, your squad was revived, wounds were healed and new squad members even spawned with full ammo.
In Arma III, I find myself running out of ammo very quickly, I'm only capable of carrying one rifle (an option to carry a rifle instead of a secondary weapon, such as a rocket launcher, would be welcome), and if I get hit at any point - It's going to affect the rest of the mission, and missions are very very long.
This is a bit too brutal for my liking - it wouldn't matter in a multiplayer game, but in a single player campaign where the missions are so long that I often feel like I could make a full time job out of playing the game, it's too much.
That said, you can't ask for a more realistic military infantry simulator. It very accurately represents what it feels like to be in the infantry.
The producers should have put in some optional missions that were skippable, showing some of the less exciting parts of being in the armed forces, such as building a camp, weapon and gear maintenance, dealing with a complicated and sometimes not 100% efficient chain of command and the many menial duties of being a soldier.
It'd be cool if there was a "I'm military" mode that could be activated, which results in you being assigned to a fire team in your unit, instead of basically being a joker.
The AI in your unit does operate like a military unit, with proper "fire and movement" maneuvers, but you're left out of this, because the producer knew the player wasn't necessarily going to be able to keep up with that, but some players have it the other way around, they sit there, confused, wondering why you're not getting advancement orders, why your team is acting like they have orders, but they didn't reach you.
That said, I think that it's GOOD that they did it like they did, because this game is supposed to be for everyone, and not just for people with military experience, but it wouldn't have taken them that much longer to incorporate a mode like that.
With the verdict that sometimes, the realism level in this game makes it TOO difficult to play through a limited interface, such as keyboard+mouse and monitor, then I can really recommend this game to anyone who likes military simulators.
It's not your average run of the mill FPS game though, so if you like high-paced and less punishing gameplay, I recommend something like battlefield instead.

Very fun game, despite the hurdles and problems.
-Multiple Gamemodes: From Payload, King of the Hill and CTF, to Mannpower, PASS time and more.
-One game is never the same: You'll ALWAYS have a fun time with a different experience.
-9 different classes, every one of them took a year each to develop (not really)
-Different Loadouts: Many Primary, Secondary and Melee weapons for each class, that makes possible playstyles almost infinite.
-Everyone looks different: It's very rare that you'll find two Scouts looking the same. Everyone has a certain style and fashion sense, so you'll never get bored of seeing the same look, cause there isn't any.
-An amazing community, and a chance to befriend many wonderful people.
-Hats
-Hats
-Hats
-Updates that have actual content can take a year or more to roll out.
-The developers don't talk much to the community, although that's a huge improvement from the silence we've been getting before.
-Some weapons are still unbalanced, making some Loadouts unusable while making others overpowered.
-Some bad apples in the bunch: from squeakers, to hackers and people who kick other people from servers for killing them and pushing the payload (Looking at you, Watchtower friendlies.)
-Trading is getting progressively harder, because the economy is slowly crumbling.
-Badly optimized.
Regardless, it's a game that I had fun with for more than 2000 hours, and I intend on playing more. If somehow you don't have this game in your library already (Come on, it's 2017), then you should download it. You're almost guaranteed to have fun.

It is NOT easy to hit a target with an assault rifle from 300 yards in real life, and this game seems to match that same difficulty. Fatigue is a real thing and it seriously hinders your accuracy in real life...Arma 3 makes you stop and catch your breath if you run too far or carry too much gear, or you will have a hard time hitting your target. Enemies are not stupid and they have great vision. I was engaged by two enemies from about 200 yards away and they were using bushes for cover as well as 3-5 second rushes when moving.
