Widely considered the best military simulator, ARMA III most certainly lives up to this title, at least in part. It is true that ARMA III and the ARMA series in general, have long been the best military simulators for infantry combat. The series’ modeling and depiction of other elements, in places, leaves something to be desired. If you are looking for a pure flight or armour simulator look somewhere else. Series like, DCS World, Blazes of War, Steel Beasts and Il-2 are more capable of scratching these more specific itches. Having said that, these games do all lack something ARMA III has in spades...the in-depth multilayered feeling it can give you. Opposed to the aforementioned simulators, ARMA III will have you alongside real players filling all roles; from rifleman to tank driver and Helo pilot to platoon commander. Though other simulators offer AI to fill these roles, (and I am not lying when I say that AI may sometimes do better than the people who pick this up thinking it is Battlefield) ARMA is evidence that there is nothing quite like the true feeling of being a part of a fully human combined arms operation, despite its flaws.
As I touched upon, ARMA is not like Battlefield or Call of Duty in the way it plays. If you approach the game in the same way you might approach other FPSs, you are not likely to find success. There are loads of videos of this game on YouTube and you should first familiarize yourself with the general feel of the game through this medium. Once you have an understanding of how it plays, you will know if it is something you are willing to put time and money into. Though somewhat contradictory to my previous statement, some videos may give a false impression of the game and so here are some (in want of a better word) vague guidelines as to what you can expect from ARMA III. At its core it is not (as it may first appear) a sandbox battlefield. It is a ‘hardcore’ military simulation focusing on infantry combat but including armoured vehicles, aircraft (fixed and rotary wing), boats, UAVs and more. That is what ARMA aims to be and in many ways is but on the other hand it is also a massive sandbox playground environment and with a few mods can be transformed from its original purpose. To this end I encourage you to look at the workshop and mod sites like Armaholic (
) to see if anything peaks your interest.
ARMA III has many interesting and unique features compared with other games which are worth noting. In this section of my review I will be talking about things generally outside of gameplay. If I were to cover all the interesting elements of ARMA III’s gameplay, I would quickly run out of space. To see these elements of the game I would direct you to YouTube or other mediums better suited to display them.
For starters, the modding scene for ARMA III is by far the biggest and well supported in the entire genre. This has resulted in a multitude of different things from many content creators which can change your entire experience. Though a lot of mods focus on adding modern military equipment, there are also mods to overhaul the game to the Vietnam War, a city based role playing experience or even the HALO universe. The possibilities are nearly endless so again, I encourage you to look. With ARMA IIIs integration with Steam Workshop, downloading mods has never been easier. Or hay, create your own mods! There is a thriving modding community and a lot of help out there so never say never.
Another notably feature is the way ARMA III’s DLC works. Instead of things like map packs, (which often lock a large portion of players away from others) ARMA III’s DLC is set out to specifically eliminate community divides. ARMA III’s DLCs have so far added in a combination of new equipment; helicopters and guns for example but also new mechanics such as; shooting from Helos and weapon resting. All key mechanics and functions of new DLC are always available to everyone regardless of whether you buy the DLC or not. The benefits to buying the DLC generally includes access to more equipment but nothing unbalancing. It is a really interesting system which keeps everyone at the same competitive level and in the same place compared with most other games in which DLC often serves to divide the community.
But of course I would be lying to you if I told you it was perfect, it by no means is. As no game is. The flight models or the aircraft and models for the ground vehicles are not very advanced, nor are the damage models of vehicles either. They do their job but pale in comparison to modeling in more specialised simulators like DCS World. Another issue many have with the game is the action menu. This is the menu which is used to interact with items and other people in the world. Though it is not an issue for everyone, it often plays up and sometimes fails to interact with certain things unless they are approached at the correct angle. Not so much a problem when walking around base but it can become annoying when it gets you killed because you just could not open that gate to get away from an enemy in time. Something else ARMA III seems to suffer from in my experience is its online player base. Most often incompetent children (who all think they are snipers) with a passion for team killing and an underappreciation for the game. Though the game has multiple campaigns, the meat of the game is in multiplayer. Unless you plan to steer clear of this portion of the player base, (or at least still have fun alongside them) it is best to either have a friend at your side or join one of the game’s many serious communities. Finally, the last and arguably largest problem ARMA III has is that of its game engine. The ARMA series in general is notorious for poor optimization and ARMA III is no exception. It is defiantly worth checking your computer specs before your buy. ARMA III is a hog of a game, even for high-end systems and so attempting to run it with low end hardware is often as bad as wasting money.
Though despite all of these issues and many smaller ones I could address, ARMA III is a fantastic game for what it is and what it achieves. No other game outside of the series is quite like it and its flaws are somewhat symptoms of its massive scale and the scope of what it encompasses. Despite everything, the positives, I feel, far outweigh the negatives and when you hit those perfect moments in ARMA III they are often incomparable to any other experiences in video gaming. Maybe not because of how good they are next to something else but because of what they are and what they mean. Moments which are unachievable in almost any other game. If either a military simulator with an infantry centric combined arms focus or a sandbox playground sounds appealing to you, ARMA III has all you need…and more.

Ive spent my fair share of money on this game, and with little regret up until now. The in game economy has begun to collapse as its main currency Refined metal, and Keys have all fluxuated unstably in the past year. The developers are unable to keep up with the expectations of its players, and have♥♥♥♥♥♥out 'major' updates such as MYM, as a poor attempt to introduce a matchmaking system that would rely on 'ranks', which might as well be glorified stickers as they have NO, ZILCH, NADA, role in sorting you into a server. This fantastic game has been overrun with hackers and scammers that are looking to make a quick profit over its broken, and dying in game currency. The time i have spent in UGC games have been some of the last fun times i have had in this game. The backlash from the TF2 community everytime Valve fails to deliver a promise has helped excavate a deep, sizeable grave for this dying game. Rest In Peace. Pootis will be missed.

H1Z1
King of the Kill is an upcoming deathmatch survival video game developed by Daybreak Game Company for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. H1Z1: King of the Kill was created after the original H1Z1 game was split into two separate projects in February 2016.
Release:
The game was originally released on Steam as an early access title on January 15, 2015. At release, the game suffered from severe technical issues. Players reported that they could not login to their account or enter any active server. Framerate issues, lack of voice chat and AI problems were also reported. A new bug, which made all servers go offline, was also introduced to the game after the developer released a patch to fix other problems. Despite the unstable launch, John Smedley, CEO of Daybreak Game Company, announced that the game had sold over a million copies by March 2015.
In February 2016, it was announced by Daybreak that the game originally known simply as H1Z1 had been split into two separate projects with their own dedicated development teams, subtitled Just Survive and King of the Kill. Later that year, it was announced that development of the console versions were paused in order to focus on the Windows version of the game, which was given an official release date of September 20, 2016. However, a week prior release, the game's executive producer stated that due to many features remaining unfinished by then, the game would remain in early access until further notice. As a compromise, the game received a large update on September 20, including many of the features intended for the official release.

For everyone else with a normal and healthy attention span:
Before i even get into commenting about the game it self, I want to say how well optimized this game actually is, compared to Arma2 and many other games of today in my experience, and how happy i am to see this for a change!
Now i can run Arma2 on top settings with lower filter settings, but there's always a twitch somewhere, thankfully with Arma3, there's no such twitching to be found at all, and as we all know, Arma3 looks vastly more pretty than Arma2 does. That is what i call awesome work!
My lowly PC Specs:
- 8Gb of 2400Mhz RAM @2392.2Mhz
- A10-7850K APU
APU stats:
CPU: Stock 3.7Ghz w/Turbo Boost to 4Ghz enabled
iGPU: BIOS OC'd from 720Mhz to 960Mhz w/2Gb RAM allocated.
NO DISCRETE GFX CARD ON THIS SYSTEM!
(1920x1080) 16:9 Widescreen mode on a 42" LCD tv with V-Sync Enabled and ANISO FILTERING: Ultra
QUALITY Settings:
Sampaling: 100%
Texture: Ultra
Objects: Ultra
Terrain: Ultra
Shadow: Low
Particles: Low
Cloud: Ultra
PIP: Standard
HDR: Low
Dynamic Lights: Standard
VISABILITY Settings:
Overall: 1600
Object: 1300
Shadow: 50
I think visability settings are at default, i can't recall changing them anyway.
Now i haven't really played around with the settings that much so far, i simply put everything up to ultra/maximum and then start dropping things down from there. I could still play around with some filter settings etc, but as it is now, I'm happy with everything.
Generally, the system hovers around 28fps to 40fps during bits with plenty of action going on so it's very good.
So while frame rates do vary, just as terms and conditions apply, the game has been smoothly playable despite it being a lowly stinking not even entry level PC.
Sometimes i even hit 58fps according to the fps counter built into Steam. I've never had a slideshow moment playing this game!
It's certainly no i7trillion with DDR10 RAM or a graphics card with 10 Billion Gb of GDDR6million RAM and platinum plated Rolls Royce engine fans on it, but for all that it is, it plays Arma3 smooth enough to be enjoyed with no let downs, and for that, I'm a happy chappy!
So thanks to the whole team at Bohemia Interactive for a very well put together game that works awesome on such an allegedly lowly system!
Now for the review of the game, which i will likely come back and update as i play different parts of it:
- ARMA 3:
Anyone else love that Game Launcher? Tis quite packed with awesome! I like how they implimented Presets for mods, very nice touch indeed. Thanks to those who came up with and created that little gem.
Overall, the MilSim part has big improvements over Arma2 that warrent purchase alone. I haz zero complaints about the gameplay.
Buy Arma 3 NOW!!!!!!!!
I don't get wow'd much by computer games these days, but now and again i see some awesome graphics in a game and it hits me just how awesome it is. Arma3 is that awesome, considering the massive scale of the land and everything that is on the terrain and still managing to pull off stunning scenery. Just wow.
I like the new streamlined look and feel and the menu and options si well laid out.
The new and additional training courses along with the new VR training system is a very nice touch to the game as well.
They have managed to make it all feel so familiar while making it all feel new. This isn't a copy and paste title at all like you get with COD.
If any game is warrented to be charging £65 each time, it's Arma, not COD. COD should be going for £20 because it really is a copy and paste title.
There's probably more devolopment work going into the weapons and character models in Arma that there has ever been in the whole call of duty franchise since COD4. Why the drooling and foaming at the mouth masses keep piling n the COD train I've no idea other than they're the types who ate the jumbo r/tard crayolas at school.
The Scuba mission was awesome, it was great to swim upto the boat and kill the bad guys while staying just below the surface. I hope there will be more scuba missions throughout the missions!
- KARTING DLC:
When it comes to the "Kart Racing" DLC... it's not so good here.
Now this isn't a biggie because it is something i can control and change the setting myself to how i like them set. but you can tell who ever set the default controls for the Karts is more of a Tank sim player than a racing sim player, that was clear the moment i tried to drive!
I started off using the keyboard, because i came straight from the target practice (which is awesome) and it was a horrid experience. Using the keyboard fro driving is probably like hitting on a girl only to find out that it's a tranny... yeah, that's how bad it is.
So I plugged in the xbox 360 controller (which this game does support!) and it turns out that even the default control settings with the control pad i had to use one of the sticks to acclerate/brake and the other of course for steering as you'd all expect and while it was still weird, i did managed to adapt to it and i even scored a gold soon after on the first Kart track. So I'll have to fire up the Xpadder and rework the driving controls to put accelerate/Brake onto the Left and Right Trigger buttons where they belong.
It would be great if the team could add a seperate control scheme just for the Kart racing DLC that is actually geared toward racing as oppsed to trank driving... that'd be very nice.
In regards to the Karting tracks, the 1st one was great, it flowed like a race course should flow, but the following tracks flowed only so far as flowing into the toilet. The street racing courses were very poorly marked and i even wound up heading down a side street because the placement of the TT marker appeared to want me to head straight on down that way instead of taking the corner.
I quickly got frustrated with the street courses as a result of the poor track layout and moved on to the next one.
The last course which is set on the runway, is more like a maze than a course. Now I've done plenty of real world kart racing on some pretty advanced driver complex courses, but I've never seen any real world course like that. Driving through a maze isn't fun, no sir, not one bit.
If who ever designed that course meant it as a test of patience, then well done to you, you certainly tested my patience. No track flow, what-so-ever.
Now, seeing as this is an Arma game, and now you guys have added Kart racing, howabout some Kart racing with WEAPONS?
Think Mario Kart but instead of firing shells at each other, we're firing proper Heat Seeking missles!
You could also manage firing a pistol while driving the karts as well. How about it?
Well that concludes this very long and very boring failure of a review for now.
Sadly for everyone i will likely update when i do more things in Arma3.
Thanks for reading, now go buy the game and enjoy yourselves.

I have played this game for a couple of hours since it was released back in Alpha. So far I can say that I am not disappointed.
For everyone who wants to buy this game I thought I'd put my review here to give some important pointers and hints which I think will prevent bad gaming experiences and help people to not get angry when they have or perceive issues with the game.

This game does not feature a flashy scoreboard or shiny medals for things like 360° no scopes. You will most likely not be awarded anything for playing good. The rewarding part about this game are the team experiences you can have if you open yourself for them. Even seemingly boring stuff like a foot patrol through a middle eastern map can turn out to be an amazing operation.
Following that team mentality, don't be the guy that asks for the lone wolf sniper role. You will most likely not be needed and you are simply annoying other people by even asking. In all my time in Arma 3 I have never found myself in dire need of a sniper rifle. Instead why don't you rather ask to be the AT guy. Those are always useful.
Same goes for vehicles and their use. Jets and tanks are usually taking away from the game more than they add and should only be brought in if they don't interfere with the infantry gameplay. You don't want to be the infantry man to run after a tank only to find everything in its path already dead. Returning back to base having done nothing because of a overstaffed tank section or air wing is the worst experience ever. This game is
and I can not stress that enough.
Finally I can only tell you, that if it turns out you like Arma 3 make sure you play around in it as much as you can. Even after 2000 Hours in it I still find new things in the vanilla game and am still learning. If you are open minded this game offers fun thousands of hours without being repetitive.
Even tho it has tons of bugs, it's still fun game to play. Fast paced, action packed, all I need to relax for a couple of hours.

I was very excited to get this game. I had read the reviews beforehand, and thought "well, maybe the reviews are just overexaggerated. The game can't be that bad, considering there's tons of people playing it". Boy, was I wrong.
The first game I played was probably the most fun I had in this game. I jumped in with a friend of mine and we were thrown into a world with 170 other players, each one trying to kill us. We gathered few supplies, while not entirely sure what said supplies do. This game does a great job at building tension and atmosphere for new players. Gun shots in the distance will make your heart race, and the sound of a car driving past will cause you to grip your mouse just a little tighter.
As the player count at the top of the screen gets lower and the gas gets closer, the real game begins. You hide behind a rock or in a patch of trees, knowing that the other players are doing the same. The tension is high as each team waits for the other to make a move. Gunshots are heard being exchanged in the distance. You can choose to follow the sound and catch few of the players off guard, or stay safe in the shadows. This is where the game shines, where the choices you make have stakes that are life and death. You have to decide whether taking an opponent out of the game is worth you putting your own life on the line.
But then you get to around 10 hours of playtime, and everything that I just stated above goes to♥♥♥♥♥♥
H1Z1 has the potential to be one of the greatest games of the year. Problem is, they missed the chance in 2016, when the game was released, and now aren't showing any desire to fix their game in 2017. H1 is an awful experience. I do not enjoy myself when playing it. It has been a full year since its release and it keeps getting worse. I wish people would stop buying this game and supporting the developers.
What I descirbed above was just the first few games you will play. As you start getting better with your aim, learning the game mechanics, you start to find the flaws that very much exist in this game, as you probably already know by reading other reviews.
You have the choice of playing a Solo, Duos, or Fives match. Unless you enjoy single-player experiences, Duos is the way to go. Grab a friend and party up. If you happen to have more than two friends, jump into a Fives match. However, I do not advise joining a Fives game unless you have 4 other people that you know on your team. The in-game mics in this game work 10% of the time, so communicating with your team is nearly impossible. In a game where communication and intel is key, having no communication is a death sentence. On top of that, if you don't have 5 players in a Fives match, you are immediately at a disadvantage. This is no means a game that you can pull off clutches when you are down a man. A squad of 5 with competent players can go around and completely wipe any team that does not have 5 players.
The biggest problem that I have with this game is the fact that there are no rewards for winning. At all. I've won Duos matches twice now, and the only sort of 'congratulations' you get is a screen that reads:
"Your team survived"
And below it is a button that returns you to the main menu. Solo is the only gamemode that shows your best matches, however with Duos and Fives you're left with nothing. As a fan of games like Destiny and The Division, I enjoy playing games for the rewards that I get. With H1Z1, I don't feel like I need to play. I can say that I've won every Duos match that I've ever played and you would have to believe me, because there is no way of knowing whether I'm telling the truth. There's no benefit to winning. In a game where winning is the ONLY objective, that's a huge problem for me.
I haven't even discussed the bugs. I won't go into detail; you can keep scrolling for the full list, but I'll just list a few that happened a little too often.
- Falling through the ground during the parachute phase.
- Random frame-drop spikes
- Delay between pressing a button and it actually registering in game
- Being unable to pick up items from the ground
- Shooting point blank with a shotgun but only doing 2 damage (This one happens way too often)
- Aiming over an object yet the bullets are hitting the object
- Asians
- Shooting somebody in the face with a shotgun at point blank range and only taking off their helmet, doing minimal damage
- Taking damage from jumping
- Firing blanks and not hitting an opponent
- Asians
- Pressing E to get into a car, only to have it fail and somebody else take the car from you
- Bumping other players while parachuting and getting thrown to bum-♥♥♥♥ nowhere
- Not being able to loot even though you have room in your backpack
- Doors not working properly
- Reload animation finishing but no reload was committed
- Car randomly flipping after colliding with a bush
- Asians
Oh, and the Asians run the game. Good luck trying to shoot them.

PROS:

CONS:

- Very repetitive
- High skill gap
- Asians

- LOTS of time out of combat, may not be a con for some, but I don't like running for 20 minutes.

Following that team mentality, don't be the guy that asks for the lone wolf sniper role. You will most likely not be needed and you are simply annoying other people by even asking. In all my time in Arma 3 I have never found myself in dire need of a sniper rifle. Instead why don't you rather ask to be the AT guy. Those are always useful.
Same goes for vehicles and their use. Jets and tanks are usually taking away from the game more than they add and should only be brought in if they don't interfere with the infantry gameplay. You don't want to be the infantry man to run after a tank only to find everything in its path already dead. Returning back to base having done nothing because of a overstaffed tank section or air wing is the worst experience ever. This game is
and I can not stress that enough.

Team Fortress 2 has been a source of great joy and fun for me in the past 1800 hours ive played, this game has a very special dynamic of timeless ingame graphics that still remain modern disregarding the fact this game is 10 years old. Its only in light of recent times, that this game has managed to instigate a new TF2 era of greed, hackers, un-balances, and false promises. The introdution of weapon skins in the game has moved tf2 one step closer to being like every other FPS on steam. Lack of updates and patches in recent time has led to a all time high in bugs and hackers. Valves Anti Cheat system, is a complete and utter joke, as it does nothing to stop or recognise atleast 3/4 of the hackers that are present in almost every game. Wait times for casual and competitive are ungodly, sometimes reaching into the 30 minute mark just so you can play a single game thats about to end. Ive spent my fair share of money on this game, and with little regret up until now. The in game economy has begun to collapse as its main currency Refined metal, and Keys have all fluxuated unstably in the past year. The developers are unable to keep up with the expectations of its players, and have♥♥♥♥♥♥out 'major' updates such as MYM, as a poor attempt to introduce a matchmaking system that would rely on 'ranks', which might as well be glorified stickers as they have NO, ZILCH, NADA, role in sorting you into a server. This fantastic game has been overrun with hackers and scammers that are looking to make a quick profit over its broken, and dying in game currency. The time i have spent in UGC games have been some of the last fun times i have had in this game. The backlash from the TF2 community everytime Valve fails to deliver a promise has helped excavate a deep, sizeable grave for this dying game. Rest In Peace. Pootis will be missed.

If you're looking for true military combat, with realism in every detail, then this game is for you. Arma 3 at its core is a true military simulation sandbox game. It is the Minecraft of military shooters. Arma allows you to engage in combat at all levels, from ground infantry, to dogfights, to vehicle combat, heck, you can even fight underwater.
If it's possible in real life, it's most likely possible in Arma. If not, there are plenty of mods made by the healthy, active community which can help make your dreams come true. Arma has been known for its modability. DayZ? Yea that was an Arma 2 mod before it was a standalone game. For some, Arma, as a great game alone, is simply a baseplate for you to make whatever you want. There are no limits.
The vast land of Altis (~270 square km) is all playable. There is no "backdrop" like Call of Duty or Battlefield. There is no one stopping you from playing on top of that awesome looking hill or in that large town. Too big for you? Stratis is only 20 square km. Still too big? Well there's never an issue with going smaller with the great map tools like the editor and Zeus.
The options are limitless. No levels, no unlocks, no pay to win, no stupid DLC so you can have forests or Close Quarters Combat specific maps. Arma 3 is here so you can experience war the way YOU want to. No matter what your interest is, there's sure to be a server or group out there for you. There is no feeling similar to accomplishing a mission that was made and played by real people. No AI, no scripted events, all people. It feels like you just came out of a badass movie battle, because that's pretty much what it just was. That's what this game is about. You want to do it? Go right on ahead. As the saying goes,
Now this review didn't cover everything, and by no means is this game flawless, but it is a game that has kept me interested for quite some time. As such, I will try my best to make a cons vs pros list (cons first because there aren't as much).
- Arma 3 has been known to be unoptimized. You need a pretty strong rig to even hit 40 FPS. However, don't let this
stop you from playing. Use this link to see if you can run Arma 3:
(Not the best accuracy, but it gives you an idea.)
- The optimization is also based off the server you join. If you join a crappy server with a ping of 300, consider joining
a different server.
- As you may have heard, this game uses almost all the buttons on your keyboard. Which may sound scary, but come
on let's be realistic. This is a military simulation, were you expecting simple controls? Is war easy?
- You will fear death, no doubt
- Guns are loud, so be careful
- Realistic travel time - Bullets take time to travel, and they drop. Also, sound travels too, so expect to see an
explosion before hearing it
- Just came back from your last tour and want to relive the experiences of battle without PTSD? There is a server for
you. EXTREME military simulation servers are out there. Watch out, 1 toe out of line, and you're banned in an instant.
- The terrain is very life-like. There is wildlife, there can be civilians if you choose, the stars can actually be used as a
map, etc
- The engine is simply beautiful. The tiniest details are prevalent, such as butterflies' shadows, and your muzzle is
below your optic
- Zeus is like a real-time gamemaster. As a multiplayer battle is going on, you can change the map, infantry #'s, and
a lot more with the power of Zeus. Zeus is a specific game mode, so come join the community!
To end, Arma 3 will not disappoint. As emphasized enough, what you want to do, you can do. Writing a review is hard, so off the top of my head, I probably missed a lot of things. However, i got the big points down.

TL;DR: tf2 was a great game that suffered from neglect and poor decision making on the part of the developers, which made sour my memories of the game.
Tf2 used to be one of my favorite games, and I spent a lot of time on it (~4,000 hours divided among multiple accounts) and it held a special place in my heart.  I loved the game (mainly because I could run it on integrated graphics when little else could), and when I first found it several years ago I was captivated by the charm and wit of each of the different characters.  However, upon revisiting the game on another account I was saddened to see that the game that I had once loved had become a shell of its former self, due to a few main points that I'll cover.
one of my favorite parts of this game was the in game trading and the cosmetic items.  The ability to customize each class how you wanted them made me feel like I was giving them a personal touch that could be shown to everyone else.  This was one of the reasons that I felt this game was becoming stale, and when I revisited it I was confused by all of the changes they made to many existing hats, such as making them multi class or adding workshop items that were given lots of care by their creators but left me wondering, "does this really fit in this game?"  They seemed odd to me, but what really struck me as lazy was adding the rarities to the contract items, which I felt was frivolous and only there to generate revenue quicker by artificially inflating the value.  In addition to this, the third party gambling sites (which steam sent cease and desists) were shut down, and rightfully so, but offered a broader scope of replay value for the game, since in my personal experience, whenever I won I was always excited to buy the new shiny gun or gaudy hat and flaunt them.  I understood that the sites were fundamentally flawed, and abused it, but this exploit was no secret to anybody (having an item limit in a jackpot where your bet value is proportional to win % made it easy for late entries to "snipe" pots with large bets.).  When they shut this down, I felt like they closed off a facilitator to make good profit (if you were smart and knew the risks) and that getting the new hats or weapons would be a lot harder.  I can't speak about the trading scene, since I've been out of it for so long, but my inference is that it hasn't fared well with age either.  It used to be a magical place where you could steal a kids hat, then laugh your way to the bank after you get banned from the trade server, but I don't feel that magic anymore.
a lot of you tubers touched on similar topics like this.  As of my departure from this game (around Gun Mettle's close), a lot of the significant updates seemed watered down or lackluster.  I see a lot of reskins and hats, occasionally new maps, but very little to get excited for anymore.  The reality is that you cannot continue to play a game forever, but good content can help to prolong this expiration.  After Gun Mettle was over, I asked myself "what's next?" And they came out with Tough Break, which I picked up for maybe a few hours out of pure nostalgia, then remembered gun mettle and how they were nearly identical to me, and quit again.  I played for about an hour after the Matchmaking update was out for a few months, but I was not impressed by it and put the game down, probably for good this time.
the server browser was one of my favorite features of the game.  It allowed you to find whatever kooky game mode or community you wanted, and connected you there with an easy to understand user interface.  A lot of my time in this game was spent hanging around on trade servers and the like with other people who wanted to hang around as well.  I think that when the server browser went the way of the dinosaur, a lot of communities rooted within tf2 were impacted. A new barrier stood between them and potential new members of their community, and I think it helped to doom smaller ones such as one of my favorites, Swirlclinic.  Although there's still a group for Swirlclinic, there are no existing servers anymore, I watched the player base dwindle.  And although it seemed like it had died, I felt that there may have still been hope for it if the servers stayed up, until the final nail in the coffin manifested in the form of the server browser disappearing.
These are just a few of my personal complaints and experiences with this once great game.  I understand that these might not apply to everyone, and if you feel differently about some of these points, feel free to respond if you have the time

My thoughts on Team Fortress 2:
So, Team Fortress 2 is a FPS game, with many different classes to choose from (9 selectable classes).
These different classes all have unique weapon load-outs, movement speeds and health points. The fastest being Scout, and the slowest being Heavy (Or as the community calls him, Hoovy). The only downside, is that some classes are too over powered. Like the Spy with his ability to disguise as somebody from the enemy team! The Medic can run as fast as a Scout if he uses the Stock Medi-Gun or the Kritzgraig (Is that how you say it?). For a bonus affect, he builds up "Uber Charge" the more he heals his team-mates during a round or before it even begins (Healing team-mates before the round starts makes the Uber Charge increase faster).
Now, all though these things are very useful, they can be a huge pain sometimes. Say, a Medic is healing a Pyro and his Uber Charge is ready, but then an enemy Spy backstabs the Medic, meaning he looses his Uber, having to charge it again. This can be avoidable, if the Medic Ubers before theSpy backstabs him. The medic would be immune to the backstab, since he immune to any damage (apart from trains or saws or falling out of the map) and can alert the Pyro he was healing, therefor putting the Spy in a bad situation.
A very over powered weapon for the Scout class, is: Bonk! Atomic Punch. Once drank, the player is invincible to any attack for only a phew short seconds. This is a pain for Engineers, as he can just run past the sentry only getting pushed back by the force of the bullets. The only downside for the Scout, is that he cannot use any guns or weapons during this time. He cannot shoot or hit anybody until the effect has worn off.

After putting more time into this game, I can see why many people hate it, and why there are so many negative reviews. I've run the game on my SSD and hard drive, and for those running on hard drive, RIP. The game runs pretty well on my i5-7500 16GB RAM GTX 1050TI 4gb. I get about 90+ frames on max. The gameplay is very, well, odd. A lot of times you feel like you get cheesed by players who know how play better, or you just get beat by the games mechanics. Lack of weapons, vehicles, and, due to the cost of crates for character customization (for the record, you get a crate every 5 levels, which takes AGES), really bring this game down. It's not very fun to have a shotgun and AR every game. Overall, not bad, but I give it 7/10. Recommend if you want some competition, otherwise, skip it.

Arma 3 is a military simulator with 2 islands as the setting, Stratis and Altis, based off of Greek Islands in the Mediterranean. The campaign focuses on the time period of 2035 and follows Kerry, a soldier in NATO stationed in Stratis. Personally I have only gotten halfway through the 3 episode campaign  (2nd episode) Arma 3 is much more beautiful and it's obvious a lot of work has been put into graphical detail, though this hindered other key things such as vehicles  (Arma 2 has so much more!)
Pros: Looks truly amazing
Much higher FPS than Arma 2
Great campaign
Clothing choices
Mods are easier to get (Steam workshop)
Virtual Arsenal allows you to gear up your character for anything and saves a lot of time making your character manually.
Crazy stuff is possible even though it's a simulator
3D editor will be coming in the first quarter of 2016 allowing for more scenarios to be made with little to no difficulty  (maybe more work though)
Editor allows for many different scenarios such as demolition, sniping, etc
DLC content is included in base game though has an annoying ad if not purchased
Cons: Editor can still be confusing and scripts are easy to forget
Less content than I would have expected though there are attachments for weapons which satisfies those who want high customizability
Getting the original maps like Chernarus and Sahrani are in AiA and can be a more complicated process to get than for most
Some things seen in game are so unrealistic, see how the hunter will take airtime
In conclusion, Arma 3 is a great game with more content coming and it's easy to get many many hours into the game. Anything is possible and it reminds me of a gmod with military focus. There's tons of potential and I recommend  it for anyone who can run it

I'm going to talk about the game modes and the classes, pros and cons.
CLASSES:
Scout- he is the fastest class, and having the ability to double jump is very helpful! He starts off with a scatter gun, a shortstop (I think it's called), and a baseball bat.
Solider- he is one of the slower classes but he can rocket jump with his RPG. He also has a shovel and a shotgun, a solider indeed.
Pyro- he mumbles and sees everything in Pyroland, if you have the googles or the rainblower. He has a flamethrower which sets his enemys on fire, (it's helpful for exposing spys!) he also is one of the classes that have a shotgun, and a fire axe to wack and hack.
Demo Man- A scottish drunk that can shoot genades, which expolde on contact, plus he also has sticky bombs, place them and wait for your enemy before... BOOM! He also has a bottle for melee
Heavy- he is the slowest, but has the most health, with his minigun he can easily kill at close range, also having a shotgun and his fist.
Enginer- he can build sentrys, which lock on and kills enemys, at level one they shoot slow and have low health, level two adds machine guns, and level 3 adds rockets and the maximun health. Dispenser give ammo and health, and can be upgraded. Teleporters only go one way, but can transfer players quickly, like from spawn to the battlefield. All of these can't be placed IN spawn, and they cost metal, which is given from ammo crates. He also gets a shotgun, wrench, and pistol, a destroyer and builder. Buildings can be upgraded by hitting them with a wrench.
Medic- He can shoot people with his syring gun, but when his teammates need help? use the medigun! When healing, your ubercharge grows, which can be used on another player making the medic and other player invincible for a short time.
Sniper- Headshots count! Zoom in with your scope to shoot people long range, also while zoomed in, your charge will go up! Let get full for maximum damage! He also carries a Kuri, and a SMG.
Spy- playing as him will let you cloak with right click (can't use it forever!), he also has a revolver, great for picking off enemys with low health. Also has a knife which does low damage, but can kill them instantly when backstabbing the person. He can also sap sentrys and disguise as enemy players! Attacking will reveal you.
GAMEMODES:
Attack and Defend: Blue must capture all of the points, capturing a point adds time. Red must defend
Capture The Flag: Blue and Red must capture each others intelligence and bring back to there own.
Control The Points: Red and Blue must fight to control all the points.
Payload: Blue must push a blue cart to the end, going threw the control points, which add time, Red must defend

I cannot recommend this game enough! If you are like me and you like realistic war scenarios, then this game is for you! If you like funny moments with your friends, this game is for you! If you are a graphics and visual type, this game is for you! Lets get started with the main game.
1. The story is horrid, but not as bad as other storylines such as Battlefield.
2. The graphics are beautiful! This game shows off what the PC can handle!
3. The gunplay is very fun and realistic!
4. The editor is very detailed and fun to mess around with!
5.The multiplayer is astounding! It feels like you are moving through a alive battlefield with real people, pondering the next strategy!
Thats enough with the base game, lets move to the real kicker... The multiplayer mods! I will be making a list of the main mods, and details surrounding them.
1.(my personal favorite) Altis Life: Altis Life is pretty much just real life simulator! You get to be a civilian, a cop, a rebel, a drug dealer, a medic, and really anything you want to be. But remember, there are laws! KIDNEYS :D!
2. Wasteland: Wasteland is just living in a war torn world, with gangs roaming around, and whats left of the military to fight them off. Wasteland is pretty much the base game, but with gangs, shops, and of course, base building!
3. DayZ Exile: Remember that buggy mess known as DayZ Standalone? It was fantastic, but this improves it in every aspect!
It feels more zombie like! Hoards will pass through your base while you try to avoid them, herds will get in your way leaving you to try to fight them off! Not glitching through walls every 5 seconds *cough cough* DayZ SA*cough cough*.
Overall rating of this almost perfect game is..................

You can play as an RTS game master as well, so you can give your buddies helicopters whenever they ask for them and go do missions that way, too. Just make sure to give lots of helicopters, since newer players are prone to crashing them.
Just remember, more helicopters.

PROS
1: fun, simple & detailed graphics, allowing for a non-overwhelming feel that many other gun related games would give, coupled with it's simplistic design makes it easier to get into.
2: The game has plenty to offer, ranging from switchblades, to Soda's that give you a boost in speed & strength, along with a fairly easy to get into, customization system allowing for one to combine items onto a character, to play them as you'd see fit.
3: There is a relatively fun & passive community, where even at the very basic of skill levels, you can still find help with just asking in chat, on different servers.
4: There are often people whom can tell you tips & tricks, along with an old community & fun customized servers, such as surfing etc.
CONS
1: Suffers from a lack of character variety, you can always use items to change how you play, however, the basis of the classes will stay the same.
2: Can be difficult to learn, with such an old community, It can take months to get to just the average player level, and some classes can be hard to play, but, if other classes aren't interesting to you, then you are forced to spend months learning those classes.
3: Often times there will be an issue of a lack of healers or having too many of one specific class, which can be a bit difficult to work out when some of the community is too focused on playing the game rather than communicate.
Overall, I'll give the game a good... 68/100.

ArmA 3 is a military sandbox/simulation videogame developed by Bohemia Interactive and released in 2013. It offers both singleplayer and multiplayer modes, and the game can be played both offline and online. ArmA 3 is a very fun videogame, and in my opinion, better than Arma 2, for a variety of reasons.
First off, the game's animations have vastly improved. No longer do the animations look clunky and/or laggy (as they did in ArmA 2), the animations in 3 look smooth as silk. Watching a friendly squad of BLUFOR (USA) units move across the landscape looks realistic and presentable. Vaulting over a fence that stands between you and a vehicle feels (and looks) good. Bohemia really did a fantastic job with the animations.
Secondly, the game's graphics have been enhanced. The game's engine (called the "RV4") allows for greater graphical fidelity than ArmA 2, and because of this, offers crisp and beautiful scenes in the game's world. Not speaking from personal experience, ArmA 3 on ultra looks as good, if not even better, than GTA V on ultra. The grass looks real, uniforms look soft, objects look smooth, and so on so forth. Played on low settings, ArmA 3 still manages to look decent, which is awesome.
Thirdly, ArmA 3's audio is nothing short of amazing. Being pinned down by enemy gunfire makes you feel like you're really there in the scene. Being right next to a rifle or lmg while it's being fired is loud and it feels like an actual gun going off. I will say, however that this game does unfornatuely suffer from an odd bug; the footsteps created by your player character actually appear from behind you, which confuses some players.
Last but not least, the performance of ArmA 3 has been increased. The game does manage to run better than ArmA 2 did, however it still isn't completely optimized and can run bad on your machine, even if you're rocking a 970, i7 and 8 gigs of ram; the performance in ArmA 3 is seemingly random and apparently doesn't entirely rely on your gpu, but rather your cpu to do most of the work. Personally I'm not too bothered by ArmA 3's performance; the game runs smooth while in the wilderness (away from towns and the such) but while in towns the frames drop some, which is fine for me personally.
Overall, I think ArmA 3 is definitely worth the price, however there is one more thing that in my opinion, is ArmA 3's greatest flaw; the dlc for ArmA 3 is overpriced. The recently released "Apex" expansion costs about 34 dollars, and what it includes is one map, some more uniforms, units, vehicles and weapons. While I think the map is very cool and a nice deperature from the previous ArmA maps (like ArmA 2's Chernarus), I just can't recommend the dlc at that price, due to mods existing and even being a pivotal part of the ArmA experience nowadays; with mods you can get pretty much everything the dlc has to offer, aside from the map, for free. This makes the dlc almost obsolete, and if it weren't for the map, I wouldn't recommend the dlc at all. I personally think Bohemia should release the Marksmen and Helicopters dlc (which each only add a couple of weapons and/or vehicles) for free, and lower the price of the apex dlc, because they owe us ArmA gamers that much.

Well, as most have probably said this game has almost complete limitations. You can fly a helicopter on your own, or join a police department in some advanced roleplay communities. This game could be considered a "simulator" to some, but to those who play it understand what it is, a game where you can literally do what you want. Mod support through the community is amazing, and the servers are pretty great aswell.
As for singleplayer, I have not touched it once. I played the singleplayer within Arma 2, the previous version of this game, was not the best thing in the world. The communities for this game are endless, as I said previously there are vast online communities that are based on roleplay, such as Critical Gaming, but also communities that are more based in hard-core military roleplay, which use radio-codes, coordinates and more militaristic banter, these are communities such as Shack Tactical.
Another cool this? If you do not understand the game on how to do specific things, check out the steam workshop! You can find mission style tutorials on there, where you may find yourself very interested. It has limitless possibilites.
Now that I have said all the things good about it, let's get to the cons, and yes, this game has a few. Graphics, you do not  need a beefy grapahics card, although it does help. You need a good CPU though, as this game basis almost all of it's functions off of the CPU. You can adjust your settings which will help in some cases, but alot of times not in others. Errors are a common thing if you are interested in mods, if not, you should be good. This is a very specification intensive game, which most would not consider this a bad thing but in my book it limits the playerbase.
Well, that's really it for my review. At the end, would I suggest this game? Absolutely, if you are looking for a game that provides almost COUNTLESS HOURS, this is your area! Remember how I mentioned modifications previously? Not only are there software mods, but also hardware such as TrackIR, and you could also use a joystick with advanced piloting mode.

2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

- The game offers many special features, such as an entire economy and many websites dedicated to making it easier.
- It is one of the many games that features the ability to switch between DirectX versions.
- Things like Mods and Sprays are simple to add to the game.
- Running your own servers with your own bots is easy and quick.
- The game is 10 years old as of now, and the community is still growing.
NEGATIVES
- The recommended settings in the Video section are complete bull****.
- The community, despite meeting all of my friends on this game, is toxic, and I think anyone could agree.
- The training menu/maps are awful and buggy, and only 3 classes are featured.
- As much as I love supporting you Valve, hats are rediculously overpriced on the Mann Co Store.
- There are very, very few updates for this game, and the past few ones have been total let downs. [SIDE NOTE: don't get me wrong, there are lots of things I enjoyed in the past few updates, but I think we can all come to a consensus that most of it was bad.]
- Most games, especially capture the flag, drag on for a long time. I spent 3 hours in a single 2fort game once.
- Competative cannot be used in Directx v8.
- This game has relied almost entirely on the community for several years, so much that parts of the TFteam acknowledged it. Note that this wouldn't be a negative thing if the community wasn't getting slowly smaller/more toxic due to lack of new content.
That's all i have to say. I will try my hardest to find more things about this game in the future, and let you all know what they are. Thank you for reading, have a wonderful day.

My experience with this game can be summed as thus: every update I found myself testing the changes, nodding in satisfaction, then quitting the game to await the next update.
Arkane knows how to make a good game. No question. But if you film an Oscar-worthy movie and the lens is smudged while filming, you can't judge what's underneath without acknowledging what's been marring your experience the entire time.
=============================
PERFORMANCE
Everyone is aware of the performance issues, and these still persist to this day. It runs much better than at launch, where it was literally unplayable, but that's because the game looks worse than before - the most noticeable change being the extremely aggressive LOD scaling. Out of the corner of your eye you notice the shapes of window frames and posters on distant buildings morphing in shape, or the furniture at the opposite end of a long hallway suddenly blinking into existence. FPS dropped to 15 when stabbing a gravehound, so they simply removed the inky visual effect that was causing the problem instead of optimizing it.
Also, Denuvo authentication is one of the longest "loading screens" of the game. Around half a minute to a full minute or more every startup.
=============================
GAMEPLAY
For the most part, gameplay is excellent and is Dishonored's strongest suit.
Dark Vision was changed to a blurry short range sonar so unlike Dishonored 1 you aren't constantly seeing blue and yellow because you had no reason not to
AI is much smarter
Nonlethal combat options are a blast
Bonecharm crafting system allows for player flexibility and "builds"
Each level feels lived-in while maintaining the duality of directive flow and open options that made the first game so good.
Emily and Corvo have distinct animations and final weapon upgrades. The animations are supremely cool.
Each level is fairly distinct, some with extremely interesting central "gimmicks." I do, however, wish the game relied less on them and had more "regular" areas.
However, under the hood lie other problems. Most of them are quality-of-life issues:
Gone are the hotkeys for journal, inventory, bonecharms, powers. Only one "journal" exists now, despite still having separate subsections.
It took months for the power wheel to be fixed. It took almost a full second after activating to pop up and be usable, breaking flow so badly I almost never used it in the first place. It's finally fixed now, but this issue was glaring and it took so long to be addressed most of us played through without it fixed.
Thrown objects don't always go exactly where your crosshair is. While this adds a layer of difficulty, it feels noticeably more clunky than in the first game.
Mana regen is pitifully slow. From using a power to fully regenerating, Dishonored 1's time is 4.7 seconds -> 3.1 seconds with Spiritual Pool. Dishonored 2's time with 4x Spiritual Pool is 6.3s -> 5.5s. The devs said they fixed this effect, but it was only made worse.
Bugs. Street speakers not playing. Dying after possessing gravehounds. An arc pylon never shutting down after pulling out its power, leaving it to either be dangerous to you to dangerous to your nonlethal playthrough. Some of these still aren't fixed.
=============================
STORY AND ATMOSPHERE
Reactivity
Great. My favorite part of Dishonored. You need to hide from a gang member to access a certain black market shop, and there are different scenarios and dialogue for if you hide, if you run into him outside, kill him outside, or kill him inside.
It made sense to me to play Emily first, but her story felt lackluster, like people at every turn were saying "check your royal privilege" despite my efforts to resolve everyone's problems without drawing blood. Corvo's is MUCH more interesting as a veteran of Dishonored 1.
The Outsider and The Void
I hate the new Outsider and his new voice. He felt threatening and malicious in the first game due to how calm and composed he was, and the Void felt like a strange and otherworldly place. The vignettes of Dunwall made it feel both unnatural and unnerving yet fundamentally woven into the universe. In Dishonored 2, it's just smoky blackness and sharp rocks. The Outsider is much jollier and moves around erratically, making grandiose hand gestures. They actually had a plot plot that could explain this change, but it was never addressed, so it just seems like a pointless retcon to me.
Main Plot
Dishonored's worldbuilding was always one of its appeals, and that remains true in Dishonored 2. However, the villains felt lackluster. Only the main villain has a real presence throughout the game, whereas everyone else feels introduced abruptly only to fall by your hand, all within the same mission. In Dishonored 1 everything felt personal and real. Perhaps it was because of the long intro where you interacted with most of them, or the Hound Pits's cast of characters all having different connections to your targets.
As you can see, I've played this game a LOT and have put a lot of thought into it. It was definitely worth all those hours and all that money, but the condition it was at launch and the sluggish drip-feed of support we barely get now is unacceptable. To set a precedent for future games, I can't recommend buying this unless they manage to fix all the performance issues and bugs, which doesn't seem to be happening anytime soon.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Awesome game.  Bought it during the Christmas sale and not only can I not stop playing but also when I am not playing I am thinking about it... tactics, different approaches, etc.  For me a sign of a great game is not one that you get frustrated having to replay missions (from the SP Campaign) but when you replay them over and over because you know YOU could have done something differently... different move, different tactic, etc.  A3 provides that in spades!  So fun to keep working till you get the SKILL correct to move on in the mission.
Thus far I have only played mostly SP campaign missions and the VR training to learn the details of the game, however I have played some MP games (stole a boat, a truck, secured some points...) but MP thus far concerns me.  I want to play some serious MP but its a bit daunting for the newb without a core group of friends.  I am looking into more info about how to link up with a group, but to be honest the SP campaign and the downloadable content is enough to rationalize the price.
Also, I read a bunch of reviews and posts about frame rate being poor, not optimized, etc... I am running it on High settings that look great and it runs supurb with great FPS and no lag.  Not sure what people are experiencing that is slow but for me its been great (beautiful even) and I am running it on a 3 year old Samsung Gamer 7 laptop...  runs like a charm for me and hasnt crashed once (knock wood).
Note - I did play Operation Flashpoint back in the day and this of course is a lot like that.  LOVED that game, so really enjoying this.

After almost spending my entire life (almost 1000 hours, including the original H1Z1) here is my final review for you guys.
It all began 2015, where the glorious H1Z1 has been released. At this time the game was full of bugs, well I didn't judge in those days, because it was an Early-Access-Version of the game.
Though it had a lot of bugs, it was really fun to play, with friends of course.
At this time you actually were getting rewards for winning, even if you were playing in a group. Nowadays you will not get rewarded after winning when playing with a group. So for some people (including me), the motivation to win was missing, since those days.
After the Developer Studio switched and reorganized from Sony Online Entertainment to Daybreak Games (TheyBreak Games     ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) ) the game was on their way to fall down.
You couldn't see any progress in developing, major bugs existed for months, the priority list of Daybreak Games was disastrous. Well though I had those bad impressions, I wasn't missing the fun at this time.
In 2016 they made the decision split the game into two. H1Z1: Just Survive and H1Z1: King of the Kill. I had hope in the developement of this game again, because I thought maybe it will help them to organize themselfs better and to set priorities.
On one side I was happy that they brought some new stuff, new gamemodes to play, events, etc., like Ignition, Skirmish, Green Dawn, Hardcore, but on the other side major bugs still existed. But for me, it was still fun to play.
Later 2016 they have made their biggest mistake. They (re)-"launched" their game (fun-fact: its still in early-access) and promised a major change in gameplay, graphics, performance and developing. So let's see what the "launch" brought us:
(1) They have removed the old map and replaced it with the new Z2-Map. You might ask yourself now, what, is so bad about the new Z2-Map?:
- Though they promised graphic enhancements, they've just increased the color saturation, to pretend, that graphics are better now. But as you might guess: They are not even close to better. The lightnings in the buildings are worse then ever. You can hardly see the loot inside of the buildings.
- The actual reason for why the map was changed was that the devs thought, that the original map was maybe a bit too much copy and pasted. Here is my opionion on that: The new map is even more copy and pasted. Almost every buildings looks the same.
- There are no real memorial places or fighting spots, like they were on the original map. Maybe it is because that I am a little bit nostalgic, but people who have played the original H1Z1 will understand me, when I rave about PV Police-Station, Radio-Tower, Opfer Camp, Reservoir Dam, B2, Hospital, etc, etc...
- Loot is clipping inside of the textures so you cannot pick it up. This bug exists since almost half a year now.
- Floating trees and ugly streets and textures are daily fare.
- They won't give us the opportunity to play the old map, since they "deleted it by mistake" so they said. (Another fun-fact: the old map is still available in H1Z1: JS, so there is no way that it had been deleted)
- There is no pit in the new Box of Destiny. Where the hell shall summit go then?
(2) They have made a major change to the Interface and the HUD, which in my eyes clearly looks fancier but is actually worse than the original, because it seems really unclearly to me.
(3) The translations are actually worse than google translator.
(4) They have removed previous exlusive gamemodes, so you can't play them anymore. Well there is the ability to do so, but there never had been an event where you can play them.
(5) They brought in a new rewards system and removed the old one. Unfortunatley, I never could experience those, because as you might noticed, I was always playing with friends. But nope, there are still no rewards for groups.
(6) The performance is still as bad as in the old H1Z1.
You might ask yourself now, why did they make those changes and why did they relaunch the game?
Clear answer boys: to market the game more efficient.
I have lost faith in this game and thats why I felt the need to write this review.
I have the bad feeling that this game won't get any better, since the problem-solving approaches from the developers are slow, less efficient and mostly alternative and do not treat the cause of most problems.

ArmA 3 is probably one of the better things that happened in my gaming experiances. I bought it this Christmas during the winter sale of 2015. I was highly anticipating this game to be on sale so you can probably imagine my grace when I got this game.
The game itself is really good. It has details mostly with the 40+ different guns and gear. The community is great and constantly work for the game. It is what makes ArmA 3 stand out as a video game. The game itself is not very optimised, so you will need a good PC to get 60fps when playing or turn your settings down. But its nothing too bad. I got 60 fps constantly in any enviorment because I lowered my graphics to standard. The Steam Workshop is a great source for mods and custom content. Something ArmA 1 and 2 didnt have, it makes playing modded gamemodes like Battle Royale, DayZ (Exile, Breaking Point, Epoch etc.), various RPG gamemodes like Altis Life and Life mod, Wasteland, Domination and many others easier to get into without going to Armaholic websites. This is something I havent seen since the GMod workshop.
It does have some server issues and as I previously stated optimisation issues, but nothing like DayZ Standalone. The review for that game you can check out at my reviews on my Steam profile.
Overall this game is detailed and if you have some time, it deserves you to play it. It has all that a good game should have.
8/10

H1Z1 KOTK is a TPS/FPS battle royale game that places over 150 player on a single map for an all out brawl to see one man stand as the victor. Sounds fun!!. There is however only one big glareing flaw that many players notice when playing this game and that is the simple fact that you can theoretically experince everything the game has to offer in one game, given the nature of its gameplay. On paper this type of game seems perfect with seemingly endless replayability as you look for new ways to strategicly take down your enemies or make a crucial decision to engage your enemy or leave your losing battle to re equip yourself.
H1Z1 KOTK biggest flaw is that the game wasnt originally suppose to be a battle royale brawler. Makeing a new game based on the same mechanics of your original does not support healthy gameplay and can lead to terrible balance issues, lack of depth, and a lack of self personality. However for not being the game they originally designed and promised when the original H1Z1 release (Now called H1Z1 Just Survive) i can confidently say that the developers of this project have been only moving forward with this game, giving constant updates and provideing a great vanity progression system that does nothing but compliment the theme of the game just that much more.
This game does have it's problems but that doesn't mean you cant have a great time with it and the being one of the top most played games on steam only proves this to be true. Hopefully in the future we can see more updates giving us more variety in gameplay, through gun attatchments or new maps. Overall H1Z1 KOTK can offer you some great experiences and if you got a few friends I dont see a reason for you to not pick this game up.

A great underrated classic that still has populated servers 24/7. (You can check for players with the in-game server list, bots won't be shown.) TFC offers one-of-a-kind exciting fast paced gameplay with tons of tactics and ways of playing the game. Easy to get into and enjoy, hard to master. However, you're bound to have fun along the way.
Despite old age, the game has a timeless design with a completely customizable appearance; you can choose from many custom models, sprites, skins, textures etc. There are active community servers hosting many of thousands of custom maps total with official game modes like; Capture The Flag, Control point, Attack/Defend, Escort, Deathmatch as well as custom ones like King of the Hill, Hold or Score Ball etc.
If you're interested in skill jumping (with weapons) there are servers hosting maps made for conc-, grenade-, rocket- and pipe jumping. There are also a lot of movement skill maps where you can climb, bunnyhop, strafe, surf, ramp slide and even water glide (shark) on a few servers. Or if you just want to play some random fun maps and mess around, there's escape, puzzle, hide & seek, sniping, role-play, secret hunting, low gravity and so on. As for mods, there's NeoTF (which gives you extra abilities and buildables), AdminOP (Ent Mod, Radio Mod, Hook Mod) and others.
It's not just one of, but The most popular online multiplayer game of all back in 1999 before CS took the crown. Nowadays, there are barely any FPS games that don't get boring after a few hours. TFC will have you keep coming back for more, time and time again. Without relying on achievements or item drops.

Ever since its release, Arma 3 has aged like a fine wine. While the single player was average, the bread and butter of the Arma franchise is its multiplayer. There is a variety of game modes to choose from, from your average TDM match to Capture the Base, there is something for everyone to do. Thanks to the Steam Workshop, adding mods to Arma is as easy as 1-2-3 and since Bohemia updated the server browser to work when you open the Arma 3 Launcher, switching to a server/required mods for the server is really easy.
The DLCs, while a bit pricey sometimes, are really worth spending. The Apex expansion for an example adds a whole new map complete with new vehicles for you to try and even a co-op campaign for you to play solo or with friends.Don't have the money to purchase the DLC you want? Not a problem. Bohemia is kind enough to let you use the guns and vehicles from the DLCs but at the cost of the DLC watermark to appear on your screen. I'd recommend to get the DLCs on a sale so your wallet doesn't cry. 1 more thing to mention, the DLC includes a free update which all players have access to. For an example: the Jets DLC's free update includes the ability to use the USS Freedom as a base in your game, as well as the added bonus of tweaking the sensors in air vehicles.
A feature I really like is the Eden Editor. Remember when you were younger and played with toy soldiers and made them fight each other? The Eden Editor is basically that, but a bit more tacky. You can create missions and upload them to the steam workshop for others to enjoy, or simply boot it up and create a scenario to your liking.
Overall, Arma 3 is a really good game to pick up. It's been 3-4 years since Arma 3 launched and Bohemia has continued to develop the game and shows no sign of stopping any time soon. The modding community is very much active and continue to deliver high quality mods for everyone to use. I'd recommend you pick this game up if you're into military sim games.
(BTW, if you're afraid of not being able to run Arma 3 on your computer/laptop, I run Arma 3 with everything low except textured and high distance scaling and get 30-40 fps with a GT 740M and an i7-4500Q. During battles it drops to 20 to 10 depending on how many infantryman/explosions are near me.)

I can't recommend this game. It's a classic-styled class-based FPS that has withstood the test of time; an FPS that relies on hit-detection from 2007 (that should probably be enough to speak for itself). It has a massive personality that far surpasses the game itself, as the characters will long outlive the game. There's a reason everyone's heard of Team Fortress 2. It's most likely from one of two places:
1.) The washed-up wannabe Youtubers who think that this game is perfect, only because their computers are from the same time that TF2 came out and physically can't run anything else.
2.) All of the brilliant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who make SFM shorts using the amazing characters, while also for some reason ignoring the face that those characters are actually tied to a legitimate game.
I love the characters of this game; who couldn't? If they weren't as strong as they are, the game would have fallen off a long time ago. But the combination of an old FPS (which, let's be honest, any game from that genre needs to be updated just to function properly), as well as coming from Valve, (putting in new life into a game at an unconsistent rate of about— well actually they seemingly don't, the community covers that part for them), I just can't stand behind the game as it is.
If you want to play this game for the astoundingly well-created characters, or the loads of fun cooperative functions, or just simply the Gmod assets, go for it, because Team Fortress 2 has all of of those things. But if you don't want to play a functioning FPS where the performance is genuinley slowed down by how many hats there are, then you might want to stay away.
