Bought this game originally for Arma Life mod as many of my friends were playing at the time. Little did i know that I was about to purchase a truly unique and satisifying game experience. Many will say this game is over priced and that the DLC should have been stock game etc. etc. IMO this game was worth double what I paid and here is why.
Pros-
-Replay value is unlimited. First off it is hands down the best military sim out there not to mention it is visually stunning. Secondly the number of mods that offer different experiences are also unlimted as there is a very strong community following and creating for this game.
-Visuals. While it does take a higher end machine to truly enjoy this game it is well worth it. this is a huge sandbox enviroment that looks as real as it gets in this type of game. With that comes the need for hardware to back it up.
-Item selection. I can talk all day about the customization options that are available to you for loading out your troops. Tons of weapons, ammo, utility, etc.
-Vehicles. Land, Air, water (surface, and submerged), UAV. this game has a huge selection of life like transport units that will offer hours of fun trying to master.
-Mission editor. This feature can take some getting use to and for more in depth mission building some scripting is required; however with the zues system along with community mods made for making mission building easier. I promise if you give this some time and work with it you will find that this may be the best part of Arma. You can create any type of scenario for you and your freinds to conquer.
-DLC. Some say its over priced but i think this is a matter of opinion. My opinion is this. The DLC does not make or break the game. You can still play and experience this game without it; however once you play the game enough you will probably have no issue purchasing the DLC packs to enhance your gameplay. Also you can honestly tell that the DLC for the game truly was an afterthought. What i mean by that is that Bohemia did not intentionally hold back features to sell them for additonall money later which is a tactic that companies like EA, Ubisoft, etc. clearly do. This DLC IMO is a true testament from the developer to the players of continued support and content for a spectacular game.
-Clans. There are very few games out there anymore that have whole communites built around them outside of MMORPGS and Guilds for those. Arma 2 and Arma 3 both have a large selection of very active clans that range from serious sim execution to casual scenarios. If you buy this game I highly reccomend you find a clan to hook up with and be as active as you can as it will make your Arma experience unforgettable.
-Single player. If your not into the whole multiplayer thing this game offers a very rewarding single player experince as well. WIth fine tuned AI both freindly and enemy this can be one of the most challenging single play military games around.
Cons-
-System req. while i do love the way this game looks and plays i also realize that the barrier of entry for most is a little high in regards to hardware. I run it fine with haswell i5, gtx 970, 24gig ram; however render distance is your worst enemy in this game when it comes to FPS loss. you have to be a realist when it comes to what your system is capable of. DO NOT expect to max this game completly out on a gtx 970 as i can tell you it will not happen. You will have to adjust some of the advanced sliders. What i can tell you is that even with the sliders adjusted to a good visual/performance medium the game still looks stunning.
-Size. while this is not a huge issue for me as i finally dedicated a spare sdd for this game. With the game install along with mods this game can take up alot of space real fast. your gonna want to make sure you have ample space.
-Learning curve. This game is not as "pick up and play" as say battlefield or call of duty. Keep in mind this is a "sim" type game. There are many mechanics to this game there fore many controls and control schemes. I highly recomend going through the tutorials and doing the virtual training grounds before heading off into multiplayer. Keep in mind that while the controls are complicated they are also very customizable and compatibale with different controllers such as x52 HOTAS set up i use to fly helicopter missions.
I could go on and on with this game but ill spare you all and leave it with this. This games is great but all pros and cons on any post are a matter of opinion when it comes down to it. Watch youtube videos of both vanilla Arma 3 and mods. Watch streams and make your own decision. I do hope that this guide helps and if i missed something important or if you have a question before purchasing shoot me a message ill be glad to help.

Arma 3 is beautiful, both Iin graphics and in the way guns and damage work. The amount of mods out there are great, so if you don't want to play a military sim, you could pick this game up and play a rescue helicopter sim or a zombie survival sim. The best mods are King of the Hill, where 3 teams of 40 fight for control of a 1km wide circle using jets, tanks, armored vehicles, attack helicopters, snipers, aandan assortment of infantry, all uniquely equipped. The bullet trajectory physics is awesome, you can shoot through most walls depending on their make up. The learning curve is sharp, as there are a lot of buttons to know and rebind, but taking the time to learn them and set up a configuration that's right for you is worth it. The game is a lot more complicated than most shooters. After playing arma, going back to other shooters lime CS GO seem so gross, the idea of running around and shooting a fully automatic rifle (which by the way has only tracer rounds) and actually being accurate is ridiculous. Arma is the best shooter I have ever played, it offers a sandbox of tools and content for people to create their very own experience.

Great concept and fun when it wants to work as intended, problem is that almost never happens. Every game, whether it be a solo or with friends, always has some stupid issue plaguing me and my friends even though this game has been out almost as long as DayZ. Cars exploding randomly while driving, falling under the map, getting your weapon locked because of crap servers, terrible lag compensation (getting shot behind cover, while your shots don't register even though you see the blood spray), and inconsistent weapon behavior are only the tip of the proverbial iceberg that is this game. Daybreak, quite possibly, has to be the most inept developer team on this side of the solar system. These bugs have been in the game for a long time now, and are more focused on adding more crates for microtransactions or changing things that do not need to be changed. Every patch note says "fixed the shotgun" yet it is the most unreliable weapon in the game. Shotgun pellets do not stick together in a clump for 5 feet after being fired, then suddenly start spreading out. The only gun in the game that works the way you want it to is the AR-15, and even that is a stretch.
Save your $20, go buy Insurgency or Rocket League. Alternatively, save another $10 on top of that and buy PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds.

Tf2 is everything I want in a nonobjective game. Multiple gamemodes, no campaign. All without the hastle of purchacing the game. If you play the game and think you won't enjoy it you didn't waste however much money it woulve cost to but it. My favorite part of this game is the taunts. Sure they have em in overwatch but  you can't kill people with them. And if you're having a bad day you can have a hoovy picnic with conga to dance the day away. You might have the occasional hacker, and you might have the occasional mic spammer,  and you even might have a team of tryhards or f2P's but in the end it's just one round of any addicting rounds you may or may not play. You help each other out,  you teach each other how to play,  and you be an overall team.  Thus the name is what it is. And to end it all, you don't need any fancy cosmetics or kill streak guns to be good at this game. Don't spend money to look cool cause you don't need a hat with fire clouds or a fancy Golden wrench to be a good player. You will get the full experience as long as you enjoy the game overall.

Arma 3 is beautiful, both Iin graphics and in the way guns and damage work. The amount of mods out there are great, so if you don't want to play a military sim, you could pick this game up and play a rescue helicopter sim or a zombie survival sim. The best mods are King of the Hill, where 3 teams of 40 fight for control of a 1km wide circle using jets, tanks, armored vehicles, attack helicopters, snipers, aandan assortment of infantry, all uniquely equipped. The bullet trajectory physics is awesome, you can shoot through most walls depending on their make up. The learning curve is sharp, as there are a lot of buttons to know and rebind, but taking the time to learn them and set up a configuration that's right for you is worth it. The game is a lot more complicated than most shooters. After playing arma, going back to other shooters lime CS GO seem so gross, the idea of running around and shooting a fully automatic rifle (which by the way has only tracer rounds) and actually being accurate is ridiculous. Arma is the best shooter I have ever played, it offers a sandbox of tools and content for people to create their very own experience.
Good game.

Overall I'd say the base game is great.It runs well, I normally get around 40 to 60 frames on an i5 and a 550ti while on standard settings. This is surprising seeing as other games with worse graphics I can only get 30 frames on.
Gun play is vastly improved since Arma 2 with one of my favourite features being the new stances that make staying in cover much easier.
The campaign is interesting as does a good job of introducing  game mechanics as you progress although players new to arma may find the AI to be insanely accurate but you just have to keep your distance from them whenever possible.
The thing I love most about this game is the abundance of extra content available on the steam workshop and through things like A3 Launcher, however some times they can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥to set up.
Something that kinda sucks is that you are going to need all the DLC to get a full experience on any server or game mode and the DLC's (in my opinion) are over priced. I'd recommend waiting for them to come on sale and not paying full price.
Overall I love this game for its pethora of content on the workshop and its possibility of hours of gameplay.

(Edited opening statement.) I've put in 542 hours on ArmA III so far. I've played ArmA: Cold War Assault, ArmA 2, ArmA 2: Operation Arrowhead, and ArmA III. I am a big fan of this series due to that it is very realistic and the possibilities are nearly endless thanks to the Steam Workshop integration. ArmA III takes ArmA II and improves it plus more. ArmA III is more smooth and less clunky compared to ArmA II. ArmA III is a lot better then ArmA II because whereas you had to go to 3rd party websites to get mods for ArmA II, ArmA III has Steam Workshop to get most of your add-ons.
The integration of Steam Workshop is the icing on the cake for this game because the integration is so tight knit into the ArmA III launcher. A new addition to the ArmA series is a launcher, ArmA III has a launcher that starts up before you play the game and it allows you to choose which mods you want active while playing or if you want to play stock ArmA III. This launcher also adds in "Presets", you can use these presets for servers if you are on a RP server which has special mods you can check the servers mods, and add them to a preset. The combat in ArmA III is more refined and smooth compared to ArmA II. ArmA III brings a stamina system which affects your weapon accuracy after sprinting for long periods of times (this can be disabled on servers).
You can also crouch run now! This has been asked for since ArmA II and they brought it in ArmA III. Another new feature they added is the ability to run while swapping weapons. There are also 9 different stances that allows you to be more flexible in a firefight and rewards anyone that uses them correctly. Here is a pros and cons list for this game!
Pros:
- More refined and robust combat system
- More refined and robust movement system
- Adds in more realism
- A vast variety of weapons
- Weapon attachments such as Suppressors, Sights, Bi-pods, Flashlights/Lasers.
- New stamina system
- Constantly receiving updates from Bohemia Interactive
- New DLC's and Map's being added
- Steam Workshop Integration
- Flexible and useful launcher
- Amazing servers
- New 3D Editor which came in Eden update
- Better resource management with it better balancing out your GPU usage and CPU usage which came in the Eden update
- More Refined Textures which came in the Eden update
- A tad bit more optimized then previously which came in the Eden update
- Constant improvements to UI, Preformance, Lighting, and Textures
Neutral:
- Steam Trading Cards (for anyone that is interested in them, that's why it's under "Neutral".)
-Frame rate can be a problem due to optimization (not Bohemia's fault, they can't optimize a game with such freedom for mods, and a open editor.)
Cons:
- FPS Drops upon entering highly populated areas
- Combat can be hectic at times if you do not understand compass bearings and map coordinates
- Very steep learning curve
- Desync is still a very big problem but that's more server-side
- No FoV (Field of View) option, the default FoV can make you feel a bit claustrophobic. There is a tool that you can get to fix this, you can get it here
.
It's hard to find cons for this game but those are the only ones I can think of. My rating of this game is a 8.5/10 it takes ArmA II's problems and improves upon them to make one amazing military simulator.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place... Buuut if youre looking for an exquisite ravioli recipe you've come to the right place!
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

The game suffers horribly from lack of content and weak campaign. The DLCs barely add anything yet they require ~$30 for at least Helicopters and Marksmen. Both DLCs add a few choppers and sniper rifles that should have been in the base game in the first place. But Bohemia has decided to follow the extremely anti-consumer trend and ads for these DLCs pop up everywhere in the game. I can forgive Karts, they're cheap and actually add more than Helicopters and Marksmen. Now Apex, on the other hand, is an actual Expansion Pack, adding a new map, a new campaign, new stuff everywhere. Even though the new campaign is short and lackluster.
I previously said that Arma 3 wasn't enjoyable without mods, but now it is. Took Bohemia a while - like, over 3 years.
The campaign was abysmal even in comparison to campaigns from Arma 2 Expansions. Characters abruptly killed off, characters dissappearing from the story until the very last mission, a story-critical McGuffin appearing at the very same mission, no explanations at all, et cetera, et cetera. And yes, the campaign itself also abruptly ends.
Now to the good side. The controls are a bit smoother than Arma 2 - I particularly like the combat pace and simple bipod resting. The aiming is improved - now you can actually zoom into an RCO and not go into another screen. Sway is debatable, but it's a bit more realistic, so I don't mind it most of the time. The new maps are quite big and nice. The graphics are great and the optimization at the time of writing this review isn't that bad when we talk about Bohemia. The original OFP music cues are back with a vengeance, they got amazing remixes.
Buy only on a sale, the number of mods requiring DLC Bundle 1 is increasing.

Ah where to begin with ARMA 3....
I had just landed on a beach in a rubber boat with my four man team. We are assaulting enemy positions to capture intel and eliminate a HVT. Soon after landing, we are ambushed by an enemy assault boat that promply decimates my team. I manage to land a rocket hit on the boat and incapacitate its crew before it can annihilate me. With the boat disabled, I am now on my own. Do I continue the mission by myself, or do I abort and let my team die for nothing? I choose to continue, using a silenced weapon to help conceal my position. I call for friendly reinforcments to begin the assault on the town. A convoy with friendly troops starts coming down the road. Suddenly, rockets from a hilltop position begin to rain down on the convoy, disabling several vehicles. Everyone dismounts and begins engaging the enemy on the hilltop. I use the distraction to flank the enemy position and eliminate the fireteam. We proceed towards the town, eliminating small pockets of resistance along the way. Suddenly we are pinned down by enemy machinegun fire that kills several friendlies. I call in an airstrike that levels the houses containing the position, eliminating the threat along with the HVT. I then see a target of opportunity: an enemy cargo truck. I align my sights slightly above the target to compensate for the distance and fire. The truck erupts into flames. This came at a price, as my postion was compromised and drew heavy enemy fire towards my position. We have no choice but to engage. After several bloody minutes, four enemy fireteams lay dead on the battlefield with only light casualties on our side. I decide this is the moment to assault the position containing the intel. I successfully acquire the intel and call in an evac chopper to extract me to a safe position. We extract under fire and secure the intel, dealing a severe blow to the enemy.
10/10

Have you ever played a modern/futuristic (Arma 3 is in the middle, it's in 2035, not that futuristic after all) FPS war game with a full-scale war? If you haven't then please play this game, 3D art is done fantastically well, the game lets you control almost everything, there is a wide variety of vehicles and weapons you can drive and shoot, however it was one of the most difficult campaigns i have ever played, it took me 47 hours to complete with skipping ~6 missions if i remember precisely because they were too difficult, if you are coming from cod or bf you will have a hard time transitioning into arma, but it is totally worth the time, at sometimes the AI was acting a bit stupid but not as much as arma 2. Unfortunately those AI moments where the soldiers used cover were scripted, but hell, the atmosphere, I've never experienced something as cool as this. The game takes place on 2 beautifull greek islands, Agios Efstratios (mentioned as stratis in-game) and Lemnos(mentioned as altis in-game). The storyline was also good, instead of being the typical world savior you are a normal soldier who takes part on a war, nothing more or less, you'll love it though.
I have to mention a funny incident that happened during gameplay:  I am a greek citizen and i have to point out that cicadas show up during the summer, and you don't usually build a fire in the summer during day time... something that some soldiers were doing in the game. Looking forward to arma 4 being released, im sure it will be as good as arma 3 and maybe even better (maybe better optimised than arma 3 since it does not sympathize amd cpus). That's it, amazing game overall.

Extremely fun game with many gamemodes and scenarios, and in most cases no rules to be followed. Arma 3 is said to be a military sandbox, which matches the games features perfectly. You can be sky high in a jet or on the ground blowin crap up with RPGs and such. My favorite part of Arma 3 has to be it's online gameplay. You can roleplay being a civilian or a cop on Altis Life or work with a squad to take over objectives in King of the Hill.
Overall, Arma 3 has many pros, but there are some Cons.
PROS
- Amazing Graphics
- Realistic physics (in some cases atleast)
- You can do what you want
- Many Missions and Scenarios to choose from
- Easily moddable from 3rd party websites or the Steam Workshop
- Great DLC
CONS
- Not very well optimized engine (Favors Intel big time)
- Some minors glitches and bugs
Overall it's worth the $60

I would really recommend this game to everyone. It is a game that really gives what you pays for. I know everyone wont be satisfied with this game, but there are a lot of game modes in this game so I think most people will like it. Myself, I love it and I intent of playing it for atleast 1000 more hours. My favourite game mode is altis life, which is a simulator of real life I guess. You can choose to be a ''hobo'' which do things legally, which I have done a lot myself, but also be a rebel or drug dealer where yoy can do basicly whatever you want. You can also become a cop, which is a lot of fun, but comes with a lot of work, due to the altis life rules. Most servers have very strict rules and so on. IF this doesnt seem anything you woud like, the game is actually most about military. In my perspective it is kinda like a military simulator, but you can play multiplayer or coop. The combat is great in the game and you can choose from being infantry, aerial or whatever. There are a lot, and I mean A LOT of vehicles in the game so I dont think you will miss that feature. If you like fps games you can play in first person, but you can also choose to play in third person. This is important to note due to combat, you may come in that situation in multiplayer, where you are playing in first person, and you will maybe see that people tend to ''abuse'' the third person feature and hide behind a wall or below a window and see you with the third person view although you cant see them and they will get an advantage. I have played this game for 665 hours atm so I feel like I can give a pretty good example of how the game is.
Pros:
-Good teamplay in coop
-Great servers and a massive amount of servers to choose from
-Loads of vehicles
-Giant maps (Altis is my favourite)
-A lot of game-modes to choose from
-Massive amount of weapons to choose from.
-Editor mode, a lot of fun to build and place vehicles to have some fun with
-SO much fun with friends.
-Good language and no racism as I have seen (most racists get banned or warned)
-Supports community maps.
Cons:
-Hard to learn the game in the start (kinda bad tutorials, use youtube and google!)
Thats all! I hope you buy this game if you feel like this sounds like a good game, Bohemia interactive really deserves the attention :). Thank you for the great game and guys, have fun! I hope this review helped :).

I knew what to expect going into Arma III from previous experience with Bohemia Interactive games, yet I was still overwhelmed by the amount of features I had to wrap my head around before I could play it with even moderate proficiency. It’s a first-person shooter alright, but it’s not another “left trigger to aim down the sights, right trigger to shoot” kind of game. You’re going to have to use almost every key on your keyboard, memorize specific key combinations and what each does depending on whether you’re on foot, in a tank, a helicopter, etc.
I felt comically inept fumbling through my first few hours. With so many different firing modes, stances, movement speeds, and other options, I had difficulty just walking, drawing my weapon and firing, to say nothing of using my equipment, making sense of the map, and working with my squad. I had to wonder what my AI squadmates thought of me, the clueless rookie, stumbling into the bushes before I accidently pulverized myself with a satchel charge I didn’t even mean to deploy.
To make matters even more difficult, in its current state Arma III doesn’t offer a real tutorial. Its Showcases (playable scenarios showing off its many features) follow a logical progression that introduce you to increasingly complicated mechanics. However, they each do a poor job of explaining how to use them or how they may be useful later on. The only real instruction comes in the form of on-screen hints that tell you which keys do what. It’s an inefficient method to teach you how to fly a helicopter, and practically useless when it comes to explaining the tactical value of more esoteric equipment and features.
In one of the more interesting Showcases you are given access to a non-lethal aerial drone and an armed ground vehicle drone which you can use to eliminate targets in a nearby town. After much experimentation, I devised a tactic of sending my aerial drone ahead to scout and tag targets, which then allowed me to coordinate mortar fire and corner enemies in the town. It was satisfying because it allowed me come up with a strategy which felt entirely my own, and one which nearly no other shooter could accommodate. On the other hand, there was a needless amount of frustration along the way that could have been avoided with clearer UI and better instruction.
As you can imagine, Arma III’s potentially much more enjoyable when you’re playing online with real people – especially those who already know how to play and can teach us its secrets. It doesn’t have a capped player limit, so in theory a server where 100 players are facing another 100 players in a gigantic sandbox where almost everything is possible is one of the best shooters I’ve ever played. But without investing long-term in a clan or other group that will ensure a reliable team of significant size, those are hard to come by. In practice, new players are presented with a list of servers half-full of random people who aren’t communicating, and where everything that can go wrong is going wrong. Since Arma III doesn’t offer obvious incentives for players to cooperate or even funnel them to the same areas of its enormous maps, multiplayer’s mostly uncurated chaos. It’s amusing in its own way, but something I would rather watch in a YouTube video than it play myself.
Counterintuitively, smaller matches are more fun for a new player trying to find his way in this world. In one pick up co-op game, six fellow players and I (and a group of AI bots) were tasked with a simple mission: find a way off the island. We spawned at a random spot along the coast and were given two locations, miles away, where we could find a boat or a helicopter for extraction. We ended up not even making it halfway to either destination, but I enjoyed our journey quite a lot. We heard a gunship in the distance and dashed across a field to take cover in a forest. We stumbled upon and successfully seized an enemy outpost, where we commandeered a truck. We arrogantly tried repeating the same strategy with a larger town on our way to an airfield... and were caught in the open by snipers. This is what developers mean when they talk about emergent gameplay, and it’s where Arma III shines.
Altis and Stratis, the two islands that serve as its massive military sandboxes (270 km² and 20 km² respectively), are truly impressive and the foundations that make everything else about ARMA 3 possible. Whether you’re scuba diving to disable mines or sniping from a church atop a high hill, everything looks crisp and sufficiently believable... as long as you don’t look too close. There’s an obvious amount of recycled assets used to fill all this space, and many empty buildings. With its overall clinical style, Arma III can seem sparse, even boring when you stop to smell the roses.
Its sound design, however, is disappointing at any distance. It suffers from laughably cheesy electronic music and sound effects that make some actions feel insignificant, vehicle movement and firing in particular. For all I know that’s what tanks and helicopters really sound like, but it makes them feel like toys.
But like I said, this is a game where we have to make our own fun, and at least Arma III makes that much relatively easy with a built-in mission editor and Steam Workshop integration. It’s inherited the modding community that brought us such hits as DayZ, and as its marketing materials insist, Arma III really is a “platform” more than a stand-alone game, and what it may evolve into in the months and years after release adds immeasurable replay value to its $60 asking price.
Arma III’s complexity is a double-edged sword. It takes a long time to comprehend, but once you’re comfortable enough with its mechanics to take advantage of them under pressure, you’re able to engage in a kind of large-scale tactical combat that’s simply not offered elsewhere. Weak sound and a sparsely decorated map are forgivable, making Arma III’s nearly endless content definitely worth experiencing as long as you know there’s a long, dark tunnel to get through before you can see the light.

My refund request after a few hours of gameplay. I think I covered most of my experience with it.
"I've waited patiently for proper online gameplay, bug fixes, improved mechanics (+ physics) and for this game to go from an alpha/early access stage to a full on, polished stand-alone title. But it just doesn't seem to check out, and I still experience dissatisfaction with these games. I had hopes when I first played it as I saw potential, and i've been following updates regularely, but it just doesn't seem to satisfy.
There are too many unpredictable bugs. Weird scripted and random physics glitches and bugs, poorly designed animations, glitches both in veichles and character movement/combat/shooting and camera panning. For me, it eats off of the competetive aspect and gameplay of King of the Kill/Just survive. Random bug or glitch incidents of all sorts are too frequent, and has too much impact to the extent where it rends off the intended essence of this game genre. I think both game modes performes too shy of what it's meant to be, and what it could have been. And that's where I've been waiting in vain.
I think it's a shame that both King of the Kill and Just survive are engorged with bugs and glitches, considering its competitive based play, teamwork, winning and surviving in both gamemodes. It's meant to punish the players for their action, perfomance and skill. That he or she performes bad or dies in either gamemode because of how they perform. But it's the other way around a little too often because of the faulty mechanics and physics in the engine. It also makes it increasingly more difficult to adapt, improve and apply skill, when the frequent glitches, wonky mechanics and bugs enfolds major portions of the playfield. There is no solid ground where adaptation and improvement can commence(imo), and often I find myself performing bad purely based on arbitary incidents that are not even meant to be present in-game.
So raw skill and brains will frequently be insignificant in several situations and encounters when playing. My encounters in only few hours of gameplay has taught me that the malfunction-based gameplay and unpredictable mechanics, stagger the players performance. Sadly enough, these reoccuring flaws leaves large portions of skill in PVP encounters to be based on inconsistent, random malfunctioning game-incidents. Furthermore, these varying incidents of broken gameplay overthrows the players average performance to the point where its no longer rewarding in both King of the Kill and Just survive. When for example killing enemies in KotK, it can feel discouraging or non rewarding, because you/your enemies raw skill is affected by many factors like glitched/bugged mechanics, animations, hit boxes, lag, or even luck since your hits don't always register when shooting an enemy. Therefore you are NOT in control.  When you are IN control, you know the results of your actions with 100% certainty, which lacks in this game with all of its malfunctions. 100% IN control is when you know that nothing impaired or affected your actions, and you got the result you intended because of your performance. This is what rewarding gameplay would be like, although in this case, it's not.
So regarding my issue i'd like to request a refund, because I had hopes for both these games as I enjoy the genre of both survival and competitive play, but as i've nagged about this entire time, the gameplay falls short on me. I think the game is unfinished to the point where it's not enjoyable in both competetive King of the Kill, and the more relaxed Just survive. The game feels like i'm to blame for not being mechanically skilled and experienced, when too often the game lacks fixing, improvement and consistency for the player to become better and feel rewarded. The game presents itself to me as abandoned, and its gameplay almost feels based off of these glitchy, punishing physics, bugs, unpolished animations inconsistent gameplay malfunctions. It takes a very patient and persistent mind to adapt this faulty gameplay.
I hope my in-depth refund submission accounts a deemworthy reasoning for both my approach, and displeasing experience with the game. "

Arma 3 is one of those games you hate, but you still play it because it is so good.
Arma 3 is unique in how it plays out but without doubt has some flaws. A common problem is optimization; this problem is a big one considering if you would like to play on a server with a decent amount of players, you will be ploughed down to 30 frames per second or below. It can be a horrible experience. However, with the right tweaks to the game you can easily run it at 100 fps+ (in singleplayer) with decent specs (if you would consider a 560 ti and i5 3570 as somewhere between good and bad).
I suspect that the framerate problem on servers may because how the Arma server is designed, but that is for bohemia to improve.
For out this Arma 3 is a brilliant designed game in the manner that pretty much everything you'll find on the server browser is user made. To the extent where a mod or mission may completely overcome the "Military simulator" aspect of the game. At one point I even found a mod where you played as a robot car war machine, just like that old tv show with the bots fighting in an arena.
If you are into tactics and survival, wasteland might be the place for you, with the constant feeling of being watched by someone with a very big weapon, while attempting to gear up so you can fight back. Alternatively, the great feeling of wiping a 5-man squad purely based on your skill and intelligence, by outplaying them.
If you are into big battles, king of the hill is something you may like. With giant battles going on, including infantry, armoured cars, and air support.
Even if these things are not for you, Altis life might be. With the biggest (or one of the biggest) player-base in Arma, the incredible Altis life is really something in its own. You start out by being a civilian with nothing, where you get to choose a path of Justice as a police officer, medic or something alike. Alternatively, if you strive after being the biggest drug lord on the server by harvesting crops and processing them into drugs to sell. On the other hand, if you simply just want to pluck apples for a little cash you can do that as well. For you Garry’s mod veterans, this is pretty much the DarkRP of Arma.
And if none of these are something that you'd spend time playing, why not grab a text editor and start scripting a mission exactly how you'd want it!
Though I recommend this game, I would like to point out that it is not that fun to play alone; you definitely need some friends to play with.

Arma 3 is one of those games you hate, but you still play it because it is so good.
Arma 3 is unique in how it plays out but without doubt has some flaws. A common problem is optimization; this problem is a big one considering if you would like to play on a server with a decent amount of players, you will be ploughed down to 30 frames per second or below. It can be a horrible experience. However, with the right tweaks to the game you can easily run it at 100 fps+ (in singleplayer) with decent specs (if you would consider a 560 ti and i5 3570 as somewhere between good and bad).
I suspect that the framerate problem on servers may because how the Arma server is designed, but that is for bohemia to improve.
For out this Arma 3 is a brilliant designed game in the manner that pretty much everything you'll find on the server browser is user made. To the extent where a mod or mission may completely overcome the "Military simulator" aspect of the game. At one point I even found a mod where you played as a robot car war machine, just like that old tv show with the bots fighting in an arena.
If you are into tactics and survival, wasteland might be the place for you, with the constant feeling of being watched by someone with a very big weapon, while attempting to gear up so you can fight back. Alternatively, the great feeling of wiping a 5-man squad purely based on your skill and intelligence, by outplaying them.
If you are into big battles, king of the hill is something you may like. With giant battles going on, including infantry, armoured cars, and air support.
Even if these things are not for you, Altis life might be. With the biggest (or one of the biggest) player-base in Arma, the incredible Altis life is really something in its own. You start out by being a civilian with nothing, where you get to choose a path of Justice as a police officer, medic or something alike. Alternatively, if you strive after being the biggest drug lord on the server by harvesting crops and processing them into drugs to sell. On the other hand, if you simply just want to pluck apples for a little cash you can do that as well. For you Garry’s mod veterans, this is pretty much the DarkRP of Arma.
And if none of these are something that you'd spend time playing, why not grab a text editor and start scripting a mission exactly how you'd want it!
Though I recommend this game, I would like to point out that it is not that fun to play alone; you definitely need some friends to play with.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Most servers are just Altis Life, Wasteland, or Exile. Not a whole lot of pure military combat going on.

The Ugly:
FPS can get pretty low, very easily. This has more to do with your computer but the game very much tailors to next gen PCs over some of the older ones.
Content. They really expect you to pay $15 for a damn rifle pack (or the other packs). Overall I think this game is very solid but it's not free from frustration.

3 years in early access and this game is still a mess. It doesn't matter what your ping to the server is, you can expect anywhere from 50-100ms added latency from the server its self. Hacks require simple C# scripts, and you will encounter many. Players from China infest US servers and the net code gives them a tactical edge - this is the first competitive FPS I've played online that disadvantages players with good ping.
Will it improve? It's doubtful. Daybreak waited until 2017 to hire someone for QA, and right now (even with all the complainst they are getting) are more focused on creating new skins and crates, plus an esports tournament, than fixing the game. Fixes that are promised are always "TBD" and are often rolled back because they cause additional issues. If you read reviews by former employees on glassdoor, you can see why: the company is a mess and they show no signs of improving.

Arma 3 provides one of the best gaming experiences I've ever had. I played Operation Flashpoint in 2009 but didn't know about Arma 1 or 2's release until years later. After playing Arma 2 both in DayZ and a Milsim unit and Arma 3 in a lot of various gamemodes and a milsim unit I can say that Arma is one of the best game series ever. Arma 3 provides a huge combined arms experience. With an accesible but difficult flight model for helicopters (we don't talk about the AFM), fantastically modeled infantry and vehicles, support for large scale battles on gigantic maps, an in-game 2d editor (something I haven't seen before) that works very well, a huge library of scripting commands that allow for someone to make almost anything happen, amazing modding tools, and an inventory system that's 10x better than Arma 2's you can make almost anything involving the military you want. Arma 3 is probably the greatest out of the Arma series and therefore, one of the greatest games I've played.

I'll start off positive with the things I like:
- Character models
- Character Design (Clothes and such)
- Map design (Looks good)
- Building funtions (layout and working doors and stairways
- Fun car mechanics (Fun to drive and work)
For the things I don't like, the list is a tad longer:
- Gun handling (Clunky and awkward for anyone used to conventional gun handling like Arma or any other FPS/3rd)
- Gun leading/distancing (Awkward for anyone used to conventional gun handling)
- 3rd person shooting (Not a fan of the 3rd person style, 1st person is available, but you are at a disadvantage for using it)
- Annoying gun physics (Shotguns are extremely short range and deal little to no damage once outside of a 8 meter radius) (You can jump around and spin, and still be mostly accurate, leaving people who use conventional military tactics at a disadvantage)
- Parachuting (Clunky to operate, requires some odd swaying and spinning to gain momentum if you want to actually go anywhere)
- Steep learning curve for new players (If you don't know how to play this game, or even if you have played other battle royal games, you will probably have troubles starting off. Lobbies are always full of professional players who will two shot you in the head before you even know what is happening. Solution: Ranked matches)
- No map variety (I'll put this one down  to it just being in alpha, but the same map every time gets old. A snow map, or desert map would be a good improvement.)
- Crashing issues (For me, my game crashes almost each time I play it, making it a struggle to even enjoy myself. I will gather some gear, a car, and finally be off and ready, and my game will crash with the "Break point exception error" or "Break point has been reached"
There is nothing wrong with my computer as I have the correct specs, and adequate RAM to run the game and other games more intense than it. (Ex. BF1, BF4, Arma 3, Dayz, War Thunder, World of Tanks. All of which on max settings)
- Death bugs (Randomly exploding cars, randomly dying)
- Game freezing (I will hear a pop in my headphones, then suddenly I cannot move, nor shoot or access inventory. Very annoying.
- Bad Spawning (If you get a bad spawn away from the safe zone [area free from deadly gas] and you don't have a vehicle readily availble, be prepared to die. You will not be able to run quick enough to get to safety, nor get equpment to deffend yourself from other players, if you manage to reach it in time. [Skip looting to run to it].
Overall, I had placed some good thoughts into this game as my friends had recomended it to me (none of which have played Arma 3 Royal) and I thought it would be a cool game to have a go. I bought the game a while back and couldn't play it due to bugs and crashing. Recently I was able to play the game, and have not had a very positive experience. I had hoped that the creators of "Planet Side 2" would be able to make a good battle royal game, but sadly they seemed to have come up short. I can't say I would recomend this to another friend, since I would rather have them purchase Arma to play instead, as it it more developed and also less buggy and has other applications than just battle royal (Dayz, City life). Although a quirky game in areas, not what I would be looking to play long term as a dedicated battle royal game.
I will continue to test the game for fixes, or improvements, and re-write my review if things change.

Summary - H1Z1 King Of The Kill is a large scale game which features a huge amount of players per game, It's a solo game were everybody starts from parachuting and then once you land you start off with nothing and then you must explore the map to find weapons to fight off other players, once a certain amount of time as passed gas from all directions with come closer and closer and fill the entire map, the last point that gas covers, is the place that you should strive to be. You can use cars to get there, the only thing you need to remember is everyman for himself and the last man standing is the winner.
Pros
- Good idea, the developers made a great idea for a game, a game in which you are to be the last man alive in a massive land filled with lots of players.
Cons
-Very buggy, omg, this has to be the worst game I've ever played for bugs, I would go through some of them but the problem is I DON'T KNOW WHERE TO START?
-Lack of content, very few guns, few cars, few everything if I'm honest.
-Shooting mechanics suck, for real you never have any idea of where you're shooting, you could be shooting behind you could be shooting at the sun, I don't fu*king know.
-Graphics suck, the rendering speed is just awful, nothing else to say.
Verdict: I simply got bored of saying all the reasons why this game sucks, but it just does, I guess regardless of the games issues it's kinda fun due to the concept but that doesn't suggest that I like the game at all, or even recommend it. Sorry for this one, but I can't recommend this game.

The game itself is basically a sandbox with many potential scenarios and situations the only limits was your imagination and your will. Once you finished the campaign you probably trying any casual gameplay like Wasteland, Altis Life, Exile etc. Or if you like zombies you might like Breaking Point, Exile with Zombies, and many variation of them until you don't even know what do you want to play. Or if you into realism or immersion of military simulation, you can join any Unit and play like actual soldier in battlefield following some protocols, radio and♥♥♥♥♥♥ It maybe sound so serious but trust me it was fun. There are many things you don't expect to be happen but turns out it was a hilarious experience with your teammates or some dumb acts someone did makes you laugh.
For regular player you might found Arma have complicated action button on the keyboard, a lot of it but you will get used to it. And Arma have REALLY BIG maps like, dude it was 20km square ! people sometimes joking about it called "asthmatic jogging simulator" because you will mostly run one to other place very often. even running 1km take a few minutes on foot. But if you playing a scenario mission it wont be matter as long as you put some vehicle in advantage point and keep the immersive gameplay.
what its good about Arma ? its THE MODS. the community keeps growing and there is some awesome authors put their effort and times making cool mods like new maps, new weapon and etc. You may ended up having mod running 50gb on your disk.
Lets talk about downside.
Some people complaining about its performance on multiplayer like having very low fps although you running a monster pc race. Well, basically arma is calculating everything ingame, your character, the environment, weather, time, bullet trajectory, ambient sound, animation, AI, etc. It's not suprised if you lagging if you put too much mod and a heavily scripted mission because the server or your pc calculating every script on air and sync it to every player, so if the server have 40 player on it its like the server have 40 time load than regular one. Its logical i think but I hope BIS would improve their coding so we have a better fps on multiplayer.
Also if you even enter the forums.bistudio, many people complaining about BIS didn't looking after problem that existed but focusing on adding new feature. Well, there is some demand from player to fix some their basic feature I hope they listen to their community.
So overall verdict from me:
Graphics : 7.5/10 (gettings better)
Sound     : 8.5/10 (just like real life)
Gameplay : 8/10 (just what I am into)
Overall : 8/10 (recommended for you if you like gameplay like arma)

H1Z1: King of the Kill is a bug ridden, un-optimized and un-balanced king of the hill game. The game is plagued with problems and frankly isn't worth the price tag that is set for it. The game suffers from a lot of problems that really take away from player's experiences, it's main problems are:
Shooting/Combat: The shooting and dare I say melee combat in this game are very broken to the point where the only way to get a kill is to use exploits like jumping around and shooting people with shotguns that seem to not lose any accuracy from jumping, thats assuming you actually hit enough shots to kill them as the armor is very unbalanced in the game, for example if you shoot at a person with improvised body armor and hit him 3-4 times in the chest with a shotgun at 8-10 metres you will only end up doing around 18 damage. With the combat even when you have the tactical advantage of being either behind someone or waiting for them around a corner, half the time you will die because of how much damage people are able to take with armor that you can pretty much make within the first 3 minutes of the game.
Hitboxes and Hit registration: I have nothing more to say than they are both garbage, you can be aiming directly at someone with a sniper rifle and take a shot only to miss completely.
Final verdict: H1Z1: King of the Kill, while being the only big, king of the hill game you are going to find until PlayerUnknown's: Battlegrounds comes out, it is not worth your money unless you like dying to bull**** and exploits. Until then I recommend that you wait for something a bit better like PlayerUnknown's: Battlegrounds to come out, as it is being developed by a developer that has worked on the Arma 3 KOTH and I think even this game and fully understands the problems with this game in which he hopes to improve on in Battlegrounds.

One of the most fun games out in the steam store. There's so much variety that inlcudes mods and different gamemodes. Even though simulator games are not your type you can still find a place in Arma. You can play gamemodes ranging from all of the Life mods (Altis Life, Arma 3 Life, etc), King of the Hill, Domination (coop Players vs. AI), Wasteland, Epoch, Exile, Breaking Point, Battle Royale, and many more. Those are just multiplayers mods and gamemodes you can play, there is also a huge variety of mods and missions available in the workshop that you can download and play nonstop. All of this available in huge maps, such as Altis that is around 260 sq km.
Every day, whatever you play, you will always experience something new. Be it either encountering a Wipeout for the first time, getting Allahu Akbar'd at Kavala Square in Altis Life, robbing a bank, being the most powerful group in a Wasteland server, meeting random people and start chaos around Altis, etc. There are just so many things you can do in Arma, the possibilities might be endless. I really recommend this game for anyone who is looking to have a unique experience. One thing though, playing with other people together in a group or clan is 1000 times more recommendable to get the most out of the experience.

-Do a 10 min stealth mission around Kavala to avoid cops with the 5 guys
-Plan out a robbery
-PUT YOUR HANDS UP
-Turns out to be an officer
-Turns around, spam tazes
-Restrained
-Go to jail for 15 minutes
-10/10 would Altis Life again

The game itself is basically a sandbox with many potential scenarios and situations the only limits was your imagination and your will. Once you finished the campaign you probably trying any casual gameplay like Wasteland, Altis Life, Exile etc. Or if you like zombies you might like Breaking Point, Exile with Zombies, and many variation of them until you don't even know what do you want to play. So much things to do.
Or if you into realism or immersion of military simulation, you can join any Unit and play like actual soldier in battlefield following some protocols, radio and♥♥♥♥♥♥ It maybe sound so serious but trust me it was fun. There are many things you don't expect to be happen but turns out it was a hilarious experience with your teammates or some dumb acts someone did makes you laugh.
For regular player you might found Arma have complicated action button on the keyboard, a lot of it but you will get used to it. And Arma have REALLY BIG maps like, dude it was 20km square ! people sometimes joking about it called "asthmatic jogging simulator" because you will mostly run one to other place very often. even running 1km take a few minutes on foot. But if you playing a scenario mission it wont be matter as long as you put some vehicle in advantage point and keep the immersive gameplay.
what its good about Arma ? its THE MODS. the community keeps growing and there is some awesome authors put their effort and times making cool mods like new maps, new weapon and etc. You may ended up having mod running 50gb on your disk.
Lets talk about downside.
Some people complaining about its performance on multiplayer like having very low fps although you running a monster pc race. Well, basically arma is calculating everything ingame, your character, the environment, weather, time, bullet trajectory, ambient sound, animation, AI, etc. It's not suprised if you lagging if you put too much mod and a heavily scripted mission because the server or your pc calculating every script on air and sync it to every player, so if the server have 40 player on it its like the server have 40 time load than regular one. Its logical i think but I hope BIS would improve their coding so we have a better fps on multiplayer.
Also if you even enter the forums.bistudio, many people complaining about BIS didn't looking after problem that existed but focusing on adding new feature. Well, there is some demand from player to fix some their basic feature I hope they listen to their community.
So overall verdict from me:
Graphics : 7.5/10 (gettings better)
Sound     : 8.5/10 (just like real life)
Gameplay : 8/10 (just what I am into)
Overall : 8/10 (recommended for you if you like gameplay like arma)

BEWARE before buying this game! Arma III is not a game, its a f**king legitimate simulator. And the best one.
This game is by far the most realistic combat & warfare simulator ever made. It takes a long time to get a hang of all the aspects of the game and even longer to master them fully. Even after playing for 50+ hours, you will still find yourself not knowing a lot of things.
Do not be fooled by my 1 hour gameplay, for I probably have 100+ hours of offline gameplay.
Battlefield realism can only be described in two words. F**king Realistic. Seriously though, from seperately injured limbs giving you their own limitations depending on where you are shot at to extremely detailed stance and stamina, this game is no different than real life.
Graphical realism is also taken to extreme heights in many aspects such as dynamic lighting quality, shader quality, amazing god rays, particle quality and if your PC can take it, maximum view distance. Thats when you get an EPIC scenery. This game also offers the best projectile ballistics and physics in gaming history.
Buy this game if you want to really experience what it feels like to be in a warzone. However you will need a lot of time to even learn how to play this game so do not expect something like Call of Duty or Battlefield, those don't even come close to the realism this game has to offer.
If only this game had VR support, all gamers now would be professional & hardened soldiers.
10/10 would buy again.

There are too many positive and negative things to say about this game. I'll be mentioning the negative things mostly in this review to express my disappointment in order to raise the public awareness thus the devs can take measures against them. First of all I have to say that I've played this game alone most of the time, trying fives and duos. It cannot be denied that griefing and players being toxic are the most important problems. When you play fives alone, game gives you four other players to play as a team of five. As there is no punishment for it, you're most likely to get killed by one of your team mates, which happens a lot and drives you crazy. The developers of the game should immediately take action against this situation. The second is, of course, the bugs! There are a lot of them. You stuck underground after landing, your car explodes without a reason; getting you killed, there are items which you cannot pick up and sometimes there are bullets of the weapon on ground but not the gun itself. These problems might seem small but after you wait for 5 minutes to get into the game and come across one of these problems, you might go bananas. I have to say that although I've never bump into no cheater in this game, it's said that there are a lot of them (I've seen a lot of them in streams). Besides all these negative things, the format of the game is tempting. Most of the time it makes your heart beat really fast when you're the second one to be alive or even when you hear footsteps around you. Moreover, this game gives you the opportunity to meet perfect people to play with, other than the toxic ones.
If I am to sum up, if you're a patient person about the bugs and possible toxic environment, sure you will enjoy this game and have a really good time playing it.

Arma 3 is a singleplayer and multiplayer realistic military combat sim. Mouthful, I know, but if you think that's a lot you should try learning the controls.
No, really, Arma 3 is a fantastic game, and I couldn't recommend it anymore than I do to my friends already. The Singleplayer aspect offers the Bohemia Interactive campaign, where you play as Ben Kerry, the main protagonist of the campaign. It offers intuitive missions that can be played in multiple different ways placing you at the frontlines of guerrila and combined arms warfare. The story is good and (most important to me) believable. I recommend playing the campaign.
Multiplayer is where the game starts to become very diverse. There are hosted servers online that offer a variety of different gamemodes and types, with "King of the Hill" and "Altis Life" as my personal favorites. There is also a milsim community out there, if that is your thing. Since this game has a steam workshop, it throws in an entire new variable on your multiplayer experience. Missions can be downloaded from the steam workshop and can be played in either singleplayer OR multiplayer with friends. This extends the life of the game if you ever get bored or finish the default campgain and have had enough of online multiplayer. A good percentage of my time spent in Arma 3 had been with friends playing missions and having fun.
• Above average singleplayer campaign expereince
• Very engaging and diverse multiplayer
• Steam workshop
• Large and Active community
• Graphics on max settings make the game pretty to look at
• Optimization isn't that great, and getting above 60fps on a decent computer is rare
Overall, the game is great fun to play and I've had a blast playing it. I give this game a thumbs up.

Note: I bought H1Z1 in Dec. 2015 and enjoyed it for 40+ hours. After the split, my hours were moved to H1Z1: Just Survive, hence why I have 49 minutes played in H1Z1: Kotk. Though, I play H1Z1 on my second account:
.
TL;DR Go buy PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS. It's 200% better than H1Z1 and it has what H1Z1 will probably never have; Great development team, weapon attachments, winner/loser rewards, better gunplay & combat and much more...
H1Z1: King of the Kill is an okayish first person/third person shooter. Before, it was called Battle Royale (sorta still is), over a hundred people participating in a huge death match. It will make you paranoid and you have to really loot fast, listen, shoot, kill and look all around you to survive. You can select Solo, Duo and Fives. Playing H1Z1: King of the Kill is decent with friends and sometimes even solo play. They also have a "Pre Season" leaderboard where you can track your solo progress (kills, score, etc).
H1Z1: Kotk has around 25k+ players at minimum playing almost constantly. I've seen as high as a 73k+ player base at times. There's no shortage of people or queue times (they recently fixed queue times which made it pretty much instant to get into a game). Starting out, you'll wait in a lobby until the timer runs out for the game to start. Once the game has started you'll begin to parachute down to a huge map from a decent height to choose a spot that might have good loot or you can hover in the air, look where everybody else is going so you can avoid them as you parachute down. Most of the time it's about getting to the ground as fast as possible to gather loot or even a vehicle to have a better start for yourself.
Yes, loot and vehicles. There's only 4 vehicles: Truck, Jeep, Police Car and ATV. Truck is the slowest of them all, but it's better than nothing. Jeep is the second fastest whilst police car and ATV will go faster than the rest. However, ATV can only hold 2 players, whilst the other vehicles hold 5 players. Vehicles allow you to move around the map faster, but they do have fuel and health.
Loot, ahh yes. There's a lot of loot. RNG depicts where loot goes. Pistols, assault rifles, grenades, molotovs, helmets, armor (makeshift/lammy) and more! Loot is always something to make everyone fight over and I've had my fair share of experience with that. You can choose to go all out and loot everything you see or gather a certain amount of items and kill other people for their items instead. Try not to loot everything you see - There's bag space. You can have an ordinary backpack that holds 1200~ weight or a military backpack that holds 2200~. Each item you loot will take up bag space. Becareful looting though, players can easily pick you off while you're looting. I've had bad experiences with that too.
I think the most lethal to you besides those pesky serial killers we call players is the toxic gas. The gas is released after the safe zone is revealed and the 5 minute timer is up. Before that you'll need to be near that safe zone circle or you're toast. The gas will get powerful as the game progresses so you'll always need to be a step ahead of it. I've even used the gas to my advantage. Know where the gas is going to spread to and if you're in the safe zone & the enemy isn't you can fire at them, drop their health and the gas will do the rest (given they are still in it). It's amusing when that happens. Although, I've had my fair share of gas deaths.
I can't really say much about their graphics in the game other than they aren't that great at max settings. My settings are on low so I can see other players better (mainly just lighting off, shadows low, other is medium to high). It's best if you tinker with your settings to find it easier to see items and players much better without much darkness.
H1Z1: King of the Kill has a crate system. The game isn't P2W, it's just cosmetics. They even have a "scrap" system where you can scrap items for the scrap currency and turn scrap in for more items. Their skull system allows you to back yourself in solo play. If you do well in solo play you'll earn skulls once bet. After leveling every 5 levels you'll also receive free unlocked crates to open; otherwise, playing the game will earn you locked crates you can sell on the steam community market.
The feeling you feel when winning a game is pretty intense at times, until you realize there's no rewards for winning.
Let's not forget H1Z1: King of the Kill is still in early access and it does have a lot of issues. This is what makes me mainly dislike this game. They
release updates every month or so, but I feel like there's not enough hotfixes to fix common bugs or updates to the game to bring in different, items, features, etc. H1Z1: Kotk has been in development for several years++ and no major improvements. It's pretty upsetting.
The most common bug I run into is stuck parachuting. You're hovering above the ground whilst the parachute is still intact and will force you to exit the match, but normally it ends up crashing your client instead. Second common bug is parachuting under the world, forcing you to logout and again it'll crash the client instead. Not to mention the glorious amount of loot bugs where some loot has sunk into the ground, object its on, etc. It'll even cause the ammo to do the same depending if any objects are near, the ammo will go inside of that object and you won't be able to loot them. Let's also not forget a large amount of objects floating in midair.
Collision is another thing. It might as well not exist, especially with vehicles. Trying to run over someone with a vehicle at full speed will not always kill players.
Gunplay is terrible. You can jump around like the ground is hot lava to avoid being shot or have an enemy do the same. They need to limit jumping.
I think the most frustrating part of H1Z1: King of the Kill is how static the map is and the places you never parachute down to anymore. It would make gameplay experience better if their map or map objects in general was procedurally generated. Of course loot is based on RNG, but I feel like the map should have a significant difference almost every playthrough.
I ask myself every time I play H1Z1 Kotk, "How come we never spawn at the Dam anymore?". In the old map it was fun parachuting down to the dam, gathering loot and killing people since the place is FULL of loot. Nowadays to even loot the dam you need to be lucky enough to spawn close by, get a vehicle and drive 3 minutes to arrive there. You'll have roughly 4 minutes to loot the richness of the Dam, but it's worth it since nobody goes there anymore.
I feel like the utilization of the map edges A-J 1-10 is horribly lacking. They only have it where people are spawned more inside of the map than on the sides.
The second most frustrating thing is, they removed the rewards for winning or losing. Back in 2015 you used to receive a loot bag that you can open. Depending on how well your position was in a game you'll get a better loot bag. But, when I came back to H1Z1 early 2016 that was removed. Winning or dying at a certain number is no longer rewarding. The only thing you have is bragging rights and that's not really incenitive to keep playing besides the Solo Season, which is 1% better than being rewarded with item(s).
There's more issues to this game that I feel could be resolved. I think there's more things Daybreak can do to H1Z1: Kotk since it does have potential. Would be nice if they introduced new weapons or new items in general, game modes, etc - That's the potential this game has, but development is too slow and hotfixes are almost always non-existent.
H1Z1: King of the Kill as I wrote has potential, but it's on a bad development path with redundant decision making and development team.

H1Z1: king of the Kill is a 2 world/map online survival based game in which the objective is to survive against other human players, looting different buildings, camp sites, open areas and even churches, for weapons, vehicles and and medical supplies. All of this, and the ever closing threat of a dangerous gas surrounding the map, which in turn every so often stops for a certain time, then changes the point of intrest for you to get to. My thoughts on the game are a follows;
Good:
1. Friends=fun: The game is, in my opinion much more entertaining when accompanied with friends, whether with 1 or 4 other people. (1player=Solo 2 People=duos and 3-5 players=Fives)
2. Tension: When you play this game, whether in solo duos or fives, it gets really tense as you see the number of people remaining go down on your screen. Also as you look around for your vital survival equipment you know that just next door could be another player.
3. How getting kills can be satisfying: How does this game do it? when you are roaming the streets or checking out villages, coming across players 99% of the time result in gun-fights, and when you pull out your AR, or your Shotgun for close combat, then proceed to kill someone you get a feeling of accomplishment and that you have earned whatever place you finish. (Many other shooters lack this feeling)
Bad;
1. Repetitive: This game is by far one of thee most repetitive shooters i have ever played, You start by parachuting in looking for a good spot to start, then proceed to loot around then stay in the safe area of the world until there is only one player left alive. Gas closes in, the longer you remain alive. There are only 4 weapons that are of any use (AR15 AK47 Shotgun and magnum), use any of the others and you dont really stand a chance.
2. Tough for newbies to the keyboard: If you are tempted, i suggest plenty of practise. As this game is purely online, you have a lobby of around 170 people who load in at the same time as you, many of which are acustomed to the keyboard and mouse setup, in turn when you do load into the game and come to a gunfight it will most certainly end badly and in the process become frustrated with how quick and frequent you end up on the losing side.
3. Price?: On Steam this game is currently £14.99, Which to me is such a steep amount for the basic game it actually is. There is no depth at all, Parachute in, Loot, Kill, Stay alive. i could even narrow it down to, Stay alive. Graphically the game is ok, however i have seen many people turn their settings down reducing the quality just to play the game better, now fair enough if it improves individual performance then so be it, but it then shows a seriousness to the game, when it is, only a game.
I have only listed 3 points on each, however i wanted to leave it at a basic overview.
my conclusion is that this game could have a bit more depth to it and maybe different lobbies for newer members, even though there is a ranking system it just shows the skill level. Overal i give this game a 5.5/10, its not an awful game, it just lacks variety. I would recommend this game but not for the price.

Hello everyone,
I'm writing this review with plenty of experience off-line and on-line. With almost 900 hours of gameplay during the writing of this review I think a review is suitable. So let's get started shall we.
First, let me talk about the multiple aspects of ArmA 3. You have multiple ways to play and enjoy ArmA.
The singleplayer campaign is perfect, but also isn't bad in any aspects. I, myself, enjoyed the singeplayer campaign as I'm sopmeone who gets dragged into a story really quickly. It's compelling, quite long and it will keep you busy for some time. I actually recommend on completing it if you want to practice your in-game skills.
Scenarios are a great way to pass time and really learn about the game. Their are amazing campaigns you can find on the steam workshop, or on of the many forums online like armaholic or withSix.
The multiplayer aspect of it is where this game really shines. You have multiple communities and choices when playing online. You have altis life, which is real-life roleplay. Then you have milsim servers, which make you roleplay as an actual soldier. You also have wasteland, king of the hill or invade and annex. You have a lot of choices.
The modding community is just great. You have more 1000 mods you can find and download on Armaholic, withSix or any other website like these. There a lot of role-play community roleplaying like actual real-life army companies/units.
Now, after we discussed the multiple ways of playing and enjoying arma 3. Why should I buy it? Well, let me sum up some pros and cons.
Pros:
Intriging campaign
Great community
More then enough gamemodes
Beautifull game
Cons:
Require a good cumputer to run on high, or higher graphics
Quite steep learning curve
I hope this review helped you making your decision,

It is a more realistic game by far over COD and Battlefield. You can also download a lot of gear and vehicles from the previous arma games.
