I used a number of different combat simulators when I was In the Army, this game is military grade.It does have performance issues for many users however, If the game just learned to utilize your p.c. and its hardware better. For example if they had grandtheft auto fives detailed world and smooth transition in textures in the world and kept the rest of the game this would be the best military sim ever as far as ground/air together.  Its a game you want to love but the choppy loading terrain and pop ups take a lot away when using aircraft. It does give you an open world military experience. I think they just stuck to many objects bushes trees etc.. and the game is not friendly to machines that tend to lean toward the middle of performance. its like the settings are either high or low and low will sometimes even slow down your computer because it shifts from gpu to cpu. If your looking for mil sim its one of the few games, I would also try DCS it may give you a more satisfactory experience, where your not hacking files to make it run smoothly. It will take you time to learn the the more real you go the more time you will have invested in the learning curve. it may be a pain on some systems to get set up to run to your satisifaction. Remember this when configuring your game if you have a high spec system some settings should be on high + Standard works for many setting low settings are for low spec or intigrated graphics cards and can actually reduce your p.c. performance. Also look the game up online on Bohemia Interactives forums site for help with tweaking parameters if your looking to squeeze more frames per second from the game. I also would reccomend this title even more on an Alienware or Steam Machine console So you have the ability to use gaming mode which also will enhance the game noticably on Alienware Alpha console I can vouch for that, or any game for that matter running under console mode gives me between .6 and .9 GB of Ram back from Windows greedy little paws. If they sold a program that enhanced this game and its performance I would buy it. I give it an 8/10 but then it would be a 10/10 for years to come if had a better and more fluid scenery. The scenery just gets a bit choppy at times you kind have have to get that right configuration.

Review -
To start with, the base game is great. There is enough content there to have fun with for a fairly long time, especially with the zues mode and its on the fly mission editor style of play. The multiplayer can be great fun if played with the right people, just like any other game of course, however this one you will NEED the right people otherwise it will get tedious and boring.
To expand from the base game there is the Steam Workshop and many other websites where you can download a whole crap tonne of mods from the incredibly active modding community. These can vary from simple tweaks to the original game like sound tweaks and ragdoll physics all the way to large collections where it adds a whole host of modern vehicles and expansive maps. This will increase the play value of this game well over 300%!. The only reason I have over 400 hours of play time is due to having so many mods that I have great fun with and other people to have fun with.
If you get this game then you will see that it is all near future technology and even some current tech, however if you are like me and prefer the modern style of things then mods is the way forward.
Like mentioned right at the start, this game is well worth the money, the dlcs are more of just a little side thing if you wish to support the devs. They cost a fair amount and to be honest you could get similar things with mods, with the exception of things like shooting out of vehicles and stuff (which is given to everyone for free might I add!).
KNOWLEDGE

Review -
To start with, the base game is great. There is enough content there to have fun with for a fairly long time, especially with the zues mode and its on the fly mission editor style of play. The multiplayer can be great fun if played with the right people, just like any other game of course, however this one you will NEED the right people otherwise it will get tedious and boring.
To expand from the base game there is the Steam Workshop and many other websites where you can download a whole crap tonne of mods from the incredibly active modding community. These can vary from simple tweaks to the original game like sound tweaks and ragdoll physics all the way to large collections where it adds a whole host of modern vehicles and expansive maps. This will increase the play value of this game well over 300%!. The only reason I have over 400 hours of play time is due to having so many mods that I have great fun with and other people to have fun with.
If you get this game then you will see that it is all near future technology and even some current tech, however if you are like me and prefer the modern style of things then mods is the way forward.
Like mentioned right at the start, this game is well worth the money, the dlcs are more of just a little side thing if you wish to support the devs. They cost a fair amount and to be honest you could get similar things with mods, with the exception of things like shooting out of vehicles and stuff (which is given to everyone for free might I add!).

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest

My experience- I have over 1500 hours invested between all of the Arma versions, and their mods. more than half of that I spent playing Arma 3, on Epoch and Exile servers.
The mods really do make these games come alive, but if it wasnt for the awesome Dev team and massive amount of content available with the vanilla game, the community as we know it wouldnt exist. I have never shared so many different emotions playing one game, Anger, fear, frustration, joy and curiousity as I let my imagination write a tale every time I log in. Of course your gaming experience will vary depending what type of mod you are playing, but thats just another great asset this game has, you can literally go from a battlefield 4 style game mode with 100+ players on a simply massive map, to a zombie survival in a wasteland, or strugling to survive as a prisoner recently dropped into a unkown island.
If you are looking for THE military simulator, that simply has it all and then some.. this is it.
The learning curve is steep, and there isnt much forgiveness from veteran players, but how you handle being thrown into the fire is up to you. Did I mention the modding community? because its insane, literally everything you wanted to create or play your own custom server is here, from base building, crafting, farming, flying, weapons, vehicles, maps, npcs etc etc etc the list is endless.
Currently I have been playing Exile servers with my Wife, there is persistent base building, missions, trading, looting, raiding, crafting and much more. Eventually you find the community that fits your play style and thats when you really get addicted. PVE/PVP, Roaming AI, Vehicles etc there are thousands of persistent servers running hundreds of variations of each mod, and almost all have very active players and admins.

So, the good:
-upgraded graphics engine
-gigantic map
-bipods! Yea, after few years they put bipods in game!
-shooting from vehicles - same as with bipods - finally!
-new more smooth and natural animations
-game is super moddable
-as usual great mission editor (I pretty much spent all my time creating my own missions).
-driving is way more enjoyable than in any prev Armas
Now the bad:
-no female soldiers/civilians -(if COD could we can too)
-insane gun swaying and bobbing, gets infuriating
-stamina - your soldier will fall on his face after running for 10 seconds
-compare to A2 not that many various units
-still no tank/apc interiors
-lots of people reporting insane lag/fps issues MP and SP.
Its a great game, and you can pretty much mod it to whatever you want - rpg/zombies/survival (blah...booring)/ military ops/racing- peek your fix.
Still, if you are looking only for realistic military sim - get Arma 2 Operation Arrowhead and put the ACE mod into it - it will be insanely good and sadly better experience than A3.

Arma 3 is probably the best shooter I've ever played.  If you're a COD player, or an active Battlefield player, like I was, this is going to be a huge step for you.  It's a hard game to play, yes, but Bohemia does a great job in giving a comprehensive training course in the virtual reality.  After you get out of virtual reality, enter the world of Altis and Stratis, two Mediterranean islands, most likely off the coast of Greece.  The map size is incredible.  Larger than Skyrim, Fallout 4, and probably The Witcher III put together.  Try running from side to side... just try.  The two islands feature millions and millions of placed objects.  The game ($60 on steam) is totally worth every penny, ESPECIALLY with user-created mods.  Dive into the mods, this game basically becomes invaluable.  Arma 3 truly is an incredible feet of gaming.
On the maps - They're huge!  You'll need a vehicle to get around definitely.  Their size is only rivalled by their beauty, if you're playing on ultra high settings it's almost like real life, or at least as close as a game can get.  The country side is not thrown aside in terms of details, actually, it's focused on.  You'll find things such as harbors, wind turbine fields, solar farms, small villages, forests, and rolling plains.   All of these areas are included with immense wildlife, you'll never find yourself alone.  The cities are also well built and great for close quarter combat.  Make sure you download the All in Arma Terrain Pack - this comes with ALL the maps from Arma 2 revamped up to Arma 3 quality.
On the gameplay - It's immenseful.  It's set about 20 yeras in the future.  You'll lose track of time, you'll probably lose your eyesight from getting to close to your PC screen.  Battles are realisticly timed because of the combat system.  You WILL die if you are hit in the head or upper torso, you'll break your legs if you're shot there.  No more rushing into battle or leading to charge, you stick with your team, you'll need them desperately.  You always will have a group of soldiers to command and place, use them to your advantage.  Think of downloading Blastcore, JSRS, and the Enhanced Movement mods, they will decrease your performance slightly, but it's worth the even more realistic feeling.  The battles are HARD.  The United States has been fighting unmathched and outdated opposing forces ever since the end of World War 2.  In this game you are fighting the AAF, a well modernized domestic defense force.  You will also be coming in contact with CSAT, which is basically an army of the Chinese, Russian, and Iranian forces coming together and is very powerful - NATO struggles.
On the weapons - They're almost real to the touch.  The amount of detail that went into these weapons is incredible.  The mechanics are also great.  You'll have to practice recoil management, as well as being able to zero an optic or use the mil-dot system to account for bullet drop.  If you want to make sharpshooting even for difficult/realistic, download the Arma Enhanced Combat mod, now you'll not only have to account for drop, but for wind, and even the rotation of the Earth.  Size matters!  You'll have greater success in hitting a target with a 5.56 and slightly less with the MX's 6.5mm.  Once you get into 7.62 small arms, you'll find a sufficient decrease in accuracy, but better stopping power.  Bullet penetration is a thing, and you will be shot inside a building from the outside if you're not being smart.  Let's also not leave out the insane amount of accessories you cant attach to your weapons, especially if you download some mods.  For example, CUP weapons pack, HLC, RH, etc.  There are great mods out there as always.
On the vehicles - I don't know where to start.  On the ground, you'll usually find yourself rolling in the 2030's MRAP called the Hunter, or a modernized M2A3 Bradley fighting vehicle.  You'll find yourself reinforced by Slammers, the main battle tanks of the future which are vamped up M1 Abrams.  Or even supported by 155mm Howitzers that can even fire laser guided shells.  Go as far as to even be in a Nissan pickup with a .50 cal in the bed.  In the air, you can find yourself in a stealth A-10C, an RAH-66 Commanche, an armed Huey, stealth Blackhawk (the Nighthawk), and Little Bird, fixed-wing UAVs, and even a quadcopter.  Use air support to your advantage!  Even in the sea you'll find yourself in an attack boat or a submersible.  And always, vehicle mods abounds.  REMEMBER - you are fighting modernized military defense forces, they will have everything you have, including hell storms of AA.
Arma 3 is a fantastic game that once you've got the hang of you'll fall in love with.  The community is huge and you'll always find yourself exploring new scenarios and options.  The developers care!  You'll receive weekly or biweekly updates or news items.  Yes, there are bugs.  There are bugs with every game.  With a game this scale, how can you blame them?  They're working on it.  Most of all, explore multiplayer and do scenarios with a group of friends, or maybe 100 friends.  The opportunities are endless, enjoy!

Arma 3 is another in Bohemia Interactive's Arma series. It is Open-World. Military Tactic Simulation with Multiplayer function. The game has a log of singleplayer missions and tutorials. The thing with this game though, is the community and how expansive the game is. Arma 3 has a large community which leads to modding the hell out of the game; adding more fun and possibilities. The scale of Arma 3 is enormous with the possibilities. I came into Arma 3 mainly just to play Altis Life, ended playing almost every feature I could. The amount of mods is unbelievable. So much content!
The maps of Arma 3 are a key factor as well. Arma 3 takes place on the two main maps of Altis and Stratis. Both being enormous maps, but Altis being the biggest one. Again with the content, there are even more maps for the game. You can go back to World War II and play on Wake Island, or even fight in modern day Afghanistan. All the maps are so big with Altis being 270 square kilometers. Now Stratis only comes in with 20 square kilometers, but the new 2016 DLC map, Tanoa, which will be km with new realistic structures
The multiplayer of this game has many game modes; Domination, CTF, TDM, Warfare, Zeus, and so many more. You can even create your own scenarios to play with friends of groups. One very popular gamemode is Altis Life made by Asylum Entertainment. Altis Life is a roleplay mode where you can be a cop, an EMT, towtruck man, ANYTHING. The content creator can be used to make missions and scenarios to play with friends, or even yourself.
The community for Arma 3 is enormous. Which allows for more expansive features and mods. Mods for the game can add more vehicles, weapons, maps, and pretty much, anything. The community has tips and tricks for new players. The videos on YouTube and steam are great to watch.
Arma 3 comes with a unique content creator built within the game. The content creator can be used to do whatever. You can create a mission or scenario to play with your friends or even yourself. You can add a few AI team members, few AI enemy players, and test it out  to fight them. It is very powerful and has great potential if you know how to use it. Some people of the community have used very well to make great missions.

This game is amazing! I thought CoD was good when I first got it XD but this makes CoD look like childs play!
-Free roaming!
-Epic weapons and equipment you can use to destroy your enemies and save your friends!
-Many vehicles to choose from to either transport your buddies to a safezone or blow them up! (Or make them roadkill if you want to XD)
-Zeus! (A god mode where someone can edit the map and/or help and/or challenge players and customize the map and create missions! You get a new game basically every time!)
-There is a VR (Virtual Reality) that you can use to practice and hone your skills before you step out onto the battlefield, or to pick up old and rusts skills after a prolonged break!
-Excellent NPC A.I. ! though sometimes it seems a little crappy, it seems the most realistic that I have ever seen! They even react well to noise, but it is a shame that they instantly know where you are if you launch a Grenade launcher, and instead of looking where the explosion happens they shoot you in the face... Oh well, it would probably happen in real life...
- Cons -
-Sometimes the server devs or admins could be kind of rude and kick you for the littlest mistakes...
-There is no easier difficulty for those of us who suck at games -ahem cough cough *me* cough cough-
-The Zeus is kind of difficult to get used to (in my opinion) the controls aren't very simple it seems, and it is difficult to figure out what to do and do it quickly without LOTS of practice (just an opinion, dont judge me)
-Not a very "casual" game, you can't just pick up the game and just play a little here and there, this game seems to demand a lot of time and you cant just play an hour, because nothing would probably happen, it takes a while to get anywhere and get some action, except in campaign, but the save zones are a little stretched out... just make sure you have a few hours on hand so you don't end up messing yourself up, just a suggestion. (not really a con or a pro, it's kind of in between.)
- The graphics are also cool and all, but it may take a beefy computer to run this if you want anything besides the lowest quality... or my computer just sucks... either way, it is still fun with or without seeing Joe Shmoes hair folicles XD.
All in all I would give this game a rating of 8/10 It is very fun and exciting when there is action, but it is just so boring a lot (especially in multiplayer) because you have to run around and find the people, and if youre inexperienced you will most likely get blown to bits and have to restart all over, back to where you spawned the first time... over and over.... Zeus adds a little more excitement, but sometimes you can just get a troll that wants to make everyone mad and ruin the game for everyone. All in all, I feel the purchase is worth it, especially if you plan on playing with a few friends as the servers can hold up to 100+ people in them as I have seen (just make sure your internet is good and your ping is LOW (like max should be 70 for optimal experience).

Arma 3 is another in Bohemia Interactive's Arma series. It is Open-World. Military Tactic Simulation with Multiplayer function. The game has a log of singleplayer missions and tutorials. The thing with this game though, is the community and how expansive the game is. Arma 3 has a large community which leads to modding the hell out of the game; adding more fun and possibilities. The scale of Arma 3 is enormous with the possibilities. I came into Arma 3 mainly just to play Altis Life, ended playing almost every feature I could. The amount of mods is unbelievable. So much content!
The maps of Arma 3 are a key factor as well. Arma 3 takes place on the two main maps of Altis and Stratis. Both being enormous maps, but Altis being the biggest one. Again with the content, there are even more maps for the game. You can go back to World War II and play on Wake Island, or even fight in modern day Afghanistan. All the maps are so big with Altis being 270 square kilometers. Now Stratis only comes in with 20 square kilometers, but the new 2016 DLC map, Tanoa, which will be km with new realistic structures
The multiplayer of this game has many game modes; Domination, CTF, TDM, Warfare, Zeus, and so many more. You can even create your own scenarios to play with friends of groups. One very popular gamemode is Altis Life made by Asylum Entertainment. Altis Life is a roleplay mode where you can be a cop, an EMT, towtruck man, ANYTHING. The content creator can be used to make missions and scenarios to play with friends, or even yourself.
The community for Arma 3 is enormous. Which allows for more expansive features and mods. Mods for the game can add more vehicles, weapons, maps, and pretty much, anything. The community has tips and tricks for new players. The videos on YouTube and steam are great to watch.
Arma 3 comes with a unique content creator built within the game. The content creator can be used to do whatever. You can create a mission or scenario to play with your friends or even yourself. You can add a few AI team members, few AI enemy players, and test it out  to fight them. It is very powerful and has great potential if you know how to use it. Some people of the community have used very well to make great missions.

This game is amazing! I thought CoD was good when I first got it XD but this makes CoD look like childs play!
-Free roaming!
-Epic weapons and equipment you can use to destroy your enemies and save your friends!
-Many vehicles to choose from to either transport your buddies to a safezone or blow them up! (Or make them roadkill if you want to XD)
-Zeus! (A god mode where someone can edit the map and/or help and/or challenge players and customize the map and create missions! You get a new game basically every time!)
-There is a VR (Virtual Reality) that you can use to practice and hone your skills before you step out onto the battlefield, or to pick up old and rusts skills after a prolonged break!
-Excellent NPC A.I. ! though sometimes it seems a little crappy, it seems the most realistic that I have ever seen! They even react well to noise, but it is a shame that they instantly know where you are if you launch a Grenade launcher, and instead of looking where the explosion happens they shoot you in the face... Oh well, it would probably happen in real life...
- Cons -
-Sometimes the server devs or admins could be kind of rude and kick you for the littlest mistakes...
-There is no easier difficulty for those of us who suck at games -ahem cough cough *me* cough cough-
-The Zeus is kind of difficult to get used to (in my opinion) the controls aren't very simple it seems, and it is difficult to figure out what to do and do it quickly without LOTS of practice (just an opinion, dont judge me)
-Not a very "casual" game, you can't just pick up the game and just play a little here and there, this game seems to demand a lot of time and you cant just play an hour, because nothing would probably happen, it takes a while to get anywhere and get some action, except in campaign, but the save zones are a little stretched out... just make sure you have a few hours on hand so you don't end up messing yourself up, just a suggestion. (not really a con or a pro, it's kind of in between.)
- The graphics are also cool and all, but it may take a beefy computer to run this if you want anything besides the lowest quality... or my computer just sucks... either way, it is still fun with or without seeing Joe Shmoes hair folicles XD.
All in all I would give this game a rating of 8/10 It is very fun and exciting when there is action, but it is just so boring a lot (especially in multiplayer) because you have to run around and find the people, and if youre inexperienced you will most likely get blown to bits and have to restart all over, back to where you spawned the first time... over and over.... Zeus adds a little more excitement, but sometimes you can just get a troll that wants to make everyone mad and ruin the game for everyone. All in all, I feel the purchase is worth it, especially if you plan on playing with a few friends as the servers can hold up to 100+ people in them as I have seen (just make sure your internet is good and your ping is LOW (like max should be 70 for optimal experience).

OVERALL: 9/10
Arma 3 is a very fun military simulation that focuses on a focus of simulation within access of everyone. What I mean by this is anyone can play Arma 3 and enjoy it. I will not go onto the reasons why I have Arma 3 the score I did:
Base Game (7/10)
When you first buy the game I will highly recommend that you spend some time playing the singleplayer missions just to get the handle of how to play this game. The singleplayer has an "ok" storyline that will keep you entertained long enough and actually care somewhat about the story.
When you get finish / have enough of singleplayer you can hop onto the Multiplayer where most of the action is! This is completly up to you on what you decide to do in multiplayer... You have a variety of different modes to choose from, be it King-Of-The-Hill or Capture-The-Island you will work with other players to complete your objective. The multiplayer provides a lot of fun and enjoyment for people who give it time and some effort. There are some trolls in multiplayer however most of the server deal with them within a short time.
Cart DLC (4/10)
The Cart DLC was a small addition to Arma 3 that added some go-carts and some clothing. This is a very small and cheap DLC. There is no real reason to buy it, however for the price it does allow you to do races and drive the go-carts into battle like the badass you are!
Marksman DLC (8/10)
This DLC added quite a few new guns into the game that allow players to have a new way to play the game. It also added some singleplayer missions to try out the new guns and "playstyle". Overall I do believe this DLC is one of the "required" DLC's as it allows you to use the guns. And in some situations you don't want to have a gun and deal with the DLC watermark every once in a while.
KEEP IN MIND: You don't need to own the DLC to pick up / use the guns, you will simply have to deal with a watermark on your screen.
Helicopter DLC (6/10)
I am a huge fan of helicopters in Arma 3, however I do kind of feel like this DLC could have been added as a free DLC into the game, but meh. This DLC adds some new helicopters into the game (just as the name suggests) that mainly focus on heavy transportation of troops and vehicles. Unless you plan to fly those helicopters you don't need to own the DLC!
Jet DLC (8/10)
Overall this DLC adds some new jets, new drone, jet carrier and a new singleplayer mission to test out the new jets. These jets are quite good and VERY fast. If you like flying jets that make you feel like Sonic...well this is definetly for you! These new jets (also the old ones...possibly) can go faster than the speed of sound and yes...we know this since it creates the sonic boom everytime you go faster than the speed of sound. I would say this DLC is more of a way of us appriciating the devs of making more content for us so we pay a little but more cash.
Apex DLC (9/10)
This is a HUGE DLC that the devs gave up that adds a brand new map that is full of small details and atmosphere. This map is a little bit FPS heavy in some cases however it is beautiful and very good when you want to have some jungle warfare. Not only did it add the new map Tanoa, it also added new guns, clothing, vehicles, singleplayer missions AND some Co-Op missions that you can play with up to 4 people. This DLC is VERY worth the money!
Laws of War DLC (10/10)
This DLC was all about the Civilian Casualities and Horrors of war. This DLC adds quite a sizable campaign that was VERY enjoyable and atmospheric. It also added a whole new faction called IDAP (International Development & Aid Project) that is centered about responding to humanitarian disasters. It adds couple of new vehicles and some new retextures to already existing vehicles. If you are a fan of RolePlay this DLC also adds some new clothing with IDAP logos on it as well as some Medic & Demo Specialist clothing and vests. The DLC also adds some new drones that can be used for storing items as well as exploding mines.
Tac-Ops DLC (2/10)
First of...yes I did give this DLC a low score and you will find out why. Right so...Tac-Ops...without given any sort of hint of what the DLC was going to be fully about there were quite a few good expectations as it could have brought loads new fun things something to do with...Tactical Operations, but no. Anyhow, what this DLC is all about is it adds couple of missions for you. These missions are ok, the voice acting sounds a bit lazy and...bored but oh well this game isn't made for voice acting so that can be forgiven. However the missions are a little bit "meh" they are mostly just the same as the others. This DLC also adds a very small amount of vehicle retextures. No new weapons, no new gear, no new vehicles. This could be called "If you enjoy our game and want to donate CLICK HERE!" overall I do not believe this DLC is all that worth it but it can extend you playing time of the game by a bit. So its your choice.
Arma 3 Modded (10/10)
Now once you get bored of the un-modded Arma 3, well get ready to spend a hell of a lot more time in the game due to the mods that are being made DAILY for Arma 3. The modding scene for Arma 3 is HUGE! Do you want a HALO mod? Yep we got that. A WW2 mod? Yep we got that too. Scared of snakes? No worries, the devs released a mod to remove them!

I spent several years in the army and I gotta say this game is spot on with the training and atmosphere the military provides. I love how difficult this game is, and I love all of the different features the game provides. It is NOT easy to hit a target with an assault rifle from 300 yards in real life, and this game seems to match that same difficulty. Enemies are not stupid and they have great vision. I was engaged by two enemies from about 200 yards away and they were using bushes for cover as well as 3-5 second rushes when moving. H1Z1 KoTK is a fun game, the idea of the game is great and theres a skill gap (which I love in every game), the very good players will rek everyone else, but because of uncountable bugs that are in the game and the very unconsistent hitreg it completly ruins it. There's multiple small bugs that will frustrate you and just as many game breaking ones that will make you lose the game. Every patch fixes 5 bugs and add 10 more. It's been like this for almost 2 years. The hitreg either works barely or it doesn't. Shooting behind cover makes your bullets hit the obstacle. Shooting between the gap in a wooden fence makes you hit the fence. The game has slowly improved and if the developers wasn't focusing on adding more cases and creating a 300 000 bucks tournament for a barely playable game it would have improved faster. A king of the hill game should be a game where the strong dominate the weak, but since the gas is such a low threat players can easily stack the gas and hide until few remains. This review isn't about hating on the game. I love KoTK and daybreak have fixed and imporoved a lot of things, but theres still things to do to make the game playable.
What should be improved:
1. Fix the hitreg (This includes fixing shooting over obstacles)
2. Make the gas more unforgiving
3. Focus on the game breaking bugs and test the patch before releasing
I want to recommend KoTK because I enjoy playing it solo and with friends. It's quick, it's unforgiving and the idea is gold. But if you want a quality King of the Hill game without getting frustrated about the countless of bugs, I recommend the Arma 3 mod.

Mixed feelings for Multiplayer.
#1 - Game is fun and the gametype elements are pretty cool. You have one big city with surrounding area and a designated landing zone. Three teams fly and drive their troops close to the LZ and try and take 4-5 tower areas within the LZ. Makes for a lot of fun building to building fighting but likewise can choose to sit and wait or snipe outside of the LZ. It's one of a few game modes (King of the Hill).
#2 - The gaming engine for multiplayer is super buggy. EXPECT to have between 15-30 frames AT BEST. If you have an i5/i7, you'll do better. If you have an AMD prepare for the hurt. It does NOT matter about your video card or ram(I have a GTX 980  and 32GB of RAM and get around 15-25 frames). The game is CPU intensive.
Actually this isn't the proper wording. It's a serious flaw that the game is CPU intensive rather than GPU intensive.
Everyone will say "well upgrade your CPU". Ok Ok, I could but a guy I play with (no joke) has a dual i7, 3 titan video cards and 128MB of ram and he still sometimes drops below 20 and never over 35ish on average.
Sometimes it's ok to play othertimes it's just too damn stupid. Server syncs are sometimes really choppy.
It's actually really sad that for $59.99 (about the most expensive a PC game gets these days) that it has these types of issues. Then once in game about 1/2 the guns, scopes, vehicles and others they want you to pay more for.
I find myself many times having to sit back and not play the way I want to but rather the way I know I can shoot and kill people because of FPS issues.
Most I can say is that they did not build this game with the intention of having huge multiplayer battles. If the gameplay type wasn't superb no one would put up with this serious flaw.
No joke. 15-20 frames the average person will have ....nearly unacceptable for the price paid if solely intend on multiplayer.
10/10 if it was built for large world multiplayer in mind. Unfortunatly, it's not so I'll rate it a 6.5/10

Hi! I have been playing this game for just enough time to tell that this game is a fun and fast paced battle royale. The main problem of this game is that it seems to be full of bugs, desync and hit reg issues (Alpha state). The problem is that Daybreak never really improves the game and they just milk it through crates, skins etc. For example at the moment of this post they just released patch notes to tell that they were implementing a ping indicator.....so yeah!. They made the money already so dont expect this game to imporve a lot if you buy it, just enjoy H1 wihout giving any value to rankings etc.
Map design 3/10: Just random cities and roads makes no sense to start other than Pleasant valley (Center of the map). Full of random rocks on every field. I only like that you can enter most of the buildings.
Guns 2/10: AR and AK are fine, magnum is too strong at the moment and other pistols irrelevant. The shotgun is one of the worst guns ever made in a game, it just won't work or one-shot through full body armor, makes no sense.
Cars 6/10: Driving the police car or the jeep is really fun and it has a nice feeling to it. But the ammount of vehicles on this game just makes no sense to me.
Looting 6/10: Fast and clean loot system. Just the lack of content makes it boring. No weapon sights to loot or other addons for the guns etc.
1st/3rd POV 5/10: The first person is just usefull for CQC. 3rd person it seems too op for me since you can peek around everything but whatever.
Players 8/10 : Most of the players that you face are legit rushers that you'll enjoy playing against but there are some of them that they won't move in the entire game and there is another kind of player who only arrives at fights when someone is healing or has to retreat, at first i thought that this was coinicidence but later I realised that they are just waiting for a fight to happent then they'll rush the remaining player while he is healing or looting.
Sound 1/10: So bad.
Graphics 4/10: medium to low engine, where you can have fun playing but it is nothing to talk about when you play all on ultra. It feels like a 2010 engine to me.

Before I begin, this review is subjective, obviously, but I have plenty of experience with TF2, Overwatch, and Paladins. Paladins I have the least played, and I probably have more hours in total on Overwatch than TF2, although that is beginning to change. With the whole controversy arising around September of 2016, a pivotal point in which I would switch from TF2 to Overwatch, Paladins came into open beta. Paladins sparked the whole discussion about TF2 vs. Overwatch vs. Paladins, saying that Overwatch ripped off TF2, and Paladins ripped off of Overwatch. This whole discussion continues, and there is never a true settlement, but the games, really, just got inspiration from eachother, derivities of TF2. Each game consists of unique aspects that make their gameplay fun and interesting. In this review, I'm not going to focus on Paladins because I have little experience, but I have a slightly beyond the basic assessment of the game. Anyway, I spent quite some time on Overwatch consistently. It was after about six to seven months of solely investing my time in Overwatch, I eventually returned to TF2 because I needed the prior, no limits experience I had in the game. I just felt that it has so much more content than Overwatch. Not only that, Overwatch is so much about focusing on the objective in the casual setting (nothing wrong with that, but I just didn't enjoy my experience as much as I did in TF2). A game like Overwatch, after playing it consistently, can definitely get repetitive, even with the continous updates that brought new heroes, maps, skins, emotes, etc. This game, unlike Overwatch, allows more freedom than other games of this genre, which in turn makes this game more interesting, removing the repetitive feeling. You won't be judged, for the most part, if you chose to be "friendly," at least in most community servers. One may still encounter "tryhards," but that's perfectly normal. I usually tend to ignore the friendlies and move on. I digress, but there are so many aspects different about TF2 and Overwatch. For example, TF2 allows more customization, creativity, and so much more. Overwatch, on the other hand, is more organized, has a better community (for the most part, not even going to get into the pornography section), but Overwatch has more limitations than TF2, which could definitely be a good thing for most people. Although, for me personally, the limits definitely have a great impact. TF2, unfortunately tried to change their game to fit with modern day FPS games with the Meet your Match update, that definitely dissapointed so many, making TF2's fate unsure. This game is unique because of the freedom it gives players, and I hope it doesn't change too much. Most are now awaiting the new update, which I really hope this update brings new content, new balance changes, and so much more that will make this game so much better, that will enhance this game without setting limits to one's personal playstyle. Before I end off, there should be a warning given about this community, seriously, because some can be very exclusive, especially to newer players, which I don't quite understand, but also I have met so many friendly people in this game. This community, unlike can definitely be a bit absurd. From racist, homophobic, sexist comments to really clever jokes. As long as you don't care about those types of "jokes," as in people are intentionally using the derogatory comments as a joke. As long as you don't care about those potentially minor things, it will be fine. Anyway, for everyone out there wondering if they should download this FREE game, just do it. It's a fun game with loads of content.

Team Fortress 2: What do I even have to say about this game?
Its a packed FPS with alot of different gamemodes and classes.
the variation of this game is almost endless by just default.
I can almost gurantee you with 30-50 hours as "Free-to-Play", and if you throw in as much as 0.99 into the Man Co. shop, you will unlock "Premium".
Whats "Premium" you ask? It adds 10 more pages of inventory slots, wich means you dont have to be picky about what gun you want to keep.
Hats and Cosmetics will also start dropping by default.
With the "Premium" you will most liekly stick arround for another 20 hours.
70 hours total gameplay.
Now, from personal experience.
What made Team Fortress 2 so addicting for me was the amazing community it have!
Searching the Server Browser gave me a almost endless sea of oppertunities.
I met people that molded me into the person I am today. And most off them have been sticking arround for almost aslong I've been on Steam.
Custom Gamemodes, Custome Boss Fights and alot more!
All made by the amazing community Team Fortress 2 have.
Despite what people says, the Team Fortress 2 community will remains one of the top 3 communities out there in my book.
When you're done with this amazing adventure of community exploration, you will most likely have 400-1000 hours gameplay.
By far, Team Fortress 2 remains nostalgic aswell as a loveable game for me.
9/10, I hope I can sit down in the future sometime, find the old crew and play another match of Team Fortress 2.

Overall, i would reccomend this game to a person that likes a rush and loves FPS with great graphics. I would rate this game a 10/10! I reviewed this game in mass detail when I was very yound, my exact words were "This is an amazing game!"
Now I shall review this game properly, providing a non biased view and my opinion of thegame based on a non biased review.
The pros of this game include the following:
Multiple, Highly Variable missions and scenarios, From life RP to Wasteland.
Hours of enjoyment, alot of content to get through, new experiences.
MODDING, if it were not for modding I am highly certain this game would be where it is right now
because this adds literally infinite new content to play, if the community thinks it needs it, this contributes to the modded part of arma III, obviously.
As optimised as Arma 2 but with MUCH UNDENIABLY better graphics.
Realism, One shot headshot kills, not for your COD Fanboys out there.
Simplicity of creating a mission in the editor.
They were some of the pros, now lets move onto the cons.
You need a pretty strong PC to run at 60 FPS, Something I have yet to achieve.
Physics, Car physics ( Crashing ), Walking over rocks(You vets know what i mean ... )
Well, now it is time for my own opinion, this is a great game and even with the low frame rates, ( 10 - 20 FPS ) I have still continued playing, and looking back on it now I can only say that is because I was having a really great time, some of the communites on serrvers can be cancerous but let's be honest, that's the people, Not Bohemia, Bless Bohemia, our lords and saviours.
I completely reccomend this game for an7yone with a PC that can run it well, trust me, you will have stacked hours of enjoyment and suffering all at once, and if you learn to fly a plane, be careful landing it, as I mentioned, A3 Physics 101.

Let me start by giving this game a 9/10. -1 point for multiplayer graphics problems.
If you want to know more about the rating that keep reading.
The game is immense. I played about zero percent of single player so IDK about that. I played the training and showcase missions a lot so I wouldn't show my♥♥♥♥♥on multiplayer servers while trying to fly a damn helicopter.
Oh yeah, the controls are a bit mind boggling at first. I highly recommend you play through the training and show case missions a few times and also rebind the keys as you see fit.
The graphics are unreal. Effort was deffinately put into this game and then handed to the community. Mods are great and theres a mod for almost anything in Arma now. This game series has the best communnity in terms of game Etiquette too. They are willing to help teach you if your new and take the game seriously.
This isn't a Call of Duty type game. The enemy will see you from very far away and has great accuracy. You'll probably die in two hits. Play the game tactically and with teamwork (def don't walk into a building alone).
The games only downfall is the multiplayer graphics optimization. I have a 970 OC 4GB and I get crazy frame drops in matches on ultra if theres more than 50 players in the match. To play with 100+ players I have to set my brand new gaming computer to medium settings to avoid crazy amounts of lag.
One last note,
If you want to fly the helicopters in multiplayer make sure you practice a lot in the training and showcase missions. You do not want to be the one that wipes a whole squad of infantry because you forgot to put down the landing gear and had a vertical descent faster than 5 m/s. I highly suggest auto-hover and telling the guys to fast rope out themselves so you can bug out faster.

I remembered having a lot of fun playing Operation Flashpoint (the birth of the Arma series). Having had a brief look at Arma 2 and not liking it, and then being hugely disappointed with DayZ, a friend had to offer me $10 to convince me to buy Arma 3 at sale price. Like the other Arma games it offers a huge game world and lots of content. Unfortunately, it still suffers from the same quirks as it's predecessors. The game feels laggy and unresponsive even with a high frame rate and enemy soldiers don't react realistically when being shot. Whilst you can control various vehicles, they fly/drive poorly with no regard for physics. What's worse, in Arma 3 the landscape and most of the equipment is fictional, which removes an element of immersion. There are plenty of mods to tailor the game to your tastes, but you'll never fix the underlying flaws of the engine.
If you're a diehard military FPS fan, you'll find something to like here (as many others have). If you pay attention to the finer details, physics, realism, damage modelling, hit boxes and overall quality of a game engine you should steer clear.

Please consider that this is a fairly detailed review that will help you to find out if ArmA 3 suits YOU (ignoring your system specifications).
Armed Assault 3 is a tactical military shooter. And I'm not saying it's the best out there, because it cannot be compared to ANY other military-themed games like Insurgency or Battlefield. Arma 3 is UNIQUE in its gameplay. Try it yourself if you don't believe me.
This game will require a few mods (and the "elite" setting) to become - to some extent - a realistic military simulator. Without realism-enhancing addons you'll find yourself facing ridiculous things like an arcade-style medical system and will probably have to hit enemies up to five times before they die, even with marksman rifles.
Moreover, unlike the previous game of the Armed Assault Series, ArmA 3 does not feature a massive variety of firearms and vehicles, which was hugely disappointing for me when I first launched the game. Not to forget the game's 2035 setting (including the insect-like helmets standardized amongst soldiers of the OPFOR faction). This could be a pro or a con according to your opinion, nevertheless.
Surprisingly, this game has its creative edge, too. There is a built-in Mission editor in ArmA3, which allows you to create your own scenarios and provides an excellent way to make yourself familiar with all factions and equipment.
Do NOT expect any multiplayer game mode to have any sort of even minor realistic touch. Just don't. You'd then probably have the worst experience you can imagine, playing amongst teamgriefing 12-year-olds pretending to be Rambo. At some point I came to the conclusion that this game was designed solely for cooperative gameplay against AI.
So what about the singleplayer mode?
Maybe give it a shot or two, but don't waste your time there. And don't get frustrated. Although ArmA 3's singleplayer mode is based on an interesting story and features lots of detailed missions, you will quickly begin to hate the game for the unbelievably stupid AI following you on the battlefield.
Well, that sounds like the game's complete crap...
No, it isn't. Not at all. Given that you are interested in this kind of game, have some patience and found yourself a community (or "clan") that supports your playstyle and experience, which also allows you to know what ArmA is really like and realize how it's supposed to be played. If you're willing to do all this, I definitely recommend the game!
Overall impression:
+ Authentic and (given certain conditions) realistic gameplay
+ Tons of mods are available (1500+)
+ Great to play with friends
+ Mission editor
+ Large maps
+ Fantastic developers
- Fairly difficult to familiarize with
- Singleplayer mode may not meet a gamer's expectations
- Not as variegated as the previous ArmA
- Too many DLCs containing too little content
+/- Futuristic setting
+/- Very different from any other games
+/- Very time consuming
Please consider that I may have forgotten some aspects here.

The first person shooter for those who dislike the far fetched things in games like call of duty and halo and who want the expansive enviroments that put battlefield to shame. While the Arma franchise prides its self on being a simulator it still has it's gimicks and comedic hickups, be it some very interesting animations, ragdolling or just physics occasionally breaking (
).
Don't be put off by that if you're looking for the ultimate military simulator however as when it works (which is does more often than not) arma offers some intense fighting with a range of weaponry and veichles. Arma allows you to operate ( with multiple people) veichles such as the standard civilian cars, trucks and jeeps as well as the more traditional viechles seen in warfare games, tanks, APCs, AA viehcles and artillery. Arma also offers a range of aircraft veichles ( be it more helicopters than jets) like the A-10 warthog bomber and the huron heavy lift chopper. Each veichle type follows its own set of physics which are relativley accurate to that of the real thing.
Weapons are o'plenty in arma 3 but I see little point in detailing every weapon in the game. In short theirs everything you'd expect to find soldiers armed with. The weapons in arma 3 offer different fire modes and caliber of round, different calibers doing specific penetration and damage, for example the  5.63mm Katibla rifle hardly scratches anything armored where as a well placed shot from the 12.7mm GMB Lynx sniper rifle can disable a chopper or jet.
there are a variety of game modes to suit your liking and mods if those are your thing. The three most common game modes you'll see on the server browser are
They are all distinctly different. Wasteland offers you a choice of 3 teams to join with preset load outs. You then scavange veichles and weapons from the veichles and attempt to do missions on the map to raise fun for better gear to wage war on other players. In short its sandbox survival. Some servers also include a base building function.
Altis life is something a lot of new players seem to enjoy both playing and watching people stream. Personally I hate it, but thats just my opinion. Altis life is a role playing community that aims to represent some form of normality. Civilian players work to earn money and Police players enforce the laws. Civilians can make money through illicit activities as well as legal ones, the illcit ones paying more. Each server is different so I won't go in to too much detail.
Warfare is what it says on the tin. 3 factions battling for contorl of strategic points across altis. OPFOR, BLUFOR and Independant. These servers tend to be a lot more formal and require much more teamwork than the prior two, baisically you have to know what you're doing on the game before venturing on to one of these servers as Armas combat system is like no other first person shooter.
I reccomend this game as something to play with friends and enjoy discovering it together as playing it alone (at least I find) is incredibly dull.
The dlc for this game is not essential to play on servers that have the dlc enabled. However you will not be able to pilot DLC viechles or use DLC weapons ( you can still enter DLC veichles as passangers) . In comparison to Arma 2 the DLC for Arma 3 is very lackluster.
Currently Arma 3 needs a pretty decent computer to run and even then you're likely not going to hit above 60fps. The game is very poorly optimized
My other fued with arma 3 is that manually dropping bombs from a jet is a task that is near impossible. The only way to drop unguided bombs is dive bomb. Using a strafe approach is difficult because the interface on the jets no matter what type they are is configured to that of a fighter jet.
These are all small disadvantages to a game that is so fun with friends
However due to the game only having two maps that are pretty similar it can get repetive very quickly
Over all I say 7/10

Well here I am, over 200 hours into the first game I ever got on steam and finally becoming a P2P player, so I figured it would be fitting to make it my first review.
Hands down, this is one of the best shooters you will ever play. I don't understand all the gripe about the toxic community; nearly everyone I have met has been pretty nice, with a few exceptions. The main things I've learned to be accepted in the community: don't kill friendlies, don't mention Overwatch or COD in comparison to TF2, and don't use the ♥♥♥♥ing reserve shooter as pyro for gods sake. I've also heard people say the game is dead, but far from it. I have never spent more than 3-5 minutes queued up for a match in casual, although almost no one plays comp.
While the learning curve can be off putting for some people, just stick it out and you'll get the hang of it.
All and all, TF2 is a generally well-balanced and fun to play shooter with a supportive and generally easygoing and dedicated community that I will be playing for a long time yet.
P.S. Play with bots for a bit before going in to multiplayer. I promise it will help.
